stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Beijing for talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping days after US President Trump concluded his own visit to China, making the summit closely watched by international observers.

stories.title: Navy greenlights low-rate production of drone refueler
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy has approved low-rate initial production of the MQ-25A Stingray unmanned aerial refueling drone. A contract for three aircraft is expected to be awarded this summer.

stories.title: Putin on the back foot? Russian president in China as Ukraine campaign stalls
stories.summary: Vladimir Putin visited Beijing days after Donald Trump's trip to China, with Russia seeking to demonstrate strong ties with its key partner. However, Xi Jinping showed no urgency to finalize the Power of Siberia 2 gas pipeline, which would double Russian gas exports to China.

stories.title: 2 killed, 11 injured in rain-related incidents in KP: PDMA
stories.summary: Two people were killed and 11 injured in rain-related incidents in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Monday, according to the Provincial Disaster Management Authority. Deaths were reported in Mardan, while injuries occurred in Battagram, Mardan, and Swat, with multiple houses damaged.

stories.title: Minab school struck at start of Iran war was located on active missile base, CENTCOM chief says
stories.summary: CENTCOM chief stated that a girls' school in Minab, Iran, struck at the start of the US-Iran war was located on an active missile base. Reuters had previously reported that an internal US military investigation found US forces were likely responsible for the school's destruction.

stories.title: TTAP, PTI announces countrywide protests on Friday against Imran's imprisonment, rising inflation
stories.summary: Pakistan's opposition alliance TTAP and PTI announced countrywide protests for Friday against the imprisonment of former Prime Minister Imran Khan and rising inflation. The announcement was made by senior PTI leaders including former National Assembly speaker Asad Qaiser outside Parliament House in Islamabad.

stories.title: US lawmakers press Centcom chief over Iran war civilian deaths
stories.summary: Democratic Representative John Garamendi questioned CENTCOM chief Admiral Brad Cooper during a congressional hearing about whether hostilities between the US and Iran have truly ceased since last month's ceasefire announcement. Cooper maintained the US remained in a ceasefire despite recent attacks by both sides.

stories.title: 'Ebola has tortured us': Fear grips eastern DR Congo as deadly virus spreads
stories.summary: An Ebola outbreak is spreading in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, causing widespread fear. The DRC health minister acknowledged that medical responders were slow to detect the virus and are now playing catch-up.

stories.title: In Focus podcast | Why Trump is in a strategic gridlock over Iran?
stories.summary: A podcast episode examines President Trump's evolving posture toward Iran and the strategic constraints he faces. Analyst Stanly Johny discusses how Gulf powers are influencing U.S. decision-making behind the scenes regarding the Iran standoff.

stories.title: Beijing brushes off allegations Chinese ship hit by Russian drone
stories.summary: Beijing downplayed allegations that a Russian Shahed drone struck the Chinese cargo vessel KSL Deyang in the Black Sea. Ukraine had reported the incident, claiming the drone hit the Chinese ship. China's response brushed off the claims without elaborating.

stories.title: Estonian FM on drone incident: Ukraine has full right to strike Russian military targets
stories.summary: Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna stated that Ukraine has full legal and moral right to strike Russian military targets, commenting after a drone incident over Estonian territory.

stories.title: Trump was 'an hour away' from a decision on Iran before being called to wait
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said he was one hour away from ordering a military strike on Iran before several Middle Eastern governments called and asked him to wait several days to allow negotiations to continue.

stories.title: Israel assesses ICC will issue arrest warrants for five officials over Gaza war crime allegations
stories.summary: Israel assesses that the International Criminal Court will issue arrest warrants for five Israeli officials over allegations of war crimes in Gaza. Those expected to be named include Defense Minister Katz, Finance Minister Smotrich, National Security Minister Ben-Gvir, IDF Chief Zamir, and Southern Command Chief Yaniv Asor.

stories.title: Hungary's new Prime Minister Magyar seeks to fix Poland ties
stories.summary: Hungary's new Prime Minister Peter Magyar visited Warsaw seeking to repair relations with Poland. The trip marked his first state visit and an effort to rebuild ties strained under his predecessor.

stories.title: Hamas rejects Board of Peace report on Gaza truce stalling
stories.summary: Hamas rejected a report by the Trump-appointed Board of Peace that identified the group's refusal to disarm as the main obstacle to fully implementing the Gaza ceasefire.

stories.title: Somaliland to open embassy in Jerusalem, Israel in Hargeisa: Envoy
stories.summary: Somaliland has announced plans to open an embassy in Jerusalem, while Israel will establish an embassy in Hargeisa. The move follows Israel's official recognition of Somaliland's independence from Somalia.

stories.title: One year in, Army’s transformation efforts are under fire
stories.summary: One year into the U.S. Army's transformation efforts, the initiative faces scrutiny. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is reportedly reconsidering his directive to retire legacy systems in favor of newer technology.

stories.title: Police say extra funds to hunt grooming gangs in England and Wales will ‘likely fall short’
stories.summary: The UK government announced a near tenfold funding increase to £38 million for Operation Beaconport, which reviews closed group-based sexual exploitation cases in England and Wales. Police warned the amount will likely fall short of what is needed to establish dedicated grooming gang investigation teams.

stories.title: G7 to maintain sanctions pressure to prevent Russia from financing war against Ukraine – French minister
stories.summary: G7 finance ministers reaffirmed support for Ukraine and agreed to maintain sanctions pressure on Russia to prevent Moscow from generating revenues to finance its war effort, according to a French minister.

stories.title: Ukraine apologizes to Estonia after drone enters its airspace and is shot down by NATO fighter jets
stories.summary: Ukraine formally apologized to Estonia after a Ukrainian drone entered Estonian airspace and was shot down by a NATO fighter jet. Ukrainian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Heorhii Tykhyi issued the apology on social media.

stories.title: Putin arrives in China for talks with Chinese leader Xi Jinping
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Beijing for talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, in a visit closely watched amid shifting global diplomacy.

stories.title: Suspected gunman in deadly shootings in southern Türkiye ends life as police close in during a major search effort
stories.summary: A 37-year-old suspect armed with a rifle killed his wife and five other people in Tarsus, Mersin Province, Turkey, on May 18, 2026, and wounded eight others. The suspect ended his own life as police closed in during a major search operation.

stories.title: Canada faces pressure over killing of citizen in Israeli strike on Lebanon
stories.summary: The Canadian government faces growing pressure to pursue accountability after citizen Hassan Haidar, a 38-year-old father of five from Windsor, Ontario, was killed in an Israeli drone strike on the village of Qana in southern Lebanon on April 10. Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand was questioned about Ottawa's decision to ask Israel to investigate the killing.

stories.title: In Berlin, ex-captive Alon Ohel plays piano in appreciation of support
stories.summary: Former Israeli captive and pianist Alon Ohel performed at an event hosted by the Israeli ambassador in Berlin. Ohel shared how music helped him survive his time in captivity.

stories.title: Somaliland’s first-ever embassy anywhere will open in Jerusalem, envoy says
stories.summary: A Somaliland diplomat announced that the breakaway East African state will open its first-ever embassy in Jerusalem. Israel is also expected to open an embassy in Somaliland's capital, Hargeisa.

stories.title: Big data AI startup will open Tel Aviv engineering hub to tap into local tech talent
stories.summary: US-based big data AI startup Fundamental announced plans to open an engineering hub in Tel Aviv to access local tech talent. The company intends to hire dozens of employees for its risk-prediction and trend-analysis platform.

stories.title: Norway reports Europe’s first case of bird flu in a polar bear
stories.summary: Norwegian authorities confirmed Europe's first documented case of bird flu in a polar bear, detected in the Svalbard archipelago in the Arctic. The H5N5 variant was found in a young male bear and a walrus discovered dead in mid-May, according to the Norwegian Veterinary Institute.

stories.title: Russian missile, drone strikes kill four in Ukraine's northern regions, officials say
stories.summary: Russian missile and drone strikes on Ukraine's northern Chernihiv and Sumy regions killed four people and injured several others on Tuesday. Ukrainian officials reported the attacks, which targeted civilian areas in the two regions bordering Russia.

stories.title: How the Iranian regime ensures civilians bear the burden of its war against the US, Israel
stories.summary: An analysis describes how the Iranian regime's policies ensure civilians bear disproportionate consequences of the war against the US and Israel. The system reportedly limits access to financial stability opportunities to those who subscribe to the state's religious governance framework of Velayat-e Faqih.

stories.title: US imposes sanctions on Gaza flotilla organisers amid Israeli crackdown
stories.summary: The United States has imposed sanctions on organisers of a Gaza-bound aid flotilla. Rights advocates have accused Washington of using terrorism designations to suppress pro-Palestinian activism internationally.

stories.title: Israel’s far-right Finance Minister Smotrich says ICC seeking his arrest
stories.summary: Israel's far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich stated that the International Criminal Court is seeking his arrest. Following the ICC warrant request, Smotrich threatened to displace Palestinians from the West Bank.

stories.title: Israeli minister Smotrich says ICC prosecutor seeking warrant for his arrest
stories.summary: Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich stated that the ICC prosecutor is seeking an arrest warrant against him. The Hague-based International Criminal Court declined to comment, noting that warrant applications are classified as secret.

stories.title: Asian Reactions to Trump’s Summit with Xi
stories.summary: President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping held a summit in Beijing on May 14–15, discussing Iran, the Strait of Hormuz, Taiwan, and bilateral trade. Experts from Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, and the Philippines offered perspectives on how the summit and its outcomes were received across Asia.

stories.title: Shield AI tapped to integrate autonomous software on LUCAS drone
stories.summary: Shield AI announced it will integrate its Hivemind autonomous software onto the LUCAS drone platform. The company plans to demonstrate the drone's swarming capability later this year.

stories.title: Diplomacy under fire: Where are Lebanon-Israel talks heading?
stories.summary: Lebanon-Israel negotiations continue amid a ceasefire extension, but familiar obstacles persist including Israeli maximalism and Lebanon's limited negotiating leverage. Questions remain about the US's effectiveness as a mediator in the talks.

stories.title: NS&I to contact bereaved families owed £367m after missing savings scandal
stories.summary: UK state-backed bank National Savings and Investments will begin contacting thousands of bereaved families next week who are owed a total of £367 million due to failures in tracing accounts of deceased customers. The bank's interim chief executive acknowledged the issue should never have occurred.

stories.title: British Airways delays Middle East flights until August
stories.summary: British Airways postponed the resumption of flights to Dubai, Doha, and Tel Aviv until August 1 due to continued instability in the Middle East. The airline also plans to reduce the number of flights to the region once operations resume.

stories.title: Tributes pour in for ‘hero’ guard killed in San Diego mosque shooting
stories.summary: Amin Abdullah, a security guard at the Islamic Centre of San Diego, was killed while attempting to stop gunmen from entering the mosque. Tributes have been paid to Abdullah, who has been called a hero.

stories.title: Official says Germany has already provided EUR 1.2B in energy sector support to Ukraine
stories.summary: Germany has provided more than EUR 1.2 billion in emergency support to Ukraine's energy sector, making it the largest bilateral donor in that field, according to an official statement.

stories.title: Surrey police launch investigation into UK Epstein abuse allegations
stories.summary: Surrey police in the UK have launched a criminal investigation into child sexual abuse allegations after two women came forward claiming they were victims of attacks detailed in the Epstein files. The allegations date back to the 1980s and 1990s, involving locations in Surrey and Berkshire.

stories.title: Iran starts Bitcoin-backed shipping insurance for Hormuz strait
stories.summary: Iran launched a Bitcoin-backed shipping insurance service called "Hormuz Safe" for the Strait of Hormuz. The service is designed for Iranian shipping companies and cargo owners navigating the strategic waterway.

stories.title: San Diego mosque guard hailed a hero after deadly shooting
stories.summary: A security guard at the Islamic Center in San Diego was hailed as a hero after being killed while attempting to stop gunmen during the deadly mosque shooting.

stories.title: Russian Director Andrey Zvyagintsev Returns to Cannes Film Festival After Near-Fatal Illness
stories.summary: Russian film director Andrey Zvyagintsev, known for "Leviathan" and "Loveless," returned to the Cannes Film Festival after a near-fatal illness. He had been left in a coma and unable to walk for a year following a severe reaction to Russia's Sputnik V vaccine in 2021.

stories.title: Three Toronto police officers charged with sexual assault in Barcelona
stories.summary: Three off-duty Toronto police officers were charged with sexual assault in Barcelona after allegedly attacking a sex worker in a taxi in the Ciutat Vella neighborhood on May 13, according to Catalan police.

stories.title: UK supermarkets urged to consider voluntary price caps on essential foods
stories.summary: The UK government urged supermarkets to consider voluntary price caps on essential food items to shield consumers from inflation driven by the Middle East conflict. Retailers rejected the proposal, arguing it was unjustified and could increase costs across the board amid rising taxes and energy prices.

stories.title: Police to seek criminal charges against 77 companies and people over Grenfell fire
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police announced plans to seek criminal charges against 77 companies and individuals in connection with the Grenfell Tower fire, which killed 72 people. A senior lawyer has been appointed to lead the prosecutions, though trials are not expected to begin until a decade after the 2017 disaster.

stories.title: More US troop withdrawals from Europe expected, NATO commander says
stories.summary: NATO Supreme Allied Commander Gen. Alexus Grynkewich said on Tuesday that Europe should expect additional U.S. troop withdrawals as allied nations take on greater responsibility for their own defense.

stories.title: Can Armenia’s Democracy Prevail?
stories.summary: Armenia's democratic governance faces challenges, with analysts warning that unconditional Western support for incumbent Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan could have unintended negative consequences for the country's democratic trajectory.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces strike Russian command post in Pokrovsk
stories.summary: Operators from the Raid regiment of Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces struck a command post belonging to Russia's 9th Motor Rifle Brigade of the 51st Combined Arms Army in the occupied city of Pokrovsk in Donetsk Oblast.

stories.title: Trump says US could strike Iran again within days without deal
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump warned that the US could launch another military strike on Iran within days if no agreement is reached. Speaking at the White House, Trump claimed Tehran was eager to negotiate and stressed the urgency of preventing Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons.

stories.title: Trump endorses attorney general Ken Paxton in Texas Senate primary
stories.summary: President Trump endorsed Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton in the Republican Senate primary runoff against incumbent Senator John Cornyn. Trump praised Paxton as an "America First Patriot" in a social media post on Tuesday.

stories.title: Rescuers search for three missing after German building collapse possibly caused by gas explosion
stories.summary: Emergency crews in Germany continued searching for three missing people after a building collapse reportedly triggered by a suspected gas explosion. Several other people were injured in the incident.

stories.title: Trump says Xi assured him China would not send weapons to Iran
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said Chinese President Xi Jinping assured him that China would not send weapons to Iran. Trump also warned he could strike Iran again if progress on a ceasefire is not achieved within days.

stories.title: US wants Ukraine’s AI-assisted targeting, GPS-free navigation, and IP to reproduce it, but Zelenskyy has red line
stories.summary: Ukraine plans to produce three million attack drones in 2025, while the United States—having built 300,000 last year—is seeking access to Ukrainian AI-assisted targeting, GPS-free navigation, and related intellectual property to replicate the technology. President Zelenskyy has set limits on technology transfers.

stories.title: In 65% of JWed’s 4,100+ marriages, Jewish women made the first move - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Jewish dating platform JWed reported that in 65% of its more than 4,100 marriages, women initiated contact first. The service has operated for over 25 years, helping Jewish singles connect.

stories.title: Death toll from Russian strike on Pryluky rises to three, 29 injured
stories.summary: A Russian ballistic missile struck the central part of Pryluky, Ukraine, killing three people including a 15-year-old boy who later died in hospital. Twenty-nine others were injured in the attack.

stories.title: Israel Air Force introduces all-women Arad special commando unit
stories.summary: The Israel Air Force established an all-women special commando unit called "Arad," created as an intervention force based on lessons learned from the October 7 massacre and Operation Iron Swords.

stories.title: Woman shot dead by police in Jamaica at protest over previous police shooting
stories.summary: Jamaican authorities launched an investigation after a police officer fatally shot 45-year-old Latoya Bulgin during a protest in Granville, St. James parish, on Sunday. CCTV footage circulating online shows the officer firing at the vehicle Bulgin was driving during a demonstration over a previous police shooting.

stories.title: Israel orders evacuations in 12 towns in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli military spokesperson Avichay Adraee issued evacuation orders to residents of 12 towns and villages in southern Lebanon ahead of anticipated Israeli attacks. The warnings came despite a ceasefire that took effect the previous month.

stories.title: Trades of Eli Lilly shares were made on Trump’s behalf as drugmaker benefited from his policies
stories.summary: Financial disclosures revealed that trades worth between $220 million and $750 million were made on President Trump's behalf in the first quarter of 2026, including investments in Eli Lilly. The drugmaker had benefited from the administration's move to expand access to its obesity treatments.

stories.title: From battlefield to backyard: Inside Israel's Cando drone revolution
stories.summary: Israeli company Cando is developing drone technology for civilian applications, including potential organ delivery. CEO Ghil Hardy outlined the company's vision of transitioning military drone expertise to everyday domestic uses.

stories.title: Iran stages mass weddings for couples pledging to sacrifices lives in war with US, Israel
stories.summary: Iran held mass weddings in Tehran for couples who pledged to sacrifice their lives in the war against the US and Israel. More than 100 couples arrived at Imam Hossein Square in military jeeps with mounted machine guns and were wed on stage by a cleric.

stories.title: Liberman says his goal for the upcoming election is to become prime minister
stories.summary: Israeli politician Avigdor Liberman announced that his goal for the upcoming election is to become prime minister. His Yisrael Beytenu party currently polls at around nine Knesset seats, and he ruled out joining a Netanyahu-led coalition for leverage.

stories.title: Mobutu-Era Abacost suit makes stylish comeback in DR Congo
stories.summary: The Abacost suit, a collarless jacket popularized by former president Mobutu Sese Seko in 1970s Zaire as a symbol of African identity, is experiencing a fashion revival in the Democratic Republic of Congo nearly three decades after Mobutu's fall.

stories.title: Diving into Golden Dome’s new pricetag, plus winning the Army’s network wars
stories.summary: A defense analysis program reviewed updated cost projections for the Golden Dome missile defense system. The episode also covered a joint exercise at Fort Carson, Colorado, where special forces and infantry units tested novel networked operations.

stories.title: WATCH: Car bomb explodes near Defense Ministry building in Damascus
stories.summary: A car bomb exploded near the Defense Ministry building in Damascus, Syria. The health ministry said emergency teams responded to the blast, which killed one soldier and wounded approximately 12 people.

stories.title: At least 22 killed in Israeli attacks on Lebanon in 24 hours: Ministry
stories.summary: At least 22 people were killed in Israeli attacks across Lebanon over a 24-hour period, according to Lebanon's Health Ministry. The ministry reported that the cumulative death toll since March 2 has reached 3,042.

stories.title: At least 2 dead, 4 injured in southern Spain shooting
stories.summary: A gunman in southern Spain killed his parents and injured four others, including his son. At least two people died in the shooting. Authorities are investigating the incident.

stories.title: G7 Finance Ministers explore responses to Iran war fallout
stories.summary: French Finance Minister Roland Lescure hosted a G7 Finance Ministers' meeting in Paris to explore coordinated responses to the economic fallout from the war involving Iran.

stories.title: Iraq condemns drone attacks on Saudi Arabia amid US pressure on Iranian-backed militias
stories.summary: Iraq condemned recent drone attacks targeting Saudi Arabia and pledged cooperation in the investigation. Baghdad moved to distance Iranian-backed militias from the attacks amid growing U.S. pressure on such groups.

stories.title: Ukraine apologizes to Estonia over unintended drone incident – Foreign Ministry
stories.summary: Ukraine's Foreign Ministry apologized to Estonia over a drone that entered Estonian airspace, attributing the unintended incident to interference from Russian electronic warfare systems. Spokesperson Heorhii Tykhyi confirmed the apology.

stories.title: Estonian military shoots down Ukrainian drone for the first time after it enters the country’s airspace
stories.summary: Estonian air defense forces shot down a drone over Lake Võrtsjärv on the morning of May 19 after it entered the country's airspace. Defense Minister Hanno Pevkur confirmed it was the first time Estonia had shot down a drone itself.

stories.title: Trump says US was close to launching new strike on Iran
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump revealed the US came within an hour of launching another military strike on Iran before delaying the operation. Trump said naval vessels had already been loaded with missiles ahead of the planned attack, adding that the military could still carry out another strike during ongoing negotiations.

stories.title: Beijing is far more directly involved in war than previously understood: China secretly trained 200 Russian troops in 2025
stories.summary: According to European intelligence sources, approximately 200 Russian military personnel secretly trained in China in late 2025 under a bilateral agreement, marking a deeper level of Chinese involvement in the war than previously known.

stories.title: Tai Po blaze: Hong Kong to ban smoking at construction sites from July 17
stories.summary: Hong Kong's government announced a ban on smoking at construction sites effective July 17, submitting three legislative amendments on Tuesday. The measure follows the deadly fire at Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po in November 2025, which spurred community consensus for stricter fire-safety rules at construction sites.

stories.title: Brush fire near Los Angeles forces thousands to evacuate
stories.summary: A wind-driven wildfire called the Sandy Fire forced thousands of people to evacuate from areas near Simi Valley, approximately 30 miles northwest of Los Angeles. The fire was reported Monday morning in hills above the suburban community in Southern California.

stories.title: San Diego mosque shooting: Social media decries 'dehumanising' coverage and anti-Muslim rhetoric
stories.summary: Three people were killed in a shooting at the Islamic Center in San Diego, California, on May 18. Social media users criticized media framing of the attack and denounced widespread anti-Muslim rhetoric in its aftermath.

stories.title: Gunman kills eight at busy Egypt transport hub
stories.summary: A gunman killed eight people and injured five others at a busy transport hub in Egypt before being shot dead by security forces. No further details about the attacker's identity or motive were immediately provided.

stories.title: Israel Bonds unveils new stamp marking 75 Years of Investment in Israel - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Israel Bonds unveiled a commemorative stamp in Tel Aviv issued by the Israel Postal Service to mark its 75th anniversary of facilitating investment in Israel.

stories.title: Rising Cuba-US tensions amid talk of drones, emergency plans
stories.summary: Rising tensions between Cuba and the United States have intensified amid reports of Cuban drone purchases and renewed threats. Many Cubans expressed outrage at official advice to prepare for a potential attack while the country faces blackouts and shortages.

stories.title: Ghana hopes to attract investors after €3 billion IMF bailout ends
stories.summary: Ghana's three-year, €3 billion IMF bailout program has concluded, and the country now seeks to attract international investors. Ghana needed the IMF support to recover from its worst economic downturn in decades, driven by the pandemic, Russia's invasion of Ukraine, and high inflation.

stories.title: Replay: Trump addresses Iran war and FRANCE 24's analysis
stories.summary: President Trump publicly addressed the ongoing conflict with Iran amid stalled diplomatic talks between Washington and Tehran. He also discussed Cuba during the remarks, which were followed by analysis from FRANCE 24.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces strike Russian pontoon crossings in Donetsk region
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces struck a Russian command and observation post near Tyotkino in Russia's Kursk region on May 18, along with several other targets in the Kherson, Sumy, Dnipropetrovsk, and Donetsk regions.

stories.title: Flash warns air defense crews not to wait for orders, as Russia is now hunting them with real-time-piloted Shaheds
stories.summary: A Ukrainian commander known as Flash warned air defense crews to engage Russian drones without waiting for orders, as Russia is now using real-time-piloted Shahed drones to hunt air defense positions. He also cautioned crews against firing carelessly to avoid revealing their locations.

stories.title: Public complaints in Israel soar as state failures compound
stories.summary: Public complaints filed in Israel surged, with the state ombudsman finding 56 percent of adjudicated complaints justified — the highest rate since the commission's establishment. An additional 7,429 complaints were resolved without a formal decision.

stories.title: 'Rats are eating our food': Palestinians describe harrowing conditions in Gaza camp
stories.summary: Palestinians in the al-Mawasi refugee camp in southern Gaza described dire conditions including rat-infested tents, poor sanitation, and spreading diseases. Residents shared testimonies while waiting for support at a Medical Aid for Palestinians-supported healthcare centre in Khan Younis.

stories.title: Iraq pledges cooperation with Saudi Arabia over drone attack
stories.summary: Iraq pledged to cooperate with Saudi Arabia in investigating an alleged drone attack while denying any evidence that drones crossed Iraqi airspace.

stories.title: Russian jamming blamed after Nato jet downs Ukrainian drone over Estonia
stories.summary: A Romanian F-16 fighter jet operating under NATO's Baltic air policing mission shot down a Ukrainian drone over Estonia on Tuesday. Officials from Baltic states blamed Russian electronic jamming for diverting the long-range Ukrainian drone into NATO airspace, while also urging Kyiv to adjust its drone routing.

stories.title: WHO warns of ‘scale and speed’ of deadly Ebola outbreak in DR Congo
stories.summary: The World Health Organization warned about the alarming scale and speed of a deadly Ebola outbreak spreading in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

stories.title: Defense department watchdog opens inquiry into US airstrikes on alleged drug boats
stories.summary: The Pentagon's inspector general opened an investigation into whether U.S. military commanders followed proper procedures before conducting lethal strikes on alleged drug boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific.

stories.title: Islamabad court hands death sentence to convict in Sana Yousaf murder case
stories.summary: An Islamabad court sentenced Umar Hayat to death for the 2025 murder of 17-year-old TikTok influencer Sana Yousaf, who was shot dead at her home on June 2, 2025. Judge Afzal Majoka also imposed 10 years imprisonment and a two-million-rupee fine.

stories.title: Tanker delivers Russian LNG to China after almost six months at sea, LSEG ship-tracking data shows
stories.summary: A tanker carrying Russian liquefied natural gas arrived in China after a nearly six-month voyage, according to LSEG ship-tracking data. Russia has continued LNG exports to China despite Western sanctions.

stories.title: U.S. military watchdog probes strikes on alleged drug boats: reports
stories.summary: A U.S. military watchdog is investigating strikes on vessels alleged to be drug boats. Legal experts and human rights groups have raised concerns that the attacks could constitute extrajudicial killings, as the targeted civilians reportedly posed no immediate threat to the United States.

stories.title: Nigeria: Elumelu Warns Against Disinformation Ahead of 2027 Elections
stories.summary: Nigerian lawmaker Ndudi Elumelu warned against the rising spread of disinformation ahead of the country's 2027 general elections, urging journalists and political actors to act responsibly to protect democracy.

stories.title: WHO worried about ‘scale and speed’ of deadly Ebola outbreak
stories.summary: The WHO expressed concern about the scale and speed of the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with at least 500 suspected cases and 130 suspected deaths reported.

stories.title: New Zealand's government plans to cut 14% of public sector jobs to slash spending
stories.summary: New Zealand's government announced plans to cut approximately 14 percent of public sector jobs as part of a spending reduction effort. Military personnel, teachers, and doctors would be exempt from the cuts. The number of government departments and agencies would also be reduced from the current 39.

stories.title: Israeli police establish special department to monitor foreign journalists
stories.summary: Israeli police established a special department to monitor foreign journalists working in Israel. Foreign reporters have faced increased monitoring and restrictions, particularly in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Gaza aid flotilla says Israeli forces intercepted 41 vessels, 10 still sailing
stories.summary: A Gaza-bound aid flotilla reported that Israeli forces intercepted 41 of its vessels, with 10 still sailing. The closest vessel, the Sirius, was 145 nautical miles from Gaza at the time of the report.

stories.title: Pakistan sentences man to death for killing TikTok star Sana Yousaf
stories.summary: A Pakistani court sentenced Umar Hayat to death for the murder of teenage TikTok star Sana Yousaf, who was killed in her home. The victim's father said the verdict sends a message to all of society.

stories.title: Russian strike on Shevchenkove in Kharkiv region kills woman, injures three others
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out a drone strike on the settlement of Shevchenkove in the Kupiansk district of Kharkiv region, killing a woman and leaving three others suffering from acute stress reactions.

stories.title: A Ukrainian ground robot defended a position from Russian assault for six weeks
stories.summary: A Ukrainian unmanned ground vehicle independently defended a frontline position against Russian assaults for six weeks. The deployment signals the growing role of ground robots in replacing infantry on Ukraine's front lines.

stories.title: Security guards face probe after last week’s Philippine Senate shooting
stories.summary: Philippine authorities launched a probe into security guards involved in a shooting incident at the Senate last week. Officials said the event was not an attack on the Senate and identified the person who fired the first shot.

stories.title: Masked Men Raid Central Moscow Office Building Housing Pro-Kremlin Tabloid
stories.summary: Masked men raided an office building in central Moscow that houses the pro-Kremlin tabloid Moskovsky Komsomolets. Surveillance footage showed at least four masked individuals forcing their way into the building's lobby.

stories.title: Qatar says US-Iran negotiations need ‘more time’
stories.summary: Qatar's foreign ministry stated that ongoing US-Iran negotiations require more time to make progress. The Gulf state has been serving as a mediator in the diplomatic process between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Ukraine trains demining specialists to use unique drone-mounted magnetometers
stories.summary: Ukraine is training demining specialists to operate drone-mounted magnetometers that detect explosive ordnance by reading magnetic shifts in the soil, reducing the need for sappers to walk through minefields.

stories.title: US imposes fresh sanctions on Iranian exchange house, 19 ships from shadow fleet
stories.summary: The Trump administration imposed new sanctions on an Iranian foreign currency exchange house, associated front companies, and 19 ships from Iran's shadow fleet. The action came as Iran presented a peace proposal addressing the U.S.-Israeli-led conflict, including calls for a ceasefire on all fronts and U.S. force withdrawals from areas near Iran.

stories.title: WHO chief says 'deeply concerned' by 'scale and speed' of Democratic Republic Congo’s Ebola outbreak
stories.summary: WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus declared the DRC Ebola outbreak a public health emergency of international concern, the second-highest alert level under international health regulations. He expressed deep concern over the outbreak's scale and speed.

stories.title: At least one killed, 21 wounded in car bomb explosion in Syria’s Damascus
stories.summary: A car bomb explosion in the Bab Sharqi district of Damascus, near Syria's Defence Ministry building, killed at least one person and wounded 21 others.

stories.title: Iran says peace proposal includes reparations for war damage, US troop withdrawal
stories.summary: Iran presented a peace proposal that includes demands for reparations for war damage and the withdrawal of US troops. The terms appeared largely unchanged from Tehran's previous negotiating positions.

stories.title: Nigeria: 2027 - 'I'm 63, You Can't Call Me Boy, Be Careful!' Kano Governor Warns Kwankwaso
stories.summary: Kano State Governor Yusuf responded to political rival Rabiu Kwankwaso, warning him to be careful with his language ahead of Nigeria's 2027 elections. The governor stated his silence should not be mistaken for weakness.

stories.title: Gaza aid flotilla says Israeli forces intercepted 41 vessels, 10 still sailing
stories.summary: A Gaza-bound aid flotilla reported that Israeli forces intercepted 41 of its vessels, with 10 still sailing. Israel's Foreign Ministry had stated it would not permit any breach of its naval blockade on Gaza.

stories.title: Nigeria: Alleged Whatsapp Group Call - Pman Suspend Treasurer, Others, Appoint Uche James
stories.summary: Nigeria's Performing Musicians Association of Nigeria suspended its treasurer and other officials for 12 months over an alleged WhatsApp group call incident, appointing Uche James as a replacement.

stories.title: US imposes fresh sanctions on Iranian currency exchange house
stories.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department imposed sanctions on Iran-based Amin Exchange and 19 vessels, along with front companies operating across the UAE, Turkey, and Hong Kong that allegedly facilitated transactions on behalf of Iranian banks.

stories.title: Nigeria: APC Primaries - Abiru Secures Lagos East Ticket Unopposed for Third Term
stories.summary: Senator Tokunbo Abiru secured the All Progressives Congress ticket unopposed for a third term representing Lagos East in Nigeria's Senate, receiving affirmation votes across all wards in five local government areas.

stories.title: Uganda: Crime Scene - Detectives Raid Speaker's Office
stories.summary: Police detectives in Kampala raided the Ugandan Parliament Speaker's office as part of ongoing investigations into the activities of outgoing Speaker Anita Among.

stories.title: Russia begins three days of nuclear drills
stories.summary: Russia began three days of nuclear drills involving more than 65,000 soldiers and 7,800 types of equipment and weapons. No further details about specific locations or scenarios were immediately disclosed.

stories.title: British student leader among those detained by Israel from Gaza flotilla
stories.summary: Hasnain Jafer, vice president of King's College London's student union, was detained by Israeli authorities after joining the Global Sumud Flotilla attempting to break the siege on Gaza. KCL's student union confirmed he was believed detained in international waters.

stories.title: Nigeria: Stakeholders Advocate Strong Local Defence Industry to Enhance National Security
stories.summary: Nigerian defence stakeholders, led by Defence Industries Association of Nigeria chairman Major General Ibrahim Alaya, called for urgent efforts to strengthen the country's local defence industry to enhance national security and reduce dependence on foreign military hardware.

stories.title: Frontline tool Ukraine can’t fight without: 5,000 pickups now procured through largest-ever open tender
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Procurement Agency launched its largest-ever open tender to procure 5,000 pickup trucks for frontline use, with deliveries through framework agreements expected by year's end.

stories.title: Firebrand Likud MK indicted for disclosing Shin Bet agent’s identity
stories.summary: Likud MK Tally Gotliv was indicted for disclosing the identity of a Shin Bet agent linked to an opposition activist while spreading a conspiracy theory. Gotliv submitted an immunity request to a Knesset panel, and government ministers denounced the Attorney General for what they called persecution of the right.

stories.title: At least ten killed as torrential rains batter southern, central China
stories.summary: Torrential rains in southern and central China killed at least ten people. China's weather agency warned that provinces including Jiangxi, Anhui, Hunan, Hubei, Guizhou, Guangxi, Guangdong, and Hainan faced high risks of rain-related disasters.

stories.title: Ruble leads world currencies in gains against dollar. That’s cutting into revenues for Russian exporters and the state budget.
stories.summary: The Russian ruble became the world's best-performing currency against the U.S. dollar in the second quarter of 2026, according to Bloomberg. The ruble's strength is reportedly cutting into revenues for Russian exporters and the state budget.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces push up to 3 km into Russian defenses near Pokrovsk – Bratchuk
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces advanced up to three kilometers into Russian defensive lines in areas near Pokrovsk on the Donetsk front. The advance was reported by Serhii Bratchuk, spokesperson for the Ukrainian Volunteer Army "South."

stories.title: Hovercraft Accident Kills 5 Russian Tourists on Lake Baikal
stories.summary: Five Russian tourists were killed in a hovercraft accident on Lake Baikal. Emergency service sources said the vehicle was believed to have been heavily overloaded beyond its passenger capacity when it capsized.

stories.title: Russian leader Vladimir Putin arrives in China just days after Donald Trump’s visit
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Beijing on Tuesday for his 25th visit to China, four days after President Trump's trip to the Chinese capital. Putin was greeted with a red-carpet reception by Foreign Minister Wang Yi, with the visit aimed at deepening the countries' comprehensive strategic partnership.

stories.title: KP governor says PM has formed committee to address CNG crisis in province
stories.summary: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi announced that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif formed a committee to address the province's compressed natural gas (CNG) crisis. The KP government and opposition had jointly demanded the federal government resume wheat supply and reverse CNG station closures.

stories.title: New ‘PTSD-friendly’ scheme aims to adapt Israel’s public spaces
stories.summary: Israel is launching a new initiative to make public spaces more accommodating for people with PTSD. Popular apps including Ontopo and Easy business directory will add PTSD-related filters, with participating venues self-certifying their suitability.

stories.title: Police investigating deadly San Diego mosque shooting as hate crime
stories.summary: Police in San Diego are investigating the deadly shooting at a mosque as a hate crime, citing hate rhetoric connected to the attack. The teenage shooter's mother had contacted police before the incident, reporting her son as suicidal and armed.

stories.title: Ukrainian mid-range strikes deal double blow to Russia's war effort
stories.summary: Ukraine's increasing use of medium-range drone strikes is damaging Russian oil refineries and hindering Russia's ground offensive. These attacks represent a growing Ukrainian military capability that is creating significant problems for Russia's war effort.

stories.title: Gunman kills eight at busy Egypt transport hub
stories.summary: A gunman opened fire at a transport hub in southern Egypt, killing eight people before being shot dead by police.

stories.title: Hezbollah drones limiting 80% of Israeli military ops in Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli media reported that Hezbollah's explosive drones are restricting up to 80 percent of Israeli military operations in southern Lebanon, significantly limiting the army's operational capacity in the area.

stories.title: Israeli army reports rise in sexual harassment complaints
stories.summary: The Israeli military reported 2,420 sexual violence complaints filed in 2025, an increase of approximately 350 over the previous year. Indictments were filed in only 42 cases, while 21 incidents led to internal disciplinary action.

stories.title: From job offers to “meat assaults”: The deception of Russia’s foreign fighters
stories.summary: A joint human rights report found that Russia's global recruitment system uses deception, coercion, and economic desperation to funnel tens of thousands of foreign nationals into high-intensity combat roles in Ukraine, often luring recruits with false job offers.

stories.title: ‘Foolish’ CSIRO job cuts will mean Australia unable to provide climate projections to global reports, scientists warn
stories.summary: Australia's national science agency CSIRO is planning to cut a third of the team working on its national climate model. Scientists warn the reductions will prevent Australia from submitting climate projections to global reports and severely diminish the country's ability to forecast future climate impacts.

stories.title: Ukraine strikes Kstovo refinery, supplying 30% of Moscow Oblast’s gasoline 800 km from border
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces struck the Kstovo oil refinery, located roughly 800 kilometers from the border, which supplies about 30 percent of Moscow Oblast's gasoline. It was at least the third strike on the same facility since November.

stories.title: Ukraine denies Russian claims of planned attacks from Latvia, calls them disinformation
stories.summary: Ukraine officially denied Russian claims that Ukrainian forces were preparing attacks on Russia from Latvian territory. Kyiv called the allegations a disinformation campaign aimed at destabilizing the Baltic region.

stories.title: Strike near UAE reactor revives concerns over nuclear plant safety in wartime
stories.summary: A drone strike cut off external power to Reactor No. 3 at the UAE's Barakah nuclear power plant on Sunday, forcing it to rely on emergency diesel generators for approximately 24 hours. The incident has renewed international concerns about the vulnerability of operating nuclear facilities during wartime.

stories.title: Declassified affidavit says Gofman denied approving intel. material transfer to Telegram channels
stories.summary: A declassified IDF affidavit revealed that Major General Roman Gofman denied approving the transfer of division intelligence material to Telegram channels. The document is central to High Court petitions challenging his appointment.

stories.title: Why the Iran war is breaking the US‑European strategic alliance
stories.summary: The ongoing US-Iran conflict is straining the transatlantic strategic alliance, as European nations increasingly recognize they cannot rely on Washington for coordinated policy responses in the Middle East.

stories.title: U.S. plans major expansion of Afrikaner refugee admissions amid political debate
stories.summary: The United States is planning a major expansion of refugee admissions for Afrikaners from South Africa. Supporters cite targeted violence against farmers, while critics argue the move is politically motivated and departs from standard refugee criteria.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces strike Lukoil oil refinery, Yaroslavl-3 pumping station in Russia
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Forces struck the Lukoil-Nizhegorodnefteorgsintez oil refinery on Russian territory on May 18 and hit the Yaroslavl-3 pumping station on May 19.

stories.title: China in a stronger position with US and Russia "embroiled in wars they started"
stories.summary: Russian President Putin's visit to Beijing comes as both the U.S. and Russia are engaged in conflicts, with analysts noting China occupies a strengthened strategic position. The Kremlin described the trip as aimed at deepening a "privileged partnership," building on ties that have grown since Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: Putin hopes to deepen China's commitment to Russian oil
stories.summary: President Putin began a visit to China on May 19, days after President Trump's trip to Beijing, aiming to demonstrate the durability of Sino-Russian ties. The Kremlin said Putin and Xi Jinping would discuss strengthening their strategic partnership and exchange views on key international issues.

stories.title: How dependent is Russia on its economic ties with China?
stories.summary: Since the start of the Ukraine invasion, Western sanctions have pushed Russia to deepen economic ties with China, particularly in oil exports and dual-use technology. An analysis examines the extent of Russia's growing economic dependence on China to sustain its war effort.

stories.title: Thai Singha beer heir dismissed from family firm amid brother’s sexual abuse claims
stories.summary: Thailand's Singha beer empire dismissed a family member from the company after allegations surfaced that he had sexually abused his younger brother. Environmental activist Siranudh Scott, a scion of the Bhirombhakdi family, publicly accused his elder brother in an emotional social media video.

stories.title: NATO planes down suspected Ukrainian drone over Estonia
stories.summary: A NATO fighter jet shot down a suspected Ukrainian drone over Estonian airspace. Incidents of drones straying into allied territory have increased as Ukraine intensifies strikes on Russian Baltic oil facilities.

stories.title: Russia’s four-month budget deficit hit $75.4 billion — 50% above what Moscow planned for entire year
stories.summary: Russia's budget deficit reached $75.4 billion in the first four months of the year, exceeding 50 percent of what Moscow had planned for the entire year. Ukraine's prime minister noted that high oil prices are failing to stabilize Russian finances.

stories.title: Pentagon inks $500 million deal with Perennial Autonomy for counter-drone tech
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Defense awarded a $500 million contract to Perennial Autonomy to accelerate the procurement of counter-drone technology. The deal aims to bolster Pentagon capabilities against unmanned aerial threats.

stories.title: China's Africa trade push: Partnership or power grab?
stories.summary: China has opened its market to 53 African countries, describing the initiative as a "golden key" to prosperity. Analysts caution that the economic impact on African nations may be more complex than Beijing's framing suggests, raising questions about long-term trade imbalances.

stories.title: China's zero-tariff for Africa: Win-win or winner takes all?
stories.summary: China extended zero-tariff market access to 53 African countries, calling it a "golden key" to prosperity. Analysts warn the impact on African economies may be more complex than the win-win narrative suggests.

stories.title: Families of Syrian prisoners unable to get death certificates
stories.summary: Families of Syrian prisoners who were tortured to death under the Assad regime are struggling to obtain death certificates for their loved ones, facing severe bureaucratic obstacles in the process.

stories.title: Israeli army reports rise in sexual harassment complaints
stories.summary: The Israeli military recorded 2,420 sexual harassment complaints in 2025, marking a rise in reported cases. Israeli lawmakers described the figures as "very troubling."

stories.title: Children’s reading should prioritise pleasure over learning, says laureate
stories.summary: UK Children's Laureate Frank Cottrell-Boyce urged the government to prioritize pleasure over learning in children's reading. He told MPs on the education committee that discussions about children's reading too often focus on school attainment rather than enjoyment.

stories.title: Flight to Argentina: How significant is it for Israel’s LatAm outreach?
stories.summary: Israel launched a new direct flight route to Argentina, which experts say serves as a geopolitical tool to strengthen Israeli diplomatic and strategic ties across Latin America.

stories.title: Explosions heard in Iran's Qeshm Island in Strait of Hormuz, cause unknown, news agency says
stories.summary: Explosions were heard on Qeshm Island in Iran's Strait of Hormuz, where air defenses had reportedly been triggered. The cause remained unknown, and pro-regime protesters chanted against Israel and the UAE following earlier U.S. warnings of possible strikes.

stories.title: UHaifa International: Master Your Mind. Live Your Israel Experience. - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: The University of Haifa is promoting its English-language international master's programs, offering completion in one year with a 50% tuition discount for 2026 applicants.

stories.title: Russian forces shelling Bohodukhiv in Kharkiv region, injuries reported
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled the town of Bohodukhiv in Ukraine's Kharkiv region, causing injuries and damage to the area.

stories.title: Clint Eastwood cannon from The Good, the Bad and the Ugly traced to Spanish museum
stories.summary: A cannon used by Clint Eastwood in the 1966 film The Good, the Bad and the Ugly has been traced to a museum in southeastern Spain. The Manchester-made artillery piece was tracked down by the Sad Hill Cultural Association ahead of the film's 60th anniversary.

stories.title: Syrian soldier killed and at least 18 people wounded by Damascus car bomb
stories.summary: A car bomb exploded outside a defence ministry building in Damascus on Tuesday, killing one Syrian soldier and wounding at least 18 people. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack.

stories.title: Channel 14 presenter reveals allegedly sensitive US-Iran security information live
stories.summary: An Israeli Channel 14 presenter hinted during a live broadcast that he possessed sensitive, unpublished information related to U.S.-Iran security matters, stating he was not permitted to disclose it publicly.

stories.title: Boy, 9, recounts deadly shooting at San Diego mosque: ‘We saw a bunch of bad stuff’
stories.summary: A nine-year-old boy, Odai Shanah, recounted witnessing the deadly shooting at the Islamic Center of San Diego, describing huddling in a closet during the attack. His mother emigrated from Gaza to southern California two decades ago.

stories.title: ‘I saw bad stuff’, says 9-year-old who huddled in closet during San Diego mosque attack
stories.summary: A nine-year-old student described witnessing the attack on an Islamic day school associated with a mosque in San Diego. Authorities confirmed that all students were accounted for and safe following the incident.

stories.title: Video, satellite photos show Iran war oil spill on Gulf island
stories.summary: Video footage and satellite imagery revealed an oil spill affecting Maroo Island in the Persian Gulf, reportedly linked to damage from the Iran conflict. A local resident documented extensive oil contamination in surrounding waters.

stories.title: EU-China spacecraft takes off on mission to probe solar winds
stories.summary: The SMILE spacecraft, a joint EU-China mission, launched on a mission to study solar winds. The probe aims to make the first-ever X-ray observations of Earth's magnetic field.

stories.title: At least two lightly wounded following drone explosion in northern Israel with no sirens
stories.summary: A drone exploded in northern Israel, lightly wounding at least two people, with no warning sirens activated. Earlier, the IDF intercepted a suspicious aerial target launched at an IDF position in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Iran war: Why is Trump blaming the Kurds?
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump accused Kurdish forces of keeping American weapons intended for Iranian protesters, allegations that Kurdish leaders categorically deny. Experts say Trump is scapegoating the Kurds for his own policy failures in the Iran conflict.

stories.title: Jackson Pollock painting sells for record $181m at Christie’s in New York
stories.summary: Jackson Pollock's painting Number 7A, 1948 sold for a record $181.2 million at Christie's in New York on Monday. The sale made it the fourth most expensive artwork ever sold at auction.

stories.title: Hong Kong steps up Ebola precautions, prepares Lantau Island quarantine facility
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities prepared a quarantine facility on Lantau Island as a precaution against the potential spread of Ebola following an outbreak in Central Africa. The Centre for Health Protection is implementing stringent prevention measures after the WHO declared the outbreak a public health emergency of international concern.

stories.title: Stranger Things star Gaten Matarazzo to make West End debut in Rent revival
stories.summary: Actor Gaten Matarazzo of Stranger Things will make his West End debut in a 30th-anniversary revival of the musical Rent at London's Duke of York's Theatre. The production, directed by Luke Sheppard, celebrates Jonathan Larson's Pulitzer Prize-winning rock opera.

stories.title: Tehran sees US 'softening' as Iran rebuilds military leverage
stories.summary: Iranian analysts assessed that Washington has softened elements of its negotiating position toward Tehran. Meanwhile, U.S. officials warned that Iran used the ceasefire period to rebuild and strengthen its military capabilities.

stories.title: Far-right Israeli minister Bezalel Smotrich says ICC is seeking his arrest
stories.summary: Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich said the ICC prosecutor has sought a confidential arrest warrant against him. In response, he ordered the evacuation of the Palestinian village of Khan al-Ahmar in the occupied West Bank and vowed to wage a campaign against the Palestinian Authority.

stories.title: Why has FIFA not signed a World Cup broadcast deal in India?
stories.summary: FIFA has yet to secure a broadcast deal for the upcoming World Cup in India, the world's most populous country. With the tournament only weeks away, the organization is struggling to find buyers for broadcast rights.

stories.title: Why has FIFA not signed a World Cup broadcast deal in India?
stories.summary: FIFA has been unable to secure a broadcast rights deal for the upcoming World Cup in India, the world's most populous country, with only weeks remaining before the tournament begins.

stories.title: As the world retreats from US Treasuries, will the sell-off deepen?
stories.summary: Global investors retreated from U.S. Treasuries in March, the first full month of the U.S.-Israel war on Iran, pushing the 30-year yield to its highest level in an extended period. Analysts cite inflation pressures, Federal Reserve policy under new chair Kevin Warsh, and prolonged Middle East tensions as key concerns.

stories.title: Zelensky instructs diplomats to “reset” relations with Hungary and Georgia
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky updated Ukraine's foreign policy priorities for May–June, instructing diplomats to reset relations with Hungary and Georgia, open EU accession negotiation clusters, and involve Europe more actively in peace talks.

stories.title: Secrecy surrounds UK foreign secretary’s Middle East talks with Tony Blair
stories.summary: UK Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper held undisclosed Middle East talks with former Prime Minister Tony Blair, who has been advocating for Trump's Gaza 'Board of Peace.' The Foreign Office said no minutes of the meeting exist.

stories.title: G7 finance ministers call for action on trade imbalances as Russia sanctions divide US from allies
stories.summary: G7 finance ministers meeting in Paris issued a joint statement calling for action on global trade imbalances. However, the group remained divided after the U.S. extended a waiver on Russia sanctions in the context of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: Russia’s Spy Agency Claims Ukraine Plans to Launch Drone Attacks From Latvia
stories.summary: Latvia rejected claims by Russia's SVR intelligence service that Ukraine is planning to launch drone attacks from Latvian territory. Riga accused the SVR of conducting a disinformation campaign against the country.

stories.title: Sebastian Stan’s Cannes transformation stuns in 'Fjord' premiere
stories.summary: Actor Sebastian Stan premiered Cristian Mungiu's competition film Fjord at the Cannes Film Festival, playing a Romanian who moves with his family to rural Norway. The film, co-starring Renate Reinsve, marks Stan's first role performed in Romanian.

stories.title: Hungary's Magyar visits Poland on first tour abroad as PM, seeks to reset EU ties
stories.summary: Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar began a two-day visit to Warsaw on Tuesday, his first foreign trip since taking office. The visit signals Magyar's effort to reset Hungary's relations with the European Union and steer the country back toward the European mainstream.

stories.title: Ebola declared 'continental emergency'; WHO chief concerned at 'scale and speed' of DR Congo outbreak
stories.summary: The WHO declared the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo a continental emergency, with an estimated 131 deaths from 513 suspected cases. One death has also been reported in neighboring Uganda. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus expressed concern at the outbreak's scale and speed.

stories.title: Philippine Senate guards investigated for firing shots as fugitive senator fled
stories.summary: Philippine Senate security officers are under investigation for firing their weapons without provocation as Senator Ronald dela Rosa, wanted by the International Criminal Court, sought refuge in the Senate building. Dela Rosa, a former national police chief under Rodrigo Duterte, was evading arrest by government agents.

stories.title: US extends sanctions waiver on Russian oil: Why it matters
stories.summary: The United States extended its sanctions waiver on Russian oil until June 17, allowing certain transactions involving sanctioned Russian energy exports to continue.

stories.title: Israel's Bezalel Smotrich says ICC arrest warrant request is 'declaration of war'
stories.summary: Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called the ICC arrest warrant application against him a 'declaration of war' and threatened immediate retaliation against Palestinians. The warrant is believed linked to his role in expanding settlements in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: SBU exposes Russian agent directing strikes on Kyiv
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) detained a Russian military intelligence agent in Kyiv who had been directing Russian air strikes on targets in Kyiv and the Donetsk region.

stories.title: Potential $4.2B military helicopter sale for S. Korea approved by Washington
stories.summary: Washington approved a potential $4.2 billion military helicopter sale to South Korea. Separately, India has also received approval for howitzer and helicopter sustainment packages from the United States.

stories.title: Israeli-Palestinian author duo: ‘We must break the cycle of violence’
stories.summary: Palestinian writer Aziz Abu Sarah and Israeli author Maoz Inon, both of whom lost family members in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, have co-authored a book titled "The Future of Peace." Abu Sarah's brother was killed by the Israeli military, while Inon's parents were killed by Hamas in October 2023. The book is now being released in French.

stories.title: Kenya strike over rising fuel prices pauses after mass shutdown
stories.summary: A Kenyan transport strike triggered by rising fuel prices linked to the Middle East war was paused on Tuesday after causing four deaths and major economic disruption. The unrest has raised concerns about potential wider instability across Africa.

stories.title: MKs vote to advance bills splitting and weakening role of AG, making it harder to indict PM
stories.summary: Israeli coalition lawmakers unanimously advanced bills in first readings that would split and weaken the role of the Attorney General and make it harder to indict a sitting prime minister. Opposition members walked out in protest, and the deputy AG warned of dangers to democratic elections.

stories.title: Smotrich says ICC prosecutor has requested warrant for his arrest; orders demolition of West Bank hamlet
stories.summary: Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich disclosed that the ICC prosecutor requested an arrest warrant against him, potentially related to settlement expansion as a war crime. In response, he ordered the demolition of a Palestinian hamlet east of Jerusalem in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: IDF has destroyed 60% of Hezbollah infrastructure in southern Lebanon, senior commander says
stories.summary: A senior IDF commander stated that Israeli forces have destroyed approximately 60% of Hezbollah's military infrastructure in southern Lebanon. Operations up to a designated forward defense line aim to clear the area, while targeted actions continue beyond it.

stories.title: Vladimir Putin to arrive in Beijing for state visit hot on heels of Trump
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Beijing for a state visit on Tuesday, just four days after U.S. President Donald Trump departed China. It marks Putin's 25th visit to China, reflecting deepening diplomatic ties between Moscow and Beijing.

stories.title: Kenya's transportation strike suspended as negotiations take place
stories.summary: Kenya's interior minister announced a one-week suspension of a deadly transportation strike to allow negotiations to continue. The pause aims to calm unrest after four people were killed in protests across the country during the strike.

stories.title: Smotrich orders evacuation of Palestinian village after reports of ICC arrest warrant against him
stories.summary: Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich announced plans to evacuate a Palestinian village in the West Bank during a press briefing. The announcement came shortly after reports emerged of a potential ICC arrest warrant targeting him.

stories.title: U.S.-China: A temporary truce
stories.summary: The United States and China reached a temporary trade truce, though details of the arrangement were not specified in the report.

stories.title: Using discarded Israeli flags, artist tries to stitch divided country together
stories.summary: Israeli artist Tal Tenne Czaczkes created 'The Flag of Flags,' a large canopy sewn from nearly 700 discarded Israeli flags collected from roadsides, as an artistic statement about national unity.

stories.title: WHO worried about 'scale and speed' of Ebola outbreak
stories.summary: The World Health Organisation expressed concern over the scale and speed of an ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The WHO warned that the outbreak is unlikely to subside quickly and that case numbers are expected to rise.

stories.title: Funding and Ebola epidemic loom over WHO's annual summit
stories.summary: The World Health Organisation's annual summit began on May 18, following the withdrawal of the United States and Argentina from the organization, which reduced WHO funding by approximately one-fifth. The summit is also overshadowed by the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo and a recent hantavirus crisis.

stories.title: Trump's Gaza board reports funding 'gap', urges disbursement
stories.summary: Trump's Gaza 'Board of Peace' reported a funding gap in a May 15 report to the UN Security Council, urging that the disparity between financial commitments and actual disbursements be closed urgently.

stories.title: Israeli settler filmed throwing concrete block at cats days after dog beating
stories.summary: An Israeli settler was filmed throwing a concrete block at cats in the occupied West Bank, days after a separate incident involving a settler beating a dog. The incidents highlight growing settler violence against animals in the territory.

stories.title: Russian drone attack on Hlukhiv in Sumy region leaves two killed, four injured
stories.summary: Russian strike drones hit civilian infrastructure in the Hlukhiv community of Ukraine's Sumy region, killing two people and injuring four others.

stories.title: First Ukrainian drone shot down over Estonia: Kyiv apologizes, accusing Russian jamming
stories.summary: The first Ukrainian drone was shot down over Estonian territory, prompting Kyiv to apologize and blame Russian electronic jamming for diverting the drone. Ukraine's foreign ministry accused Moscow of deliberately causing such incidents.

stories.title: Russia’s Foreign Intelligence Service claims Ukraine is planning to launch drones from Latvian territory. ‘Russia lies again,’ Riga responds.
stories.summary: Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR) claimed that Ukraine plans to launch drones against Russian targets from Latvian territory. Latvia dismissed the allegation, calling it a disinformation campaign.

stories.title: Ukraine increasingly able to strike inside Russia thanks to new drones
stories.summary: Ukraine has expanded its use of mid- and long-range drones to strike targets deep inside Russian territory. After launching hundreds of drones toward multiple Russian regions over the weekend, Ukrainian officials said the attacks are effectively degrading Russian military capacities.

stories.title: Israel is killing southern Syria's agricultural sector
stories.summary: Residents of southern Syria reported that near-daily Israeli military raids and incursions are devastating the region's agricultural sector, describing the situation as a disaster for the current agricultural season.

stories.title: Ukrainian teenager tops 248 girls from 67 countries to win first-ever gold at European informatics Olympiad
stories.summary: A Ukrainian teenager won the first-ever gold medal at the European Girls' Informatics Olympiad, competing against 248 participants from 67 countries. Ukraine's team also earned two silver medals and one bronze at the competition.

stories.title: Russian drone tears off 68-year-old man’s leg in Kherson’s daily “human safari”
stories.summary: A Russian drone strike in Kherson Oblast severed the leg of a 68-year-old man. In the same 24-hour period, two additional people were killed and 14 others were wounded across the region.

stories.title: Who was Amin Abdullah, the ‘hero’ guard killed in San Diego shooting?
stories.summary: Amin Abdullah, a security guard at a mosque in San Diego, was killed along with two others during a shooting at the facility. Tributes have been widely shared honoring him as a hero.

stories.title: China hails latest breakthrough on space solar power technology
stories.summary: Chinese researchers at Xidian University successfully tested a wireless power transmission system capable of beaming kilowatt-level energy to multiple moving targets simultaneously. The breakthrough could advance the development of space-based solar power stations.

stories.title: Does pragmatism mean we must accept Hamas as part of Gaza’s future? - opinion
stories.summary: The article examines whether pragmatic considerations require accepting Hamas as a participant in Gaza's political future. Doubts persist about Hamas's willingness to genuinely relinquish control of the territory despite discussions of a governance transition.

stories.title: Suspected car bomb explodes in Syrian capital Damascus
stories.summary: A suspected car bomb detonated outside an armament management centre in Damascus, Syria's capital, sending plumes of smoke into the air. Syria's health ministry reported one soldier killed and around 12 wounded.

stories.title: Israeli restrictions deepen Gaza's hunger crisis
stories.summary: Israeli restrictions on aid entering Gaza are deepening the territory's hunger crisis. Displaced families report surviving on bread and tea for days, with fruit and meat becoming unattainable.

stories.title: Palisa says Russia lacks forces for provocation from Belarus
stories.summary: Ukrainian Brigadier General Serhii Palisa stated that Russia currently lacks the forces needed to mount a provocation from Belarusian territory, citing the strain of ongoing front-line operations.

stories.title: China projects itself as a "stable power" as it greets US and Russia in less than a week
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin visited Chinese President Xi Jinping in China, less than a week after U.S. President Donald Trump's visit. The talks are expected to focus on trade relations, with China offering economic support to sanctions-hit Russia. Beijing is positioning itself as a stabilizing force between the two powers.

stories.title: China-Russia relations are as strong as ever thanks to Trump
stories.summary: Analysts suggest that U.S. President Trump's efforts to drive a wedge between China and Russia have failed, with the two countries maintaining strong bilateral relations. Critics say Washington repeated strategic mistakes made by previous administrations.

stories.title: As WHO sounds alarm over Ebola in DRC, what can be learned from previous outbreaks?
stories.summary: The WHO declared the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo a public health emergency of international concern. The outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo variant, faces complications from conflict, public mistrust, and delayed detection in the affected region.

stories.title: Firefighters battle blaze near Beit She’an, northern Israel, as aircraft work to contain flames
stories.summary: Firefighters and aerial firefighting aircraft battled a blaze near Beit She'an in northern Israel. Afula station commander Deputy Fire Chief Asher Biton said the combined efforts of ground crews and aircraft helped contain the fire's spread.

stories.title: US tightens entry rules over deadly Ebola outbreak in Congo
stories.summary: The Trump administration announced new travel and health screening measures in response to a growing Ebola outbreak in Central Africa that has killed more than 130 people in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

stories.title: New York federal judge bans ICE arrests at Manhattan immigration courts
stories.summary: A federal judge in New York banned ICE agents from arresting immigrants at three federal courthouses in lower Manhattan except under exceptional circumstances. U.S. District Judge P. Kevin Castel issued the order amid protests over aggressive enforcement tactics at immigration hearing sites.

stories.title: Pakistani man who killed TikTok star Sana Yousaf for rejecting him sentenced to death
stories.summary: A Pakistani court sentenced 22-year-old Umar Hayat to death for the murder of teenage TikTok influencer Sana Yousaf, who was killed in June after repeatedly rejecting his advances. The case drew nationwide condemnation and reignited debate over women's safety in Pakistan.

stories.title: India's post 2014 economic transformation  an anchor point of ties with U.S.: Envoy Vinay Kwatra
stories.summary: Indian Ambassador Vinay Kwatra described India's post-2014 economic transformation as an anchor point of India-U.S. relations, noting that defense and security cooperation is one of the fastest-growing pillars of the bilateral partnership.

stories.title: Africa: Togo Removes Visa Requirement for African Nationals
stories.summary: Togo removed visa requirements for all African nationals under a new directive that took effect on Sunday. Officials linked the policy to Togo's commitment to regional integration and Pan-African cooperation.

stories.title: Nigeria: EFCC Hands Over Recovered N837 Million to Katsina Government
stories.summary: Nigeria's Economic and Financial Crimes Commission handed over recovered funds totaling approximately N837.5 million to the Katsina State Government. The transfer was made by the EFCC's Kano Zonal Directorate on Monday.

stories.title: The future of Fatah: What next for the Palestinian movement?
stories.summary: Fatah held its eighth General Conference amid ongoing war and occupation, promising organizational renewal. However, observers noted that continuity within the Palestinian movement's leadership prevailed over meaningful change.

stories.title: 'My legs were shaking, I felt like a rock': 9-year-old recounts shooting at San Diego mosque
stories.summary: A nine-year-old boy recounted the shooting at the Islamic Centre of San Diego, which houses both a mosque and an Islamic day school. Dozens of children were forced to shelter in classrooms when gunfire erupted at the complex on Monday.

stories.title: 'My legs were shaking, I felt like a rock': 9-year-old recounts shooting at California mosque
stories.summary: Nine-year-old Odai Shanah recounted the shooting at the Islamic Center of San Diego, describing how dozens of children huddled in classrooms as gunfire erupted. His mother had emigrated from Gaza to Southern California two decades ago.

stories.title: Russian Communist Party lawmaker says the country’s economy ‘won’t survive’ a prolonged war
stories.summary: Russian Communist Party State Duma deputy Renat Suleymanov from the Novosibirsk region said Russia must end the war in Ukraine as quickly as possible, warning that the country's economy cannot sustain a prolonged conflict. He made the remarks to the Novosibirsk outlet Kontinent Sibiri.

stories.title: Russian ballistic missile strike on Pryluky kills two, injures 17
stories.summary: A Russian ballistic missile struck the center of Pryluky in Ukraine's Chernihiv region, killing two people and injuring 17 others.

stories.title: Flotilla activists say Gaza-bound ships still sailing, while UN warns humanitarian situation remains dire
stories.summary: Activists from the Global Sumud Flotilla said Gaza-bound ships are still sailing despite Israeli interceptions. Meanwhile, UN agencies warned that rodent- and insect-linked infections are spreading in overcrowded displacement camps across the besieged Palestinian territory.

stories.title: Modi in Norway LIVE: PM Modi to meet leaders at the Nordic-India Summit
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi traveled to Norway for the Nordic-India Summit, where European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen renewed calls for an India-EU investment agreement alongside free trade discussions.

stories.title: Despite summit pledges, don’t expect US-China trade to improve
stories.summary: At a recent summit in Beijing, Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump pledged to pursue a stable and constructive relationship and announced new joint trade and investment councils. Analysts caution that historical patterns suggest long-running U.S.-China economic tensions are unlikely to ease substantially.

stories.title: At least two dead, four injured in southern Spain shooting
stories.summary: At least two people were killed and four injured in a shooting in southern Spain. A Civil Guard spokesperson said the deceased were related to the suspected shooter.

stories.title: Congo-Kinshasa: New Lethal Ebola Outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo 'Deeply Concerning' for WHO
