stories.summary: Ukraine's anti-corruption agencies denied Russian propaganda claims about the arrest of First Lady Olena Zelenska. Russian state media had spread the false story citing unnamed "security structures," and Ukrainian authorities confirmed none of the claims were true.

stories.title: Iran sets up new Strait of Hormuz managing body amid stalled talks with US
stories.summary: Iran established a new body to manage the Strait of Hormuz as peace talks with the United States remained stalled. Iranian media previously reported that vessels seeking transit through the strait would need to apply for permits, disclosing ownership, insurance, crew, and cargo information.

stories.title: Kenya: Ruto Vows Justice for Rachel Wandetto After Fatal Petrol Attack Over Tattoo
stories.summary: Kenyan President William Ruto vowed justice for Rachel Wandetto, a woman who died after being doused with petrol and set on fire over a tattoo bearing the president's image. The fatal attack occurred in circumstances that drew national attention in Nairobi.

stories.title: Hong Kong’s dog-friendly restaurant scheme receives 700 applications on first day
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Food and Environmental Hygiene Department received approximately 700 applications on the first day of a new licensing scheme allowing dogs into restaurants. The scheme has a cap of 1,000 places, with applications closing on June 8 and a planned launch in July.

stories.title: What we know about the deadly new Ebola outbreak in DR Congo
stories.summary: A fresh Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed more than 90 people. Health authorities are working to contain the spread of the virus in the affected regions.

stories.title: Kenya: Two Killed in Kiambu and Nakuru As Fuel Hike Protests Turn Deadly
stories.summary: At least two people were killed in Kenya's Kiambu and Nakuru counties during protests sparked by recent fuel price hikes. Police arrested several demonstrators amid reports of widespread destruction and looting.

stories.title: ‘High time to push peace agenda’: Ebola outbreak in DRC spreads in conflict-hit, hard-to-reach areas
stories.summary: The latest Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has been linked to the rare Bundibugyo strain, which was first identified in Uganda in 2007. Dr. Hypolite Muhindo Mavoko of the University of Kinshasa warned that deceased bodies can continue transmitting the disease, highlighting risks from traditional burial practices. The outbreak is spreading in conflict-affected, hard-to-reach areas.

stories.title: Lebanon’s president says he will do ‘impossible’ to end war with Israel
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun pledged to do the "impossible" to end Israel's war on Lebanon as Israeli strikes continued despite a ceasefire. Aoun outlined a negotiating framework including Israeli withdrawal, army deployment along the border, return of displaced residents, and economic assistance.

stories.title: Somalia: Somaliland Marks 35th Anniversary With Recognition Push
stories.summary: Somaliland celebrated the 35th anniversary of its restored statehood with military parades and ceremonies in the capital Hargeisa. More than 25 international delegations attended as Somaliland renewed its diplomatic push for wider international recognition.

stories.title: Nigeria: APC Now Running Akwa Ibom PDP, Exco Member of Wike-Backed PDP Faction Laments
stories.summary: An executive committee member of a faction of Nigeria's People's Democratic Party in Akwa Ibom state alleged that the ruling All Progressives Congress is effectively controlling the local PDP. The official claimed aspirants, including himself, were denied PDP nomination forms.

stories.title: Uganda: Allies of Former Speaker Among Quiet As Corruption Probe Deepens
stories.summary: Joint security teams conducted extensive searches at the Kampala residence of former Ugandan Speaker Anita Annet Among on Mackinnon Road in the Nakasero suburb. The operations reportedly expanded to properties linked to her associates as a corruption probe deepens, while her former allies have been retreating from public association with her online.

stories.title: Belarus holds nuclear weapons drills, Defence Ministry says
stories.summary: Belarus conducted nuclear weapons drills, with its Defence Ministry stating the training was not directed against any other state and posed no regional security threats.

stories.title: The Gulf’s African Aftershocks
stories.summary: The article discusses how the Iran war is intensifying proxy conflicts in the Red Sea region and the Horn of Africa, with Gulf states playing a significant role. It examines the ripple effects of Middle Eastern hostilities on African security dynamics.

stories.title: More than 30 wounded in Russian attacks on Ukraine overnight
stories.summary: Russian overnight attacks on Ukrainian cities wounded more than 30 people. The strikes came after both sides exchanged some of their bloodiest attacks in months during the conflict, which has lasted over four years.

stories.title: Putin faces 'very difficult choice' because of war in Ukraine – head of Estonia's foreign intelligence service
stories.summary: The head of Estonia's foreign intelligence service said President Putin faces a very difficult strategic choice regarding the war in Ukraine. He noted that the Russian army cannot achieve significant battlefield progress while Western sanctions continue to drain Russia's resources.

stories.title: Infectious diseases such as hantavirus and Ebola becoming more frequent and damaging, say experts
stories.summary: Experts warned that infectious disease outbreaks are becoming more frequent and damaging globally. Health authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda are scrambling to contain an Ebola outbreak, while a hantavirus outbreak has also raised international concern. The Global Preparedness Monitoring Board said pandemic risk is outpacing investments in preparedness.

stories.title: Cuba dreads possible US invasion amid energy blockade
stories.summary: Cuba accused the Trump administration of fabricating a pretext for invasion, citing U.S. media reports based on classified intelligence claiming Havana acquired hundreds of drones. Cuban officials say the economic sanctions imposed by Washington are strangling the nation and allege the U.S. is seeking justification for military action.

stories.title: 'Long live Al Aqsa Flood:' US Nakba Day protests rife with terrorism support
stories.summary: Protests took place across the United States on Nakba Day, May 15, with demonstrators expressing support for Palestinians. Some participants made statements referencing the October 7 attack and called for the liberation of Palestine.

stories.title: Dogs allowed on glitzy Cannes beach newly renamed after French film star Brigitte Bardot
stories.summary: A beach in Cannes, France, was renamed in honor of French film star Brigitte Bardot and will allow dogs in tribute to her animal rights activism. Bardot, who retired from acting, has become a controversial figure for her animal welfare work and vocal support of far-right politics.

stories.title: Some items in Luigi Mangione’s backpack won’t be used as evidence in trial, judge rules
stories.summary: A Manhattan judge ruled that several items found in Luigi Mangione's backpack during his arrest—including a magazine, cellphone, passport, wallet, and computer chip—will be suppressed as evidence. The defense argued that police who arrested Mangione in connection with the murder of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson did not properly inform him of his rights.

stories.title: Ex-assistant principal faces trial after six-year-old shot Virginia teacher
stories.summary: Former assistant principal Ebony Parker went to trial in Newport News, Virginia, on charges of ignoring warnings that a six-year-old student brought a loaded gun to Richneck Elementary School. The weapon was later used by the child to shoot his first-grade teacher in January 2023.

stories.title: Trump moves to dismiss $10bn lawsuit against IRS amid reports he’s considering settlement
stories.summary: President Donald Trump moved to dismiss his $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS amid reports he is considering a settlement with the federal government. The reported settlement would create a $1.7 billion fund to compensate allies for alleged government persecution. The filing came ahead of a court deadline requesting briefing on whether a legitimate controversy existed.

stories.title: Uganda's president signs contentious law meant to curb foreign influence
stories.summary: Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni signed a controversial law aimed at curbing foreign influence in the country. The measure has drawn heavy criticism, including from Uganda's central bank, which warned it could trigger economic disaster.

stories.title: China agrees to boost trade for U.S. agricultural products following Trump-Xi summit
stories.summary: China agreed to increase purchases of U.S. agricultural products following a summit between President Donald Trump and President Xi Jinping in Beijing, aimed at easing the impact of the ongoing trade war on American farmers.

stories.title: What is the UAE’s Barakah nuclear plant, nearly hit by a drone?
stories.summary: The Barakah nuclear power plant, located in Abu Dhabi, UAE, reportedly came close to being struck by a drone. The facility has the capacity to supply approximately one-quarter of the UAE's total electricity demand.

stories.title: WHO kicks off annual assembly amid Ebola, hantavirus, US withdrawal, funding cuts
stories.summary: The World Health Organization opened its annual assembly of global health ministers amid concerns over a hantavirus outbreak on a cruise ship and an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The meeting also faced uncertainty surrounding announced withdrawals by the United States and Argentina, along with funding cuts.

stories.title: Russia offers continued military cooperation to Equatorial Guinea
stories.summary: Equatorial Guinea's Foreign Minister Simeon Oyono Esono Angue met Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in Moscow on Monday. The two officials discussed defense cooperation and Russia's broader military engagement in Africa.

stories.title: Spared Wang Fuk Court block owners given mid-October to finalise buyback offer
stories.summary: Owners of Wang Chi House, the only block spared in the fire-ravaged Wang Fuk Court complex in Hong Kong, have been given until October 15 to finalize sales under a government buyback scheme. At least 75 percent of owners must indicate their intention to sell by the end of next month. Residents have expressed frustration over the tight timeline and lack of details on insurance and maintenance.

stories.title: Russia and Belarus Launch Joint Nuclear Drills
stories.summary: Russia and Belarus launched joint nuclear military exercises. The Belarusian army stated the drills are not directed against third countries and do not threaten regional security.

stories.title: Biggest French cinema producer's blacklist threat could recall Hollywood 'McCarthyism'
stories.summary: Canal+ head Maxime Saada threatened to blacklist approximately 600 French cinema professionals who signed a petition opposing right-wing billionaire owner Vincent Bolloré's influence on the industry. The petition called for mobilization against what signatories described as the growing grip of the far right on French cinema. Critics have compared the move to Hollywood-era McCarthyism.

stories.title: PM Modi lands in Norway; to hold talks on trade, technology
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in Norway for talks on trade and technology, marking the first visit by an Indian prime minister to the country in 43 years.

stories.title: The world cannot afford to fail women, children and adolescents
stories.summary: International aid cuts, rising debt burdens, and ongoing armed conflicts are severely undermining maternal and child health services worldwide, pushing healthcare systems for women, children, and adolescents toward a critical breaking point.

stories.title: China's moment? Putin heads to Beijing after Trump courts Xi
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping is set to host Russian President Vladimir Putin in Beijing just days after receiving U.S. President Donald Trump. The back-to-back summits highlight Beijing's growing centrality in an increasingly fragmented geopolitical landscape.

stories.title: Ukrainian troops carry out counterattacks on certain sections of front in southern regions – Voloshyn
stories.summary: Vladyslav Voloshyn, spokesperson for Ukraine's Southern Defense Forces, reported that Ukrainian troops are conducting counterattacks on certain sections of the southern front. He noted that Russian forces continue active assault operations using aviation and kamikaze drones in the region.

stories.title: Can women's football help reconnect North and South Korea?
stories.summary: North Korean athletes are set to compete in South Korea for the first time in over seven years through a women's football event. Analysts are divided on whether Pyongyang's participation represents a propaganda effort or a genuine step toward détente.

stories.title: Can a women's football team reconnect North and South Korea?
stories.summary: For the first time in over seven years, North Korean athletes will compete in South Korea through a women's football event. Analysts are divided on whether Pyongyang's participation represents a propaganda move or a genuine step toward easing inter-Korean tensions.

stories.title: Nigeria: Who was the targeted Islamic State group leader and why was he targeted by the US?
stories.summary: A senior Islamic State figure identified as Abu-Bilal al-Minuki was killed on May 16 in a joint Nigerian-U.S. strike in northeastern Nigeria. Despite U.S. President Trump's claims, analysts say al-Minuki was not the second-in-command of IS worldwide, though he was a prominent figure within the group's West African operations.

stories.title: Experts locate bodies of four missing Italian divers inside Maldives cave
stories.summary: Rescue teams located the bodies of four Italian divers deep inside an underwater cave in a Maldives atoll, four days after they were reported missing. A local military diver had previously died during a perilous search mission to reach them. Authorities said they would attempt to recover the bodies within the next couple of days.

stories.title: International Gymnastics Federation lifts all sanctions on Russia and Belarus without explanation
stories.summary: The International Gymnastics Federation lifted all sanctions on Russia and Belarus, allowing both countries to return to full international competition under their own flags and anthems. The decision was made without public explanation while Russia's invasion of Ukraine continues.

stories.title: Iran submits updated 14-point proposal to US through Pakistan
stories.summary: Iran submitted an updated version of its 14-point proposal to the United States through Pakistani mediation. The revised draft reportedly focuses on ending the ongoing war between the two countries.

stories.title: Israel raid of Gaza-bound flotilla near Cyprus sparks outrage
stories.summary: Israeli forces seized the Global Sumud Flotilla, a Gaza-bound aid convoy, in international waters near Cyprus. The raid is the latest in a series of Israeli interceptions of vessels attempting to break the naval blockade on Gaza.

stories.title: The only Iran deal Trump can get is no better than Obama’s ‘horrible’ JCPOA
stories.summary: Analysis suggests that any nuclear deal the US can negotiate with Iran would not significantly differ from the 2015 JCPOA, which was previously abandoned. Weeks of bombing and threats have reportedly not changed Iran's position on ballistic missiles or regional proxies.

stories.title: Russian drone attack in Odesa leaves damaged residential buildings, kindergarten and lyceum
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack overnight on May 18 damaged residential buildings in two districts of Odesa, along with a kindergarten, a lyceum, and a police station. No casualty figures were immediately provided.

stories.title: Iran's nuclear project is 'unchanged', says senior ex-Israeli intelligence officer
stories.summary: Former senior Israeli military intelligence officer Tamir Hayman, executive director of Israel's Institute for National Security Studies, stated that Iran's nuclear project remains "essentially unchanged" despite Israeli and US attacks during the ongoing war.

stories.title: Iran says it responded to ‘excessive’ US proposal, after Trump warns ‘clock ticking’
stories.summary: Iran announced it responded to what it called an "excessive" US proposal while President Trump warned the "clock is ticking." Tehran also said it created a new body to manage the Strait of Hormuz and warned Gulf countries against cooperating with Israel.

stories.title: PA partially coordinating with Israel for security while glorifying terror, US State Dept. says
stories.summary: The US State Department reported that the Palestinian Authority is partially coordinating with Israel on security matters while simultaneously glorifying acts of violence. The department noted that recent statements by senior PLO members are incompatible with recognizing Israel's right to exist free from threats.

stories.title: Lebanon braces for Pentagon talks over Hezbollah disarmament
stories.summary: Lebanon is preparing for Pentagon-led talks concerning the disarmament of Hezbollah. There are concerns that US-backed discussions with Israel could pressure the Lebanese army into a direct military confrontation with Hezbollah.

stories.title: Former University of Michigan researcher accused of hiding Chinese military drone ties
stories.summary: Former University of Michigan researcher Chuan Wang was accused of concealing his ties to the Chinese military's drone program. Investigators allege Wang claimed modest roles on U.S. visa applications while being publicly known in China for his involvement in military drone development.

stories.title: Italy's Andrea Maldera named new Ukraine football manager
stories.summary: Italy's Andrea Maldera has been officially appointed as the new head coach of Ukraine's national football team. The appointment marks a new chapter for Ukrainian football management.

stories.title: Kristen Stewart on the red carpet in Cannes, while Javier Bardem slams toxic masculinity
stories.summary: The 79th Cannes Film Festival reached its midpoint with premieres including "Paper Tiger," directed by James Gray and starring Adam Driver and Miles Teller. The film explores corruption and moral decline in 1980s America. Actor Javier Bardem also spoke out against toxic masculinity during the festival.

stories.title: Israel to build military 'museum' on ruins of Unrwa HQ in Jerusalem
stories.summary: Israel announced plans to build a military museum and recruitment center on the site of the demolished UNRWA headquarters in the Sheikh Jarrah neighborhood of East Jerusalem. Israeli forces had demolished the UN agency's building in January 2026.

stories.title: CM Afridi seeks PM's intervention on CNG crisis in KP, warns of possible 'widespread agitation'
stories.summary: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi wrote to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif urging intervention in an ongoing CNG crisis that has shut filling stations across the province since April. Afridi warned the shortage could trigger widespread public unrest.

stories.title: London tube strikes called off at last minute
stories.summary: The RMT union called off planned strikes by London Underground drivers at the last minute. Two 24-hour stoppages that were set to begin midday Tuesday and disrupt travel over four days were suspended.

stories.title: Defense Intelligence shows how soldiers clear Russian forces out of Stepnohirsk in Zaporizhzhia region
stories.summary: Soldiers from the Artan special unit of Ukraine's military intelligence, alongside other defense forces, drove Russian troops from fortified positions in Stepnohirsk in the Zaporizhzhia region. The Defense Intelligence directorate released footage of the clearing operation.

stories.title: The 15 May deadline for Ukrainian elections has passed. Only one in ten Ukrainians wanted to meet it
stories.summary: The May 15 deadline for holding Ukrainian elections has passed, with polling showing only about one in ten Ukrainians supported meeting that timeline. Sociologist Tymofii Brik presented the data at the Lviv Media Forum, noting deeper unresolved questions about post-war governance.

stories.title: Israeli attacks across Lebanon kill seven
stories.summary: At least seven people were killed in Israeli attacks across Lebanon since dawn on Monday, according to Lebanon's health ministry. The Israeli army also issued forced evacuation orders for residents of three southern Lebanese villages, including Harouf, Borj El Chmali, and Debaal.

stories.title: Somaliland’s first ambassador to Israel welcomed by Herzog in historic ceremony
stories.summary: Somaliland's first ambassador to Israel was welcomed by President Isaac Herzog in a ceremony marking the establishment of formal diplomatic ties. Herzog said the partnership would promote cooperation benefiting both peoples and the wider region.

stories.title: Iran's foreign ministry: US talks ongoing through Pakistan
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry confirmed that negotiations with the United States are continuing through Pakistani mediation. Spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said the US rejected Iran's initial 14-point proposal but later submitted amendments via Pakistan. Iranian and Omani technical teams also met in Oman for separate discussions.

stories.title: Lebanon-Israel UAVs: Uncounted Acts of Violence
stories.summary: An editorial cartoon by Palestinian-Jordanian cartoonist Emad Hajjaj addresses the issue of Israeli UAV operations over Lebanon. The cartoon highlights what the artist characterizes as uncounted acts of violence resulting from drone use.

stories.title: Ukraine lets companies build their own air defense, and 24 have already signed up
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Ministry launched a program allowing private companies to build their own air defense capabilities to protect their facilities from drone attacks. Twenty-four companies have already enrolled, using trained staff or licensed security firms.

stories.title: Iran eyes challenging stock market reopening after lengthy war closure
stories.summary: Iran is preparing to reopen its stock market after an extended closure caused by the war. While the capital market is not the primary financing mechanism for Iran's economy, its reopening carries significant political and psychological weight.

stories.title: Ukrainian Drone Attack Kills 2 in Belgorod Region
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone attack killed two people in the village of Borisovka in Russia's Belgorod region, located north of the border with Ukraine's Kharkiv region.

stories.title: Rare strike forces busiest US commuter line to a halt
stories.summary: A strike by five unions shut down the Long Island Rail Road, the busiest commuter rail line in the United States, beginning May 16. Negotiations between union leaders and New York government representatives continued into Sunday night as workers sought higher wages from the Metropolitan Transportation Authority after years of failed talks.

stories.title: Trump’s Taiwan independence comments: a blow to William Lai and ruling DPP?
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated he is "not looking to have somebody go independent" regarding Taiwan, sparking debate over the implications for President Lai Ching-te and the ruling Democratic Progressive Party's pro-independence stance. The remark came after Trump's summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Beijing, where Taiwan was a key topic.

stories.title: Russian forces concentrate artillery in Pokrovsk agglomeration to support offensive operations – Ukrainian military
stories.summary: In the Pokrovsk area of eastern Ukraine, Russian forces are concentrating artillery and building an extensive network of drone launch sites to support offensive operations. Ukrainian military officials said the buildup is aimed at bolstering Russian assault actions in the region.

stories.title: PM Modi woos Swedish companies to invest in India, says 'reform express' going at full speed
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi encouraged Swedish companies to invest in India, promoting what he described as a fast-moving reform agenda during his visit to Sweden.

stories.title: Take food for three days. Then you’ll come back. The Crimean Tatars never did
stories.summary: An article examines the 1944 Soviet deportation of Crimean Tatars, who were told to take food for three days but were never allowed to return home. Those who returned to Crimea in the 1990s and their descendants now face political persecution under Russian rule.

stories.title: PSX loses 2,000 points during intraday trade as bearish momentum persists
stories.summary: Pakistan's KSE-100 index fell over 2,000 points during Monday intraday trading, declining 1.31% to 163,424.91 points amid rising oil prices driven by Middle East tensions and stalled US-Iran negotiations.

stories.title: The Afghan problem
stories.summary: A wave of terrorist attacks in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province between May 9 and 14 struck targets in Bannu, Lakki Marwat, and Bajaur, raising concerns about cross-border militancy from Afghanistan. Pakistan's Foreign Office issued a strong demarche to the Afghan chargé d'affaires following the Bannu attack.

stories.title: Shakira acquitted by Spanish court of tax fraud, over US$64 million to be returned
stories.summary: A Spanish court acquitted Colombian singer Shakira of tax fraud for the 2011 tax year, finding that authorities failed to prove she was a resident of Spain. The court ordered the government to return more than 55 million euros (over US$64 million) in wrongly imposed fines.

stories.title: Pakistan deploys thousands of troops to Saudi during Iran war
stories.summary: Pakistan has deployed approximately 8,000 troops to Saudi Arabia during the Iran war, with a pledge to send additional forces if needed. The deployment also includes a Chinese-made HQ-9 air defense system, according to five sources who spoke to Reuters.

stories.title: How fight for Philippine Senate presidency will shape Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial
stories.summary: The Philippine Senate convened as an impeachment court for Vice-President Sara Duterte-Carpio, who was impeached by the House of Representatives on allegations of corruption and constitutional violations. A parallel battle for control of the Senate presidency could shape the trial's direction, alongside the International Criminal Court case against her father, former President Rodrigo Duterte, in The Hague.

stories.title: The Gulf does not have to choose Iran or Israel
stories.summary: Gulf states face strategic decisions regarding their relationships with both Iran and Israel amid the ongoing regional conflict. The central choice is framed as one between pursuing regional stability or risking prolonged warfare.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: 'Staggering' Iran toll drives up global executions: Amnesty
stories.summary: Amnesty International highlighted Iran's high execution toll. Separately, the UAE reported a drone strike near the Barakah nuclear power plant, and Saudi Arabia intercepted three drones originating from Iraqi airspace.

stories.title: Four crew members eject safely after two Navy jets crash during air show in Idaho
stories.summary: Two U.S. Navy EA-18G Growler jets from Electronic Attack Squadron 129, based at Whidbey Island, Washington, collided during an air show near Mountain Home Air Force Base in Idaho. All four crew members ejected safely.

stories.title: G7 finance ministers meet amid Middle East war economic fallout
stories.summary: G7 finance ministers convened in Paris to discuss economic fallout from the ongoing Middle East war. France, holding the G7 presidency, faces the challenge of maintaining dialogue amid rising tensions with Washington over tariff threats from President Donald Trump.

stories.title: PM Modi in Norway: PM Modi emplanes for Oslo
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi departed for Oslo, Norway, as part of a Nordic visit. Trade, energy, and discussions on global conflicts are expected to top the agenda. India and Sweden agreed to elevate their bilateral relationship to a Strategic Partnership.

stories.title: Iran sends response to US proposal to end war via mediator Pakistan
stories.summary: Iran has sent a response to a US proposal to end the war, using Pakistan as a mediator. Tehran's demands include the release of frozen assets held abroad, the lifting of international sanctions, and control over the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Uganda enacts new law to protect sovereignty despite opposition
stories.summary: Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni signed into law legislation prohibiting foreign interference in the country's affairs. The law was enacted despite warnings from opposition groups and other concerned parties.

stories.title: Russian attack in Dnipro leaves tax administration building damaged
stories.summary: A Russian overnight attack on May 18 damaged a tax administration building in one district of Dnipro, Ukraine.

stories.title: World Gymnastics Lifts Ban on Russian and Belarusian Flags and Anthems
stories.summary: The World Gymnastics governing body lifted its ban on Russian and Belarusian flags and anthems at competitions. Russia's Gymnastics Federation welcomed the decision, calling it a step toward strengthening unity in the global gymnastics community.

stories.title: Hantavirus cruise ship arrives in the Netherlands to be disinfected
stories.summary: The cruise ship MV Hondius arrived in Rotterdam, Netherlands, for crew disembarkation and disinfection following a hantavirus outbreak that killed three people. The World Health Organization maintained its assessment that the outbreak poses a low global risk, and disease specialists said a pandemic of the virus is very unlikely.

stories.title: The secret Israeli bases scandal roiling Iraqi politics
stories.summary: The discovery of two secret Israeli military bases in Iraq has triggered a major political controversy in Baghdad. The revelation complicates Iraq's efforts to balance its relationships with both Iran and the United States.

stories.title: Israeli attacks in Gaza have stepped up since halt in bombing in Iran
stories.summary: Israel stepped up military strikes on the Gaza Strip after halting its joint bombing campaign with the United States in Iran. At least five Palestinians were killed in Israeli strikes on May 17. The Gaza Strip has experienced near-daily Israeli fire since an October ceasefire between Israel and Hamas took effect.

stories.title: Pakistan condemns drone attack on UAE nuclear power plant
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Office condemned a drone attack on the UAE's Barakah Nuclear Power Plant in Abu Dhabi, calling it reckless. The UAE defence ministry reported a fire near the facility but no injuries or radiation impact, and said two additional drones were intercepted.

stories.title: Israeli forces storm Gaza aid flotilla in international waters
stories.summary: Israeli naval forces boarded and seized Gaza-bound aid boats in international waters. Activists aboard the vessels accused Israel of piracy and of enforcing what they described as a siege on Gaza.

stories.title: China and Russia hold trade expo as Putin and Trump visits draw global attention
stories.summary: China is hosting the 10th edition of a major bilateral trade expo with Russia ahead of Russian President Vladimir Putin's expected visit to Beijing. The event follows U.S. President Donald Trump's visit to the Chinese capital the previous week, highlighting intensified diplomatic activity as Beijing balances relations with Washington and Moscow.

stories.title: France & Africa partnering on jobs, education, investment: 'Not just about money, also the diaspora'
stories.summary: France's Minister Delegate for Francophonie Éléonore Caroit highlighted a renewed partnership between France and African nations focused on private investment, education, and digital innovation. The remarks came against the backdrop of 23 billion euros in investment commitments tied to the Africa Forward summit in Kenya, split between French and African companies.

stories.title: Islamic regime’s extremism being imported to Europe, Kosar Eftekhari warns ‘Post’
stories.summary: Iranian activist Kosar Eftekhari, who lost an eye after being shot by security forces during the Women, Life, Freedom protests, warned of the Islamic regime's extremism spreading to Europe. She was attacked in Germany by supporters of Supreme Leader Khamenei.

stories.title: Iran Nobel winner Narges Mohammadi discharged from hospital
stories.summary: Iranian Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi was discharged from a Tehran hospital after 18 days of treatment. She had initially been hospitalized in Zanjan, where she was imprisoned, before being transferred to Tehran, according to her foundation.

stories.title: DRC health minister visits hotspot for Ebola outbreak
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo's health minister visited a hotspot area affected by the ongoing Ebola outbreak to assess the response and conditions on the ground.

stories.title: Zambia's media freedom under scrutiny ahead of 2026 elections
stories.summary: Ahead of Zambia's August 2026 elections, rights groups report growing pressure on journalists in the country. Critics warn that legal restrictions and unequal media access could undermine fair election coverage.

stories.title: Ukraine today honors memory of victims of genocide of Crimean Tatar people
stories.summary: On May 18, Ukraine commemorated the Day of Struggle for the Rights of the Crimean Tatar People, marking the 82nd anniversary of the mass deportation and genocide of Crimean Tatars.

stories.title: IRGC says it struck US-Israeli backed 'terrorist groups' in Iraq
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said its Hamzeh Sayyed al-Shuhada Command struck groups in Iraq's Kurdistan Province accused of smuggling US weapons. The IRGC described the targets as US-Israeli-backed terrorist organizations attempting to bring sealed American weapons and ammunition into the country.

stories.title: IDF struggles to throttle endless feed of soldiers posting misdeeds on social media
stories.summary: The Israeli military is struggling to prevent soldiers from posting videos of misconduct on social media, including footage of troops smashing a statue of Jesus in Lebanon. The IDF says such posts fuel international criticism and compromise operational security.

stories.title: Australia orders China-linked investors to sell stakes in rare earths firm
stories.summary: Australia ordered investors linked to China to divest their stakes in Northern Minerals, a company seeking to challenge China's dominance in dysprosium production. Dysprosium is a rare earth mineral used in high-performance magnets for electric vehicles.

stories.title: Namibia: German City Mourns Desert Air Plane Crash Victims
stories.summary: Tributes are being paid to a German family killed in a Desert Air plane crash in Namibia. The crash occurred last Sunday and has drawn mourning from a German city connected to the victims.

stories.title: French judge to probe complaints against Saudi crown prince over Khashoggi killing
stories.summary: A French judge has opened an investigation into complaints filed by NGOs against Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman over the 2018 assassination of journalist Jamal Khashoggi. The probe follows long-standing accusations that the crown prince ordered the killing.

stories.title: Nigeria: Peter Obi Risks Losing Support of Obidient Movement, Says Coordinators
stories.summary: Coordinators of Nigeria's Obidient Movement, previously loyal to former presidential candidate Peter Obi, warned that he risks losing the movement's support ahead of the 2027 general election.

stories.title: Netanyahu's coalition 'massively pressuring' MKs to vote for haredi draft bill, Haskel tells 'Post'
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's coalition is reportedly pressuring coalition lawmakers to vote in favor of a haredi military draft bill. MK Sharren Haskel told The Jerusalem Post that phone calls were made to nearly all coalition members over the weekend to check positions and apply pressure.

stories.title: US, Nigeria carry out fresh strikes on Islamic State group
stories.summary: U.S. and Nigerian forces conducted air strikes against Islamic State group targets in northeastern Nigeria on Sunday. The region faces threats from both IS-allied jihadist groups and criminal gangs responsible for kidnappings, including one on Friday that resulted in the abduction of 46 people, mostly children.

stories.title: International Gymnastics Federation lifts ban on Russian athletes competing under national flag and anthem
stories.summary: The International Gymnastics Federation lifted restrictions on Russian and Belarusian athletes, permitting them to compete under their national flags and anthems. The ban had been imposed in February 2022 following Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: Russian strike hits Naftogaz facilities in Dnipropetrovsk region, two workers injured
stories.summary: Russian drones struck several Naftogaz Group facilities in the Dnipropetrovsk region overnight on May 18, injuring two female employees at an Ukrnafta gas station.

stories.title: Shakira wins £50m tax refund from Spanish government
stories.summary: Colombian singer Shakira won a £50 million tax refund from the Spanish government following a court ruling in her favor. Shakira stated the ruling disproves the narrative that she was guilty of tax evasion in Spain.

stories.title: Iran plans to offer insurance for Hormuz transit: Will it work?
stories.summary: Iran has proposed a Bitcoin-based ship insurance scheme for vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz. The proposal is expected to raise concerns among global maritime stakeholders about the practicality and legitimacy of such a system.

stories.title: Court petitioned against ‘deadly’ lifeline granted to coal-fired power station
stories.summary: The Sharon-Carmel Cities Association and environmental organizations petitioned an Israeli court against an amended emissions permit granted to a coal-fired power station. The petitioners argue the permit violates Israeli law and European directives, predicting multiple deaths from pollution.

stories.title: Man charged with murder after woman and two children found dead inside Sydney home
stories.summary: A 47-year-old man was charged with murder after a woman and two children were found dead inside a home in Campbelltown, in southwestern Sydney. New South Wales police responded after a triple-zero call from the residence on Monday night.

stories.title: Loneliness: South Korea's silent epidemic
stories.summary: Over 40 percent of South Koreans aged 25 to 49 say they do not want to marry, contributing to half of all households in Seoul being single-person homes. Seoul's municipal government is investing more than €260 million over five years to address what it considers a serious public health epidemic of loneliness.

stories.title: Russia strikes Dnipro with missiles, injuring 18
stories.summary: Russian missile strikes on Dnipro overnight on May 18 injured 18 people and damaged apartment buildings, private homes, a religious institution, a university, and an industrial facility, according to regional military administration head Oleksandr Hanzha.

stories.title: US weighs secure AI base in Israel’s Negev to counter China - report
stories.summary: Reports indicate the US is considering building a secure AI facility called Project Spire in Israel's Negev desert to counter Chinese technological advances. The base would be the first in a planned network allowing American and allied researchers to collaborate under strict US security standards.

stories.title: Israel advances plan to seize Palestinian property near Al-Aqsa Mosque
stories.summary: Israel is advancing plans to seize Palestinian property near Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem's Old City. A new committee will implement historic confiscation orders, prompting Palestinian warnings about efforts to alter the area's character.

stories.title: Addressing the law around banking
stories.summary: Pakistan's banking sector faces rising non-performing loans, which reached nearly Rs980 billion by the end of 2025. Commercial banks account for the bulk at Rs943 billion. Structural weaknesses in loan recovery frameworks and weak enforcement are cited as obstacles to credit expansion in agriculture, housing, and SMEs.

stories.title: Ryanair has ‘near-zero concerns’ on fuel shortages but warns of future price rises
stories.summary: Ryanair CEO Michael O'Leary said the airline has "almost zero concerns" about jet fuel supplies this summer despite the Iran war, noting Europe has secured alternative fuel sources. However, he warned that persistent consumer uncertainty has led to later bookings, which could result in higher fares later in the year.

stories.title: Kenya: Heavy Security Deployed On Thika Road, Kiambu As Fuel Protests Turn Violent
stories.summary: Heavy security was deployed along Thika Road and across parts of Kiambu County in Kenya after nationwide protests by public service vehicle operators over soaring fuel prices turned violent, with vandalism and road barricades reported.

stories.title: Ukraine's first guided aerial bomb passes testing, ready for combat use – Fedorov
stories.summary: Ukraine's first domestically developed guided aerial bomb has completed testing and is now cleared for combat deployment, according to officials including Mykhailo Fedorov.

stories.title: Mentally ill woman spends 2 days in Hong Kong flat with dead mother on sofa
stories.summary: A woman with a chronic illness was found dead in a public housing flat in Sham Shui Po, Hong Kong, where her 34-year-old daughter, who suffers from mental illness, had remained with the body for at least two days. Police were alerted by another family member who was unable to reach the pair.

stories.title: Report: Russian state TV channels played down scale of Ukraine’s strike on Moscow
stories.summary: Russia's three main state television channels — Channel One, Russia-1, and NTV — reportedly downplayed the scale of a major Ukrainian drone strike on Moscow, according to the independent Russian outlet Agentstvo on May 17.

stories.title: Rwanda: Ebola Virus - Uganda Postpones Martyrs' Day Celebration
stories.summary: Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni announced the postponement of this year's Martyrs' Day celebrations due to an Ebola virus outbreak. The decision was made on Sunday, May 17, as health authorities work to contain the disease.

stories.title: Tribal chief among 3 killed in IED blast in KP's Wana
stories.summary: A tribal elder and chief of the Ahmadzai Wazir tribe, Malik Tariq Wazir, was among three people killed in an IED blast at Rustam Bazaar in Wana, Lower South Waziristan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Four others were injured.

stories.title: U.S. Allows Russian Oil Waiver to Expire Again
stories.summary: The United States allowed a waiver permitting certain purchases of Russian oil to expire again. Sanctions experts anticipate Washington may issue a short-term extension or grant specific exemptions to major Asian refineries.

stories.title: US, Nigeria carry out more strikes on IS, at least 20 militants dead
stories.summary: U.S. Africa Command and Nigeria's Defence Headquarters conducted joint air strikes against Islamic State West Africa Province targets in the Metele area of Borno State in northeastern Nigeria on Sunday, killing more than 20 militants.

stories.title: 'I don't believe the war is coming to an end': Kyiv-based photographer Mark Neville
stories.summary: British photographer Mark Neville, based in Kyiv, told FRANCE 24 he does not believe the war in Ukraine is nearing its end. Despite recent positive developments on the front line, Neville said Russian President Vladimir Putin remains under pressure but that this does not necessarily signal the conflict's conclusion.

stories.title: Ghana: Africa Needs Strong Leadership, Global Governance Reforms - Vice President
stories.summary: Ghana's Vice President Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang called for stronger African leadership and reforms to global governance systems, warning that developing countries remain constrained by unfair economic conditions and weak international representation.

stories.title: Nigeria: Don't 'Abduct' El-Rufai From Court, Timi Frank Warns
stories.summary: Former APC spokesman Timi Frank warned against an alleged plot by intelligence operatives to take former Kaduna State Governor Nasir el-Rufai into custody from the Federal High Court in Abuja.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigeria, U.S. Carry Out New Strikes On Isis
stories.summary: Nigeria and the United States conducted fresh airstrikes against Islamic State militants in northeast Nigeria, according to the U.S. military.

stories.title: The US-Israeli war on Iran has cost companies around the world at least $25bn, with the bill continuing to climb
stories.summary: A Reuters analysis found that the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran has cost companies worldwide at least $25 billion. At least 279 firms in the U.S., Europe, and Asia have cited the conflict as a trigger for defensive actions, citing soaring energy prices, fractured supply chains, and disrupted trade routes through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Europe should pick negotiator for possible Russian talks, says Zelenskyy – Europe live
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy urged Europe to select a negotiator for possible peace talks with Russia, stating that Europe must maintain a strong voice. Separately, Italian authorities confirmed the recovery of four Italian divers' bodies from an underwater cave in the Maldives.

stories.title: Liberia: Communities Cry for Clean Water As EPA Shuts Down Nugget Era Mining for Illegal Operations in Gbarpolu
stories.summary: Liberia's Environmental Protection Agency shut down Nugget Era Mining Company in Gbarpolu County for illegal operations. Residents of Korninga Chiefdom reported that their drinking water had been polluted by the mining activity.

stories.title: Liberia: 'The Noise Pollution Situation Is Not Under Control,' EPA Launches Crackdown As Experts Call for Public Awareness
stories.summary: Liberia's Environmental Protection Agency launched a crackdown on noise pollution, with experts calling for greater public awareness of the issue.

stories.title: First Thing: Trump warns ‘clock is ticking’ for Iran to secure peace deal
stories.summary: President Donald Trump warned Iran that "the clock is ticking" to reach a peace deal, posting on social media that there "won't be anything left" of the country without an agreement. The UAE blamed a fire near its nuclear plant on a drone launched by Iran or its proxies.

stories.title: Redistricting debate shifts to South Carolina as Republicans seek clean sweep of House seats – US politics live
stories.summary: Republicans in South Carolina are pursuing redistricting efforts aimed at the seat held by Democratic Representative Jim Clyburn, the state's sole Democrat among seven House members. Separately, dozens of state-level anti-vaccine bills supported by Make America Healthy Again (MAHA) coalition groups have failed after public health advocates persuaded Republican lawmakers to oppose them.

stories.title: Dozens injured: Zelensky reports consequences of overnight attack, strike on Chinese vessel
stories.summary: During a large-scale overnight attack on May 18, Russian forces launched 524 attack drones and 22 missiles against Ukraine. One of the drones struck a Chinese-flagged vessel. President Zelensky reported dozens of people were injured.

stories.title: Starmer says he will back Labour’s Makerfield byelection candidate ‘100%’ – UK politics live
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer expressed full support for Labour's Makerfield byelection candidate while defending his government's record. Separately, the European Commission declined to speculate on Britain's potential future EU membership, focusing instead on closer cooperation discussions.

stories.title: Iran says nuclear enrichment rights cannot be ‘negotiated’
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei stated that nuclear enrichment is an existing right that cannot be subject to negotiation. The remarks underscore Tehran's firm stance ahead of ongoing diplomatic discussions.

stories.title: Kenya: Thousands Stranded As PSV Strike Cripples Transport Nationwide
stories.summary: A nationwide public service vehicle strike over soaring fuel prices stranded thousands of commuters across Kenya on Monday, paralyzing transport in major towns and along key highways.

stories.title: North Korea's new constitution deepens split with Seoul
stories.summary: North Korea's updated constitution has removed references to reunification with South Korea. Experts say the changes reinforce Kim Jong Un's authority as a nuclear leader and could increase the risk of future border confrontations.

stories.title: Kenya: Nairobi Fuel Protest Turns Violent as Clashes Erupt
stories.summary: Fuel protests in Nairobi turned violent on Monday as clashes erupted on Thika Road between protesters and police. A private vehicle was set ablaze and others were vandalized during the unrest.

stories.title: ‘I don’t know what would have happened if we’d won,’ says Israel’s Eurovision chief
stories.summary: Israel's Eurovision delegation chief Yoav Tsafir said he felt relief when Israel's entry by Noam Bettan narrowly lost, citing intense booing from the crowd when Israel briefly led in the voting.

stories.title: Indian student killed in road accident near Chicago
stories.summary: An Indian student identified as Navya Gadusu was killed in a road accident near Chicago. The Lake County Coroner's office pronounced her dead at 12:16 a.m. on Sunday, May 17, 2026.

stories.title: 2 cops martyred as speeding dumper crashes into parked police van on M9 Motorway
stories.summary: Two police officers, Constable Wajid and Sub-Inspector Sahib Dad Solangi, were killed on Karachi's M9 Motorway when a speeding dumper truck from Hyderabad crashed into their parked patrol van near Gadap City. The driver was taken into custody.

stories.title: IMF urges UK to ‘stay the course’ on borrowing amid Starmer uncertainty
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund urged the UK to maintain its course on reducing government borrowing amid bond market concerns and uncertainty over Labour leadership. The IMF praised Chancellor Rachel Reeves for targeting budget deficit cuts while upgrading Britain's growth forecasts.

stories.title: Could Ukraine's drone strikes mark a turning point in war with Russia?
stories.summary: A press review dated May 18, 2026, highlights Ukraine's drone strikes on Russian territory as a possible turning point in the war. The review also covers Venezuela's post-Maduro political transition, a dispute between Canal+ and filmmakers at the Cannes Film Festival, and Gen Z budget entertainment trends.

stories.title: Trump highlights war talks amid mounting domestic backlash
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump has reintroduced military options against Iran amid stalled negotiations and growing domestic criticism. Democrats have framed the confrontation as economically damaging and strategically inconsistent. Iran's demand for reciprocal recognition remains a key obstacle to a peace agreement.

stories.title: Deeply concerned: India on drone strike near UAE's Barakah nuclear plant
stories.summary: India's Ministry of External Affairs expressed deep concern over a drone strike targeting the Barakah nuclear power plant in the UAE. The statement condemned the attack on the facility.

stories.title: CXMT’s blowout earnings outlook fuels rally in Chinese memory chip stocks
stories.summary: Chinese memory chip stocks rallied after ChangXin Memory Technologies disclosed strong first-quarter results and an upbeat outlook in its listing prospectus. Shareholder GigaDevice rose 6.57% in mainland trading and 8% in Hong Kong amid a global memory shortage.

stories.title: Daily Briefing May 18: As personnel crisis looms, IDF needs Knesset legislation
stories.summary: The Times of Israel's daily briefing covered several Israeli military topics including the Lebanon ceasefire, Israel's quiet expansion in Gaza, a looming IDF personnel shortage requiring Knesset legislation, and a soldier disciplined for wearing a Messiah patch.

stories.title: Shakira in line for €55m payout as Spanish court rules tax fines were wrong
stories.summary: A Madrid court ordered Spain's tax authority to repay Shakira more than €55 million after ruling that fines imposed on the Colombian singer over her 2011 tax status were based on mistakes by the tax agency.

stories.title: East Africa: Somali Piracy Returns - a Warning From the Western Indian Ocean
stories.summary: Somali piracy has resurfaced in the western Indian Ocean as joint naval patrols are stretched thin by the broader Middle East crisis. Analysts note the patrols' ability to fully eradicate piracy was always limited.

stories.title: Africa: Africa's Golden Future
stories.summary: The Africa Forward Summit was held in Nairobi, Kenya, with speakers drawing parallels between Africa's development challenges and the perseverance shown by Kenyan marathon runner Sabastian Sawe, who ran a sub-two-hour marathon.

stories.title: Africa: Media As Bedrock for Developing Russian-African Relations
stories.summary: The Russian-African Club held its fourth International Forum of Journalists from Russia and Africa at Lomonosov Moscow State University in late April. Discussions focused on media structures, content challenges, and future cooperation between Russian and African media.

stories.title: Africa: LGBTIQ+ Face Mounting Violence and Discrimination, Warns UN Rights Chief
stories.summary: The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights warned of mounting violence and discrimination against LGBTIQ+ people globally. Data cited indicates that 45 percent of LGBT youth report experiencing bullying at school.

stories.title: Magic mushrooms could be effective treatment for cocaine addiction, study shows
stories.summary: A clinical trial published in JAMA Network Open found that a single dose of psilocybin may help treat cocaine addiction. Of 36 participants, the 19 who received psilocybin were more likely to abstain from cocaine than the 17 who received a placebo of diphenhydramine, a common antihistamine.

stories.title: China arrests 16 in drone hacking cases, vowing ‘clean skies’ crackdown
stories.summary: China's Ministry of Public Security announced the arrests of 16 people suspected of hacking drone systems between January and March as part of a nationwide "Clean Skies" campaign launched in December to combat illegal drone use.

stories.title: Russia is ‘largely defeated’ from Mali to Syria, France’s foreign minister says
stories.summary: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot stated that Russia has been largely defeated across its operations from Mali to Syria. He noted that Russia's Africa Corps has fled the Malian city of Kidal, with Mali's military junta expressing feelings of betrayal.

stories.title: Nigeria: Akwa Ibom Doctors Set Deadline for EFCC Amid Strike Threat
stories.summary: Doctors in Nigeria's Akwa Ibom state set a deadline for the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission amid a strike threat. The Nigerian Medical Association demanded a written apology and compensation over an EFCC raid at the University of Uyo Teaching Hospital.

stories.title: Uganda: Justine Nameere Released, Turns Around to Denounce Among's Speakership Bid
stories.summary: Ugandan MP Justine Nameere Nsubuga resurfaced after what some described as a military abduction and publicly denounced outgoing Speaker Anita Among's bid for the speakership.

stories.title: WATCH: Israel begins boarding Gaza-bound Turkish flotilla boats
stories.summary: Israeli forces began boarding boats from a Turkish-linked flotilla heading toward Gaza. Israel's Foreign Ministry called the flotilla a deliberate provocation and stated it would not permit any breach of the naval blockade.

stories.title: Uganda: Among X Message - 'I Have Thrown in the Towel'
stories.summary: Ugandan Parliament Speaker Anita Annet Among reportedly signaled on X that she has withdrawn from the race for Speaker. The message followed security raids on her homes as part of a corruption investigation.

stories.title: Cuba accuses US of building 'fraudulent case' for military action
stories.summary: Cuba's foreign minister accused the United States of building a "fraudulent case" to justify military action against the island nation. Havana said a report alleging it had acquired attack drones was being used as a pretext for potential U.S. aggression.

stories.title: Strike over high fuel prices paralyses transport in Kenya
stories.summary: A strike over high fuel prices paralyzed transport across Kenya, leaving key roads largely empty. Some schools asked students to stay home due to the disruption.

stories.title: Iran forms new body to manage Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme National Security Council announced the creation of a new Persian Gulf Strait Authority to manage the Strait of Hormuz. The body said it would provide real-time updates on operations and developments in the strategic waterway.

stories.title: Russian drone hits Chinese ship off Ukraine before Putin visits Xi Jinping
stories.summary: Ukraine reported overnight attacks involving 524 drones and 22 missiles targeting its territory. Separately, a Russian drone struck a Chinese-flagged ship off Ukraine's coast shortly before President Putin was scheduled to visit Chinese President Xi Jinping.

stories.title: Moscow and Moscow Region — after unprecedented Ukrainian strikes. Photos and video
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck Moscow and the Moscow region on May 17 in what Ukrainian sources called the largest such attack since the start of the full-scale war. Russian authorities reported three people killed and 16 injured, with strikes hitting the Moscow oil refinery in Kapotnya and the Solnechnogorskaya petroleum transfer station in Durykino.

stories.title: Israeli forces begin intercepting Gaza-bound aid flotilla near Cyprus
stories.summary: Israeli naval forces began intercepting boats from the Global Sumud Flotilla heading toward Gaza near the coast of Cyprus. The flotilla aimed to deliver aid by breaching Israel's maritime blockade of the enclave.

stories.title: Two dozen injured in Ukraine following Russian strikes
stories.summary: Russia targeted eight Ukrainian regions in an overnight drone and missile barrage, launching more than 500 drones and wounding over two dozen civilians, including three children. The city of Dnipro in central Ukraine sustained the heaviest damage from the strikes.

stories.title: Ukraine ready to intensify dialogue with Hungary on national minorities – Sybiha
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said Ukraine is ready to intensify dialogue with Hungary on national minorities and open a new chapter in bilateral relations with Hungary's new government.

stories.title: Pakistan forces kill 35 terrorists in Balochistan operation, capture 3 high-profile commanders
stories.summary: Pakistani security forces killed 35 terrorists and captured three high-profile commanders during operations in Balochistan. The Pakistan military had not yet released an official statement on the anti-terror operation at the time of reporting.

stories.title: Us-Iran truce under strain amid stalled talks and attacks on US allies
stories.summary: The fragile US-Iran ceasefire, in place since April 8 following a conflict that began on February 28, is under strain after a likely-Iranian attack near a UAE power plant. Washington and Tehran have held only one round of talks so far, and the stalled negotiations and rising tensions are unsettling global markets.

stories.title: Crashed Ukrainian drone found in Lithuania
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone was found crashed in a field near the village of Samane in Lithuania's northeastern Utena district, according to Lithuania's Crisis Management Center.

stories.title: Somaliland’s first ambassador in country’s history presents credentials to Herzog
stories.summary: Somaliland's first-ever ambassador, Dr. Mohamed Hagi, presented credentials to Israeli President Isaac Herzog. Herzog described the diplomatic relationship as an important new partnership intended to benefit the broader region.

stories.title: Nigeria: Borno Steps Up Efforts to Rescue 42 Askira-UBA School Abductees
stories.summary: The Borno State government in Nigeria is working with security agencies to rescue 42 students and children abducted from a primary and junior secondary school in Mussa, Askira-Uba Local Government Area.

stories.title: Kenya protesters block roads in public transport strike over fuel prices
stories.summary: Protests erupted in Nairobi on Monday as a nationwide public transport strike over rising fuel prices left commuters stranded. Protesters burned tires on major roads, and most schools switched to online learning after safety advisories were issued.

stories.title: Death sentences and executions on the rise worldwide
stories.summary: Amnesty International's annual report documents a record increase in death sentences and executions worldwide in 2025. China remains the suspected leading executioner globally, while Iran saw its number of executions nearly double compared to 2024.

stories.title: Israeli forces kill six Palestinians and wound 40 others in Gaza in last 24 hours
stories.summary: Israeli attacks killed at least six Palestinians and wounded 40 others across Gaza in a 24-hour period, according to Gaza's health ministry. Since the start of a ceasefire in October, Israel has killed approximately 877 people and wounded over 2,600 in the enclave.

stories.title: Dr Hook co-frontman Dennis Locorriere dies aged 76
stories.summary: Dennis Locorriere, co-frontman and lead vocalist of the soft rock band Dr Hook, has died at age 76 after a long battle with kidney disease. He was known for singing lead on hits including the UK number-one single "When You're in Love With a Beautiful Woman."

stories.title: UAH 140M bail paid for ex-chief of Ukraine's Presidential Office
stories.summary: A bail payment of 140 million Ukrainian hryvnias was posted for Andriy Yermak, the former head of Ukraine's Presidential Office. The bail had been ordered by Ukraine's High Anti-Corruption Court.

stories.title: Military jets' crew members safely ejected after Idaho air show collision, US Navy says
stories.summary: Two U.S. Navy EA-18G Growler jets from Electronic Attack Squadron 129 collided mid-air during the Gunfighter Skies Air Show near Mountain Home Air Force Base in Idaho on Sunday. All four crew members ejected safely. The incident is under investigation.

stories.title: Fighter jets collide at US air show
stories.summary: Two US Navy EA-18G Growler fighter jets collided midair during the Gunfighter Skies Air Show in Idaho on Sunday. All four crew members ejected safely and parachuted to the ground. An investigation is underway to determine the cause of the collision.

stories.title: UAE nuclear power plant targeted in likely-Iranian attack
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates reported that a drone strike caused a fire near the Barakah nuclear power plant in Abu Dhabi, with no casualties or radiological release. The origin of the strike is unconfirmed, but suspicion has focused on Iran. US President Donald Trump is reportedly planning to convene national security advisers on May 18 to discuss military options.

stories.title: Israeli Navy begins to intercept vessels in Gaza-bound flotilla off Cyprus coast
stories.summary: The Israeli Navy began intercepting vessels of the Gaza-bound flotilla off the coast of Cyprus. A flotilla livestream ended abruptly after Israeli commandos boarded a boat; Israel had earlier accused approximately 50 vessels of provocation.

stories.title: Russian drone hits Chinese commercial vessel in Ukrainian waters overnight
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a Chinese commercial vessel in Ukrainian waters overnight on May 18. The incident involves a ship belonging to Russia's key strategic partner.

stories.title: Evergrande liquidators seek US$8.4 billion from PwC entities in Hong Kong lawsuit
stories.summary: Liquidators of China Evergrande Group filed a lawsuit in Hong Kong seeking 57 billion yuan (US$8.4 billion) from three PricewaterhouseCoopers entities, alleging PwC's global coordinating arm bore responsibility for audits tied to the collapsed developer's accounting scandal.

stories.title: 4 plead guilty to rioting during 2019 PolyU siege in Hong Kong
stories.summary: Four men pleaded guilty in Hong Kong's District Court to rioting during the 2019 police siege of the Polytechnic University. The defendants were aged between 16 and 27 at the time of the anti-government protests.

stories.title: China hosts 23rd edition of iconic Great Wall marathon
stories.summary: The 23rd edition of the Great Wall of China Marathon took place on May 16 near the Huangyaguan fortress. Runners from around the world competed in the event, which is widely regarded as one of the most gruelling marathon courses and features on the Forbes Top 10 list of marathons worth travelling for.

stories.title: Israel is becoming less Jewish, not just less democratic, WZO's Yizhar Hess argues
stories.summary: Dr. Yizhar Hess, vice chairman of the World Zionist Organization, argued that Israel is becoming less Jewish in character, not merely less democratic. He criticized what he described as an unholy connection between state and religion in the country.

stories.title: Trump’s immigration crackdown could cost up to $479bn in lost taxes over 10 years
stories.summary: Tax experts warn that the Trump administration's immigration enforcement measures could result in up to $479 billion in lost federal tax revenue over the next decade. Proposed IRS data sharing with immigration authorities and ICE raids have discouraged undocumented workers from filing taxes, while tax benefits for immigrant parents have also been removed.

stories.title: Israeli forces boarding Gaza-bound flotilla near Cyprus, activists say
stories.summary: Israeli commandos boarded several vessels of the Global Sumud flotilla attempting to breach the Gaza maritime blockade near Cyprus. Live broadcasts from the flotilla captured the boarding operation.

stories.title: Modi’s grand tour: India links up with UAE, Europe to ‘hedge’ global shocks
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi began a five-nation tour starting with the United Arab Emirates, followed by the Netherlands, Sweden, Norway, and Italy, amid shifting Middle East dynamics and volatile oil prices.

stories.title: Oil touches two-week high after drone attack on UAE nuclear power plant
stories.summary: Oil prices rose to two-week highs after a drone attack on a UAE nuclear power plant and stalled Iran negotiations. Brent crude climbed to $111.27 per barrel while WTI reached $107.75, with markets anticipating possible US military discussions on Iran.

stories.title: France hopes for cooperation with Algeria to tackle DZ Mafia criminal organisation
stories.summary: French Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin visited Algeria seeking enhanced judicial cooperation between Paris and Algiers. The discussions focused on the criminal organisation known as DZ Mafia, whose leaders are allegedly directing drug trafficking and related violence in France from Algerian territory.

stories.title: DR Congo takes emergency measures to contain new Ebola outbreak
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo has implemented emergency measures to contain a new Ebola outbreak that has already claimed dozens of lives. The World Health Organization declared the outbreak a public health emergency of international concern. Cases have also been reported in neighboring Uganda among travelers from the DRC.

stories.title: How war affects civilians for generations
stories.summary: Research highlights the long-term, multigenerational effects of armed conflict on civilian populations, including physical and psychological consequences that often go unaddressed.

stories.title: Israel intercepts Gaza flotilla and arrests activists
stories.summary: Israeli forces intercepted the Gaza-bound Global Sumud Flotilla in international waters and arrested around 100 activists. Israeli media reported the boats were seized off the coast of Cyprus and that detained activists would be transferred to the port of Ashdod.

stories.title: War against Iran is "growing more unpopular by the day" in the US
stories.summary: A drone strike near a UAE nuclear plant has heightened fears of escalation in the US-Iran conflict. President Trump is expected to meet national security advisers on May 19 to discuss military options and warned that the "clock is ticking" for Iran. Domestically, the war is reportedly growing increasingly unpopular among Americans.

stories.title: G7 finance ministers meet in Paris as headwinds mount for global economy
stories.summary: G7 finance ministers and central bankers are meeting in Paris amid concerns that the US-Iran war is threatening global financial stability. War-related inflation has triggered turbulence in bond markets. Separately, the busiest commuter rail system in the United States has shut down due to a labor dispute.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine exchange overnight drone attacks
stories.summary: Russia launched hundreds of drones and nearly two dozen missiles at Ukraine overnight, wounding more than 30 people in Odesa and Dnipro. A Russian drone also struck a Chinese cargo ship in the Black Sea, one day before President Putin's scheduled meeting with Xi Jinping in Beijing. Ukraine's largest overnight drone attack on Moscow in over a year killed at least four people.

stories.title: Russian drones hit two ships off Ukraine's coast, including Chinese-owned vessel
stories.summary: Russia launched hundreds of drones and nearly two dozen missiles at Ukraine overnight, striking two civilian ships in the Black Sea near Ukraine's Odesa region and wounding more than 30 people. Ukrainian authorities identified the vessels as sailing under the flags of the Marshall Islands and Guinea-Bissau, including one Chinese-owned ship.

stories.title: How Trump and Iran use the same industry networks for their growing crypto empires
stories.summary: Data analysis reveals that Iran's crypto exchange processed at least $2.3 billion on the same two blockchains used by the Trump family's World Liberty Financial venture. The report highlights overlapping industry networks between Iranian and US-linked cryptocurrency operations.

stories.title: Video: US calls on G7 to impose US-led sanctions on Iran
stories.summary: US Treasury Secretary called on G7 nations to join Washington in imposing sanctions on Iran. The push seeks broader international alignment with the US-led pressure campaign against Tehran.

stories.title: Earthquake hits southwest China; thousands evacuate, buildings collapse
stories.summary: An earthquake struck southwest China in the early hours of Monday, May 18, 2026, causing at least 13 buildings to collapse and prompting thousands of evacuations, according to state broadcaster CCTV.

stories.title: Ukraine downs 503 drones, four Iskander-K missiles in massive overnight Russian attack
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense intercepted four Iskander-K cruise missiles and 503 drones during a large-scale Russian overnight attack that began on the evening of May 17.

stories.title: US military carries out more strikes against ISIL fighters in Nigeria
stories.summary: The US military conducted additional airstrikes against ISIL fighters in Nigeria. The operations followed a joint US-Nigerian announcement days earlier that they had killed a deputy ISIL leader in the region.

stories.title: Weather tracker: Europe braces for swing from Arctic chill to extreme heat
stories.summary: Europe is expecting a sharp temperature swing after a prolonged cold spell brought Arctic air and temperatures 10-15°C below seasonal averages. Warmer air is forecast to surge northward into western and central Europe in coming days.

stories.title: Somalia: Somaliland Condemns Strike Near UAE's Barakah Nuclear Facility
stories.summary: Somaliland's government condemned a drone attack carried out near the United Arab Emirates' Barakah Nuclear Facility, calling it a serious threat to regional peace, stability, and critical civilian infrastructure.

stories.title: Why Iran’s choice of Beijing envoy signals an ‘unprecedented’ commitment
stories.summary: Iran appointed parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, a veteran of peace talks with the U.S., as special envoy to oversee relations with China. Experts described the move as signaling unprecedented commitment to Beijing ties and China's role as a diplomatic intermediary.

stories.title: CENTCOM regional cooperation stopped 6,000 drones, 1,500 ballistic missiles in Iran war - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis found that U.S. Central Command's regional cooperation helped intercept approximately 6,000 drones and 1,500 ballistic missiles during the Iran war. Iran reportedly targeted multiple countries including the UAE, Israel, Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, Oman, and Iraq.

stories.title: ‘A book that should be read by all Australians’: Clare Wright wins book of the year at the NSW Literary awards
stories.summary: Melbourne historian Clare Wright won the NSW Literary Awards' book of the year and a $50,000 prize for her nonfiction work Näku Dhäruk: The Bark Petitions, which chronicles the creation of the Yirrkala Bark Petitions, a landmark moment in Australian land rights history.

stories.title: “Stop treating Russia’s bankers as faceless technocrats”: inside the war crimes case against Russia’s central bank
stories.summary: A landmark complaint filed with the International Criminal Court seeks to reframe Russia's financial occupation of Ukrainian territory as a war crime. The case highlights the pillaging of banks, forced introduction of the ruble, and tying medical care to Russian passport requirements.

stories.title: DR Congo: Health officials arrive in Bunia with Ebola supplies
stories.summary: Health officials from the Democratic Republic of Congo arrived in Bunia with Ebola medical supplies. The health minister said treatment centers would be established in Rwampara and Mongwalu, with dozens of patients already receiving care.

stories.title: War update: 242 clashes on front lines over past day, three sectors most active
stories.summary: Ukrainian and Russian forces engaged in 242 combat clashes along the front lines on Sunday, May 17, with three sectors seeing the heaviest activity.

stories.title: Who was Felicien Kabuga? The fugitive financier of genocide
stories.summary: Felicien Kabuga, once one of Rwanda's wealthiest businessmen, died in detention at a UN-backed tribunal in The Hague. He had been accused of helping finance the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi.

stories.title: Hong Kong earmarks additional HK$5 billion for national security
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities allocated an additional HK$5 billion (US$638 million) for national security efforts, bringing the total earmarked over the past five years to HK$18 billion, according to government expenditure documents.

stories.title: Nova exhibit banner in London taken down over police’s fear of attacks
stories.summary: London police asked organizers of a Nova massacre memorial exhibit to take down a promotional banner to prevent potential protests or attacks. The banner is to be displayed only when the exhibition opens on Wednesday to avoid revealing the location prematurely.

stories.title: Russia hits Ukraine's Odesa, Dnipro with drones and missiles overnight, officials say
stories.summary: On May 18, Russian forces struck the Ukrainian cities of Odesa in the south and Dnipro in the southeast using drones and missiles in an overnight attack, according to Ukrainian officials.

stories.title: Israeli settlers run over livestock in occupied West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli settlers drove vehicles into a herd of livestock belonging to a Palestinian shepherd in the occupied West Bank. The incident is part of a broader pattern of settler violence against Palestinian communities in the territory.

stories.title: Why Beijing is outraged over Taiwan’s Lai honouring WWII-era Japanese engineer
stories.summary: Beijing strongly criticized Taiwanese leader William Lai Ching-te for attending a memorial service in Tainan honoring a Japanese colonial-era engineer. The People's Daily accused Lai of "forgetting his ancestors" and ingratiating himself with Japan.

stories.title: South Korea stifling Samsung workers’ US$400,000 bonus strike risks wider crisis
stories.summary: Approximately 50,000 Samsung Electronics workers in South Korea planned an 18-day strike over bonuses, with the government warning of up to 100 trillion won (US$66.7 billion) in projected economic damage and potential disruption to global supply chains.

stories.title: Drones reshape war in Colombia as deaths and injuries mount
stories.summary: Armed groups in Colombia are increasingly using weaponized drones, with a 2024 attack in southern Cauca killing a 10-year-old boy and injuring 12 civilians during a children's football match — the first known drone-related fatality in the country's decades-old conflict.

stories.title: Haifa’s war on wild boars drops off the grid, as key oversight quietly disappears
stories.summary: Israel's Nature and Parks Authority withdrew from a joint project in Haifa aimed at managing the city's wild boar population. The departure of oversight has raised concerns that unregulated hunting could increase on city streets.

stories.title: Russian drone hits public transport stop in Kherson, one person injured
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a public transport stop in the Korabelnyi district of Kherson on the morning of May 18, injuring a 60-year-old man.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia targeted by drones ‘from Iraq,' condemns strike on UAE nuclear plant
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia reported a drone attack it said originated from Iraq, while also condemning the strike near Abu Dhabi's Barakah nuclear plant. Officials said the two attacks could potentially be connected, though investigations are ongoing.

stories.title: Israel built two military bases in Iraq before war on Iran: New York Times
stories.summary: The New York Times reported that Israel constructed two makeshift military bases in western Iraq in preparation for potential operations against Iran. The sites had reportedly been under development since late 2024.

stories.title: Oil prices rise and bonds wobble as Iran war stokes inflation fears
