stories.summary: President Zelensky said Ukraine's long-range strike capabilities are changing both the battlefield situation and global perceptions of Russia's war. He emphasized the strategic importance of these weapons in shaping international understanding of the conflict.

stories.title: Iranian media says ‘no tangible concessions’ in US response to Iran proposal
stories.summary: Iranian media reported that the US response to Iran's diplomatic proposal contained "no tangible concessions." The United States had reportedly conditioned a cessation of hostilities on all fronts on the commencement of formal negotiations.

stories.title: Russian air-defense crews are now the hunted as Ukraine bolts rocket pods to its long-range drones
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone forces struck a protected Russian air-defense position near Myrnyi in occupied Crimea, releasing thermal video of the attack. Ukraine has been equipping its long-range drones with rocket pods to target Russian air-defense crews.

stories.title: Death penalty law for Palestinian terrorists comes into effect in West Bank
stories.summary: A new Israeli law authorizing the death penalty for Palestinians convicted of terrorism offenses has taken effect in the West Bank. Defense Minister Israel Katz stated that convicted attackers would "pay the heaviest price."

stories.title: Cuba acquires 300 attack drones from Russia and Iran and discusses potential attacks on US – Axios
stories.summary: A classified U.S. assessment reported by Axios indicates Cuba has acquired more than 300 military strike drones from Russia and Iran. Cuban officials have reportedly discussed potential attacks on U.S. targets, including Guantanamo Bay Naval Base, U.S. warships, and an airbase in Key West.

stories.title: Trump issues dire warning to Iran to accept peace deal
stories.summary: President Donald Trump warned Iran that time is running out to reach a peace deal, stating there would be "nothing left" if an agreement is not reached. U.S.-Iran tensions and regional conflict continue to escalate.

stories.title: Israel to establish defence offices in former UNRWA compound
stories.summary: Israel announced plans to establish defense offices in a compound formerly used by UNRWA, the UN agency for Palestinian refugees. Defense Minister Israel Katz described the decision as one of "sovereignty, Zionism, and security."

stories.title: Suspected Ukrainian military drone discovered after crashing in Lithuania
stories.summary: A suspected Ukrainian military drone crashed in Lithuania, raising concerns among Baltic NATO members about stray drones crossing into their airspace from the war in neighboring Ukraine. Officials confirmed the drone was discovered on Sunday.

stories.title: ‘Won’t be anything left’: Trump issues threat to Iran amid stalled talks
stories.summary: President Donald Trump threatened Iran, warning that there would be "nothing left" if Tehran does not agree to U.S. demands, which include dismantling its nuclear program and missile stockpiles. Negotiations between the two countries remain stalled.

stories.title: Israel kills at least five in Lebanon after ‘ceasefire’ extended
stories.summary: Israeli air attacks struck multiple locations in southern and eastern Lebanon, killing at least five people. The strikes occurred despite an extended ceasefire arrangement between Israel and Lebanon.

stories.title: Hiker killed in attack by herd of cows in Austrian Alps
stories.summary: A 67-year-old woman was killed and her 65-year-old husband seriously injured after being attacked by a large herd of cows on a pasture in the Lienz district of East Tyrol, Austria. Authorities said the cause of the animals' aggressive behavior remains unclear.

stories.title: DRC struggling to contain Ebola outbreak as cases spread
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo is struggling to contain a new Ebola outbreak as cases continue to spread. The country has experienced repeated Ebola outbreaks over the years.

stories.title: Islamist attack on Nigerian military school kills 17 police trainees
stories.summary: Suspected Islamist militants attacked a specialized military school in Yobe state in northeastern Nigeria, killing at least 17 police trainees. Nigeria's national police spokesman confirmed the assault on the facility, which trains both military and police personnel.

stories.title: Air force base in Idaho locked down after air show incident, officials say
stories.summary: Emergency crews responded to an incident involving two aircraft during the Gunfighter Skies Air Show at Mountain Home Air Force Base in western Idaho. The base was locked down and an investigation was initiated.

stories.title: Drone strike starts fire outside UAE nuclear plant
stories.summary: A drone strike caused a fire outside the UAE's Barakah Nuclear Power Plant. Authorities reported no injuries and said radiation levels were unaffected by the incident.

stories.title: Taiwan won't be sacrificed, U.S. arms sales a commitment: President responds to Trump
stories.summary: Taiwanese President Lai responded to the recent Trump-Xi summit in Beijing by asserting that Taiwan will not be sacrificed and that U.S. arms sales represent a commitment to the island's defense.

stories.title: Will the latest Ebola outbreak in DR Congo and Uganda spread further?
stories.summary: The World Health Organization declared the latest Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda a global health emergency, raising concerns about further spread of the virus across the region.

stories.title: China will buy at least US$17 billion of US farm goods annually, White House says
stories.summary: The White House announced that China has agreed to purchase at least $17 billion in U.S. agricultural products annually through 2028. The commitment resulted from a summit between President Trump and President Xi Jinping, supplementing earlier soybean purchase agreements from October 2025.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia condemns UAE drone strike, backs security measures
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia condemned a drone strike that ignited a fire near a nuclear power plant in the United Arab Emirates, calling the attack a threat to regional security and stability. Riyadh expressed solidarity with the UAE and endorsed measures to protect its sovereignty and territorial integrity.

stories.title: Fire breaks out near nuclear power plant in United Arab Emirates following drone attack
stories.summary: A drone strike near Abu Dhabi's Barakah Nuclear Power Plant on May 17 ignited a fire in the vicinity of the facility. The incident prompted regional condemnation and raised concerns about security threats to critical infrastructure in the United Arab Emirates.

stories.title: Mass DC prayer event with top White House officials seeks to reclaim US Christian roots
stories.summary: Senior White House officials including Pete Hegseth, Marco Rubio, and Mike Johnson are scheduled to speak at "Reclaim 250," a large-scale prayer event in Washington, D.C. Critics have characterized the gathering as promoting Christian nationalism.

stories.title: UAE blames Iran or its proxies for drone strike fire near nuclear plant
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates blamed Iran or its proxies for a drone strike that caused a fire near the Barakah nuclear power plant, calling it a "dangerous escalation." The incident caused no injuries or radiation alerts but occurred during a fragile ceasefire in the sixth week of the Iran conflict.

stories.title: Israeli strikes in south Lebanon kill five, wound several
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes hit several towns in southern Lebanon, killing at least five people and wounding multiple others. Strikes on Tairfalsiya killed three, including a child, and wounded eight. In Tirdaba, two people were killed, including a child, and three others were injured.

stories.title: “There was no way back”: Captured Russian soldiers say commanders welded pipeline shut behind them
stories.summary: Captured Russian soldiers reported that commanders sent them through a gas pipeline behind Ukrainian lines and welded the entry shut, preventing retreat. Ukrainian forces had anticipated the maneuver and positioned drones at the pipeline exit.

stories.title: Russians carry out nearly 40 attacks on Dnipropetrovsk region, leaving two killed, five others injured
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out nearly 40 attacks on Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region using drones and artillery, striking four districts. The attacks killed two people and injured five others.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill five people in Gaza, medics say
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes killed at least five people in Gaza, according to medics. One Palestinian was killed near a police post and another at a tent encampment in Khan Younis.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill four people in Gaza, medics say
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed four people in Gaza, according to Palestinian medics. The Israeli military stated it had killed a militant who posed an immediate threat to its forces in the territory.

stories.title: Mexican officials announce 10 dead in early-morning shooting in Tehuitzingo
stories.summary: Mexican officials reported that 10 people were killed in an early-morning shooting in Tehuitzingo. Authorities attributed the attack to unidentified armed individuals but provided no further details about the attackers or their motives.

stories.title: Putin’s new Transnistria citizenship decree is about finding more soldiers for war against Ukraine — Moldova’s president
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a decree on May 15 fast-tracking Russian citizenship for residents of Moldova's breakaway Transnistria region. Moldovan President Maia Sandu characterized the move as an effort to recruit more soldiers for Russia's war against Ukraine.

stories.title: Iran, Pakistan discuss stalled US talks as Ghalibaf criticises US role
stories.summary: Iranian parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf met Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi to discuss stalled negotiations between Tehran and Washington. Ghalibaf criticized the U.S. role in the region, arguing that American presence creates insecurity rather than stability.

stories.title: Government approves dedicated unit to assist new immigrants serving in IDF
stories.summary: The Israeli government approved a dedicated unit to assist new immigrants serving in the IDF. The unit will specialize in guiding and supporting olim throughout their military service, following a significant rise in immigration since October 7.

stories.title: Israel kills three Palestinians in strike on an aid kitchen in Gaza
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike hit a kitchen providing meals to displaced people in Gaza, killing three Palestinians and injuring others. The kitchen had been serving as an aid distribution point for civilians.

stories.title: Palestinian leader's son wins role in Abbas' party, official says
stories.summary: Tareq Abbas, the millionaire businessman son of Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas, has secured a steering role within the Fatah party, according to a party official in Ramallah. The development comes amid a growing succession struggle for control of the Palestinian Authority.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Patriots are running out. Can a recycled Soviet missile replace them?
stories.summary: As the Iran conflict depletes global Patriot missile stockpiles, Ukraine is exploring alternatives for long-range air defense. A recycled Soviet-era missile system called Freya is being considered as a potential replacement.

stories.title: IDF faces looming manpower gap as ultra-Orthodox draft fight stalls service extension
stories.summary: The Israeli military faces a growing manpower shortage as ultra-Orthodox draft legislation stalls in the Knesset. The issue has gained urgency amid a coalition crisis that could lead to the dissolution of the Knesset.

stories.title: Prime Minister Netanyahu, US President Trump speak on Iran updates, China visit
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and US President Trump spoke about developments regarding Iran and Trump's recent visit to China. Netanyahu said Israel was prepared for any scenario.

stories.title: Bowlers, opener Joy put Bangladesh in command of second Test against Pakistan
stories.summary: In the second Test in Sylhet, Bangladesh's bowlers dominated Pakistan before opener Mahmudul Hasan Joy scored 52 off 64 balls. Bangladesh closed day two at 110-3 in their second innings, leading by 156 runs with a 1-0 series lead.

stories.title: Pakistan 'critical counter-terrorism partner' in US fight against IS-K: Centcom
stories.summary: U.S. Central Command Commander Admiral Bradford Cooper described Pakistan as a "critical counter-terrorism partner" central to the fight against Islamic State-Khorasan in South Asia. The remarks came during testimony before the Senate Armed Services Committee on the progress of Operation Epic Fury against Iran.

stories.title: PM Modi lands in Sweden; to hold talks on bilateral trade, technology, defence | LIVE
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Modi arrived in Sweden for a two-day visit to hold talks with Swedish Prime Minister Kristersson. Discussions are expected to focus on bilateral trade, technology, and defense cooperation.

stories.title: Washington lets the Russian oil loophole expire, ending months of seaborne sanctions relief
stories.summary: The U.S. administration allowed a sanctions relief carve-out for Russian seaborne oil exports to expire. Senators from both parties had pushed to end the loophole, which critics argued funneled billions of dollars into Russia's war effort.

stories.title: Israel-Lebanon ceasefire a dangerous fiction in the war against Hezbollah - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis examined the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire, noting that Hezbollah has used the agreement to adapt and regroup. The piece argued that negotiations disconnected from battlefield realities create space for armed groups to reorganize.

stories.title: Ukrainian-made weapons used to strike targets in Moscow region — General Staff
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff announced that domestically developed weapons were used to strike targets in Russia's Moscow region. No further details about the specific weapons or targets were provided.

stories.title: Iraqi farmer killed to hide evidence of two Israeli bases in country: Report
stories.summary: A New York Times investigation reported that an Iraqi shepherd was killed after discovering two secret Israeli military bases in western Iraq. The Wall Street Journal had previously revealed that Israel established a covert outpost in Iraq's desert to support air operations during its conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Andy Burnham faces perilous race to win Makerfield byelection, allies say
stories.summary: Andy Burnham is expected to be confirmed as Labour's candidate for the Makerfield byelection in north-west England. Allies warn he faces a difficult contest against Reform UK, which captured more than 50% of the vote in recent local elections. Reform is expected to campaign heavily on immigration and Brexit.

stories.title: Axios: Cuba has acquired over 300 Russian and Iranian military drones
stories.summary: A classified U.S. intelligence assessment shared with Axios indicates Cuba has acquired over 300 military drones from Russia and Iran since 2023. The assessment reportedly states that Cuba's military has begun weighing potential strikes on U.S. targets.

stories.title: Israel to ban cell phones in middle schools, Education Ministry confirms
stories.summary: Israel's Education Ministry confirmed it will ban cell phones in middle schools. A similar prohibition was introduced in elementary schools in February.

stories.title: World-famous illusionist David Blaine visits Ukraine
stories.summary: World-famous illusionist David Blaine visited Ukraine, traveling via Ukrzaliznytsia rail to Lviv, Kyiv, and Kharkiv.

stories.title: Indian worker among those killed in Moscow drone strikes, Embassy says
stories.summary: An Indian worker was among those killed in drone strikes in the Moscow region of Russia, according to India's embassy. Embassy officials visited the site, met injured workers in the hospital, and coordinated with Russian authorities to provide assistance.

stories.title: Iran chief negotiator Ghalibaf appointed to oversee ties with China: Media
stories.summary: Iran's Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf, who served as chief nuclear negotiator, has been appointed to oversee relations with China. The appointment was made at the proposal of the Iranian president.

stories.title: The miracle that shaped Israel Prize winner Avi Rivkind’s life and career - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece profiled Israel Prize winner Avi Rivkind, a trauma surgeon whose career was shaped by a split-second medical decision that saved a young soldier's life.

stories.title: Trump warns Iran ‘clock is ticking’ threatening severe consequences
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump issued a warning to Iran on Truth Social, stating that Tehran must act quickly or face severe consequences. Trump wrote that "the Clock is Ticking" and urged Iran to move fast on negotiations.

stories.title: Israel’s PM says close to killing all architects of October 7 attack
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel is close to eliminating all architects of the October 7 attack. His remarks followed the IDF's announcement that Ezzedine al-Haddad, commander of Hamas's armed wing, was killed in an air strike in Gaza on Friday.

stories.title: PM: IDF combating drones for six years, unlimited budget team formed for Hezbollah's FPV threat
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu told the cabinet that the IDF has been combating drone threats for six years and announced the formation of a team with an unlimited budget to counter Hezbollah's first-person-view drone threat.

stories.title: Cutting US aid to Israel would be a strategic disaster for America - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argued that cutting US aid to Israel would be a strategic mistake for America. The author contended that American assistance gives US diplomats significant leverage over Israeli decisions in the West Bank and Gaza.

stories.title: Ministry of Digital Transformation shares details about use of digital technologies on battlefield
stories.summary: Acting Ukrainian Digital Transformation Minister Oleksandr Bornyakov said Ukrainian forces are effectively deploying digital technologies on the battlefield against Russia. He noted this is occurring despite Russia's advantages in manpower, tanks, and ammunition.

stories.title: Coalition seeks to fast-track 2 key bills through committee, bypassing legal review
stories.summary: Israel's governing coalition moved to fast-track two bills through Knesset committee sessions, bypassing standard legal review. The legislation would split the Attorney General's role and overhaul media regulation ahead of an expected Knesset dissolution and early elections, despite opposition from the legal adviser.

stories.title: Kundi calls on PM to 'take interest' in KP's issues, says told CM Afridi to focus on governance not Adiala
stories.summary: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi urged Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to take greater interest in the province's issues after meeting KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi in Peshawar. Kundi also said he told Afridi to focus on provincial governance rather than PTI's campaign for party founder Imran Khan's release from Adiala jail in Rawalpindi.

stories.title: A one-meter gas pipe, a scooter, and a surrender: how a Russian assault group became POWs
stories.summary: A Russian assault group was captured in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia Oblast after entering positions through a one-meter gas pipe that commanders sealed behind them. Three additional Russian soldiers surrendered near Vovchansk in the Kharkiv region.

stories.title: Russia killed 52 people in Ukraine this week — firing mostly ballistic missiles, hardest for air defense to stop
stories.summary: Russian forces killed 52 people in Ukraine over the past week, primarily using ballistic missiles, which are the hardest type for air defense systems to intercept. Russia also launched 3,170 drones at Ukrainian targets during the seven-day period.

stories.title: IDF warns of severe personnel shortages, last window to solve crisis with legislation
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces warned of severe personnel shortages, stating it is still missing 12,000 troops with the gap expected to widen. Military officials said the government's current draft bill would not provide an adequate solution and called the present moment the last window for legislative action.

stories.title: London police: 20 right-wing, 12 anti-Israel protesters arrested in dueling rallies
stories.summary: London police arrested 20 right-wing and 12 anti-Israel protesters during competing rallies in the city. Nine arrests at a large rally organized by anti-Islam figure Tommy Robinson involved hate crime charges, while two arrests were made among participants of an opposing Nakba Day march.

stories.title: Air raid alerts declared in several regions due to threat of drones
stories.summary: Air raid alerts were declared across multiple regions of Ukraine due to the threat of incoming drones.

stories.title: Sudanese army advances in Blue Nile state deepen displacement crisis
stories.summary: The Sudanese Armed Forces have advanced into Blue Nile state, triggering renewed fighting that has displaced families into overcrowded camps. The escalation deepens an already severe displacement crisis in the region.

stories.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill one, wound several in Khan Younis and Gaza City
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes hit Khan Younis in southern Gaza and the Tel al-Hawa neighbourhood in Gaza City, killing one person and wounding at least nine others. The injured were transported to Al-Quds Hospital, operated by the Palestinian Red Crescent.

stories.title: Venice Art Biennale hit by upheaval over Israel's participation
stories.summary: More than 25 national pavilions closed their doors at the Venice Art Biennale in protest over the participation of Israel and Russia in the event.

stories.title: UAE condemns drone strike that caused fire outside nuclear plant
stories.summary: A drone strike caused a fire near the Barakah Nuclear Power Plant in the UAE, located approximately 200 kilometres west of Abu Dhabi. The UAE government condemned the attack. The plant has been operational since 2020.

stories.title: Trump attacks Massie as Republican critic describes ‘desperate’ attempts to oust him from primary
stories.summary: President Donald Trump publicly attacked Republican congressman Thomas Massie of Kentucky on Truth Social, urging voters to remove him ahead of Tuesday's Republican primary. Massie, one of the few senior Republicans to openly defy Trump, faces a close race against a Trump-endorsed challenger.

stories.title: US does not extend license allowing sales of Russian oil – Bloomberg
stories.summary: The Trump administration did not renew a license that had allowed temporary transactions involving the sale of Russian oil, according to Bloomberg.

stories.title: “War is returning to where it came from”: Ukraine discloses weapons it used in biggest strike on Moscow Oblast since 2022
stories.summary: Ukraine disclosed the weapons used in its largest strike on Moscow Oblast since 2022, targeting the Angstrem microchip plant. The facility, which produces components for Russian precision weapons and is under U.S. sanctions, was set ablaze in the attack.

stories.title: German police kill escaped tiger, animal handler seriously injured
stories.summary: German police shot and killed a tiger that escaped from a private facility near Leipzig in the town of Schkeuditz. A 73-year-old volunteer animal handler was seriously injured and hospitalized after the tiger broke free from its enclosure.

stories.title: Italy’s leaders visit victims of Modena car-ramming, stabbing attacks
stories.summary: Italian leaders visited victims of car-ramming and stabbing attacks in Modena carried out by 31-year-old Salim El Khoudri. Authorities have linked the attacks to a situation of psychiatric distress rather than a broader security threat.

stories.title: Israel illegally raids south Syria amid 'war crime' allegations
stories.summary: Israeli forces conducted a raid into southern Syria, entering areas in the Daraa and Quneitra regions. Monitors documented 49 alleged violations in the area in the preceding week, with allegations of war crimes reported amid rising tensions.

stories.title: ICC prosecutor seeks arrest warrants for 5 Israeli officials
stories.summary: The International Criminal Court's chief prosecutor has reportedly sought arrest warrants for five Israeli officials, including three far-right government ministers and two senior military figures.

stories.title: Drone strike causes fire outside nuclear power plant in Abu Dhabi
stories.summary: A drone strike caused a fire at an external electrical generator outside the perimeter of the Barakah Nuclear Power Plant in Al Dhafra, Abu Dhabi. The Abu Dhabi media office confirmed the blaze did not affect the plant's nuclear operations.

stories.title: UAE condemns drone strike near nuclear plant as ‘dangerous escalation’
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates condemned a drone strike that sparked a fire near the Barakah nuclear power plant in western Abu Dhabi. The UAE Foreign Ministry called it a "dangerous escalation" and an "unacceptable act of aggression" but did not assign responsibility.

stories.title: WHO declares Ebola outbreak in DR Congo, Uganda an 'emergency of international concern'
stories.summary: The World Health Organization declared the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda a public health emergency of international concern. The Bundibugyo virus outbreak has caused 80 suspected deaths and 246 suspected cases in DRC's Ituri province, with countries sharing land borders at high risk.

stories.title: War update: 46 clashes since morning, heaviest fighting continues in Kostiantynivka direction
stories.summary: Ukrainian and Russian forces engaged in 46 clashes since the morning, with the heaviest fighting reported in the Kostiantynivka, Pokrovsk, and Huliaipole sectors of eastern Ukraine.

stories.title: Police arrest man over phallic keychains portraying Netanyahu as ‘dicktator’
stories.summary: Israeli police arrested a man for distributing phallic-shaped keychains depicting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as a "dicktator." He was released hours later after being accused in court of sexual harassment. The protester said authorities were attempting to silence legitimate protest.

stories.title: Italian leaders visit Modena after car-ramming attack
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and President Sergio Mattarella visited the northern city of Modena on Sunday, one day after several people were injured in a car-ramming attack. Officials described it as the first incident of its kind in Italy.

stories.title: Rational or reckless? War, Iran, and the limits of strategy - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Analysts Yehuda Kurtzer and Michael Koplow discussed whether the actions of the Trump administration, Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu, and Iran reflect rational strategy or recklessness. The conversation examined an uncertain moment in U.S.–Iran–Israel relations amid ongoing regional tensions.

stories.title: Don’t wring your hands, roll up your sleeves: Israel education for today - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Rabbi Josh Weinberg addressed challenges facing Jewish educators in teaching about Israel when love, values, politics, and identity feel out of alignment. The discussion was published as sponsored content by The Times of Israel.

stories.title: Anti-LGBTQ violence in Israel rose sharply in 2025, national queer and trans violence report finds
stories.summary: A report found that 432 incidents of homophobic or transphobic physical violence were recorded in Israel in 2025, representing a sharp rise in anti-LGBTQ violence. The findings were published by the Aguda, Israel's national LGBTQ organization.

stories.title: Major shipping companies find partial solution to bypass blockade of Strait of Hormuz – FT
stories.summary: Major shipping companies including MSC, Maersk, and CMA CGM have developed partial workarounds to bypass the effectively closed Strait of Hormuz, according to the Financial Times. The closures are linked to the U.S. military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Europe’s Middle East Reckoning - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Professor Sharon Pardo examined European perspectives on Israel, Iran, and the broader Middle East, including debates over sanctions on Israeli settlers and the EU's role in regional security. The analysis appeared as sponsored content in The Times of Israel.

stories.title: Ukraine hits its fourth Russian ship of the mounth in the Caspian Sea, this time an FSB border patrol boat
stories.summary: Ukraine struck a Russian FSB border patrol boat—a Project 10410 Svetlyak-class vessel—near Kaspiysk in Dagestan on the Caspian Sea. It was the fourth Russian ship Ukraine hit during the month, targeting a location far from the front lines.

stories.title: Around 10 ‘new’ victims in France’s Epstein investigation, Paris prosecutor says
stories.summary: Approximately ten new suspected victims have come forward in a French investigation into the network of late U.S. sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, according to the Paris prosecutor. France opened a human trafficking probe after the U.S. Justice Department released files in January. French magistrates are examining possible offences committed in France.

stories.title: Amid rumors of renewed war, Iran may escalate attacks on UAE - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis suggests that a drone attack on the UAE on May 17 may have been an Iranian signal of intent to expand its target list in the country. The assessment comes amid rumors of renewed conflict between Israel, the United States, and Iran.

stories.title: Three community kitchen workers among five killed by Israel in Gaza
stories.summary: Israeli strikes on Gaza killed five people, including three workers at a community kitchen. According to reports, at least 871 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli attacks since a ceasefire agreement began last year.

stories.title: Canadian FM: Is the US still a reliable ally?
stories.summary: Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand publicly questioned whether the United States remains a reliable ally. Her remarks touched on issues including Donald Trump, NATO, Israel, China, and Canada's evolving international role.

stories.title: Israel built two covert military bases in Iraq to support Iran strikes – report
stories.summary: The New York Times reported that Israel built two covert military bases in Iraq to support strikes against Iran. The first base was reportedly established in late 2024, and a second installation was built more recently; one soldier and one civilian were reportedly killed to protect the secret.

stories.title: Bolivian police clash with protesters blocking roads into La Paz
stories.summary: Bolivian police and soldiers clashed on Saturday with protesters who were blocking roads into La Paz. The demonstrators were pressing for wage increases and other demands.

stories.title: Hezbollah may return to political assassinations as control over Lebanon weakens, expert says
stories.summary: An expert warned that Hezbollah may resume political assassinations as its control over Lebanon weakens. Recent Lebanese legislation has restricted Hezbollah's ability to legally possess weapons and conduct military operations.

stories.title: France moves to deport prominent Palestinian-Egyptian activist over criticism of Israel
stories.summary: French authorities have moved to deport Palestinian-Egyptian activist Ramy Shaath over his criticism of Israel. Shaath had previously been released from arbitrary detention in Egypt in 2022 following lobbying by French President Emmanuel Macron.

stories.title: Israeli officials say 50% chance of renewed war with Iran
stories.summary: Israeli officials have reportedly assessed a 50 percent probability of renewed military conflict with Iran within days. The assessment comes amid US threats and stalled nuclear negotiations between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Def. Min. complex to be built on site of fmr. UNRWA Jerusalem headquarters, Katz says
stories.summary: Israeli Defense Minister Katz announced that a new Defense Ministry complex will be built on the site of the former UNRWA headquarters at Ammunition Hill in Jerusalem. The UNRWA building was demolished in January after the organization's alleged ties to Hamas were revealed.

stories.title: Italian PM Meloni to meet victims of Modena car incident
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni is scheduled to meet victims of a car incident in Modena. Eight people were wounded in the incident, including a woman who required a double leg amputation.

stories.title: DRC faces deadly Ebola resurgence amid worsening humanitarian crisis
stories.summary: A new Ebola outbreak has been reported in the northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, affecting the towns of Rwampara, Mongwalu, and Bunia. The resurgence comes amid an ongoing humanitarian crisis in the region.

stories.title: Iranian civilians get defence training
stories.summary: Defense training sessions involving light weapons were held for Iranian civilian men and women in mosques across several cities in Iran.

stories.title: Iran thanks Pakistan, Iraq and Afghanistan for refusing US-Israeli access
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian thanked Pakistan, Iraq, and Afghanistan for refusing to allow US and Israeli forces access to their territory. He made the remarks during a meeting in Tehran with Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi.

stories.title: Taiwan is building a smart healthcare system with AI, big data - opinion
stories.summary: Taiwan is developing a digital healthcare system that integrates artificial intelligence and big data to improve patient care. The initiative also supports Taiwan's advocacy for inclusion in the World Health Organization.

stories.title: Russian army attacks enterprise in Poltava region
stories.summary: Russian forces struck an enterprise in the Myrhorod district of Ukraine's Poltava region on Sunday morning.

stories.title: Former Shas minister Moshe Arbel resigns from Knesset ahead of election
stories.summary: Former Shas minister Moshe Arbel, who served as both health and interior minister in the current Israeli government, has resigned from the Knesset ahead of the upcoming election. He will be replaced by former MK Erez Malul.

stories.title: Falling debris from Russian UAVs damages three buildings in Brovary
stories.summary: In Brovary, located in the Kyiv region of Ukraine, falling debris from Russian drones shot down by air defenses damaged two residential houses and a commercial facility. No casualty details were immediately provided.

stories.title: US college graduates face harsh job market amid economic uncertainty
stories.summary: Recent US college graduates are facing a difficult job market driven by government funding cuts, trade tariffs, the effects of war, and the rise of AI, all of which are intensifying competition for stable employment.

stories.title: ‘Calm before storm’: Donald Trump’s warning sparks alarm over possible Iran strikes, signals escalation in West Asia
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump issued a warning described as the "calm before the storm," sparking alarm about possible military strikes on Iran. Reports suggest the Trump administration is weighing critical decisions on Iran policy that could escalate tensions in West Asia.

stories.title: Taiwan not to give up ‘free way of life under pressure’: President
stories.summary: Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te stated that Taiwan will not provoke conflict with China but will not abandon its democratic values or dignity under external pressure.

stories.title: Ukraine drones kill four as Moscow faces biggest attack in year
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck Moscow in what was described as the city's largest aerial attack in a year, killing four people. Sheremetyevo, Moscow's largest airport, reported that drone debris landed on its grounds but caused no damage.

stories.title: Sons of jailed Saudi scholars urge Cambridge to drop plans to train Riyadh staff
stories.summary: The sons of two Saudi scholars facing the death penalty have urged the University of Cambridge to abandon plans to run staff training courses for Saudi Arabia's defence ministry. Cambridge's Judge Business School had been authorized to offer leadership development and innovation management training, drawing internal opposition over Riyadh's human rights record.

stories.title: Smotrich denies bid to hike retirement age to 70 as Treasury drafts multi-year plan
stories.summary: Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich denied plans to raise the retirement age to 70, though Treasury officials indicated it remains part of a long-term economic contingency plan. The denial came as the Treasury drafts a multi-year fiscal plan.

stories.title: Russian drone attack in Kherson region leaves three people injured
stories.summary: Three people were wounded in a Russian drone strike on Zelenivka in Ukraine's Kherson region. The attack was part of ongoing Russian aerial operations targeting communities in southern Ukraine.

stories.title: Iraqi farmer killed to hide evidence of two Israeli bases: Report
stories.summary: A New York Times investigation reported that an Iraqi shepherd was killed after discovering two secret Israeli military bases in Iraq's western desert. The bases were reportedly used to support air operations against Iran and housed special forces units.

stories.title: Israel strikes Lebanon while Hezbollah calls talks ‘dead end’
stories.summary: Israel carried out airstrikes on Lebanon as Hezbollah declared that ongoing negotiations are a "dead end." The strikes followed a third round of Israeli-Lebanese talks in Washington, where both sides agreed to extend a ceasefire.

stories.title: South Korea weighs arbitration to avoid Samsung semiconductor plant strike
stories.summary: South Korean Prime Minister stated the government will pursue all options, including emergency arbitration, to prevent a labor strike at Samsung Electronics. The world's largest memory chipmaker and its South Korean labor union are set to resume pay negotiations on Monday with a government mediator.

stories.title: Governor Kundi administers oath to 5 new KP ministers
stories.summary: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi administered the oath of office to five new provincial ministers in Peshawar, Pakistan. The swearing-in followed the governor's approval of a summary for 18 new cabinet members submitted by Chief Minister Sohail Afridi.

stories.title: Most of the architects of October 7 attacks have been killed, says Netanyahu
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said most of the architects of the October 7 attacks have been killed, claiming Israel is close to achieving a key war aim. The statement followed Israel's reported killing of senior Hamas commander Ezzedine Al-Haddad in an airstrike in Gaza.

stories.title: 4 IDF troops wounded, one severely, by roadside bomb in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Four Israeli Defense Forces soldiers were wounded, one severely, by a roadside bomb in southern Lebanon. Prime Minister Netanyahu claimed he had warned of the Hezbollah drone threat six years ago but did not explain why it was not addressed.

stories.title: In boon for marine life, Agriculture Ministry bans fishing drones
stories.summary: Israel's Agriculture Ministry has banned the use of fishing drones, which allowed anglers to cast lines hundreds of meters offshore into areas frequented by marine life including sea turtles.

stories.title: Big tobacco is exploiting fears of the illicit market to unwind health gains, Australian experts warn
stories.summary: A coalition of 15 Australian health organizations, including the Cancer Council and Heart Foundation, warned that big tobacco companies are exploiting concerns about illicit markets to undermine public health policies. The criticism follows a parliamentary inquiry that took secret evidence from cigarette manufacturer Philip Morris.

stories.title: FIA arrests two for 'impersonating government officials' in Karachi
stories.summary: Pakistan's Federal Investigation Agency arrested two individuals in Karachi, including a woman, for impersonating government officials. The suspects allegedly presented themselves as representatives of a so-called National Peace Force Committee for Interfaith Harmony Pakistan using fake credentials.

stories.title: Ukraine strikes Russia: Zelensky says response to Moscow's agression 'justified'
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky described strikes on Russian territory as a justified response to Moscow's aggression. Details of the specific targets or damage were not elaborated in the report.

stories.title: German minister defends decision to allow attempt to rescue whale Timmy
stories.summary: German authorities defended their decision to allow a rescue attempt for a stranded humpback whale known as Timmy, despite experts advising against it due to the animal's injuries and low survival chances. The whale had been stranded on Timmendorfer beach, a sandbank near the German coast, for nearly two months.

stories.title: Drone hits UAE nuclear power plant: IAEA reports normal radiation levels
stories.summary: The International Atomic Energy Agency reported normal radiation levels after a drone struck the UAE's Barakah nuclear power plant. The incident is being monitored from the region.

stories.title: South Korea says it will pursue all options to avoid Samsung strike
stories.summary: South Korea's government has said it will pursue all available options to prevent a strike at Samsung Electronics' semiconductor operations. Officials warned that a single day of production suspension could cause direct losses of up to approximately $668 million.

stories.title: WHO declares emergency as Ebola outbreak kills more than 80 in DR Congo
stories.summary: The World Health Organization declared an international public health emergency over an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The outbreak, caused by a strain with no available vaccine, has killed more than 80 people.

stories.title: NCB cracks major India-Myanmar drug syndicate, arrests kingpin
stories.summary: India's Narcotics Control Bureau dismantled a major India-Myanmar drug syndicate and arrested its alleged kingpin, Chintuang. He was identified as a major international supplier of methamphetamine and heroin operating along the Myanmar-Mizoram-Manipur-Assam-Tripura corridor.

stories.title: Israel built second secret military base in Iraqi desert, officials say - report
stories.summary: Reports indicate Israel constructed a second secret military base in a remote area of the Iraqi desert. The revelation follows a Wall Street Journal report the previous week disclosing the existence of a first covert Israeli military installation in the same region.

stories.title: Defense Forces strike military-industrial complex object and several oil facilities in Moscow region
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces, including specialists from the Security Service of Ukraine's Special Operations Center "A," struck a military-industrial complex facility and several oil installations in Russia's Moscow region. Additional strikes targeted positions in temporarily occupied Crimea.

stories.title: Ebola outbreak declared health emergency in DR Congo and Uganda
stories.summary: An Ebola outbreak has prompted health emergency declarations affecting the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda. International organizations including the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies are responding to the crisis.

stories.title: Netanyahu convenes security cabinet amid reports Israel, US preparing Iran strikes
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu convened his security cabinet amid reports that Israel and the United States are preparing strikes against Iran. A drone struck the UAE's Barakah nuclear power plant, and Iranian media said U.S.-Iran talks yielded no concrete concessions.

stories.title: India scrambles to steady rupee as oil shock bites
stories.summary: India is struggling to stabilize the rupee, which has fallen more than 5% since a Middle East conflict escalated in February 2026, hitting a record low above 96 to the dollar. Surging oil prices are straining the economy, and the central bank has spent billions of dollars intervening in currency markets.

stories.title: Islamabad, Baku developing ties within Pakistan-Turkiye-Azerbaijan trilateral framework: President Aliyev
stories.summary: Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev said relations between Islamabad and Baku are developing within a trilateral framework involving Pakistan, Türkiye, and Azerbaijan. The statement came during a meeting with Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, who was visiting Baku for the 13th UN World Urban Forum.

stories.title: Iraqi farmer killed to hide evidence of two Israeli bases in country: Report
stories.summary: According to local accounts, shepherd Awad al-Shammari was killed by a helicopter strike after discovering an Israeli base in Iraq's Najaf desert. The incident is linked to reports of two covert Israeli military installations in western Iraq.

stories.title: Is Christian Zionism in the US on a decline?
stories.summary: Polling suggests that support for Israel among younger American conservatives is declining, which could signal a weakening of the Christian Zionist movement in the United States.

stories.title: Four Israeli soldiers injured in southern Lebanon blast
stories.summary: Four Israeli soldiers were wounded when an explosive device detonated in southern Lebanon. The Israeli military said one soldier was seriously injured and another sustained moderate wounds.

stories.title: ‘Now 60%’: Netanyahu admits Israel taking more territory in Gaza, despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Prime Minister Netanyahu told his cabinet that Israel now controls 60 percent of Gaza's territory, expanding beyond the 53 percent demarcated under a U.S.-brokered ceasefire. Israeli strikes in the Strip reportedly killed four people.

stories.title: Ukrainian drone strikes on Russia kills at least 4 and wound 12 others
stories.summary: One of Ukraine's largest drone strikes on Russia killed at least four people, including three near Moscow, and wounded twelve others. Debris fell on Russia's largest airport but did not cause damage, according to local authorities.

stories.title: Ebola: WHO warns about risk of spread in DR Congo and Uganda
stories.summary: The World Health Organization warned of the risk of Ebola spreading in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda. Médecins Sans Frontières has deployed an emergency response team to Ituri province in the DRC.

stories.title: Large-scale Ukrainian drone attack kills three in Moscow region, says Russia
stories.summary: A large-scale Ukrainian drone attack killed three people in the Moscow region, according to Russian authorities. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called the strikes a "justified" response to deadly Russian attacks on Ukrainian cities.

stories.title: Air raid alert issued in Kyiv and several regions due to UAVs
stories.summary: An air raid alert was issued across Kyiv and several other Ukrainian regions due to the detection of unmanned aerial vehicles. The alert prompted civilians to seek shelter as air defense systems engaged the threats.

stories.title: Russia stops war only for one reason — and Ukrainians feel betrayed that Europe won’t act on it: Human rights names it
stories.summary: Human rights advocates accused European governments of financing Ukraine's defense while allowing their companies to pay taxes that feed Russia's war budget. They argued Russia only halts military action when faced with decisive force.

stories.title: Drone strike sparks fire on perimeter of UAE’s Barakah nuclear power plant
stories.summary: A drone strike caused a fire on the perimeter of the UAE's Barakah nuclear power plant. Authorities reported that radiation levels remained normal and plant operations were not affected.

stories.title: 46 targets hit in two nights: USF commander showcases work of USF in Russia and occupied territories
stories.summary: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces commander reported striking 46 enemy targets over the nights of May 16 and 17. The targets were located in the temporarily occupied Donetsk, Luhansk, and Zaporizhzhia regions, as well as in occupied Crimea and within Russia itself.

stories.title: Defying predictions, Eurovision juries gave Israel a boost amid voting reforms
stories.summary: At the Eurovision Song Contest, Israel placed second after receiving jury points from 22 of 34 participating countries. For the first time, Israel did not win the "rest of the world" popular vote, but jury scoring under reformed rules boosted its ranking.

stories.title: Will the Trump-class battleship really be able to deter China?
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy outlined a 30-year shipbuilding plan that includes up to 15 Trump-class battleships designed as strike-centric arsenal ships to deter China. Analysts questioned the vessels' vulnerability to anti-ship missiles, their operational costs, and U.S. industrial capacity to build them.

stories.title: Haredi conscription debate threatens long-standing Israeli coalitions - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece examined the growing debate over ultra-Orthodox (Haredi) military conscription in Israel, arguing it threatens long-standing coalition arrangements. The controversy has intensified as Israel's ongoing war strains the military reserve system and coalition stability.

stories.title: SriLankan Airlines accuses Indian employees of ₹22 million fraud
stories.summary: SriLankan Airlines has accused Indian employees of committing fraud amounting to approximately ₹22 million. The airline said Indian law enforcement has been contacted and investigations are underway to recover the losses.

stories.title: Argentine Air Force bought a used aircraft at double its market price, Clarín investigation finds
stories.summary: An investigation by Argentine newspaper Clarín found that the Argentine Air Force purchased an Embraer ERJ-140LR aircraft in 2025 for approximately USD 4.085 million, nearly double the market price. The deal, awarded to U.S. firm Regional One Inc., reportedly contained irregularities in the bidding process, technical evaluation, and payment procedures.

stories.title: As coalition collapses around him, Netanyahu revives Haredi draft exemption bill
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu revived a bill to exempt ultra-Orthodox (Haredi) men from military conscription as his governing coalition faces collapse. A senior Haredi official called the move a delay tactic, while opposition leader Lapid accused Netanyahu of undermining Israel's security.

stories.title: Brazil leads South America's military spending and Uruguay posts one of the largest relative rises, SIPRI says
stories.summary: Brazil led South American military spending in 2025 with a budget of approximately USD 23.9 billion, a 13% year-on-year increase, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute's annual report. Uruguay recorded one of the steepest relative rises in the region, while overall South American military spending grew by 3.4%.

stories.title: Hong Kong ramps up health checks for travellers from Africa after Ebola outbreak
stories.summary: Hong Kong increased health screenings for air passengers arriving from Africa following the WHO's declaration of the Ebola outbreak in the DRC as a public health emergency. Local authorities also announced plans to strengthen public awareness and education about the disease.

stories.title: Abu Dhabi says drone strike caused fire at Barakah Nuclear Power Plant
stories.summary: Abu Dhabi authorities confirmed that a drone strike caused a fire at the Barakah Nuclear Power Plant in the al-Dhafra region. No injuries were reported, and the Federal Authority for Nuclear Regulation said radiological safety levels and essential plant systems were unaffected.

stories.title: How will Izz al-Din al-Haddad assassination impact Hamas’s Gaza operations?
stories.summary: Israel killed Hamas's top commander Izz al-Din al-Haddad in Gaza, testing the existing ceasefire. Hamas pledged to adapt its operations in response to the assassination.

stories.title: Two men killed in Sumy region after drone detonates
stories.summary: Two men were killed in the Putyvl community of Ukraine's Sumy region when a part of a drone they had loaded into a car detonated.

stories.title: Early results in Fatah leadership vote show Abbas’s son, intelligence chief elected
stories.summary: Early results from Fatah's internal leadership elections indicate that Yasser Abbas, son of Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas, and intelligence chief figures have won seats on the party's Central Committee. Former Fatah militant leader Zakaria Zubeidi is also expected to secure a seat.

stories.title: New wave of Israeli strikes pound Lebanon despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Israel carried out a new wave of airstrikes on Lebanon despite a ceasefire agreement being in place between the two sides.

stories.title: Israel unable to destroy Hezbollah's drones with military force, needs political edge - report
stories.summary: A report indicates Israel has been unable to destroy Hezbollah's drone capabilities through military force alone and requires a political solution. The IDF is deploying anti-explosive drone barbed wire and has supplied similar measures to the Lebanese army to mitigate attacks.

stories.title: Shutdown of US’s largest commuter rail system enters second day amid strike
stories.summary: The Long Island Rail Road, North America's largest commuter rail system serving New York City and its eastern suburbs, entered a second day of shutdown on Sunday after unionized workers launched their first strike in three decades. Five unions representing about half the workforce walked off the job just after midnight Friday.

stories.title: Hamas's Gaza military chief broke his own rules, allowing IDF to snuff him out and kill him
stories.summary: Hamas's Gaza military chief Izz ad-Din al-Haddad was killed by Israeli forces after he violated his own security protocols. Israeli security officials said months of tunnel confinement led al-Haddad to expose behavioral patterns that Israeli intelligence exploited to locate him.

stories.title: How worrying is the Ebola outbreak in DR Congo?
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has declared a health emergency over an Ebola outbreak, with almost 250 suspected cases reported. The situation has raised international concern about the scale of the resurgence.

stories.title: Wang Xiaodong, derided over Covid-19 handling, comes under corruption cloud
stories.summary: Wang Xiaodong, the former governor of China's Hubei province who was criticized for his handling of the Covid-19 outbreak in 2020, is under investigation for corruption. China's top disciplinary body said Wang is suspected of "serious violations of discipline and law."

stories.title: Drones set Moscow Oblast fuel and military sites on fire as Russia claims it downed more than 1,000
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone strikes hit a fuel terminal near the village of Durykino in Moscow Oblast and set fire to a technopark in Zelenograd on May 17, 2026. Russia claimed it intercepted more than 1,000 drones during the attacks.

stories.title: Qantas flight diverted after man bites flight attendant
stories.summary: A Qantas flight traveling from Melbourne to Dallas was diverted to Papeete, French Polynesia, after a passenger reportedly bit a flight attendant. Fellow passengers restrained the man, who was handed over to local authorities and banned from all Qantas flights.

stories.title: Malaysian ex-ministers resign from Anwar’s party, snap election rumoured
stories.summary: Former Malaysian ministers Rafizi Ramli and Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad announced they would resign from Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim's ruling coalition party and vacate their parliamentary seats to take over a smaller party. The move could challenge Anwar's government amid speculation of a snap election.

stories.title: UK leadership crisis: ‘Keir Starmer is a lame duck Prime Minister’ says former Labour adviser
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces a leadership crisis after nearly 90 Labour MPs called on him to resign, accompanied by a series of ministerial resignations. Former Health Secretary Wes Streeting announced he would stand in any leadership contest, while Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham confirmed plans to return to Parliament via the Makerfield by-election.

stories.title: Zelensky: Ukraine’s long-range strikes, reaching over 500 kilometers, urge Russia to end war
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Ukraine's long-range strikes, reaching over 500 kilometers to the Moscow region, send a clear message that Russia must end the war. He framed the strikes as pressure on Moscow to pursue peace.

stories.title: Trump admin. urging UAE to seize Iran's Lavan Island, take greater role in war - report
stories.summary: The Trump administration is reportedly urging the United Arab Emirates to seize Iran's Lavan Island and take a greater role in the conflict with Iran. A former senior Trump security official said using UAE forces would avoid putting American troops at risk.

stories.title: Assad official on trial in Syria for abuses denies charges
stories.summary: Atef Najib, a cousin of former Syrian dictator Bashar al-Assad, stood trial in Syria and denied charges related to abuses allegedly committed against protesters in Daraa in March 2011. The trial marks part of broader accountability efforts following Assad's ouster.

stories.title: Hamas looking to exploit Islamic pilgrimage to Mecca in order to smuggle funds to Gaza - report
stories.summary: Hamas is reportedly attempting to exploit the Islamic pilgrimage to Mecca to smuggle funds to Gaza. Sources say the smuggled finances are laundered or redirected through Egypt using various methods before being transferred into the territory.

stories.title: Ukraine drones kill four in Russia, Moscow faces biggest attack in over a year
stories.summary: Ukraine launched a major drone attack on multiple Russian regions, including Moscow, killing at least four people in what officials described as the largest assault on the capital in over a year. Russian air defenses were engaged across the targeted regions.

stories.title: Around 10 'new' victims come forward in France's Epstein investigation
stories.summary: French prosecutors investigating Jeffrey Epstein's alleged trafficking network said around ten previously unidentified suspected victims have recently contacted authorities. The development widens the probe into possible abuse committed in France or involving French accomplices linked to the late financier.

stories.title: A sinking ship? Why the EU and China could be heading for a trade war
stories.summary: Tensions between the European Union and China over trade deepened during a conference in Beijing, where European diplomats raised long-standing complaints about the lopsided trading relationship. Chinese speakers accused the EU of protectionism and bullying, while EU officials warned of further economic confrontation.

stories.title: The Instagram bots of Indonesia and the antisemitism game making Jews feel unsafe online - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece described coordinated campaigns by Indonesian-linked Instagram bot networks targeting Jewish users with antisemitic content. The author argued the attacks aim to make Jewish youth feel unsafe expressing their identity online.

stories.title: Schoolchildren flee Israeli raid in occupied West Bank
stories.summary: Palestinian schoolchildren in the village of Burqa, near Nablus in the occupied West Bank, were forced to flee through the streets after Israeli forces raided and evacuated local schools.

stories.title: Sandu comments on Kremlin’s efforts to simplify issuing of Russian passports to residents of Transnistria
stories.summary: Moldovan President Maia Sandu criticized a decree by Russian President Vladimir Putin simplifying citizenship procedures for residents of Transnistria. Sandu described the move as a tool for mobilizing people for war against Ukraine.

stories.title: Israeli attack kills three in Gaza community kitchen
stories.summary: An Israeli drone strike killed three Palestinians at a community kitchen near al-Aqsa hospital in the Deir al-Balah area of central Gaza, according to Al Jazeera. The attack followed an earlier Israeli strike in Khan Younis in southern Gaza that killed one person on the same day.

stories.title: WHO declares Ebola outbreak in DRC a global health emergency
stories.summary: The World Health Organization declared an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo a public health emergency of international concern. The outbreak, caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain, has killed dozens.

stories.title: Inside Jerusalem’s 1948 siege through the eyes of a child who survived the Old City’s fall
stories.summary: A book titled "Forever My Jerusalem" by Shteiner recounts the 1948 siege of Jerusalem's Old City through the eyes of a child survivor. The memoir describes life before the Old City's fall and the author's emotional return decades later.

stories.title: Iran chief negotiator Ghalibaf appointed to oversee China ties
stories.summary: Iran's chief nuclear negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, who led a single round of high-stakes talks with the United States in April, has been appointed to oversee Iran's relations with China. Ghalibaf has emerged as a central figure in Tehran's diplomatic efforts.

stories.title: Russian forces strike Kryvyi Rih’s transport infrastructure
stories.summary: Russian forces struck transport infrastructure in the Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rih, causing damage. No further details on casualties were immediately provided.

stories.title: China ramps up building a national computing power network as AI token demand surges
stories.summary: China is accelerating construction of a national computing power network intended to function as a public utility for artificial intelligence infrastructure. State media described the project as a "computing version of the state grid," driven by surging demand for AI tokens and telecom operators seeking new revenue sources.

stories.title: Xi-Trump summit: what ‘strategic stability’ means for US-China ties
stories.summary: The summit between Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump in Beijing produced a reference to a "constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability" intended to guide bilateral ties over the next three years. The formulation signals efforts by both sides to manage and stabilize the fraught relationship.

stories.title: Residents of Ugandan capital fearful after Ebola death at local hospital
stories.summary: A Congolese man who died at a hospital in the Ugandan capital tested positive for Ebola, prompting fear among local residents. Ugandan officials confirmed the case of the highly contagious hemorrhagic fever.

stories.title: Who gave Israel the coveted 12 points? Noam Bettan secures 2nd at Eurovision thanks to public vote
stories.summary: Israeli contestant Noam Bettan finished second at the Eurovision Song Contest with strong public support, receiving 220 points from the televote. The result came despite widespread boycott calls over Israel's participation, which led several countries to withdraw from the competition.

stories.title: Daily Briefing May 17: Pro-Israel groups protest NYT sexual abuse op-ed, say it foments hatred
stories.summary: Pro-Israel groups held a protest outside the New York Times offices over a sexual abuse op-ed they say foments hatred. Separately, the New School attempted to defund its Hillel chapter, and anti-Israel demonstrations took place in a Jewish neighborhood in New York City, where swastikas were also reported.

stories.title: ICC denies ‘inaccurate’ report it issued warrants for Smotrich and Ben Gvir
stories.summary: The International Criminal Court denied reports that it had issued arrest warrants for Israeli ministers Bezalel Smotrich and Itamar Ben Gvir, calling the reports inaccurate. Haaretz had reported that three additional warrants were issued for unnamed Israeli political and military officials, and that the court had previously sought the ministers' arrest over West Bank settlement activity.

stories.title: Why does the PLA object to Japan’s drone plans for its southern islands?
stories.summary: China's People's Liberation Army accused Japan of making a "dangerous gamble" by planning to deploy satellite-aided drones to its southwestern islands near Taiwan. The PLA Daily characterized Japan's stated coastal defense system as having a "distinct offensive nature," calling the equipment a "spear" disguised as a "shield."

stories.title: Thames Water investors say temporary nationalisation would slow its recovery
stories.summary: Investors in Thames Water have warned the UK Labour government that temporarily nationalising the struggling utility company would hinder its recovery. The statement follows Greater Manchester mayor Andy Burnham's proposal to renationalise water and energy companies as part of his policy platform should he become prime minister.

stories.title: Russians shell settlements in Donetsk region 12 times; one person killed
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled settlements in Ukraine's Donetsk region 12 times over a 24-hour period on May 16, killing one man. The attacks targeted multiple locations across the region.

stories.title: Ukraine drone attack kills at least three in Moscow region, Governor says
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone attack killed at least three people in the Moscow region, according to the regional governor. Russia's Defence Ministry reported that 556 drones were intercepted over the country, including the Moscow region, overnight and into the morning.

stories.title: Israel comes second at Eurovision amid boycotts and backlash
stories.summary: Bulgaria won the Eurovision Song Contest, with Israel finishing in second place. The competition was marked by boycotts and protests related to Israel's war on Gaza.

stories.title: Drone targets UAE nuclear power plant, straining Iran war ceasefire
stories.summary: A drone strike targeted the Barakah nuclear power plant in the United Arab Emirates, igniting a fire at an electrical generator on its perimeter. No injuries or radiological release occurred, but the attack strained the fragile ceasefire in the broader Iran conflict, with suspicion falling on Iran.

stories.title: Drone strike causes fire at Abu Dhabi nuclear power plant
stories.summary: A drone strike caused a fire at an electrical generator at the Barakah Nuclear Energy Plant in the al-Dhafra region of Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. Emirati authorities reported no injuries and said radiological safety levels were unaffected by the incident.

stories.title: Philippines asks top court to allow ICC drug war arrest of senator
stories.summary: The Philippine government has asked its Supreme Court to allow the International Criminal Court to execute an arrest warrant against Senator Ronald Dela Rosa. The ICC accuses Dela Rosa, along with former President Duterte and other co-perpetrators, of the crime against humanity of murder in connection with the Philippines' drug war.

stories.title: Experts sound alarm as North America’s bees start swarm season unusually early
stories.summary: The 2026 bee swarm season in North America has begun 17 days earlier than the previous year, according to a report by the Swarmed tracking network of over 10,000 beekeepers. Experts attribute the shift to a warm winter and record-breaking heatwaves, raising concerns about how honeybees are responding to climate change.

stories.title: October 7 Massacre conference to be held in Toronto by branch of banned terror group
stories.summary: A conference described as an "October 7 Massacre conference" is scheduled to be held in Toronto by an organization linked to the Samidoun network, which was designated as a terrorist front by both the United States and Canada in 2024.

stories.title: Milking it: New figures show Israelis consuming more dairy products and alternatives
stories.summary: Israel's Agriculture Ministry released new figures ahead of the Shavuot holiday showing increased Israeli consumption of dairy products and dairy alternatives. The data was published following a Knesset Committee decision to expand the powers of Israel's Dairy Council, a move opposed by the Treasury.

stories.title: ICC issues secret arrest warrants against several Israeli politicians, military officials - report
stories.summary: The International Criminal Court has reportedly issued secret arrest warrants targeting three Israeli politicians and two military officials. The exact timing of when the warrants were issued remains unclear.

stories.title: Ukrenergo: No power outages today
stories.summary: Ukraine's national grid operator Ukrenergo announced that no electricity consumption restrictions are planned for Sunday, May 17. No power outages are expected across the country.

stories.title: Pete Hegseth welcomes USS Gerald R. Ford home after record deployment
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth welcomed the USS Gerald R. Ford home following its record-length deployment. Hegseth presented the crew with the Presidential Unit Citation, the highest collective honor a U.S. military unit can receive.

stories.title: Zelensky: 52 people killed and 346 others injured in Ukraine over past week due to Russian shelling
stories.summary: President Zelensky reported that 52 people were killed and 346 injured across Ukraine over the past week due to Russian shelling. Russia launched more than 3,170 attack drones, over 1,300 guided bombs, and 74 missiles — mostly ballistic — during that period.

stories.title: KP govt withdraws orders for early market closure
stories.summary: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government withdrew its orders for early market and business closure on Saturday, roughly six weeks after imposing them due to rising oil prices linked to the US-Iran war. The chief secretary's office suspended the prescribed closure timings until further notice but urged continued electricity conservation.

stories.title: What the Left can learn from settlers- Shannie Reichman - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A discussion featuring Shannie Reichman explored how Israel's political center and left could adopt lessons from the settler movement's long-term strategic vision and persistence. The conversation examined rethinking political approaches in the Israeli context.

stories.title: Netanyahu abandoned Israel's security for personal deals with Trump, Liberman claims - interview
stories.summary: Former Israeli Defense Minister Avigdor Liberman accused Prime Minister Netanyahu of abandoning Israel's security in favor of personal deals with U.S. President Trump. Liberman alleged Netanyahu is prioritizing personal legal interests over national security and ruled out any future coalition with ultra-Orthodox parties.

stories.title: Massive explosion in Beit Shemesh area was coordinated test with defense company, officials say
stories.summary: A massive explosion in the Beit Shemesh area of Israel was confirmed by officials to be a coordinated test conducted with a defense company. Speculation had circulated that the blast may have destroyed a stockpile of Arrow-3 surface-to-air missiles.

stories.title: Masada: The Making of a Myth - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A sponsored discussion explored how the ancient account of mass suicide at Masada evolved into a foundational narrative of Israeli national identity. The piece examines the historical and cultural forces that transformed the story into a national symbol.

stories.title: What’s so funny about antisemitism? with Raanan Hershberg - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Comedian Raanan Hershberg discussed the state of Jewish comedy in America amid rising antisemitism and growing divisions over Israel. The conversation explored whether Jewish comedians can continue to thrive in an increasingly hostile environment.

stories.title: WHO declares Ebola outbreak in DRC, Uganda a global emergency: What to know
stories.summary: The World Health Organization declared the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda a public health emergency of international concern. The outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo virus, has resulted in more than 80 deaths and over 246 suspected cases in DRC's Ituri province, with neighboring countries at high risk of further spread.

stories.title: Iran regime 'incapable of change' post-war, expert says
stories.summary: Analyst Khosro Isfahani assessed that Iran's regime is "incapable of change" in the post-war period. He examined the country's divided opposition, the IRGC's tightening grip on power, and the extent of Tehran's influence networks abroad.

stories.title: Israel planning to seize up to 20 properties in East Jerusalem
stories.summary: Israel is planning to seize up to 20 properties in occupied East Jerusalem. The Palestinian governorate warned that the move is part of an effort to further "Judaise" the Old City and displace Palestinian residents.

stories.title: Iraq exported 10 million barrels of oil through Hormuz in April
stories.summary: Iraq exported 10 million barrels of oil through the Strait of Hormuz in April. Iraq's oil minister said the country plans to engage with OPEC to increase its overall production and export capacity.

stories.title: Hung Shui Kiu industrial park operator eyes bond issuance, tax cuts for firms
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Hung Shui Kiu industrial park operator, chaired by industrialist Jeffrey Lam Kin-fung, plans to issue bonds to finance operations and propose tax concessions to attract enterprises. Lam is set to begin his three-year term on June 1 leading the government-owned development entity.

stories.title: Hamas leadership elections end without political leader selection, promises future vote
stories.summary: Hamas concluded its internal leadership elections without selecting a new political leader, promising a future vote. Khaled Mashal and Khalil al-Hayya are viewed as the leading contenders for the political chief position.

stories.title: Mass Ukraine Drone Barrage Kills 3 in Moscow Region
stories.summary: A massive Ukrainian drone barrage killed three people in Russia's Moscow region. Russian air defenses intercepted 556 drones across more than a dozen regions in one of the largest Ukrainian drone attacks of the conflict to date.

stories.title: ‘We’re not ready’: US lags on pandemic preparedness after Covid, experts say
stories.summary: A hantavirus outbreak in the United States has highlighted ongoing weaknesses in public health preparedness, including reduced funding, limited testing capacity for rare diseases, and growing misinformation. Experts, including former White House global health official Stephanie Psaki, warn that the country remains inadequately prepared for future pandemics despite lessons from Covid.

stories.title: Russia lures Yemenis with cash incentives to fight against Ukraine
stories.summary: Russia is recruiting Yemeni nationals with cash incentives and promises of Russian citizenship to fight on the front lines against Ukraine. While some Yemenis were reportedly deceived into joining, many have knowingly enlisted, drawn by high salaries.

stories.title: China’s motorsports industry continues to rev up with country’s first race-grade fuel
stories.summary: China debuted its first domestically developed race-grade fuel at a rally in the country's western deserts. State broadcaster CCTV described the mass-produced fuel as filling a gap in the domestic market and ending reliance on imported fuel for high-level motorsport competitions.

stories.title: Hong Kong High Court to hear Evergrande liquidators’ lawsuit against PwC on Monday
stories.summary: Liquidators of China Evergrande Group are set to have their lawsuit against PricewaterhouseCoopers International heard in Hong Kong's High Court. The case, scheduled before Deputy Judge Patrick Fung Pak-tung, involves claims related to PwC's auditing of the collapsed property developer.

stories.title: Culture secretary says Streeting’s call for UK to rejoin EU is ‘odd’
stories.summary: UK Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy criticised former Health Secretary Wes Streeting's call for Britain to rejoin the European Union, calling the proposal "odd." Nandy told the BBC that Streeting's comments risked reopening a debate she considers settled by the Brexit referendum held a decade ago.

stories.title: At UN, India flags concerns over targeting of vessels in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: India's representative Harish raised concerns at a UN Economic and Social Council special meeting about the targeting of vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. The remarks followed a recent attack on an India-flagged commercial vessel off the coast of Oman, amid broader disruptions to energy and supply flows in the region.

stories.title: ISPR takes exception after Indian army chief says Pakistan should decide between being 'part of geography' or not
stories.summary: Pakistan's Inter-Services Public Relations directorate responded to Indian Army Chief Gen Upendra Dwivedi's remarks suggesting Pakistan should decide whether to remain "part of geography." ISPR called the statement provocative and warned India against pushing South Asia toward a conflict with devastating regional consequences.

stories.title: Israel booed at Eurovision final as Bulgaria wins competition
stories.summary: Bulgaria won the Eurovision Song Contest final held in Vienna, Austria, with singer Darina Nikolaeva Yotova performing the song "Bangaranga." Israel finished in second place and was booed during the event, which was widely boycotted over the war in Gaza.

stories.title: IDF tests Jordan Valley readiness in Dead Sea surprise attack drill - analysis
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces conducted a major surprise attack drill near the Dead Sea to test readiness along the Jordan Valley's eastern border. The exercise simulated infiltrations, drone threats, and incidents in civilian areas.

stories.title: Seven people injured in Kharkiv region due to Russian shelling
stories.summary: Russian troops attacked 15 settlements in Ukraine's Kharkiv region over a 24-hour period on May 16, injuring seven people. The shelling targeted multiple communities across the region.

stories.title: Rafael's Spike missile successfully fired from German unmanned ground vehicle
