stories.summary: Ukrainian drone forces destroyed a Russian Tor-M2 air defense system in Luhansk Oblast and a Pantsir-S1 in Crimea. They also struck a ship in Berdyansk and destroyed a Be-200 aircraft and Ka-27 helicopter at Russia's Yeysk base.

stories.title: Hong Kong police call to criminalise bid-rigging in wake of Tai Po estate blaze
stories.summary: Hong Kong police have proposed legislation to criminalise bid-rigging, enforced by a designated agency, following the deadly fire at Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po last November. The proposal, submitted to an independent inquiry, also recommends enhanced leniency agreements for whistle-blowers, citing shortcomings in the current civil competition regime.

stories.title: Erling Haaland to make film acting debut – as a Viking called Haaland
stories.summary: Manchester City striker Erling Haaland will make his feature acting debut voicing a Viking character named Haaland in the animated film Viqueens. The film is directed by Dutch-Norwegian filmmaker Harald Zwart, known for The Karate Kid.

stories.title: ‘May do it. May not do it’: Trump keeps up suspense over arms to Taiwan, says no to war
stories.summary: President Donald Trump declared the United States will not go to war over Taiwan, while revealing he and Chinese President Xi Jinping discussed Taiwan extensively during his state visit to Beijing. Trump declined to confirm future arms sales to Taiwan, leaving the status of major pending arms packages uncertain.

stories.title: Palestinian Prisoners Club: over 23,000 arrested in occupied West Bank since start of Israel's genocide
stories.summary: The Palestinian Prisoners Club reported that Israel has arrested over 23,000 Palestinians in the occupied West Bank since the start of the war in Gaza, according to Wafa news agency. The figure excludes thousands more arrested in Gaza during the same period.

stories.title: Angus Taylor says migrants are a ‘net drain’ on Australia. The numbers say the opposite is true
stories.summary: Australian opposition leader Angus Taylor characterized migrants as a "net drain" on Australia. Analysis of available data indicates the opposite, showing migrants are generally younger, more skilled, and more educated than the average Australian, typically paying more in taxes than they receive in government services.

stories.title: Secret documents reveal preferred Australian nuclear submarine base – and warn it could be a military target
stories.summary: Previously secret New South Wales government documents identify Port Kembla, 75 kilometers south of Sydney, as the preferred east coast base for Australia's proposed nuclear submarine fleet under the AUKUS agreement. The documents warn the base could become a target for military adversaries and anticipate local resistance over nuclear accident risks.

stories.title: Russian troops refuse to cross Dnipro River in Prydniprovske sector, says Voloshyn
stories.summary: Ukrainian spokesperson Voloshyn reported that Russian troops resumed operations near the Antonivskyi Bridge in the Prydniprovske sector after regrouping, but assault units are refusing orders to cross the Dnipro River channels and land on the islands.

stories.title: Trump says he discussed Taiwan arms sale with China’s Xi Jinping
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump confirmed he discussed American arms sales to Taiwan during talks with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, though specifics of the exchange were not disclosed.

stories.title: Mali’s forces target rebel alliance in junta’s fight to keep power
stories.summary: Mali's armed forces, supported by Russian mercenaries, launched airstrikes against a rebel alliance comprising Islamist extremists and Tuareg separatists. The strikes targeted the northern town of Kidal, which rebels seized during a surprise offensive across much of Mali in late April, as the ruling military junta fights to maintain control.

stories.title: Civilians caught in war of drones in eastern DR Congo
stories.summary: In eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, ongoing fighting has taken a new turn as civilians are being struck by drone attacks far from front lines, even as peace talks continue.

stories.title: Israeli and Lebanese diplomats arrived at US Department of State for ceasefire negotiations
stories.summary: Israeli and Lebanese delegations arrived at the US Department of State for a second day of ceasefire negotiations ahead of the expected expiration of the Lebanon ceasefire agreement. Lebanon's Health Ministry reports Israeli attacks have killed over 657 people in Lebanon since the truce began.

stories.title: From destroyers to drones, how a Europe-led coalition aims to open the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: A European coalition led by the United Kingdom and France is planning an operation to secure the Strait of Hormuz, potentially involving up to 40 nations. The initiative, combining destroyers and drones, would only begin after a ceasefire is declared in the region.

stories.title: Russia already fights with significant shortage of manpower, says Hnatov
stories.summary: Ukrainian official Hnatov stated that the Russian army is conducting combat operations in Ukraine while facing a significant shortage of manpower on the battlefield.

stories.title: Far-right activists barred from UK before Tommy Robinson rally
stories.summary: Eleven foreign far-right activists were blocked from entering the UK ahead of a rally organized by Tommy Robinson supporters. Prime Minister Keir Starmer accused Robinson of "peddling hatred and division," while the Archbishop of Canterbury urged people to "choose hope" before the Saturday demonstration.

stories.title: India ready to extend all possible support for peace in West Asia: PM Modi in UAE
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, speaking during a visit to the UAE, condemned recent attacks on the Emirates and offered India's support for peace in West Asia. Modi made the remarks during a meeting with the UAE's leader.

stories.title: 9 terrorists killed, 4 security personnel martyred as attack on army camp in Bajaur repulsed: sources
stories.summary: Security forces in Pakistan's Bajaur district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, repulsed an attack on an army camp by Fitna-al-Khawarij militants linked to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan. Nine attackers were killed, while four Pakistani security personnel died in the engagement.

stories.title: UAE accelerates pipeline project to bypass Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced it will accelerate construction of a West-East oil pipeline to double the export capacity of Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC). The pipeline, expected to be operational by 2027, is designed to allow the UAE to bypass the Strait of Hormuz for oil exports.

stories.title: Araghchi: Iran doubts US ‘seriousness’ about talks amid nuclear deadlock
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi expressed distrust toward the United States regarding war negotiations during a BRICS meeting in India, citing doubts about Washington's seriousness in pursuing diplomatic talks.

stories.title: Putin Expected to Visit China Next Week, Reports Say
stories.summary: The Kremlin confirmed preparations are underway for President Vladimir Putin to visit China, with reports indicating the trip could take place as soon as next week. A specific date has not yet been announced.

stories.title: Egypt's farmers hit by Iran war price surge
stories.summary: Egyptian smallholder farmers have been severely affected by the Iran war, as soaring fertilizer prices have forced many to lay off workers and reduce the amount of land under cultivation.

stories.title: UAE tried to coordinate with Saudi Arabia, Qatar to strike Iran during recent war - report
stories.summary: The UAE attempted to persuade Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and other Gulf states to coordinate a military response to Iranian missile and drone attacks during the recent war, according to Bloomberg sources. The neighboring countries refused to participate in the proposed joint action.

stories.title: Nakba: Jewish voices are challenging the stories Israel tells about itself
stories.summary: A film director, historian, and Holocaust survivor spoke to Al Jazeera about shifting perspectives among Jewish voices regarding the narratives Israel tells about its own history, tied to the anniversary of the Nakba.

stories.title: India and UAE sign defence and energy deals during Modi's state visit
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi signed defense and energy agreements with the UAE during a state visit to Abu Dhabi. The deals were concluded amid rising economic pressures on India linked to the US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: Hungary’s Power Shift Opens Door for EU Sanctions on Israel
stories.summary: With a recent shift in Hungary's political stance removing Viktor Orbán's previous veto power, the European Union may now have an opening to expand sanctions against Israel over its activities in the West Bank.

stories.title: Israeli forces kill Palestinian teen, settlers set mosque ablaze
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed a Palestinian teenager in the occupied West Bank, while settlers set a mosque ablaze in a separate incident. The arson was part of a series of settler attacks reportedly carried out under Israeli police protection.

stories.title: Peugeot, Jeep take on Chinese rivals with new models using local EV technologies
stories.summary: Stellantis, the parent company of Peugeot and Jeep, announced new investments to produce four electric vehicles with Chinese partner Dongfeng Motor, with production set to begin in 2027. The move leverages Chinese EV technologies to compete with domestic Chinese automakers in the world's largest car market.

stories.title: Russians intensify artillery fire in south and increase ammunition use, says Voloshyn
stories.summary: Ukrainian spokesperson Voloshyn reported that Russian forces on the southern front have significantly intensified artillery fire and increased ammunition expenditure to support ongoing assault operations.

stories.title: Pakistan faces pressure over mediator role in Iran war
stories.summary: Pakistan faces growing pressure over its role as a mediator in the Iran conflict, balancing relationships with the United States, Iran, China, and Gulf allies. A recent US media report has placed Islamabad under additional scrutiny.

stories.title: Antisemitic comments flood posts celebrating Jewish American Heritage Month
stories.summary: The Blue Square Alliance reported that antisemitic comments have flooded social media posts celebrating Jewish American Heritage Month, including apolitical tributes from organizations like Sesame Street and the Grammys. The group warned the backlash is deterring organizations from recognizing Jewish contributions.

stories.title: Trump says he 'made no commitment either way' to Xi on Taiwan
stories.summary: President Trump stated he made "no commitment either way" to Chinese leader Xi Jinping regarding whether the US would defend Taiwan. Trump said Xi had asked directly, and he responded that he does not discuss that topic.

stories.title: 'The settlers are in control': How the West Bank is being ethnically cleansed
stories.summary: Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank, backed by Israel's far-right government, have intensified actions against Palestinian communities. Travel between cities like Ramallah and Nablus, normally an hour-long journey, now takes much longer due to increased Israeli checkpoints.

stories.title: Israeli-born Dutch politician calls for violence worse than Gaza against Palestinians
stories.summary: Dutch far-right lawmaker Gidi Markuszower, who is Israeli-born, called for the use of force against Palestinians seeking asylum in the Netherlands. He suggested they should face harsher treatment than what they experienced in Gaza.

stories.title: North Korea slams U.K. over sanctions on children's camp
stories.summary: North Korea criticized the United Kingdom over sanctions related to a children's camp. The issue is connected to broader concerns about Ukrainian children from Russian-occupied territories being subjected to political indoctrination since Russia's 2022 invasion.

stories.title: Hantavirus outbreak tests post-COVID health communications playbook
stories.summary: A hantavirus outbreak has raised public health concerns after a cruise ship was placed in quarantine at sea. Several people have died and additional cases have been reported. The incident is testing health communication strategies developed in the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic.

stories.title: Rapid-fire to restrained: China state visit reveals a changed Trump on social media
stories.summary: During his state visit to China, President Donald Trump adopted an unusually restrained social media presence, posting only about 10 updates since arriving in Beijing. His posts mostly featured arrival footage and official greetings, along with praise for Chinese President Xi Jinping as "one of the World's Great Leaders."

stories.title: Pressure mounts on embattled UK PM Keir Starmer as rivals circle
stories.summary: UK Health Secretary Wes Streeting, seen as a rival to Prime Minister Keir Starmer, publicly backed Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham as a strong potential challenger to Starmer's leadership.

stories.title: War worsens Lebanon's economic crisis with job losses, slow business, soaring prices
stories.summary: Lebanon's economic crisis has worsened due to the 2024 war between Israel and Hezbollah, which caused an estimated $11 billion in damage. The World Bank reported that the country had already suffered approximately $70 billion in financial sector losses prior to the conflict.

stories.title: Pro-Israel protests at NYT over Palestinian detainees report
stories.summary: Pro-Israel demonstrators gathered outside the New York Times headquarters in New York City to protest a published report detailing allegations of abuse against Palestinian detainees held by Israeli forces.

stories.title: Israel strikes towns near Tyre, Southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli forces launched air strikes near Hiram Hospital and residential areas on the outskirts of Tyre in southern Lebanon. An Israeli military spokesperson also announced new displacement orders for four additional villages in southern Lebanon, despite an ongoing ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Is Europe getting its act together on defence? Multiple threats prompt EU rearmament
stories.summary: The European Union is advancing its Readiness 2030 defense plan, originally called ReArmEU, to significantly boost military capacities. European intelligence agencies have warned the bloc could face a major conflict by 2030, prompting accelerated rearmament efforts.

stories.title: Drones to fight school shooters? One US company says yes
stories.summary: A U.S. company is developing drones designed to respond to school shootings. The drones do not fire bullets or any other projectiles.

stories.title: Two killed as heavy rains batter Sri Lanka; thousands affected
stories.summary: Heavy rains in Sri Lanka killed at least two people and affected more than 4,000 others. Authorities placed over 100 people from 29 families in two temporary relief centers.

stories.title: Russia deploys 320 soldiers to assault units of 5th Army following losses near Huliaipole, says Voloshyn
stories.summary: Russia deployed 320 soldiers from rear areas in the Russian Federation to the Rostov region to reinforce assault units of the 5th Army, which suffered losses in fighting near Huliaipole, according to Ukrainian spokesperson Voloshyn.

stories.title: Lebanese deeply divided over chances of peace talks with Israel
stories.summary: Lebanese public opinion is deeply divided over the prospects of peace talks with Israel. A third round of direct negotiations is taking place in the United States while fighting continues in southern Lebanon despite an existing truce.

stories.title: Russian Dissident Nina Litvinova Dies by Suicide at 80
stories.summary: Russian dissident Nina Litvinova died by suicide at the age of 80. In a note shared by her cousin, Litvinova wrote that life had become unbearable since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: Trump, Xi weigh AI ‘guardrails’ as Nvidia chip exports hang in the balance
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese officials discussed artificial intelligence "guardrails" and the status of Nvidia H200 chip exports during Trump's state visit to Beijing. Trump said both sides talked about possibly working together on AI safeguards.

stories.title: Ukraine war: 36 nations approve tribunal creation to prosecute Russia over invasion
stories.summary: Thirty-six parties—including 34 European states, Australia, Costa Rica, and the EU—approved joining a future special tribunal to prosecute Russia for its invasion of Ukraine. The tribunal is based on an accord signed between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and the Council of Europe.

stories.title: 78 years later: Palestinians are still denied their right to return.
stories.summary: The article marks 78 years since approximately 800,000 Palestinians were displaced during the events of 1948. Their descendants remain refugees, and their right to return has not been fulfilled.

stories.title: Spain's Sanchez slams Israeli minister for attack on Yamal over Palestinian flag
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez defended FC Barcelona star Lamine Yamal after Israel's defense minister accused the 18-year-old of inciting hatred for waving a Palestinian flag during a victory parade. Sanchez said he was proud of the player.

stories.title: Ukrainian flag flies again over Odradne, six months after Russia overran the village
stories.summary: Ukraine's 129th Brigade recaptured the village of Odradne in Kharkiv Oblast's Kupiansk sector, pushing Russian forces from fortified positions, treelines, and strongpoints roughly six months after Russia had overrun the settlement.

stories.title: Nigeria: Gunmen Invade Oyo School, Abduct Principal, Students
stories.summary: Gunmen attacked a school in the Ahoro-Esinele community in Oriire Local Government Area of Oyo State, Nigeria, abducting the school's principal and an unspecified number of students during a morning raid.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia pushes for regional non-aggression pact with Iran
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia is promoting a regional non-aggression pact with Iran, modeled on the 1970s détente between the West and the Soviet Union. European countries are backing Riyadh's proposal for a broad understanding with Tehran.

stories.title: Nigeria: 2027 - Daniel Challenges Abiodun to Live Debate Over Ogun East Ticket
stories.summary: Former Ogun State governor and current senator Gbenga Daniel challenged Governor Dapo Abiodun to a live television debate over the Ogun East senatorial ticket ahead of Nigeria's 2027 elections.

stories.title: Nigeria: Alleged N36m Fraud - EFCC Arraigns Blessing CEO in Lagos
stories.summary: Nigeria's Economic and Financial Crimes Commission arraigned social media figure Blessing CEO in Lagos over alleged fraud amounting to 36 million naira.

stories.title: Kenya: Matatu Operators Announce 50 Percent Fare Hike, Threaten Nationwide Strike Over Fuel Price Shock
stories.summary: Matatu operators in Kenya announced plans to raise fares by up to 50 percent following a sudden rise in fuel prices and threatened a nationwide strike starting Monday unless the government intervenes to address rising operating costs.

stories.title: Trump-Xi summit: China, US disagree on what they agreed on
stories.summary: Following the Trump-Xi summit, the US highlighted trade deals while China said it warned Washington over Taiwan. Neither side confirmed the other's version of what was agreed upon.

stories.title: What was actually achieved at Trump and Xi’s ‘stalemate summit’ in Beijing?
stories.summary: President Trump's state visit to Beijing—the first U.S. presidential visit to China in nearly a decade—concluded with Trump claiming he and President Xi Jinping "settled a lot of different problems." However, Trump provided little detail on specific outcomes or agreements reached during the talks.

stories.title: Iran has 'no trust' in the US, will negotiate only if it is serious, Araghchi says
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated in New Delhi that Iran has no trust in the United States but is willing to negotiate if Washington demonstrates seriousness. He said Iran is maintaining the ceasefire to give diplomacy an opportunity, while attending the BRICS foreign ministers' meeting.

stories.title: From Nakba to genocide: A Gaza grandmother’s lifetime of loss and resilience
stories.summary: Fatema Obaid, a 95-year-old Palestinian grandmother who survived the 1948 Nakba, has endured Israeli bombardment in Gaza and the loss of 70 family members. She refused to leave Gaza City when ordered to do so by the Israeli military during the conflict that began in 2023.

stories.title: China’s Xi Jinping to pay first state visit to US in more than a decade
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected to pay a state visit to the United States in September, the first such visit in over a decade. U.S. President Donald Trump said after departing Beijing that he and Xi plan to meet three more times this year, including at the APEC summit.

stories.title: Weaponizing the Westerlies: Ukrainian balloons sow havoc over Russia
stories.summary: Ukraine is increasingly deploying aerostats carried by westerly winds to conduct strikes and gather intelligence over Russian territory. The balloon operations also force Russia to expend air-defense resources intercepting them.

stories.title: Defense Forces regain control over Odradne in Kharkiv region
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Forces regained control of the village of Odradne and its surrounding areas in Kharkiv Oblast, reclaiming territory previously held by Russian forces.

stories.title: UK government faces weeks of uncertainty over the prime minister's future
stories.summary: The UK government faces prolonged uncertainty after internal Labour Party maneuvering failed to oust Prime Minister Keir Starmer but triggered a leadership contest that could extend into the summer. One Cabinet member resigned and dozens of lawmakers called for Starmer to step down.

stories.title: Here’s how the Army plans to spend nearly $1 billion in procuring small counter drone tech
stories.summary: The US Army's fiscal year 2027 budget request allocates approximately $994 million in discretionary funding for the procurement of small counter-drone technology, reflecting growing Pentagon investment in counter-UAS capabilities.

stories.title: Trump's silence on Taiwan during summit with Xi comes as relief for island nation
stories.summary: During his state visit to China, U.S. President Donald Trump remained silent on Taiwan while Chinese President Xi Jinping warned that mishandling the issue could lead to conflict. Analysts in Taiwan interpreted Trump's silence as a sign the U.S. would maintain its longstanding policy.

stories.title: IDF chief Zamir is latest top Israeli official said to have visited UAE amid Iran war
stories.summary: IDF Chief Zamir reportedly visited the UAE during the Iran war, adding to a series of disclosed high-level Israeli visits to the Gulf state. US officials previously confirmed that Israel provided the UAE with Iron Dome defense systems during the conflict, though the UAE has denied the reported visits.

stories.title: Indian magnate Adani agrees to multi-million-dollar penalty in US court case
stories.summary: Indian billionaire Gautam Adani agreed to pay a multi-million-dollar civil settlement in a U.S. court case linked to an alleged $250 million bribery scheme involving Indian solar energy contracts. Adani and his nephew Sagar Adani did not admit guilt as part of the agreement.

stories.title: Dakar Eilat: Inside prisons for Hamas terrorists
stories.summary: A former Israeli prison commander responded to New York Times allegations of sexual abuse of Palestinian detainees, offering his perspective on prisoner treatment and oversight mechanisms within the prison system.

stories.title: The Rubble Doctrine: Inside Israel's new security policy in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel's military has adopted what has been described as a "Rubble Doctrine" in southern Lebanon, exemplified by the destruction of El-Khiam. The approach reflects a shift in Israeli security thinking after October 7, aimed at denying adversaries the physical capability to launch attacks.

stories.title: Funeral in Jabalia after Israeli strike hits Gaza wake despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Residents of Jabalia in northern Gaza buried two Palestinians killed in an Israeli strike that hit a wake, despite the ceasefire. Gaza authorities report nearly 73,000 total deaths, with ongoing truce violations.

stories.title: US-China summit exposes Trump's limits on Iran war, Taiwan
stories.summary: During a two-day US-China summit in Beijing, President Trump sought Chinese cooperation to help end the war in Iran, but no guarantees were secured. President Xi Jinping used the meeting to warn the United States over Taiwan.

stories.title: Israeli activists protest at New York Times building after article exposes rape of Palestinians
stories.summary: Pro-Israel activists protested outside the New York Times headquarters after the newspaper published an article by journalist Nicholas Kristof detailing allegations of Israeli soldiers raping Palestinian prisoners. Israel's government vowed to sue the paper and the journalist.

stories.title: Philippines vows to hand fugitive senator to ICC following shootout
stories.summary: The Philippine government announced it would surrender Senator Ronald 'Bato' dela Rosa to the International Criminal Court. Dela Rosa is wanted for his alleged role as a key enforcer of former President Rodrigo Duterte's deadly anti-drug campaign. The decision followed a recent shootout incident.

stories.title: SSU releases exclusive footage of today’s prisoner exchange
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service released footage of the May 15 prisoner exchange in which Ukrainian captives returned home after being freed from Russian custody.

stories.title: Palestine Action prisoner with muscular dystrophy says he is forced to 'crawl like a wounded dog'
stories.summary: Muhammad Umer Khalid, a Palestine Action member with muscular dystrophy, was denied bail despite medical evidence that his condition deteriorated during detention. He is held on remand in connection with charges related to a break-in at RAF Brize Norton in the UK.

stories.title: Tories suspend leader at Worcestershire council after he made deal to oust Reform
stories.summary: The Conservative Party suspended its leader at Worcestershire county council, Adam Kent, after he struck a deal with the Greens and Liberal Democrats to oust Reform UK from minority control of the council.

stories.title: A billionaire, a taco, reality TV: the top 4 attack lines in California’s elections
stories.summary: California's gubernatorial and mayoral primary races are intensifying less than three weeks before the primary election, with candidates engaging in sharp debates and social media exchanges.

stories.title: Iran allowing more ships through Strait of Hormuz, report says
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards have begun allowing more ships to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iranian state television. Tehran had largely blocked shipping through the strategic waterway following US-Israeli strikes since the outbreak of war on February 28.

stories.title: Is the Met favouring Tommy Robinson over the peaceful Nakba marchers?
stories.summary: Questions arose about London's Metropolitan Police treatment of pro-Palestinian Nakba marchers compared to far-right activist Tommy Robinson. Critics alleged that Palestinian voices were being marginalized while xenophobic figures received more favorable treatment from authorities.

stories.title: Russia presses college students to fill ranks of drone pilots
stories.summary: Russia's military is recruiting college students to serve as drone pilots, targeting a demographic that had previously been largely shielded from frontline combat roles in the war effort.

stories.title: Russia presses college students to fill ranks of drone pilots
stories.summary: Russia's military is recruiting college students to serve as drone pilots, targeting a demographic that had previously been largely shielded from frontline conscription. The effort reflects the military's growing need to fill specialized roles amid ongoing combat operations.

stories.title: How the fall of Starmer will reshape British policy on Israel
stories.summary: The leadership contest to succeed outgoing British Prime Minister Keir Starmer is expected to bring Israel's actions in Gaza and the occupied West Bank into focus. Starmer's handling of the Gaza conflict is anticipated to become a major issue once the contest formally begins.

stories.title: Deadly attack on Pakistan outpost puts Afghanistan ceasefire at risk
stories.summary: Two attacks on Pakistani military outposts in the country's northwest region killed more than 20 people in recent days. The violence threatens to undermine a ceasefire arrangement between Pakistan and Afghanistan along their shared border.

stories.title: Prisoner swap goes ahead as Kyiv mourns 24 killed in Russian strike on flats
stories.summary: A prisoner swap between Ukraine and Russia proceeded on May 15 while Kyiv mourned 24 people killed in a Russian missile strike on a residential building. Among the victims was 12-year-old Lyubava Yakovleva, whose father had also been killed during the war.

stories.title: Rapprochement, debates, dissidents: US presidential visits to China
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump's summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing was the latest in a decades-long history of high-level diplomatic encounters between the two countries. Past presidential visits to China include Richard Nixon's groundbreaking 1972 trip to meet Chairman Mao Zedong.

stories.title: Finland says Helsinki drone threat has ended, reopens airport
stories.summary: Finland reopened Helsinki Airport after its defense forces declared that a drone threat in the area had ended. Fighter jets and emergency services had been scrambled in response to the earlier threat. Authorities did not immediately identify the source of the drone activity.

stories.title: Israeli settler attacks activist during tour on settler violence
stories.summary: A group of Israeli settlers physically attacked Israeli human rights activists during a tour focused on settler violence in the occupied West Bank. The incident occurred while the activists were documenting conditions in the territory.

stories.title: Trump leaves China without breakthroughs on Iran, Taiwan or AI
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump left China after a two-day summit with President Xi Jinping that featured extensive pageantry but produced few concrete breakthroughs on Iran, Taiwan, or AI. Details of announced trade deals remained scarce.

stories.title: IMF lauds resilient Hong Kong economy but warns of risks linked to Middle East war
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund praised Hong Kong's economic resilience and sustained recovery but warned of downside risks from escalating geopolitical tensions, including the Middle East conflict. The IMF also urged Hong Kong to pursue medium-term fiscal reforms, including introducing a goods and services tax.

stories.title: Bangalore: India's Silicon Valley, a city straining under pressure
stories.summary: Bengaluru, known as India's Silicon Valley, has grown into a major global tech hub hosting companies such as Apple, Microsoft, and Boeing, along with thousands of startups. The city of nearly 15 million people faces significant environmental pressures from its rapid development.

stories.title: Shabbat candle lighting times for Israel and US
stories.summary: The Jerusalem Post published Shabbat candle lighting times for communities in Israel and the United States.

stories.title: In Zaporizhzhia, Russians strike industrial infrastructure facility; one person killed, and others injured
stories.summary: Russian forces struck an industrial infrastructure facility in the city of Zaporizhzhia, damaging a fuel tanker. One person was killed and three others were injured in the attack.

stories.title: UK artist defends pro-Palestine drawings after show cancellation
stories.summary: A UK art exhibition titled "Drawing Against Genocide" featuring pro-Palestine artwork was cancelled after UK Lawyers for Israel accused the show of being antisemitic. The artist defended the drawings and their intended message.

stories.title: What did American allies make of Trump’s trip to China to meet Xi?
stories.summary: U.S. allies closely watched the Trump-Xi summit in Beijing, with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi speaking to Trump by phone afterward. Takaichi said they exchanged views on China-related issues including economic security and broader security matters.

stories.title: Jaishankar, Iran’s Araghchi discuss West Asia crisis, energy security and maritime stability
stories.summary: Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar held discussions with Iranian Foreign Minister Hossein Amir-Abdollahian on the West Asia crisis, energy security, and maritime stability. The two exchanged views on bilateral issues of mutual interest.

stories.title: Confirmed Ebola outbreak in Congo, says African public health agency
stories.summary: The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention confirmed an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Initial findings suggest the presence of a non-Zaire strain of the virus, with genomic sequencing ongoing to characterize it further.

stories.title: Iran's foreign minister says it 'received messages' saying US was willing to continue talks
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in New Delhi that Tehran had received messages from the Trump administration indicating willingness to continue talks aimed at ending the Iran war. Araghchi made the remarks while attending the BRICS foreign ministers' meeting.

stories.title: Boy, 15, shot dead in France as prosecutors blame drug war
stories.summary: A 15-year-old boy was shot dead in Nantes, France. Prosecutors attributed the killing to drug-related violence, but the victim's aunt denied he had any involvement in the drug trade.

stories.title: X to block UK access to accounts linked to terrorist groups in Ofcom agreement
stories.summary: Elon Musk's X platform agreed with UK regulator Ofcom to block UK access to accounts linked to banned terrorist groups. X will also review suspected illegal terrorist and hate content within 48 hours.

stories.title: Trump poured millions into Nvidia, Apple in first quarter, ethics filing shows
stories.summary: A U.S. ethics filing revealed that President Donald Trump invested millions of dollars in Apple and Nvidia during the first quarter of 2026. The CEOs of both companies were part of his business delegation during a state visit to Beijing.

stories.title: Beijing had already won before the Trump-Xi summit even started
stories.summary: Following U.S. President Donald Trump's state visit, Chinese President Xi Jinping hosted Trump for talks at Zhongnanhai, the walled compound in central Beijing that serves as the seat of Chinese political power.

stories.title: Trump says he and Xi talked US, Chinese cyberattacks, spying
stories.summary: President Trump stated that he and Chinese President Xi Jinping discussed cyberattacks and espionage conducted by both the United States and China. Trump appeared to suggest that Xi tacitly acknowledged activities that lower-level Chinese officials have routinely denied.

stories.title: Trump says US may lift sanctions on Chinese companies that buy Iranian oil
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said he is considering lifting sanctions on Chinese companies that purchase Iranian oil, speaking aboard Air Force One after a state visit to China. Trump also stated he would accept Iran suspending its nuclear program for 20 years if Tehran makes a genuine commitment.

stories.title: First Thing: China trip winds down but Trump-Xi Iran accord remains elusive | Jem Bartholomew
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump's state visit to China ended without breakthroughs on Iran, despite discussions between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. China's foreign ministry called for a ceasefire in Iran.

stories.title: Maldives rescuers search for missing Italian divers in underwater cave
stories.summary: Rescue teams in the Maldives searched for a second day for the bodies of four missing Italian divers following the country's deadliest diving accident. Italy's foreign ministry confirmed five citizens died, and Maldivian authorities have recovered one body so far.

stories.title: Palestinian ambassador Husam Zomlot to run for Fatah's central committee
stories.summary: Palestinian Ambassador to the UK Husam Zomlot announced his candidacy for Fatah's central committee on May 15, 2026, coinciding with the 78th anniversary of the Nakba. Zomlot, originally from Gaza, has been a prominent diplomatic voice during Israel's military operations there.

stories.title: Watch: Ukraine and Russia swap 205 prisoners each in major exchange deal
stories.summary: Ukraine and Russia each exchanged 205 prisoners on May 15 in the first stage of a planned 1,000-for-1,000 swap. The United Arab Emirates mediated the deal.

stories.title: Brics talks end without joint statement, exposing divisions over war in Iran
stories.summary: BRICS foreign ministers failed to produce a joint statement after a two-day meeting in Delhi, with host India issuing only a chair's statement. Iran sought condemnation of the US-Israeli war against it and accused the UAE of direct involvement in military operations, exposing deep divisions within the bloc.

stories.title: Invaders strike village in Chernihiv region; woman and her child injured
stories.summary: A Russian Geran drone struck a village in the Horodnia community of Ukraine's Chernihiv region early in the morning, setting a house on fire. A woman and her daughter were injured in the attack.

stories.title: Trump, touting deal, says China to buy 200 Boeing jets with promise for more
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced that China agreed to purchase at least 200 Boeing commercial aircraft, with the potential for up to 750 planes. A purchase of up to 450 General Electric aircraft engines was also reportedly agreed upon during Trump's state visit to Beijing.

stories.title: Gaza's children are reliving their grandparents' Nakba
stories.summary: On the 78th anniversary of the Nakba, reports highlight that children in the Gaza Strip are experiencing displacement and trauma similar to what their grandparents endured in 1948.

stories.title: X agrees to UK crackdown on hate speech, terror content after antisemitic attacks
stories.summary: Social media platform X agreed to comply with UK regulator Ofcom's demands to crack down on hate speech and terror content following recent antisemitic attacks against British Jews. An activist noted that despite the commitments, X continues to fall short in many areas.

stories.title: Ethiopia: Ethiopian National Dialogue Commission Reports Progress As Talks Enter Critical Phase
stories.summary: Ethiopia's National Dialogue Commission reported it has completed agenda collection in 93 percent of the country. The commission is preparing to enter a critical new phase aimed at producing concrete national consensus.

stories.title: Ethiopia: Ethiopia, India to Collaborate Across Range of Sectors
stories.summary: Ethiopian Foreign Minister Gedion Timothewos held discussions with India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar in Addis Ababa. The two officials discussed collaboration across a range of sectors.

stories.title: Ethiopia: PM Abiy Praises Ethiopia's Dialogue Commission, Calls for Concrete Outcomes
stories.summary: Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed praised the Ethiopian National Dialogue Commission for its work in advancing the country's national dialogue process. He called on commissioners to deliver concrete outcomes.

stories.title: Ethiopia: Ethiopia's Quest for Sea Access 'Perfectly Legitimate,' Says French Ambassador
stories.summary: France's Ambassador to Ethiopia, Alexis Lamek, stated that Ethiopia's efforts to diversify its access to the sea are "perfectly legitimate." He described the aspiration as reasonable for the world's most populous landlocked country.

stories.title: Ethiopia: Ethiopia Calls for Reform of Global Governance, Multilateral Systems At Brics Meeting
stories.summary: Ethiopia used a BRICS meeting to call for sweeping reforms to global governance and multilateral institutions. Ethiopian representatives urged the international community to create a more equitable and representative world order.

stories.title: Smotrich: It’s time to end division of West Bank, it belongs to Israel ‘in its entirety’
stories.summary: Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich declared that the West Bank belongs to Israel in its entirety and called for an end to its division. Separately, the IDF reported killing a masked Palestinian stone-thrower, identified by Palestinian authorities as a 15-year-old whose body was detained.

stories.title: Why the Iran conflict is becoming a problem for BRICS
stories.summary: The BRICS bloc's foreign ministers' meeting ended without a joint statement for the second consecutive session due to disagreements over the war on Iran. Tensions between member states, including Iran and the UAE, prevented the group from reaching a unified position on the conflict.

stories.title: Uganda: Kampala Hospital Milestone Sparks Fresh Focus On Misdiagnosis Crisis
stories.summary: Uganda's healthcare sector faces growing concerns over high rates of medical misdiagnosis linked to laboratory services. A milestone at a Kampala hospital has prompted renewed calls for prioritizing quality assurance and diagnostic accuracy.

stories.title: The most awarded Jewish film of the year is now on Prime Video & Apple TV. - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: The award-winning film "Among Neighbors" is now available on Amazon Prime Video and Apple TV. The film tells the story of an eyewitness to a historical crime in a town where the past has been silenced.

stories.title: China wants Strait of Hormuz open free of curbs, USTR Greer tells Bloomberg News
stories.summary: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told Bloomberg News that China wants the Strait of Hormuz to remain open and free of restrictions. He also expressed U.S. confidence that Beijing would act to limit material support for Iran.

stories.title: Israelis mark capture of East Jerusalem with Old City parade, provocative chants
stories.summary: Thousands of Israeli police were deployed in Jerusalem's Old City as Jewish nationalist groups marched to celebrate the capture of East Jerusalem in the 1967 war, with reports of provocative chants during the parade.

stories.title: Ukrainian drone attack kills three in Russia's Ryazan, hits residences, industry
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone strike killed three people in the central Russian city of Ryazan, according to Regional Governor Pavel Malkov. The attack damaged high-rise apartment buildings and struck an industrial facility. The incident occurred early on Friday, May 15.

stories.title: Kenya: Wave of Staff Exits Looms At Deputy President's Office Ahead of 2027 Elections
stories.summary: Senior officials in Kenya's Office of the Deputy President warn that dozens of staff members are preparing to resign ahead of the 2027 general elections, prompting an additional 95.4 million Kenyan shilling allocation for gratuity payments.

stories.title: 'Plenty of platitudes': Trump wraps China trip, claims progress
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump left Beijing on Friday after two days of meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Both leaders claimed progress in stabilising bilateral relations, though significant differences between Washington and Beijing remained unresolved.

stories.title: Warren Buffett, Stephen Curry lunch auction fetches $11.5 million for charity
stories.summary: A charity auction offering lunch with investor Warren Buffett and basketball star Stephen Curry raised $11.5 million. Buffett has long advocated partnerships between businesses and nonprofits to drive social impact.

stories.title: Health officials raise alarm over new Ebola outbreak in DR Congo
stories.summary: Health officials in the Democratic Republic of Congo raised concerns over a new Ebola outbreak. Authorities warned that the virus could spread further due to the precarious security situation in the affected area, complicating containment efforts.

stories.title: Pak-US ties have strengthened during Trump's tenure, Naqvi says in meeting with American official
stories.summary: Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi stated that Pakistan-U.S. relations have strengthened during President Donald Trump's tenure. He made the remarks during a meeting in Islamabad with U.S. Assistant Secretary of State Paul Kapur, where discussions also covered the Middle East situation.

stories.title: US-China summit ends with Xi and Trump claiming progress but differences remain
stories.summary: President Trump and President Xi Jinping concluded their summit in Beijing on Friday, walking the grounds of Zhongnanhai and sharing a working tea and lunch. Both sides said progress was made on US-China relations, but substantial disagreements persisted after two days of talks.

stories.title: Will redistricting set back America's 'multi-racial democracy'?
stories.summary: Redistricting ahead of the 2026 US midterm elections has become a contested battleground, with Democrats drawing their own aggressive maps in response to Republican gerrymandering efforts. The process raises questions about the future of multi-racial representation in American democracy.

stories.title: Ukrenergo: Power outages reported in six regions due to attacks on energy infrastructure
stories.summary: As of the morning of May 15, power outages were reported across six Ukrainian regions following new Russian attacks on energy infrastructure, according to grid operator Ukrenergo.

stories.title: Trump’s top science adviser visited Beijing. What does that mean for AI?
stories.summary: U.S. President Trump's top science adviser Michael Kratsios and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang traveled with the U.S. delegation to Beijing, raising questions about AI collaboration. China's foreign ministry did not directly confirm whether the Trump-Xi talks produced specific AI-related outcomes.

stories.title: Stephen Miran, Trump’s economic guru, is leaving the Fed. What happens now?
stories.summary: Stephen Miran resigned from the U.S. Federal Reserve Board of Governors, a move analysts say will smooth the leadership transition to incoming chair Kevin Warsh. Miran, a former top economic adviser to President Trump, is the subject of speculation about a possible return to the White House or the private sector.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine Begin First Phase of Large POW Exchange
stories.summary: Ukraine and Russia each released 205 prisoners of war on Friday in the first phase of a planned 1,000-for-1,000 exchange. President Zelensky confirmed the swap and said additional exchanges are expected soon.

stories.title: Watch: Trump thanks Xi for ‘incredible’ China trip, says both ‘feel very similar’ on Iran
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump thanked Chinese President Xi Jinping for an "incredible" visit to China, stating that both leaders "feel very similar" on the issue of Iran.

stories.title: Trump says he wants Iran’s uranium mostly for ‘public relations’
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated that his push to obtain Iran's enriched uranium is motivated largely by public relations considerations rather than security concerns. The disposition of Iran's nuclear material remains a key sticking point in ongoing negotiations between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz lauds 'historic' Pak-China ties in meeting with Chinese business delegation
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met a high-level Chinese business delegation led by IBI Beijing United Technology founder Qian Xiaojun in Islamabad, praising the "historic" ties between Pakistan and China and their all-weather strategic cooperative partnership.

stories.title: Trump says he won’t be much more patient with Iran
stories.summary: President Trump warned that his patience with Iran is running thin and urged Tehran to reach a deal with the United States. He also reiterated that efforts to retrieve Iran's enriched uranium were driven more by perception than by security necessity.

stories.title: Iran’s Araghchi says he is open to China’s help to resolve Iran war
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in New Delhi that he welcomed any support, including from China, to help resolve the Iran war. Araghchi described China as a strategic partner with good intentions and expressed appreciation for potential Chinese mediation efforts.

stories.title: Trump concludes visit to China, says made 'fantastic trade deals' with Xi
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump concluded a visit to Beijing, claiming he made "fantastic trade deals" with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Discussions covered agriculture, aviation, artificial intelligence, and geostrategic issues including the Middle East war.

stories.title: Why is Ireland not taking part in this year's Eurovision?
stories.summary: Ireland is boycotting the 2026 Eurovision Song Contest, the latest in a series of diplomatic moves reflecting Dublin's disagreements with Israel over its military operations in Gaza.

stories.title: Israel’s upcoming election season could become its ugliest yet - opinion
stories.summary: The opinion article discusses Israel's approaching election season, warning it could become the most divisive in the country's history. It raises questions about the long-term impact on Israeli society regardless of the outcome.

stories.title: Inside Israel’s Flag March and the erasure of Palestinians in Jerusalem
stories.summary: Ultra-nationalist Israelis held their annual Flag March through Jerusalem's Old City, routed through the Muslim Quarter. Palestinian shopkeepers were forced to close their businesses to avoid attacks, as the march marked Jerusalem Day in occupied East Jerusalem.

stories.title: Russians attack car with drone in Kherson, injuring four civilians
stories.summary: Russian forces struck a civilian car with a drone in the city of Kherson, injuring four civilians on the morning of May 15.

stories.title: Middle Israel: How Likud’s primaries poisoned Israeli politics - opinion
stories.summary: The opinion piece examines how the introduction of primary elections within Israel's Likud party reshaped Israeli politics. It references the long rivalry between Shimon Peres and Yitzhak Rabin, which was upended by this new internal selection process.

stories.title: Drones to fight school shooters? One US company says yes
stories.summary: A U.S. company called Campus Guardian Angel is piloting unarmed drones in Georgia and Florida schools designed to confront active shooters by acting as a deterrent. The technology has not yet been tested in a real incident.

stories.title: Embattled Hong Kong developer sued for HK$130 million, days after founder’s death
stories.summary: Hong Kong property developer Lofter Group has been sued for HK$130 million over allegedly breaching guarantor obligations in two bond subscription agreements. The lawsuit, filed by Earth Core Holdings in the High Court, comes days after the sudden death of Lofter Group's founder.

stories.title: Nigeria: Release El-Rufai Before Sallah, Atiku Tells Tinubu, UBA Sani
stories.summary: Former Nigerian Vice President Atiku Abubakar called on President Bola Tinubu and Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani to release former Kaduna Governor Nasir El-Rufai from detention before the Sallah holiday.

stories.title: Nigeria: Many Feared Abducted As Boko Haram Invades School in Borno Village
stories.summary: Armed members of Boko Haram/ISWAP attacked Mussa Primary and Junior Secondary School in Askira-Uba Local Government Area of Borno State, Nigeria. An unspecified number of students are feared to have been abducted during the early-morning raid.

stories.title: Mossad, Shin Bet chiefs joined Netanyahu on 'secret' UAE visit during Iran war, report says
stories.summary: Israel's Mossad chief and Shin Bet director reportedly accompanied Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on a visit to the UAE during the war on Iran, according to i24 News. Israel and the UAE released conflicting statements about the meeting between Netanyahu and UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed al-Nahyan.

stories.title: IDF Chief of Staff Zamir visited UAE during Op. Roaring Lion, sources confirm
stories.summary: IDF Chief of Staff Lt.-Gen. Eyal Zamir made a secret visit to the United Arab Emirates during Operation Roaring Lion, accompanied by a U.S. delegation. The visit aimed to strengthen strategic cooperation and discuss joint defense planning against Iran.

stories.title: Nigeria: 'Why I Sold My Mansions in the Us, UK' - Aliko Dangote
stories.summary: Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote disclosed that he sold his mansions in the United States and United Kingdom, sharing insights into his lifestyle choices and personal discipline.

stories.title: Ukrainian Drones Kill 4 and Set Ryazan Oil Refinery Ablaze
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone strikes on the city of Ryazan on Friday morning set an oil refinery ablaze and killed four people. Residents reported black smoke filling the sky and dark, oily rain falling over the city.

stories.title: Israel using solitary confinement against Palestinian children
stories.summary: New data indicates that the Israeli Prison Service has significantly increased its use of solitary confinement against Palestinian detainees, including children and women, drawing scrutiny from rights organizations.

stories.title: India raises retail fuel prices for first time since Mideast war began
stories.summary: India's state-run fuel retailers—Indian Oil Corp, Hindustan Petroleum Corp, and Bharat Petroleum Corp—raised petrol and diesel prices by 3 rupees per litre for the first time in four years to offset losses from higher global crude oil prices linked to the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Africa: African Lawmakers Urged to Remove Legislative Barriers Blocking Climate Finance and Methane Reduction Action
stories.summary: At a forum in Nairobi, African legislators were called upon to remove legislative and regulatory obstacles hindering climate finance and to accelerate methane reduction policies, as parliaments across the continent seek a central role in the global climate response.

stories.title: Nigeria: Energy Commission Boss Mustapha Resumes Duties Amid EFCC's Alleged N500bn Fraud Probe
stories.summary: The media office of Nigeria's Energy Commission reported that its director-general was arrested, as the agency's head, Mustapha, resumed duties amid an alleged N500 billion fraud investigation by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC).

stories.title: Africa: Why China Now Dominates Africa's Business Landscape - Dangote
stories.summary: Aliko Dangote stated that China has become Africa's dominant business partner because Western countries often fail to provide financing for large-scale industrial projects, pushing African businesses and governments to rely heavily on Chinese firms.

stories.title: UAE to complete second oil pipeline bypassing strait of Hormuz by 2027
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced it will complete a new oil pipeline bypassing the Strait of Hormuz by 2027, fast-tracking a previously undisclosed project expected to double export capacity. The move comes as an 11-week blockade of the strait disrupts global energy markets.

stories.title: Helsinki Airport resumes flights after drone alert pause
stories.summary: Helsinki Airport suspended air traffic from 4 a.m. to 7 a.m. after Finnish safety authorities issued a danger alert for the southern Uusimaa region due to a potential drone sighting. Flights resumed after the alert was cleared.

stories.title: Congo-Kinshasa: Ebola Outbreak Declared in Eastern DR Congo As Regional Alert Raised
stories.summary: The Africa Centres for Disease Control declared a new Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo's eastern Ituri province. Authorities raised a regional alert over fears of cross-border spread in an area already affected by armed conflict and significant population displacement.

stories.title: Committee of Ministers of Council of Europe approves agreement to establish Special Tribunal
stories.summary: The Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe, meeting in Chisinau, Moldova, approved an agreement to establish a Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression against Ukraine. Thirty-seven countries supported the document creating the management framework for the tribunal.

stories.title: Almost 20 million people in Sudan still face acute hunger
stories.summary: Nearly 20 million people in Sudan are facing acute hunger three years after the start of the country's civil war, according to a report by a global hunger monitoring organization.

stories.title: Inside Zhongnanhai: Xi welcomes Trump into China’s hidden heart before bidding goodbye
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping hosted U.S. President Donald Trump for talks over tea and a working lunch at Zhongnanhai, the walled compound in Beijing that serves as China's political nerve center, offering a rare glimpse of its interior.

stories.title: Ebola outbreak kills 65 people in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo
stories.summary: An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ituri province has killed 65 people, with 246 suspected cases reported. Ituri shares borders with Uganda and South Sudan, raising concerns about cross-border spread and a possible new strain of the virus.

stories.title: Kyiv in mourning after 24 killed in strike as Russia, Ukraine exchange POWs
stories.summary: Kyiv declared a day of mourning on Friday after a Russian strike killed at least 24 people, including three children, in Ukraine's capital. On the same day, Russia and Ukraine carried out a prisoner-of-war exchange, with 205 captives released by each side.

stories.title: Palestinian woman forced to demolish her home in occupied Jerusalem
stories.summary: Israeli authorities in occupied Jerusalem ordered Palestinian resident Awatif Mahmoud al-Ghoul to demolish her own home in the al-Suweih neighbourhood, according to Wafa news agency. She was compelled to comply to avoid heavy municipal fines that would be imposed if authorities carried out the demolition themselves.

stories.title: Western powers ramp up support for Philippines’ Luzon economic hub
stories.summary: The Luzon Economic Corridor in the Philippines, a trilateral infrastructure initiative led by the U.S., Japan, and the Philippines, will receive additional support from eight more countries including Canada, Australia, France, South Korea, and the United Kingdom.

stories.title: How the fall of Starmer will reshape British policy on Israel
stories.summary: The article analyzes how a potential change in British leadership following Keir Starmer could shift UK policy on Israel and the Middle East. It suggests that any successor as prime minister would likely adopt a more outspoken stance on the conflict.

stories.title: Nigeria: Economic Hardship in Nigeria Painful but Necessary - Govt
stories.summary: Nigeria's Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, acknowledged that current economic hardships are painful but described them as a necessary part of transitioning toward a more resilient and sustainable economy.

stories.title: Iran's national football team given public send-off ahead of FIFA World Cup
stories.summary: Iran's national football team received a public send-off ahead of the FIFA World Cup. The team plans to travel to Turkey for a training camp, though concerns remain over obtaining US visas for the tournament.

stories.title: Inside Nigeria's crypto craze
stories.summary: Cryptocurrency adoption has surged in Nigeria, with nearly one in ten Nigerians now using digital currencies. Many turn to crypto to circumvent the depreciation of the naira, while younger Nigerians trade crypto assets on platforms seeking quick financial returns.

stories.title: Africa confirms fatal Ebola outbreak in Congo, urgent cross-border meeting called
stories.summary: The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention confirmed a new Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo's remote Ituri province, with 246 suspected cases and 65 deaths recorded. An urgent cross-border meeting has been called to coordinate the response.

stories.title: After Trump visit, China’s top party journal doubles down on manufacturing push
stories.summary: Shortly after U.S. President Trump's departure from Beijing, China's ruling Communist Party published an article in its journal Qiushi reaffirming the importance of strengthening manufacturing and the real economy, drawing on past speeches by President Xi Jinping.

stories.title: Ukraine - UN aid convoy targeted by drone attacks
stories.summary: A United Nations humanitarian aid convoy heading to Kherson was struck twice by drones, an attack Ukraine attributes to Russia. The incident occurred amid an intense Russian aerial campaign that saw nearly 1,600 drones launched against Ukraine over two consecutive days.

stories.title: Finland ends drone alert amid regional fears of Ukraine war spillover
stories.summary: Finland ended a drone alert after its defense authorities scrambled fighter jets to respond to the threat. The Finnish defense chief warned that similar alarms are likely to recur as Russia's war in Ukraine continues, raising fears of spillover into the broader region.

stories.title: The Nakba never ended for Palestinians, I'm living it in Gaza
stories.summary: The article presents a personal account from writer Huda Skaik in Gaza, who describes over two years of displacement, horror, and loss during Israel's military campaign. She frames these experiences as a continuation of the Nakba for Palestinians.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones destroy Be-200 amphibious aircraft and strike Ka-27 helicopter in Yeysk, Russia
stories.summary: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces destroyed a Be-200 Altair amphibious aircraft and struck a Ka-27 helicopter in the Russian city of Yeysk. Additional strikes hit a Tor-M2 air defense system, a Pantsir-S1 system, and a Russian ammunition ship in occupied Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia, and Crimea.

stories.title: UAE to accelerate oil pipeline project to help bypass Hormuz amid Iran war fallout
stories.summary: The UAE announced plans to accelerate an oil pipeline project to bypass the Strait of Hormuz amid fallout from the Iran war. The pipeline, freed from OPEC output quotas following Abu Dhabi's exit from the organization, is expected to begin operating in 2027.

stories.title: This is the Palestinian Nakba, measured in land taken
stories.summary: Palestinians marked the 78th anniversary of the Nakba on May 15, commemorating their mass displacement beginning in 1948. Ongoing Israeli land acquisition in Palestinian territories continues to expand the total area taken since that period.

stories.title: Al-Amari after the Nakba: One fear shared across generations
stories.summary: The article reports on life in the Al-Amari refugee camp in the occupied West Bank, where residents live under the shadow of two displacements: the original 1948 Nakba commemorated 78 years ago and the current threat of further displacement.

stories.title: Xi, Trump reach series of new common understandings: China's foreign ministry
stories.summary: Chinese and U.S. Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump reached a series of new common understandings during their Beijing summit, agreeing to promote steady, sound, and sustainable development of bilateral relations, according to China's foreign ministry.

stories.title: Russia hits Taiwan too—and three democracies are comparing notes on public media
stories.summary: At the Lviv Media Forum on May 15, 2026, representatives from Ukraine, Georgia, and Taiwan compared experiences with Russian and broader authoritarian influence on public media, discussing how each democracy is building, defending, or dismantling independent media infrastructure.

stories.title: IDF would withdraw from Lebanon if Hezbollah disarmed as CIA plans to remove terror weapons - KAN
stories.summary: Israel indicated it would withdraw forces from Lebanon if Hezbollah disarmed, while reports said the CIA is planning to help remove the group's weapons. The discussions continued as the IDF carried out strikes in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Day of Mourning in Kyiv: final toll from Russian missile strike reaches 24 dead, including three girls aged 12, 15, and 17
stories.summary: Kyiv declared a day of mourning after the final toll from a Russian missile strike on a nine-story residential building in Darnytskyi district reached 24 dead, including three girls aged 12, 15, and 17. The search-and-rescue operation lasted 28 hours.

stories.title: Air Defense Forces shoot down anti-ship missile and 130 Russian drones
stories.summary: Ukraine's Air Defense Forces intercepted one anti-ship missile and 130 drones launched by Russian forces since the evening of May 14. The attacks targeted multiple areas across Ukraine.

stories.title: Ukraine attacks Russia with drones after suffering three days of massive strikes
stories.summary: Ukraine launched a large-scale drone attack targeting several Russian regions, including the Ryazan oil refinery, after three days of massive Russian strikes on Ukraine. The counterattacks followed a cruise missile hitting a Kyiv apartment block that killed 24 people, including three children.

stories.title: Uganda: Speakership Race - Mao Welcomes Plu Withdrawal of Support for Anita Among
stories.summary: In Uganda's speakership race for the 12th Parliament, aspirant Norbert Mao welcomed the Patriotic League of Uganda's decision to withdraw support for incumbent Speaker Anita Among and Deputy Speaker Thomas Tayebwa.

stories.title: Iran’s Araghchi says US sending ‘contradictory messages’
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi accused Washington of sending 'contradictory messages' that are complicating negotiations, according to state broadcaster IRIB. He reiterated that Iran is not responsible for disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz and said the waterway remains open to 'friendly countries' that coordinate with Tehran.

stories.title: WATCH: 'All of Israel is ours': Smotrich calls to annex West Bank in Jerusalem Day speech
stories.summary: Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called for annexation of the entire West Bank in a Jerusalem Day speech at the Religious Zionist Merkaz HaRav Yeshiva. He urged erasing the Oslo-era distinctions between Areas A, B, and C, declaring 'the entire Land of Israel is ours.'

stories.title: U.K. Health Secretary resigns, setting up potential Labour leadership challenge to Starmer
stories.summary: U.K. Health Secretary resigned, potentially setting up a Labour Party leadership challenge to Prime Minister Keir Starmer, who faces growing pressure to step down following disastrous results in recent local and regional elections.

stories.title: Sci-fi or battlefield reality? Ukraine’s bet on swarm drones
stories.summary: Ukraine is developing and deploying swarm drone technology—groups of drones capable of coordinating and executing tasks autonomously without human intervention—for use on the battlefield.

stories.title: India hikes fuel prices as Iran crisis bites
stories.summary: India, the world's third-largest oil importer, announced increased fuel prices and austerity measures in response to the energy crisis linked to the conflict involving Iran. The price hikes reflect the strain on global oil markets caused by disrupted supplies.

stories.title: Egyptian farmers struggling to survive as Iran war pushes up costs
stories.summary: Four months into the US-Israel war against Iran, disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz have driven up global energy and fertilizer costs. Egyptian farmers are struggling to survive as rising input prices squeeze agricultural livelihoods.

stories.title: Zelensky calls on world to put pressure on Russia following massive attack on May 14
stories.summary: Following a massive Russian attack on Kyiv and the surrounding region, President Volodymyr Zelensky called on the international community to increase pressure on Russia.

stories.title: China urges lasting West Asia truce, reopening of shipping lanes
stories.summary: During the Trump-Xi summit in Beijing, China called for a lasting truce in West Asia and the reopening of shipping lanes disrupted by the ongoing Middle East conflict.

stories.title: The murky waters of Chile's salmon industry
stories.summary: Chile's salmon farming industry, the country's second-largest after mining, accounts for over a quarter of global salmon production and has brought economic growth to southern regions. However, the industry faces criticism over deadly workplace accidents, water pollution, and harm to local wildlife.

stories.title: Weather tracker: Furnace Creek sizzles as snow sweeps Siberia in a week of extremes
stories.summary: Extreme weather events this week included record-breaking heat in Honduras, where Choluteca reached 42.2°C, and egg-sized hailstones in eastern China. Furnace Creek also experienced intense heat while Siberia saw snow.

stories.title: Near Russian border, NATO grapples with ground robots in combat
stories.summary: NATO forces near the Russian border in Latvia are working to integrate ground-based combat robots into their operations. A Latvian commander acknowledged that allied forces are lagging in ground robotics, having focused primarily on aerial drones.

stories.title: Exhibit on iconic designer Dorin Frankfurt looks at the clothes that made the woman
stories.summary: An exhibition on iconic Israeli fashion designer Dorin Frankfurt opened at the Ashdod Museum of Art, running through August 15. The show, titled "Fashion Worker: Dorin Frankfurt," showcases nearly 50 years of Israeli fashion and manufacturing history.

stories.title: 13 men killed by US military boat strikes identified: ‘These were flesh-and-blood people’
stories.summary: A five-month investigation has identified 13 previously unnamed victims of U.S. military boat strikes in the eastern Pacific and Caribbean targeting suspected narcotics vessels. The campaign has killed nearly 200 people, all identified victims coming from extremely poor communities. It remains unclear whether the U.S. identified any victims before attacking.

stories.title: China couple diagnosed with rare autoimmune disorder together have lost newborn baby
stories.summary: A young married couple in Tianjin, northern China, were both diagnosed with Bickerstaff brainstem encephalitis, a rare autoimmune disorder, and have lost their newborn baby. The husband said they were the first couple in China — and only the fourth globally — to be diagnosed simultaneously.

stories.title: Starmer ally admits prime minister is ‘unpopular’ but warns of ‘chaos’ if leadership contest triggered – UK politics live
stories.summary: Pressure is mounting on UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer after Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham was given a route back to parliament via the upcoming Makerfield byelection. Housing Secretary Steve Reed, a close Starmer ally, acknowledged the PM is unpopular but warned that triggering a leadership contest would cause chaos.

stories.title: Three years of the West Bank’s ‘third Nakba’
stories.summary: Palestinian Bedouin communities in the occupied West Bank have faced ongoing displacement and violence over the past three years. Many families have been forced from their homes repeatedly since the original Nakba of 1948.

stories.title: Israel threatens to sue New York Times over report on sexual abuse of Palestinian inmates
stories.summary: Israel threatened to sue The New York Times over an opinion piece by columnist Nicholas Kristof alleging widespread sexual abuse of Palestinian detainees. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Foreign Minister Gideon Saar ordered the initiation of a defamation lawsuit.

stories.title: United States seeks to re-establish ties with countries in Sahel region
stories.summary: The United States is seeking to re-establish ties with countries in Africa's Sahel region. US military officials warned a Senate committee that extremist groups have expanded their operational capacity in the area.

stories.title: Madagascar opposition moves to oust military leader in constitutional challenge
stories.summary: Opposition lawmaker in Madagascar has petitioned the country's top court to remove President Michael Randrianirina over alleged constitutional violations, escalating political tensions in the country.

stories.title: Hopes grow that London Underground strikes could be called off
stories.summary: Planned strikes by London Underground drivers belonging to the RMT union, scheduled for two 24-hour periods starting midday Tuesday and Thursday, may be averted. Sources indicate the RMT has signaled willingness to enter talks. The action would have closed some Tube lines and caused major disruption across the capital.

stories.title: Chinese EV makers hunt for idled plants in Europe as they expand global influence
stories.summary: Chinese electric vehicle manufacturers including BYD and Leapmotor are actively seeking idled assembly plants in Europe owned by companies like Stellantis and Volkswagen. The push is driven by surging global demand for battery-powered vehicles amid the energy crisis.

stories.title: Trump and Xi move towards business-first relationship after Beijing summit
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping held a summit in Beijing aimed at strengthening economic ties. However, the two leaders failed to resolve key disagreements over Iran and Taiwan, despite efforts to extend their existing trade truce.

stories.title: Chinese tourist banned from Thailand for life after kicking, damaging US$15,000 auto-gates
stories.summary: A 30-year-old Chinese tourist identified as Zheng Liwei was banned from Thailand for life after allegedly kicking and damaging automated passport gates at Bangkok's Suvarnabhumi Airport. The incident is part of a broader Thai crackdown on disorderly behavior by foreign visitors.

stories.title: Search-and-rescue operation in Kyiv concludes following Russian strike: 24 dead, 48 injured
stories.summary: A search-and-rescue operation in Kyiv's Darnytskyi district concluded after more than 28 hours following a Russian strike. Authorities confirmed 24 people were killed, including three children, and 48 others were injured.

stories.title: Xi-Trump summit: The humble soybean at the heart of a trade dispute between the US and China
stories.summary: Soybeans have become a flashpoint in the U.S.-China trade dispute. China, which purchased billions of dollars of U.S. soy in 2024, halted imports after Washington launched its trade war. Purchases resumed following an October truce between Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump, but the arrangement's durability remains uncertain.

stories.title: Lebanon seeks truce extension as Israeli strikes continue
stories.summary: Lebanon's government pushed for a full ceasefire extension during talks in Washington as Israeli strikes, evacuation orders, and clashes with Hezbollah continued in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: At least 24 killed in Kyiv in one of deadliest Russian attacks since start of war – Europe live
stories.summary: A Russian attack on Kyiv killed at least 24 people, including three children, making it one of the deadliest strikes on the Ukrainian capital since the full-scale invasion began. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed the death toll.

stories.title: Moscow’s fuel supplier under fire: Ukrainian drones strike Rosneft’s Ryazan refinery
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck Rosneft's oil refinery in Ryazan, Russia, setting vacuum distillation units on fire during an overnight attack. The refinery is a major supplier of gasoline, diesel, and jet kerosene to regions surrounding Moscow.

stories.title: Trump touts business wins as China airs Iran, Taiwan concerns
stories.summary: President Donald Trump concluded talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing, touting economic deals that drew a muted market response. China warned Washington against mishandling Taiwan and criticized the U.S. war with Iran. The visit was the first by a U.S. president to China since Trump's 2017 trip.

stories.title: US seeks to indict Cuba's ex-president Raul Castro
stories.summary: The United States is reportedly seeking to indict former Cuban President Raúl Castro, the 94-year-old brother of Fidel Castro, as part of increasing pressure on Cuba. The move comes amid a deepening crisis in U.S.-Cuba relations, with the island suffering constant power outages linked to President Trump's fuel blockade.

stories.title: At least 78 dead, 5,000 displaced in gang clashes in Haiti since Saturday
stories.summary: Gang clashes in suburbs of Haiti's capital Port-au-Prince have killed at least 78 people, including 10 bystanders, since Saturday, according to the UN Office in Haiti (BINUH). The violence has displaced approximately 5,300 people in the Caribbean nation, where gang-related instability has worsened over the past two years.

stories.title: Israeli strike targets motorbike in Lebanese town
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike targeted a motorcycle in the southern Lebanese town of al-Majadel, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. There were no immediate casualty reports. Israel's military has been intensifying targeted strikes on vehicles in southern Lebanon and around Beirut.

stories.title: ‘Panic’ over capacity crunch in mature node chips drives orders to Chinese foundries
stories.summary: The global AI boom is creating a shortage in mature-node semiconductors as major foundries shift production toward high-margin AI chips. SMIC co-CEO Zhao Haijun said this capacity crunch is driving orders back to Chinese foundries for power-management and other mature-node chips.

stories.title: Russians strike commuter train in Zaporizhzhia region; injuries reported
stories.summary: Russian forces struck a commuter train in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region using a drone. Two passengers sustained shrapnel wounds in the attack.

stories.title: Two drones targeted Iranian opposition headquarters north of Iraq's Erbil, say security sources
stories.summary: Two drones struck the headquarters of an Iranian Kurdish opposition group located north of Erbil, the capital of Iraq's Kurdistan region, according to security sources cited by Reuters. No further details on casualties or responsibility were immediately available.

stories.title: Ukraine developing new defense industry ecosystem – expert
