stories.title: Amnesty calls for 'war crimes' probe into Israeli destruction of south Syria homes
stories.summary: Amnesty International called for a war crimes investigation into Israel's destruction of homes in southern Syria. Israel has launched hundreds of strikes on Syria and conducts regular incursions into the country's south, where it demands a demilitarized zone.

stories.title: Netanyahu's coalition moves to fast-track controversial laws ahead of upcoming Knesset dissolution
stories.summary: Netanyahu's coalition is moving to fast-track controversial legislation before an upcoming Knesset dissolution. The push follows a crisis within the coalition involving ultra-Orthodox parties over a disputed conscription law.

stories.title: Senior Emirati scholar says ‘war criminal’ Netanyahu never visited UAE
stories.summary: A senior Emirati scholar stated that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu never visited the UAE, contradicting claims from Netanyahu's office that a trip took place in March. The scholar referred to Netanyahu as a "war criminal."

stories.title: Zelensky on meeting with US delegation: Ukraine cooperates with US at all levels
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky stated after meeting a U.S. delegation that Ukraine is cooperating with the United States at all levels. He cited engagement with the White House, Congress, the political community, the American corporate sector, and civil society.

stories.title: Haifa Port opens new cruise terminal as Israel’s tourism sector eyes recovery
stories.summary: Haifa Port inaugurated a new cruise terminal built with an investment of over 16 million NIS, set to begin operations with the opening of the cruise season on May 14 as Israel's tourism sector seeks recovery.

stories.title: Eurovision 2026: Delta Goodrem sends Australia to the grand final with note-perfect performance
stories.summary: Australian singer Delta Goodrem advanced to the Eurovision 2026 grand final with a performance described as note-perfect, becoming the first Australian act to qualify on the contest's 70th anniversary.

stories.title: Pakistan-UAE ties unaffected by external engagements, says FO
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Office stated that Pakistan-UAE relations remain strong and unaffected by any external engagements by the Gulf state. The spokesperson cited bilateral trade of nearly $8 billion and a Pakistani diaspora of 2.2 million in the UAE as foundations of the relationship.

stories.title: Israel to sue NYT over ‘distorted’ report on sex abuse of Palestinian inmates
stories.summary: Israel announced plans to sue The New York Times over a report it described as "distorted" concerning the sexual abuse of Palestinian inmates. The report included accounts from fourteen individuals who said they had been sexually assaulted by Israeli settlers or security forces members.

stories.title: Trump says Beijing opposes Iranian toll in Hormuz, as Chinese vessels exit waterway
stories.summary: President Trump announced that Beijing opposes Iran's toll imposed on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, as Chinese vessels exited the waterway. The White House said China agreed to purchase more US oil to reduce its dependence on Gulf supplies.

stories.title: Israeli defence minister accuses Barcelona footballer of ‘inciting hate’ for waving Palestine flag
stories.summary: Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz accused FC Barcelona footballer Lamine Yamal of "inciting hatred" against Israel after the 18-year-old waved a Palestinian flag during a victory parade in Barcelona. Katz called on FC Barcelona to distance itself from the player's actions.

stories.title: Ukraine’s kamikaze drones can now attack and return
stories.summary: Ukraine's Fire Point FP-1/2 kamikaze drone has been upgraded with the ability to attack targets and return for reuse, joining a growing trend of converting single-use Ukrainian drones into reusable platforms.

stories.title: Zelensky says Kh-101 missile produced in violation of sanctions likely used in Kyiv apartment building strike
stories.summary: President Zelensky said a Kh-101 cruise missile that struck a Kyiv apartment building during a massive Russian attack was manufactured in the second quarter of 2025, indicating Russia continues to bypass international sanctions. He called for decisive international action against sanctions-evasion schemes.

stories.title: Former Rosnano chief Anatoly Chubais denounces prosecution of ex-managers as ‘repressions’
stories.summary: Former Rosnano chief Anatoly Chubais publicly denounced the criminal prosecution of the Russian state nanotechnology corporation's former top managers, calling the cases "repressions" and "a mockery of the law."

stories.title: Russia starved Pokrovsk into submission. Kostiantynivka’s robots are blocking the encore.
stories.summary: After Russian forces starved Pokrovsk into submission in the Donetsk region, Ukraine is deploying resupply robots to help defend the nearby city of Kostiantynivka. However, human soldiers remain essential to the defense effort.

stories.title: Photo of US-China delegation criticized over absence of women: ‘masculine, militarized and exclusionary’
stories.summary: A photo of the U.S.-China delegation meeting in Beijing's Great Hall of the People drew criticism for the complete absence of women from either side. Observers called the image a signal that women's voices are excluded from shaping the global order.

stories.title: Israeli army fires at towns in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli artillery struck the southern Lebanese towns of Nabatieh al-Fouqa, Kfar Tebnit, Jebchit, and Mefdoun on Thursday, violating the ceasefire agreement. The strikes occurred as Lebanon and Israel held a new round of direct talks in Washington. Nearly 3,000 people have been killed in Israeli attacks on Lebanon since fighting resumed on March 2.

stories.title: Role of Gulf states in Iran conflict said to change over one week - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis examines how the role of Gulf states in the Iran conflict shifted over the course of a week. Iran's narrative highlighted that some Gulf states hosted US forces, while the UAE and Bahrain had signed the Abraham Accords with Israel.

stories.title: Trump hails ‘fantastic trade deals’ with Xi, China issues warning on Taiwan
stories.summary: President Trump claimed "fantastic trade deals" were reached during his final talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing. However, Xi delivered a blunt warning that U.S. missteps on Taiwan could push the two nations toward conflict, according to Chinese state media reports.

stories.title: Russia’s State Duma appoints new human rights commissioner. Meduza sources say filmmaker Nikita Mikhalkov backed her appointment.
stories.summary: Russia's State Duma appointed Yana Lantratova as the country's new human rights commissioner. Sources indicated that prominent Russian filmmaker Nikita Mikhalkov backed her appointment.

stories.title: Pakistan raises $250m equivalent in inaugural Panda bond issuance
stories.summary: Pakistan raised $250 million equivalent through its inaugural Panda bond issuance in China's onshore capital market at a 2.5% interest rate with a three-year maturity. Finance advisor Khurram Schehzad called it Pakistan's first entry into the world's second-largest capital market.

stories.title: Chants of ‘death to Arabs’ at Jerusalem Day march as Ben Gvir flies Israeli flag on Temple Mount
stories.summary: During the annual Jerusalem Day march in Jerusalem's Old City, extremist youth groups chanted anti-Arab slogans and harassed journalists. National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir flew an Israeli flag on the Temple Mount. Police arrested 13 people and dispersed a left-wing group that came to protect Palestinians.

stories.title: Abu Dhabi 'doesn't want to appear too much in cooperation with Israel', analyst says
stories.summary: Analyst Federico Donelli said Abu Dhabi does not want to appear closely aligned with Israel given its actions in the region. The UAE denied Netanyahu's claimed secret visit, and a ship was seized off the UAE coast amid Strait of Hormuz tensions.

stories.title: Last residents evacuated from frontline village in Zaporizhzhia region
stories.summary: Ukrainian Armed Forces personnel evacuated the last two remaining residents from the frontline village of Dolynka in the Zaporizhzhia region. The evacuation removed all civilians from the village near the front lines.

stories.title: Australia news live: Delta Goodrem hits the stage in Eurovision semi; Angus Taylor accused of ‘dog whistle’ budget reply
stories.summary: Australian singer Delta Goodrem performed her song "Eclipse" in Eurovision's second semi-final ahead of Sunday's grand final. The competition has drawn controversy after Israel's Noam Bettan, who was booed during his performance, advanced from the first semi-final.

stories.title: ‘China is gaining from what the US is doing in Iran’
stories.summary: Geopolitical analyst Steve Okun argued that China is benefiting from the ongoing U.S. confrontation with Iran, gaining strategic and economic advantages as Washington focuses on the conflict.

stories.title: Watch: Congress ends suspense: V. D. Satheesan to be next Kerala CM | Above the Fold | 14.05.2026
stories.summary: India's Congress party named V.D. Satheesan as the next Chief Minister of Kerala after weeks of internal deliberations. Separately, India hosted a BRICS Foreign Ministers' meeting in New Delhi, where External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar addressed global diplomatic priorities.

stories.title: BBC on the ground during march through Jerusalem's Old City
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of Israeli marchers paraded through Jerusalem's Old City, in the area captured during the 1967 Arab-Israeli war. The BBC reported from the scene during the annual march.

stories.title: Diaspora Jews aren't ‘traitors’ for not making aliyah, Diaspora Affairs Minister Chikli says
stories.summary: Israeli Diaspora Affairs Minister Amichai Chikli stated that Jews living outside Israel should not be called "traitors" for not immigrating to Israel, saying such attacks on Diaspora Jewry do not serve Israeli interests.

stories.title: New Iraq PM pledges monopoly on arms
stories.summary: Iraq's parliament voted in Ali al-Zaidi as the new prime minister on Thursday. Zaidi pledged to establish a state monopoly on weapons and reform the security apparatus amid US pressure on Baghdad to dismantle Tehran-backed armed groups.

stories.title: Iraq sought financial assistance from IMF as result of Iran war, source close to IMF says
stories.summary: Iraqi officials have approached the International Monetary Fund in Washington seeking financial assistance due to the ongoing conflict with Iran in the Middle East, according to a source close to the IMF.

stories.title: China restores US beef trade amid Trump-Xi summit, alarming Brazilian exporters
stories.summary: China renewed US beef import licences during the Trump-Xi summit in Beijing, alarming Brazilian exporters who depend on the Chinese market. A senior Brazilian government official expressed concern that the move could reshape competition and affect domestic cattle prices in Brazil.

stories.title: Top California Democratic strategist pleads guilty to $225,000 fraud charges
stories.summary: Dana Williamson, a prominent California Democratic political strategist with ties to Governor Gavin Newsom, pleaded guilty to federal fraud charges. Authorities said Williamson conspired to steal $225,000 from a dormant campaign account belonging to gubernatorial candidate Xavier Becerra.

stories.title: Cuba runs out of fuel, diesel amid US blockade
stories.summary: Cuba has exhausted its fuel and diesel supplies as the US blockade deepens the island's energy crisis. The Cuban government is considering a renewed US aid offer from the Trump administration, though the assistance would come with conditions.

stories.title: Almost 20 million people in Sudan still face acute hunger, monitors say
stories.summary: A global hunger monitor reported that approximately 19.5 million people in Sudan — over 40 percent of the population — face acute hunger. The ongoing war in Sudan has created what monitors describe as the world's worst hunger crisis.

stories.title: Day 1 of Beijing Summit Produces No Big Wins for Trump
stories.summary: The first day of the US-China summit in Beijing concluded without major breakthroughs for President Trump. Discussions covered the Iran war and trade issues, but no significant concessions were secured from President Xi Jinping.

stories.title: Trump, Xi Hold High-Stakes Summit in Beijing
stories.summary: U.S. President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping held a high-stakes summit in Beijing. Discussions covered topics ranging from the Iran conflict to trade relations. Trump reportedly failed to secure major concessions from Xi during the meeting.

stories.title: FC Barcelona apologizes to Israeli fans after player goes viral waving Palestinian flag
stories.summary: FC Barcelona issued an apology written in Hebrew specifically addressed to its Israeli fans after player Lamine Yamal went viral for waving a Palestinian flag.

stories.title: The Pentagon wants 10,000 small cruise missiles. Here’s who is making them.
stories.summary: The Pentagon is pursuing a major procurement effort to acquire 10,000 small cruise missiles. The initiative represents a significant push to expand U.S. munitions stockpiles, with multiple defense contractors competing for production contracts.

stories.title: Israel marks 59th Jerusalem Day with Old City flag march, nationwide celebrations
stories.summary: Israel celebrated its 59th Jerusalem Day on May 14 with the traditional flag march through Jerusalem's Old City and nationwide festivities. The date also coincided with the anniversary of Israel's Declaration of Independence.

stories.title: Vessel seized off UAE's Fujairah and heading toward Iranian waters, UKMTO says
stories.summary: A vessel anchored northeast of the UAE port of Fujairah was boarded by unauthorized personnel and began heading toward Iranian territorial waters, according to UK Maritime Trade Operations. The incident occurred as Iran asserted that ships entering the Strait of Hormuz must cooperate with the Iranian navy.

stories.title: Cautious optimism in Lebanon as direct talks with Israel progress
stories.summary: Lebanese and Israeli officials held two days of ambassador-level negotiations in the United States aimed at reaching a new ceasefire agreement. Lebanese officials expressed cautious optimism about the outcome of the direct talks.

stories.title: To deliver for the warfighter, acquisition reform must provide a level playing field
stories.summary: A sponsored commentary argues that defense acquisition reform should ensure all companies compete under uniform rules. Proponents contend that a level playing field in procurement fosters innovation and strengthens the U.S. defense industrial base to better serve warfighters.

stories.title: Iran’s FM urges BRICS states to condemn US-Israeli aggression
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi addressed a BRICS foreign ministers' meeting in New Delhi on Thursday, calling on member states to condemn what he described as US-Israeli aggression.

stories.title: Ukraine’s drone commander proposes “Standard-10” for every strike crew in country
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone commander proposed a "Standard-10" benchmark for every strike crew in the country. His own unit in the 414th Brigade averages 30.6 confirmed kills per month, compared to a national average of three.

stories.title: Massive Russian attack on Kyiv: Death toll climbs to 12, including two children
stories.summary: The death toll from a Russian strike on Kyiv's Darnytskyi district on May 14 rose to 12, including two children. The attack was part of a massive Russian bombardment targeting the Ukrainian capital.

stories.title: Nobel winner Mukwege warns of predatory US deal for DR Congo
stories.summary: Congolese Nobel Peace Prize laureate Denis Mukwege criticized a US-brokered peace deal for eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, calling it predatory. Separately, China and Turkey are overtaking France as leading investors in Senegal's economy.

stories.title: Vessel seized off UAE’s Fujairah and heading toward Iranian waters, UKMTO says
stories.summary: A Honduras-flagged vessel, believed to be the Hui Chuan fishery research vessel, was seized off the UAE's Fujairah coast and was heading toward Iranian waters, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations and two maritime security sources.

stories.title: Hezbollah says it targeted Israeli troops in northern Israel
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced it launched a drone attack targeting Israeli soldiers in northern Israel, injuring several Israeli civilians near the Israel-Lebanon border. The attack occurred as Lebanese and Israeli representatives met for direct talks in Washington.

stories.title: Israeli arrested in Netherlands on suspicion of drug trafficking, being in int'l smuggling ring
stories.summary: An Israeli national was arrested in the Netherlands on suspicion of drug trafficking and involvement in an international smuggling ring. Dutch police said the investigation is ongoing, with additional arrests expected in Israel and other European countries.

stories.title: FO says voices in India calling for dialogue with Pakistan a 'positive development'
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Office spokesperson Tahir Andrabi described Indian voices calling for dialogue with Pakistan as a "positive development." He expressed hope that "warmongering" and "belligerence" in India would diminish over time.

stories.title: Macron ‘slap’ was sparked by texts with Iranian actress, book claims
stories.summary: A new book by a French journalist claims that text messages between President Emmanuel Macron and Iranian-French actress Golshifteh Farahani prompted a reported "slap" from First Lady Brigitte Macron. An AI-generated fake tabloid cover falsely depicted the pair together, amplifying the story.

stories.title: Skyeton makes Raybird reconnaissance drone Ukraine has used since 2018. Russia just destroyed its Kyiv office
stories.summary: Russia destroyed the Kyiv office of Skyeton, the Ukrainian manufacturer of the Raybird reconnaissance drone, which Ukraine's military has operated since 2018. The company stated it had anticipated eventually becoming a target.

stories.title: IMF warns of 'worst-case scenario' economic impact from Iran war
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund warned that continued disruptions from the Middle East conflict risk a "worst-case scenario" for the global economy. IMF spokesperson Julie Kozack cited concerns about low growth and high inflation if the war persists.

stories.title: Beja swords remain 'cherished tradition' in Sudan market
stories.summary: At the Daim Arab Market in Port Sudan, Beja merchants continue to sell kaskara swords—straight, double-edged blades traditionally carried at weddings and on journeys. The swords remain a symbol of eastern Sudanese identity among the Beja people.

stories.title: Zelensky discusses strengthening Ukraine’s air defense with German delegation
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky discussed strengthening Ukraine's air defense capabilities with senior German officials, including Thorsten Frei, Head of the Federal Chancellery, and Martin Jäger, President of Germany's Federal Intelligence Service.

stories.title: Iran military threat is diminished but not eliminated, CENTCOM chief says
stories.summary: CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper stated that U.S. operations have severely degraded Iran's military capacity. He noted that roughly 90% of Iran's naval mine inventory has been eliminated. Cooper emphasized that while the threat is diminished, it has not been fully neutralized.

stories.title: A hero's sacrifice: The railway worker who embraced death to save lives
stories.summary: A 44-year-old Pakistani railway worker, Muhammad Liaqat Ali, was killed after confronting a suicide bomber wearing an explosive vest near the Mankoor check post in Attock's Jand-Kohat railway section, close to the Khushal Garh Bridge.

stories.title: Four killed in Israeli strikes on northern Gaza
stories.summary: At least four Palestinians were killed in Israeli strikes on northern Gaza, according to hospital sources. Several others, including children, were wounded. Separately, a Palestinian child was injured by Israeli settlers in the Silwan neighborhood of occupied East Jerusalem.

stories.title: IDF reveals it supplies Lebanese army with anti-explosive drone barbed wire
stories.summary: The Israeli military disclosed that it has been supplying the Lebanese army with anti-explosive drone barbed wire. Approximately 158,000 square meters of the material have been provided so far, covering an area equivalent to roughly 20 football fields.

stories.title: CENTCOM head: War massively reduced Iran’s capabilities, but it’s still able to strike
stories.summary: CENTCOM commander testified before Congress that the war has reduced Iran's defense industry capabilities by approximately 90%. However, he stated the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps remains a major force and Iran retains the ability to carry out strikes.

stories.title: Israel’s Lebanon Strategy Is Self-Defeating
stories.summary: Analysis suggests that Israel's current strategy in Lebanon is counterproductive. The argument centers on the idea that a weakened Lebanese state lacks the capacity to disarm Hezbollah, undermining Israel's stated objectives.

stories.title: In Talks with Israel, Lebanon is Walking a Thin Line
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon are conducting their third round of direct talks on border disputes, Hezbollah's disarmament, and ongoing Israeli military operations in Lebanon. The United States is driving the negotiations, framing them as pursuit of a comprehensive peace and security agreement. Lebanon's government faces domestic political risks from any broad deal that targets Hezbollah.

stories.title: Ukraine withstands unprecedented drone assault of over 1,500 UAVs – Defense Minister Advisor
stories.summary: A Ukrainian Defense Ministry advisor said Ukraine withstood an unprecedented Russian drone assault involving over 1,500 UAVs. The advisor described it as one of the most difficult attacks in recent times, noting that air defense systems successfully countered the attempt to overwhelm them.

stories.title: Iran, Taiwan, and trade: Trump’s high‑stakes return to Beijing
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing for the first time in nine years. The summit agenda included trade tensions, Taiwan, and Iran-related issues.

stories.title: Russia starts ninth project 22350 frigate in St. Petersburg built for Mach-8 hypersonic anti-ship missiles that have already hit Ukraine
stories.summary: Russia launched its ninth Project 22350 frigate at a St. Petersburg shipyard. The 135-meter warships are designed for open-ocean operations and equipped to carry Mach-8 hypersonic anti-ship missiles that have already been used against targets in Ukraine.

stories.title: Bessent says US, China discussing ‘board of investment’
stories.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the U.S. and China are discussing the creation of a "board of investment" during President Trump's visit to Beijing. The proposed board would allow Chinese companies to invest in the United States in non-sensitive industries.

stories.title: Lauder: Israel must urgently repair ties with Diaspora Jews before it is too late - interview
stories.summary: World Jewish Congress President Ronald Lauder warned in an interview that Israel must urgently repair its relationship with Diaspora Jews. He cautioned that Israel can no longer take Diaspora support for granted amid contemporary challenges facing the global Jewish community.

stories.title: Russia pummels Kyiv, killing at least 10 as advance in the east slows
stories.summary: Russia struck Kyiv with hundreds of drones and dozens of missiles over several hours early Thursday, killing at least 10 people. The attack further diminished prospects for a halt to the ongoing Russian invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: Egypt unveils two colorfully decorated, restored, New Kingdom tombs in Luxor
stories.summary: Egyptian authorities unveiled two restored New Kingdom tombs in Luxor belonging to Rabuya and his son Samut from the 18th Dynasty. The burial chambers feature colorful scenes depicting agriculture, harvests, crafts, and food production.

stories.title: 'A desire to lower the temperature on both sides', expert says as Trump meets Xi
stories.summary: Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping began a series of meetings in Beijing on Thursday. Analyst Garret Martin of American University noted the summit produced little substance but indicated "a desire to lower the temperature on both sides."

stories.title: IDF colonel suspended due to sexual harassment investigation
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces suspended a colonel following the opening of a Military Police investigation into alleged sexual harassment. The complaint involved an incident of a sexual nature reported by a lieutenant colonel.

stories.title: US Air Force rescues 11 after plane crashes into waters off Florida coast
stories.summary: The US Air Force rescued 11 people after a private plane crashed into the Atlantic Ocean off the coast of Florida. Footage released by the Air Force documented the rescue operation.

stories.title: Iran’s Navy won’t rebuild for 5 to 10 years, country unable to support proxies: CENTCOM
stories.summary: CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper told the Senate Armed Services Committee that Iran's navy will need five to ten years to rebuild. He stated that Hamas, Hezbollah, and the Houthis are all currently cut off from Iranian weapons supply and support.

stories.title: Germany's Merz calls for EU budget overhaul as battle looms
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called for an overhaul of the European Union's budget system, describing it as outdated. Merz advocated a streamlined approach prioritizing defense spending and improving the bloc's competitiveness.

stories.title: UNSC to hold emergency meeting over massive Russian attacks on Ukraine on May 19
stories.summary: The United Nations Security Council will hold an emergency meeting on May 19 to address the sharp escalation of Russian strikes on Ukrainian civilians and critical infrastructure.

stories.title: US infantry’s drone-warfare experiments are getting bigger
stories.summary: The U.S. Army's Project Flytrap 5.0 expanded infantry drone-warfare experiments to operations involving teams of hundreds of drones, with even larger-scale exercises planned for the future.

stories.title: Starmer will not attempt to block Burnham from standing to be MP in Makerfield - UK politics live
stories.summary: Labour MP Josh Simons announced he would stand down from his Makerfield seat to allow Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham to run in the resulting byelection. UK Defence Minister Al Carns reportedly plans to launch his own Labour leadership bid. Prime Minister Keir Starmer will not attempt to block Burnham's candidacy.

stories.title: The Adversarial: Maximalist Demands, Victory Day, and a Summit
stories.summary: Negotiations between the United States and Iran appear closer to a breakdown than a breakthrough, a month after high-level talks in Pakistan. Washington has intensified sanctions under its "Economic Fury" campaign and maintained a blockade of Iranian shipping, threatening the ceasefire President Trump announced on April 7.

stories.title: What does the US hope to achieve from Lebanon-Israel talks?
stories.summary: As Israeli military operations in Lebanon continue, the United States is facilitating Lebanon-Israel ceasefire talks in Washington. Hezbollah has voiced opposition to the negotiations.

stories.title: Iran expands tiered internet access amid continued online blackout
stories.summary: Iran has expanded a tiered internet access system while maintaining broader online restrictions imposed during the ongoing war. Iranian citizens have faced limited internet connectivity throughout the conflict.

stories.title: US jury awards $63m in damages to Boeing 737 MAX crash victim’s family
stories.summary: A U.S. jury awarded $63 million in damages to the family of a Boeing 737 MAX crash victim. Nearly all civil lawsuits related to the crashes had previously been settled out of court.

stories.title: US Border Patrol chief resigns, in latest Trump team shake-up
stories.summary: U.S. Border Patrol Chief Michael Banks announced his resignation, marking the latest leadership shake-up within the Trump administration's immigration enforcement apparatus. Banks confirmed his departure in a Fox News interview, later verified by the Department of Homeland Security.

stories.title: UK health secretary resigns, setting up potential leadership challenge to Starmer
stories.summary: UK Health Secretary Wes Streeting resigned, saying he had lost confidence in Prime Minister Keir Starmer. Former Deputy PM Angela Rayner indicated she is ready for a potential leadership contest.

stories.title: Part of Somalia at risk of famine for first time since 2022
stories.summary: A U.N.-sponsored report warned that a district in southern Somalia is at risk of famine, the first time part of the country has reached such a critical hunger level since 2022.

stories.title: ‘God gave us this city’: Israeli nationalists join Jerusalem Day protest to mark city’s capture
stories.summary: Israeli nationalist demonstrators marched through the Muslim quarter of Jerusalem's Old City during the annual Jerusalem Day event, chanting anti-Arab slogans. National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir participated in the state-sponsored march marking the anniversary of the city's 1967 capture and annexation.

stories.title: Death toll in Russia’s attack on Kyiv rises to nine
stories.summary: As of 18:00 on May 14, nine people were confirmed killed in Kyiv as a result of Russia's massive attack on the city, including a 13-year-old child. The toll later continued to rise.

stories.title: Governor Reshuffle in Border Regions Shows How Kremlin Is Militarizing Russia’s Elites, Experts Say
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin appointed a decorated army general and a former official from occupied Ukraine to govern the Belgorod and Bryansk border regions. Analysts say the reshuffle reflects the Kremlin's increasing militarization of regional leadership.

stories.title: Judge orders Trump administration to return Colombian woman deported to DRC back to the US
stories.summary: A U.S. federal judge ordered the Trump administration to return Colombian citizen Adriana María Quiroz Zapata to the United States after she was deported to the Democratic Republic of Congo. Judge Richard Leon ruled the deportation was "likely illegal," noting the DRC had refused to accept her.

stories.title: Iran accuses United Arab Emirates of being 'active partner' in US-Israeli war
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi accused the United Arab Emirates of being an "active partner" in the US-Israeli war against Iran. He referenced Israel's claim of a secret wartime meeting between Prime Minister Netanyahu and UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed, which Abu Dhabi denied.

stories.title: As rescuers clear rubble of Kyiv apartment building, Russia’s security council secretary lists same 2022 demands for ending war
stories.summary: Russia's Security Council Secretary reiterated the same demands for ending the war that Moscow presented during the failed 2022 Istanbul talks, issuing them from Bishkek. The statement came hours after Russia's largest two-day strike on Kyiv, which struck a residential apartment building.

stories.title: Iran allowing transit of Chinese vessels in Strait of Hormuz, Fars news reports
stories.summary: Iran has begun permitting some Chinese vessels to transit through the Strait of Hormuz following an understanding over Iranian management protocols for the waterway, according to Iran's semi-official Fars news agency.

stories.title: Iran and UAE clash at BRICS foreign ministers’ meeting
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi accused the UAE of direct involvement in military operations against Iran at a BRICS foreign ministers' meeting. The clash underscored rising tensions between the two countries amid the broader regional conflict involving Israel.

stories.title: What Happened in India’s West Bengal?
stories.summary: India's Bharatiya Janata Party won decisively in West Bengal state elections, ousting longtime incumbents. However, last-minute changes to voter rolls have prompted allegations of electoral irregularities and foul play.

stories.title: Israeli ultranationalists chant racist slogans during Jerusalem Day march
stories.summary: During the annual Jerusalem Day march through Jerusalem's Old City, Israeli ultranationalist participants chanted racist slogans and committed acts of violence against Palestinian residents, heightening tensions in the area.

stories.title: Hezbollah: Israel-Lebanon talks are ‘free concessions’
stories.summary: Hezbollah lawmaker Ali Ammar rejected ongoing direct talks between Israel and Lebanon in Washington, describing them as "free concessions" to Israel given the scale of Israeli military operations against Lebanon despite ceasefire arrangements.

stories.title: FIFA warned ‘gruelling heat’ could impact a quarter of World Cup games
stories.summary: Scientists have warned FIFA that global warming has significantly increased the risk of extreme heat since the 1994 US World Cup, potentially affecting up to a quarter of future World Cup matches.

stories.title: Israel’s Ben Gvir storms Al-Aqsa during Jerusalem Day march
stories.summary: Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir entered the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound in Jerusalem under heavy military protection during the annual Jerusalem Day celebrations.

stories.title: US reportedly dropped fraud charges against Indian billionaire after he hired Trump’s lawyer
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice is reportedly dropping fraud charges against Indian billionaire Gautam Adani after he hired Donald Trump's personal lawyer, Robert J. Giuffra Jr. Adani had been accused of conspiring to pay $250 million in bribes to Indian officials. At an April DOJ meeting, Giuffra offered a $10 billion U.S. investment in exchange for dropping the case.

stories.title: Activist flotilla leaves Turkey for Gaza weeks after Israel intercepted previous convoy
stories.summary: A flotilla of over 50 vessels carrying approximately 500 activists departed Turkey for Gaza, weeks after Israel intercepted a previous convoy. The flotilla includes activists who were arrested and released from the earlier attempt.

stories.title: Latvian Prime Minister resigns after controversy over stray Ukrainian drones
stories.summary: Latvian Prime Minister Evika Siliņa resigned after her coalition collapsed over the government's handling of stray Ukrainian drones that entered Latvian airspace from Russia. The crisis was triggered by her decision to fire Defence Minister Andris Sprūds, prompting the Progressives party to withdraw its support.

stories.title: Israeli tech company aiming to cool the Earth with masses of tiny particles
stories.summary: Israeli tech company Stardust Solutions is developing a plan to combat global warming by releasing millions of tons of reflective particles into the atmosphere. Critics have raised concerns about the risks of large-scale weather manipulation.

stories.title: Israelis chant ‘Death to Arabs’ during Jerusalem ‘Flag March’
stories.summary: Israeli ultranationalists chanted "Death to Arabs" and "May your villages burn" during the annual Flag March through Jerusalem's Old City. Palestinian shops were forced to close, and Israeli forces blocked Palestinian Muslims from accessing Al-Aqsa Mosque.

stories.title: Jerusalem Day: A son's tale of an Ammunition Hill hero
stories.summary: Alon Wald, whose father was a paratrooper killed at Ammunition Hill in Jerusalem during the 1967 Six-Day War, now manages the memorial site where his father fell. Wald was only 10 months old when his father died in the battle.

stories.title: B-52 modernization ‘stabilized’ after cost spikes, schedule delays, Air Force official says
stories.summary: A U.S. Air Force official said the B-52 bomber modernization program has been stabilized following cost increases and schedule delays. Representative Clay Higgins emphasized congressional scrutiny of the program's significant expenditures.

stories.title: Philippines senator wanted by the International Criminal Court flees from Senate
stories.summary: Philippine Senator Ronald dela Rosa, wanted by the International Criminal Court, fled from the Senate building where he had sought refuge to evade arrest. His escape occurred amid chaos after gunshots were exchanged between Senate security personnel and a government agent on Wednesday night.

stories.title: American poet Sasha Debevec-McKenney wins Dylan Thomas prize for ‘blistering’ debut poetry collection
stories.summary: American poet Sasha Debevec-McKenney won the Swansea University Dylan Thomas prize and its £20,000 award for her debut collection "Joy Is My Middle Name." The collection explores themes of race, addiction, and womanhood. The prize honors writers aged 39 or under.

stories.title: US House leaders announce bipartisan effort to combat sexual misconduct in Congress
stories.summary: House Speaker Mike Johnson and Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries announced a bipartisan taskforce to combat sexual misconduct in Congress. The effort is led by Representatives Kat Cammack and Teresa Leger Fernández, chairs of the Republican and Democratic women's caucuses. The announcement followed resignations of two congressmen amid misconduct allegations.

stories.title: Iran and UAE clash at Brics foreign ministers' meeting
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi accused the United Arab Emirates of direct involvement in military operations against Iran during a BRICS foreign ministers' meeting in New Delhi. The exchange followed UAE denials of a claim by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that he visited the Gulf state during the Iran conflict.

stories.title: FM Sybiha initiates UNSC meeting to respond to Russia’s killings of Ukrainian civilians
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha initiated an urgent United Nations Security Council meeting to address Russia's mass killings of Ukrainian civilians.

stories.title: Veteran Israel Air Force commanders abused young commanders, military police reveal
stories.summary: Israeli military police revealed that veteran Israel Air Force commanders subjected younger commanders to abusive 'initiation ceremonies' involving beatings and degradation. An investigation uncovered the pattern of hazing.

stories.title: Acute hunger grips nearly 20 million people in war-battered Sudan, says IPC
stories.summary: The Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) reported that nearly 20 million people in Sudan face acute hunger. The Norwegian Refugee Council warned that lack of access to food and health facilities will result in deaths.

stories.title: Palestinian President Abbas re-elected to lead Fatah movement
stories.summary: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas was unanimously re-elected as head and general commander of the Fatah movement. The vote was the first in 10 years and came amid questions about Fatah's legitimacy in confronting Israel's intensified operations.

stories.title: Netanyahu condemns racism against Ethiopians, decries Zalka murder at state memorial ceremony
stories.summary: Prime Minister Netanyahu condemned racism against Ethiopian Israelis at a state memorial ceremony, denouncing the murder of Yemanu Zalka. He said he called for the full weight of the law against the perpetrators.

stories.title: Amnesty condemns Israeli destruction of homes in south Syria
stories.summary: Amnesty International called for a war crimes investigation into the Israeli military's destruction of civilian homes in southern Syria.

stories.title: Russian Kh-101 missile that killed 12 in Kyiv was manufactured this quarter — after 21 EU sanctions packages
stories.summary: Analysis of a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile that killed 12 people in a Kyiv apartment building strike determined it was manufactured in the current quarter of 2025, despite 21 EU sanctions packages against Russia. The same missile type killed 31 people in a Ternopil apartment strike six months earlier.

stories.title: Iran convert formerly sentenced to death tells ‘Post’ Pope brought ‘shame’ by honoring envoy
stories.summary: An Iranian Christian convert who was formerly sentenced to death in Iran told the Jerusalem Post that Pope Leo brought 'shame' by honoring the Iranian ambassador to the Holy See. The honor was part of a ceremony recognizing several diplomats for long service.

stories.title: China's Xi woos Trump with state banquet: Taiwan on the table?
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping hosted US President Donald Trump at an official state banquet in Beijing, with events at the Temple of Heaven and the Forbidden City. Taiwan was among the key issues expected to be discussed during the summit.

stories.title: Labour MP to stand down to allow Burnham run for byelection amid leadership row
stories.summary: Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham confirmed he would seek to stand in a byelection in Makerfield after Labour MP Josh Simons announced his resignation from the seat. Burnham's return to parliament could position him to challenge Labour leader Keir Starmer for the party leadership.

stories.title: Dozens of ships set sail from Turkey as Gaza flotilla tries second blockade run
stories.summary: Dozens of ships departed from Marmaris, Turkey, as part of a Gaza flotilla attempting a second run at the Israeli naval blockade. The activist group's ship tracker showed the vessels heading south from the departure point.

stories.title: Israelis chant anti-Palestinian slogans at Jerusalem march
stories.summary: Thousands of Israeli nationalists marched through the Muslim Quarter of Jerusalem's Old City on Thursday under heavy security, chanting anti-Palestinian slogans during the annual event.

stories.title: Cuba plunged deeper into fuel crisis amid 22-hour blackouts
stories.summary: Cuba experienced a deepening fuel crisis after officials announced the country had completely run out of diesel and fuel oil, leading to nationwide blackouts lasting up to 22 hours.

stories.title: Trump says Xi offered help to open Hormuz, vowed not to arm Iran
stories.summary: President Trump said Chinese President Xi Jinping offered China's assistance in reopening the Strait of Hormuz and pledged not to supply military equipment to Iran during its war with the US and Israel.

stories.title: Two-thirds of Israelis support immediately forming commission of inquiry into October 7, poll finds
stories.summary: A poll found that two-thirds of Israelis support immediately forming a commission of inquiry into the October 7 attacks. The main disagreement is whether the judiciary should be involved in the inquiry.

stories.title: Closing arguments begin in high-stakes Musk v OpenAI courtroom showdown
stories.summary: Closing arguments began in Elon Musk's lawsuit against Sam Altman and OpenAI at a federal courthouse in Oakland, California. A nine-person jury will deliberate on whether Altman and the AI firm are liable. The weeks-long trial has featured prominent tech industry figures as witnesses.

stories.title: Ukraine urges UN to condemn Russian terror attack on humanitarian convoy in Kherson region
stories.summary: Ukraine called on the United Nations to condemn a Russian attack on a UN humanitarian convoy in the Kherson region, describing it as a terrorist act.

stories.title: High Court brushes off AG’s concern over Gofman meetings with Mossad official
stories.summary: Israel's High Court dismissed concerns raised by Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara's office regarding meetings between incoming Mossad chief Gofman and a Mossad official, which the AG feared could influence petitions against his appointment.

stories.title: Watchdog groups urge Senate to investigate Samuel Alito over oil stock conflicts
stories.summary: A coalition of government watchdog groups urged the Senate Judiciary Committee to investigate Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito over potential ethics violations. The groups allege Alito, the only justice with holdings in energy companies, may have conflicts of interest when participating in cases that could benefit the oil industry.

stories.title: Lebanon to press Israel to ceasefire at Washington talks, Lebanese official says
stories.summary: Lebanon plans to press Israel for a ceasefire extension during talks in Washington. The meeting marks the third round of negotiations since hostilities between Hezbollah and Israel reignited on March 2.

stories.title: Russia pummels Kyiv, killing three and denting peace hopes
stories.summary: Russia launched 675 attack drones and 56 missiles primarily targeting Kyiv, killing at least three people. The large-scale aerial assault has dampened hopes for near-term peace negotiations.

stories.title: Israeli nationalists hold parade marking their capture of East Jerusalem
stories.summary: Thousands of Israeli nationalists marched through the Muslim quarter of Jerusalem's Old City under heavy security on Thursday. The annual parade marks Israel's capture of East Jerusalem in the 1967 war nearly six decades ago.

stories.title: Xi-Trump summit day 1: everything you need to know from the meeting in Beijing
stories.summary: U.S. President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping held their first day of summit talks in Beijing, covering a broad range of bilateral and global issues. The meeting began with an elaborate welcome ceremony at the Great Hall of the People.

stories.title: Iraqi parliament approves partial government led by PM Zaidi
stories.summary: Iraq's parliament approved a partial government led by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, a businessman who took office after months of political deadlock and increasing pressure from the United States.

stories.title: Zelensky orders military to prepare a ‘response’ after Russia’s large-scale attack kills eight in Kyiv
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky ordered the Ukrainian military to prepare a response to large-scale Russian strikes on Ukrainian cities that killed eight people in Kyiv. The attacks followed the end of a three-day ceasefire.

stories.title: Why Lebanon-Israel talks could collapse over Hezbollah
stories.summary: Lebanon-Israel talks in Washington face a key impasse: Israel's envoy has proposed gradual disarmament of Hezbollah, while Lebanon insists a full ceasefire must take effect before any such discussions begin.

stories.title: Why Lebanon-Israel talks could collapse over Hezbollah
stories.summary: Lebanon-Israel talks in Washington face potential collapse over disagreements regarding Hezbollah. Israel's envoy proposed gradual disarmament of Hezbollah, while Lebanon insists a full ceasefire must take effect before further discussions.

stories.title: U.K. Health Minister Wes Streeting resigns
stories.summary: UK Health Minister Wes Streeting resigned from his position and called for a Labour Party leadership contest to replace Prime Minister Keir Starmer. Streeting stated it was clear Starmer would not lead Labour into the next general election.

stories.title: US moves to end fraud cases against Asia’s richest person, Gautam Adani
stories.summary: U.S. authorities are moving to drop fraud charges against Indian billionaire Gautam Adani, Asia's richest person. The Justice Department may announce the decision as soon as this week, and the SEC is also working to settle a parallel civil fraud case.

stories.title: Judge bans reporting on trial of six men accused of sexually assaulting teenage girls in Bristol
stories.summary: Six men went on trial at Bristol Crown Court accused of grooming and sexually assaulting vulnerable teenage girls over several years. All six deny the charges involving multiple complainants. A judge imposed reporting restrictions on the case amid a dispute with media over transparency.

stories.title: Justice in Baghdad: Iraq convicts notorious Saddam Hussein-era torturer
stories.summary: An Iraqi court convicted a notorious torturer from the Saddam Hussein era in Baghdad. The conviction is seen as a significant step in Iraq's efforts to deliver justice for victims of the former regime.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia floats non-aggression pact with Iran and regional states: Report
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia is reportedly proposing a non-aggression pact among Middle Eastern states including Iran, modeled on the 1975 Helsinki Accords. The initiative aims to reduce regional tensions, according to the Financial Times citing western diplomatic sources.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces strike Russian air defense system, radar in Belgorod region
stories.summary: Ukrainian defense forces struck a Russian Tor surface-to-air missile system and a Yastreb counter-battery radar station in Russia's Belgorod region. They also hit a Russian logistics depot in occupied Crimea.

stories.title: Mental health system is broken, says mother of Nottingham triple killer
stories.summary: Celeste Calocane, mother of Nottingham triple killer Valdo Calocane, testified at an inquiry into his June 2023 attacks, saying the UK mental health system is broken. Calocane, who has paranoid schizophrenia, killed students Barnaby Webber and Grace O'Malley-Kumar and caretaker Ian Coates before being sentenced to a suspended hospital order.

stories.title: Kremlin Rejects EU Mediation in Ukraine Peace Talks
stories.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov rejected European Union mediation in Ukraine peace talks, accusing Brussels of being a "direct participant" in the conflict due to its continued support for Ukraine.

stories.title: UAE an ‘active partner’ in US-Israeli war, says Iran
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi accused the UAE of being an "active partner" in US-Israeli aggression against Iran. Araghchi cited what Israel described as a secret meeting with the UAE, which Abu Dhabi denied took place.

stories.title: ‘May your village burn’: Israeli Flag March returns to East Jerusalem
stories.summary: During the annual Flag March through East Jerusalem's Old City, far-right Israeli participants attacked Palestinian residents and chanted racist slogans, intensifying violence in the area.

stories.title: Pope Leo decries European military spending as ‘betrayal’ of diplomacy
stories.summary: Pope Leo condemned rising European military spending as a "betrayal" of diplomacy. The Pope said the world was being "maimed by wars" and called for greater emphasis on diplomatic solutions to global conflicts.

stories.title: Israel suing NYT over piece on sexual abuse of Palestinians
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has threatened legal action against The New York Times over an article publishing Palestinian testimonies alleging sexual abuse by Israeli forces.

stories.title: War criminal Ratko Mladić's jail release request denied
stories.summary: A UN judge denied convicted war criminal Ratko Mladić's request for release from prison in The Hague. The judge acknowledged the 84-year-old is in the final stages of his life but ruled that his detention conditions ensure maximum comfort.

stories.title: Will London's Green gains reshape local policy on Palestine?
stories.summary: Following gains by the Green Party in London local elections, campaigners and council candidates are pointing to pension fund divestment as a mechanism for shifting local authority policy related to Palestine.

stories.title: Pope Leo decries European military spending as ‘betrayal’ of diplomacy
stories.summary: Pope Leo criticized rising European military spending, calling it a "betrayal" of diplomacy. The pontiff argued that rearmament increases tensions, diverts resources from education and health, and enriches elites indifferent to the common good.

stories.title: King Charles comforts wounded Jewish community in London’s Golders Green
stories.summary: King Charles visited London's Golders Green neighborhood to meet with members of the Jewish community following a terrorist stabbing attack that wounded two people and arson attacks on ambulances belonging to a Jewish emergency medical service.

stories.title: Israel says it will sue New York Times over article on sexual abuse of Palestinian prisoners
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar threatened to sue the New York Times for defamation over a Nicholas Kristof essay detailing allegations of sexual abuse of Palestinian detainees in Israeli military custody. Media law experts have questioned the viability of such a lawsuit.

stories.title: The Palestinian game fighting to exist
stories.summary: A video game developer from the occupied West Bank is creating a game based on a 75-year-old Palestinian folk tale, working to preserve cultural heritage through the gaming medium.

stories.title: Russia’s Federal Penitentiary Service acknowledges prison population drop is partly due to war recruitment
stories.summary: Russia's Federal Penitentiary Service director Arkady Gostev acknowledged that the country's prison population has dropped to 282,000 over the past four and a half years, partly due to wartime recruitment of inmates. His remarks were cited by state news agency TASS.

stories.title: Netanyahu's coalition moves to seek early vote in Israel
stories.summary: Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition moved to dissolve the Knesset and pave the way for snap elections amid deepening tensions with ultra-Orthodox parties over coalition disputes.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia suggests Middle East non-aggression pact with Iran
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia is reportedly floating a non-aggression agreement between Middle Eastern states and Iran, drawing on the 1970s Helsinki Process as a model. The proposal was reported by the Financial Times, citing western diplomatic sources.

stories.title: Syria seeks 'peace not normalisation' with Israel, FM says
stories.summary: Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani stated that Damascus is pursuing a US-mediated security agreement with Israel while rejecting any imposed normalization, emphasizing Syria seeks "peace not normalisation."

stories.title: Book claims Macron’s wife slapped him over Iranian actress texts
stories.summary: A new book alleges that French First Lady Brigitte Macron slapped President Emmanuel Macron aboard a plane after discovering text messages he had exchanged with an Iranian actress.

stories.title: President Zelensky: 94% of Russian drones, 73% of missiles intercepted during two-day attack
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky reported that Ukrainian air defenses intercepted 94% of Russian drones and 73% of missiles during a two-day attack involving 1,567 drones and 56 missiles. He instructed intelligence services to propose response options.

stories.title: Pakistan successfully test fires Fatah-IV cruise missile: ISPR
stories.summary: Pakistan's Army Rocket Force Command successfully test-fired the indigenously developed Fatah-IV ground-launched cruise missile. The Inter-Services Public Relations stated the weapon system features advanced avionics and navigational aids capable of engaging long-range targets with high precision.

stories.title: Putin visit to China will take place very soon, Kremlin says
stories.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov announced that Russian President Vladimir Putin will visit China very soon, with preparations already complete. No specific date was given for the trip.

stories.title: Trump invites Chinese President Xi Jinping for September 24 visit at White House
stories.summary: President Donald Trump invited Chinese President Xi Jinping to visit the White House on September 24. The White House said the two leaders had a productive meeting and discussed ways to enhance economic cooperation.

stories.title: Former Ekho Moskvy editor-in-chief fined for cooperating with ‘undesirable’ organization
stories.summary: Alexei Venediktov, former editor-in-chief of the shuttered independent Russian radio station Ekho Moskvy, was fined for cooperating with an organization designated as "undesirable" by Russian authorities, according to the Slovo Zashchite project.

stories.title: Trump-Xi Beijing summit tests leverage on trade, Taiwan, Iran - analysis
stories.summary: The Trump-Xi summit in Beijing addressed trade tariffs, rare earth minerals, Taiwan, and Iran. Analysts suggest the temporary agreements may provide short-term wins for both leaders while leaving deeper strategic conflicts unresolved.

stories.title: Settlers assault left-wing activist in West Bank; IDF detains activists instead of attackers
stories.summary: Israeli settlers assaulted the director of Peace Now, a left-wing organization, in the occupied West Bank. The IDF subsequently detained the left-wing activists rather than the attackers, reportedly after receiving a claim that the activists had initiated the violence.

stories.title: Iran urges BRICS nations to condemn US-Israeli war aggression
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi called on BRICS member nations to condemn what he described as US-Israeli military aggression. Araghchi also accused the United Arab Emirates of direct involvement in military operations against Iran.

stories.title: Trump says Xi offered help on Iran as China seeks to keep Hormuz open
stories.summary: President Trump said Chinese President Xi Jinping offered to help broker an end to the Iran conflict and ensure freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz during their Beijing summit. The offer reflects how Middle East tensions have become intertwined with U.S.-China relations.

stories.title: CBO’s $1.2 trillion Golden Dome estimate based on bad data: Guetlein
stories.summary: Lieutenant General Michael Guetlein disputed the Congressional Budget Office's $1.2 trillion cost estimate for the Golden Dome missile defense system, calling it based on flawed data. Guetlein, who previously estimated the project at $185 billion, said the Department of Defense plans to deploy an operational homeland defense system by 2028.

stories.title: Hezbollah claims attacks on Israeli army in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah claimed it carried out a series of drone strikes on Israeli military positions in southern Lebanon, targeting sites in Adasah, the Balat outpost, an area near the Deir Siryan river, and a Merkava tank in Taybeh.

stories.title: Iran and UAE clash at BRICS foreign ministers' meeting
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi clashed with UAE representatives at the BRICS foreign ministers' meeting, arguing that US bases and an alliance with Israel do not provide the UAE with genuine security and urging Abu Dhabi to reconsider its Iran policy.

stories.title: Arab party Hadash to pick new leaders, hopes to energize efforts for Joint List revival
stories.summary: The Arab-Israeli party Hadash is set to elect new leadership in an internal vote, with former MK Yousef Jabareen expected to replace Ayman Odeh as party head. The party is shifting focus toward crime issues in the Triangle region and exploring expansion into the Negev.

stories.title: Kyiv declares May 15 Day of Mourning
stories.summary: The city of Kyiv declared May 15 a Day of Mourning for victims killed in a massive combined Russian attack on May 14.

stories.title: Israel's defense minister condemns soccer star Lamine Yamal for flying Palestinian flag
stories.summary: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz condemned FC Barcelona player Lamine Yamal for waving a Palestinian flag, calling on the club to make clear there is "no place for incitement or support of terrorism."

stories.title: The case for a $24 Billion Special Operations budget
stories.summary: Former acting Defense Secretary Chris Miller and Phil Anderson of SOF Action argue that U.S. Special Operations Command's budget should rise to $24 billion. They note SOCOM's budget has remained flat since fiscal year 2019 while demand for special operations capabilities has increased 300 percent over the past five years.

stories.title: Iranian foreign minister: No military solution to the conflict
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that military force cannot resolve the conflict with the US and Israel, saying Iran 'will not bow down.' He dismissed renewed threats as ineffective, speaking to Iranian media on Thursday.

stories.title: Iraq’s parliament approves new Ali al-Zaidi government
stories.summary: Iraq's parliament approved a new government led by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, who was sworn in along with 14 cabinet ministers. However, lawmakers failed to reach consensus on several remaining ministerial posts.

stories.title: Can Israel actually sue 'The New York Times' over 'dog rape' column? - explainer
stories.summary: An explainer analyzes whether Israel can successfully sue The New York Times over a column about alleged abuse of Palestinian detainees. Legal experts say the procedure and chances of success depend largely on the jurisdiction where the suit is filed.

stories.title: On the Radar: Brazil’s Anti-Crime Push, an Arrest in Honduras, and Colombia’s Total Peace Gamble
stories.summary: Brazil announced a multibillion-dollar strategy to combat organized crime. In Honduras, authorities arrested a former mayor linked to a murder case. In Colombia, President Gustavo Petro's attempt to suspend arrest warrants for Gulf Clan leaders was rejected.

stories.title: Two Trypillia settlements in Ternopil region added to UNESCO Tentative List
stories.summary: Two Trypillia-culture settlements located at Verteba Cave and near the village of Hlybochok in Ukraine's Ternopil region have been added to the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List.

stories.title: Anas al-Tikriti, British-Iraqi founder of Cordoba, denied entry to Canada
stories.summary: Anas al-Tikriti, the British-Iraqi founder of the Cordoba Foundation, was denied entry to Canada this week. He had planned to speak at a Muslim Association of Canada convention in Toronto.

stories.title: British Palestinians and Arabs call for 'equal protection' from Starmer
stories.summary: Prominent British Palestinians and Arabs sent a message to Prime Minister Keir Starmer calling for 'equal protection' ahead of a Nakba 78 march in London on Saturday. A far-right rally led by Tommy Robinson is planned for the same time, prompting Metropolitan Police warnings.

stories.title: Iran hangs man on Israel spy charges, another over protests
stories.summary: Iran executed two men, one convicted of spying for Israel and another over involvement in protests. The executions are part of an intensified wave of hangings during the ongoing US-Israeli conflict with Iran.

stories.title: US Centcom says it redirected 70 vessels since blockade of Hormuz began
stories.summary: US Central Command reported it has redirected 70 commercial vessels and disabled four others to enforce its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. Iran said it would allow ships to pass if they comply with its navy, and multiple Chinese ships reportedly crossed the Strait ahead of a Trump-Xi meeting.

stories.title: Iranian, Russian foreign ministers hold talks at BRICS meeting in India
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov on the sidelines of a BRICS foreign ministers' meeting in New Delhi. The two diplomats held bilateral talks during the gathering in India.

stories.title: Gwadar University VC, pro-vice chancellor 'go missing' while travelling to Quetta
stories.summary: The vice chancellor and pro-vice chancellor of the University of Gwadar have gone missing while traveling from Gwadar to Quetta in Balochistan, Pakistan. Dr Abdul Razzaq Sabir and Syed Manzoor Ahmed, along with a driver and another university employee, left Wednesday morning but had not arrived after 24 hours.

stories.title: Russia says it's establishing 'full partnership' with Afghan Taliban
stories.summary: A senior Russian security official said Moscow is establishing a "full-fledged partnership" with Afghanistan's ruling Taliban government. Russia is also encouraging other countries in the region to expand cooperation with Kabul.

stories.title: What is Trump’s Project Vault?
stories.summary: The Trump administration's Project Vault initiative aims to create a strategic reserve of critical minerals to shield domestic industries from supply disruptions. The effort was prompted by China's restriction of rare earth magnet exports in retaliation for U.S. tariffs, which nearly shut down global car manufacturing operations.

stories.title: UK ‘Zero Net’ Miliband’s policy questioned as a threat to British security, ‘China dominates all the green technology’
stories.summary: UK Energy Secretary Ed Miliband faces criticism that his net-zero green energy policies could give China a strategic advantage over Britain's economy. Critics argue that Beijing's dominance in green technology manufacturing could create dependency, undermining the energy security goals intended to reduce reliance on Russian fuel.

stories.title: Eurovision viewership drops sharply amid Gaza war boycott
stories.summary: Eurovision viewership dropped significantly compared to 2025's semi-finals. The decline is attributed to a boycott movement over Israel's participation in the competition amid the war in Gaza.

stories.title: Iran’s small businesses collapse under war, inflation and internet blackout
stories.summary: Iran's economy is severely deteriorating after more than two months of war, ceasefire, and blockade. Prices for some goods have tripled or quadrupled, the currency has lost 60 percent of its value, at least two million jobs have been lost, and an international internet blackout has persisted for over 75 days.

stories.title: Trump says Xi pledged not to arm Iran
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said Chinese President Xi Jinping pledged not to send arms to Iran and offered help reopening the Strait of Hormuz during their meeting in Beijing. Xi also stated he is 'ready to work' with Trump on the issue.

stories.title: Ukrainian USFs hit Russia’s air defense system, communications complex, drone command post
stories.summary: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces struck several Russian military targets across the Luhansk, Donetsk, and Zaporizhzhia regions. The targets included an air defense system, a communications complex, and a drone command post.

stories.title: Israel Aerospace Industries to merge with Green Pine radar developer Elta Systems
stories.summary: Israel Aerospace Industries announced a merger with Elta Systems, the Ashdod-based developer of the Green Pine radar system. Elta produces advanced technologies including high-power radars and various interception systems.

stories.title: UN chief calls on Israel to abolish Oct 7 military tribunal
stories.summary: The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights urged Israel to repeal a new law establishing a military tribunal for Palestinians accused of involvement in the October 7 attacks.

stories.title: ‘Mom, I’m at our house’: How this war reporter covered the horrors of Sudan’s war | Yousra Elbagir
stories.summary: Sky News UK Africa correspondent Yousra Elbagir has drawn praise for her coverage of Sudan's war, now in its fourth year. The conflict has become the world's worst humanitarian crisis, displacing millions across the country.

stories.title: Karachi's Shahrah-i-Bhutto to be fully open to public by end of May: Sharjeel Memon
stories.summary: Sindh Senior Minister Sharjeel Memon announced that the 39-kilometre Shahrah-i-Bhutto Expressway in Karachi will be fully opened to the public by the end of May. The project was reported to be 88.2 percent complete as of March, with Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah having directed full completion by April 2026.

stories.title: Yemen gov’t, Houthis to release more than 1,600 POWs in ‘largest’ swap
stories.summary: The Yemeni government and Houthi forces agreed to exchange more than 1,600 prisoners of war in what is described as the largest such swap. The UN-backed deal will be facilitated by the International Committee of the Red Cross.

stories.title: US court suspends sanctions on UN rapporteur Francesca Albanese
stories.summary: A US federal judge temporarily blocked sanctions imposed on Francesca Albanese, the UN Special Rapporteur on the Palestinian territories. The Wednesday ruling suspended enforcement of the measures while the case proceeds.

stories.title: After the Iran war, could Israel's focus shift towards Turkey?
stories.summary: The article examines whether Israel's strategic focus could shift toward Turkey following the war with Iran. Israeli political elites are increasingly framing Turkey as a rival, potentially creating a new Middle Eastern fault line between Ankara and Tel Aviv.

stories.title: Lamine Yamal divides opinion with Palestinian flag gesture
stories.summary: A mural of FC Barcelona teenager Lamine Yamal was painted in Gaza after the player waved a Palestinian flag, generating divided reactions internationally.

stories.title: British Palestinians and Arabs call for 'equal protection' from Starmer
stories.summary: British Palestinians and Arabs sent a letter to UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer calling for equal protection, stating that pro-Palestinian marches in London are "spaces of shared humanity" rather than spaces of hate.

stories.title: Latvian Prime Minister Silina resigns over handling of Ukraine drone incidents
stories.summary: Latvian Prime Minister Evika Siliņa announced her resignation on Thursday over criticism of her government's handling of recent drone incursion incidents related to the Ukraine conflict. Her departure triggered the collapse of the centre-right coalition government, months before elections scheduled for October.

stories.title: Ukraine issue could end up on margins of U.S.-China talks, diplomat says
stories.summary: A diplomat indicated that the Ukraine conflict may be discussed only on the margins of upcoming U.S.-China talks between President Trump and President Xi Jinping. The main focus of the negotiations is expected to center on the economy, tariffs, technology, and global trade.

stories.title: 'Extremely positive and productive talks': Trump praises Xi meeting
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping warned U.S. President Donald Trump during a closed-door meeting in Beijing that missteps on Taiwan could lead to conflict between the two nations. The more than two-hour session was followed by a banquet where both leaders emphasized cooperation. Trump described the talks as "extremely positive and productive."

stories.title: UK: Keir Starmer is fighting for his political survival
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces a potential leadership challenge from within the Labour Party, with Health Secretary Wes Streeting expected to contest. Despite a public address and Wednesday's King's Speech, Starmer has been unable to quell internal party dissent over his leadership.

stories.title: Truck driver arrested after accident leaves 1 highway worker dead, 5 others hurt
stories.summary: A truck driver was arrested in Hong Kong after his vehicle struck a parked minivan on a closed section of the Cheung Tsing Highway in Tsing Yi, killing one highway worker. Five others were injured, including four South Korean tourists whose vehicle had pulled over due to a burst tyre.

stories.title: US-China priority is 'economic relationship':  Trump 'heavily prioritising trade and investment'
stories.summary: Analyst David Sacks of the Council on Foreign Relations discussed the U.S.-China relationship, noting that trade and investment are being heavily prioritized by the Trump administration. He observed that Taiwan has receded from Washington's immediate agenda, while semiconductor sovereignty, trade diplomacy, and energy security remain key dimensions of strategic competition.

stories.title: Israel’s Netanyahu says suing New York Times over Palestinian rape article
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced plans to sue The New York Times over a column by Nicholas Kristof that detailed allegations of sexual violence committed by Israeli forces against Palestinians.

stories.title: Russia’s 1500-drone strike on Ukraine was timed to Trump’s arrival in Beijing — Ukrainian Colonel explains why
stories.summary: Ukrainian Colonel Dmytro Kashchenko said Russia's approximately 1,500-drone strike on Ukraine was deliberately timed to coincide with U.S. President Trump's arrival in Beijing. He said Russia exploited a Victory Day lull to redeploy air defenses around Moscow and stockpile drones for the attack.

stories.title: Sanctioned State Duma Lawmaker Appointed as Russia’s Next Human Rights Chief
stories.summary: Yana Lantratova, a sanctioned State Duma lawmaker, has been appointed as Russia's next human rights commissioner. She has been accused of playing a key role in the alleged systematic transfer of children from occupied Ukrainian territories to Russia.

stories.title: Will Ukraine corruption scandal reach Volodymyr Zelenskyy?
stories.summary: Ukrainian authorities have widened a corruption investigation to include Andriy Yermak, the former head of the presidential office. Questions are growing over whether the scandal could implicate President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

stories.title: Corruption in Ukraine: Will this scandal reach Zelenskyy?
stories.summary: Ukrainian authorities have taken action against Andriy Yermak, the former head of President Zelensky's presidential office, as part of a widening corruption investigation. The case raises questions about whether the scandal could reach President Zelensky himself.

stories.title: Farooq Abdullah backs RSS leader Dattatreya Hosabale’s call for dialogue with Pakistan
stories.summary: Former Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Farooq Abdullah expressed support for RSS leader Dattatreya Hosabale's call for dialogue with Pakistan. Speaking in Srinagar, Abdullah also welcomed former Indian Army chief M.M. Naravane's backing of Hosabale's position.

stories.title: Chinese FM's remarks to Dar on Iran war 'misrepresented' in some media reports, call held with cordiality: FO
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Office stated that media reports misrepresented Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi's remarks during a call with Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar. Chinese state outlet Xinhua had reported that Wang urged Pakistan to step up mediation efforts between the United States and Iran, but Pakistan's FO said the call was held with cordiality.

stories.title: Saudi PIF named official supporter of 2026 World Cup
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund was named an official tournament supporter for the 2026 FIFA World Cup in North America and Asia. The announcement was made on Thursday.

stories.title: Xi and Trump set sights on stability for China and the US – with a note of caution
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump met at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing and agreed to prioritize stability in bilateral relations over the next three years. Trump invited Xi and first lady Peng Liyuan to visit the White House.

stories.title: Latvian PM resigns over handling of stray Ukrainian drones
stories.summary: Latvian Prime Minister Evika Silina resigned after facing criticism over her government's handling of stray Ukrainian drones that entered Latvian territory.

stories.title: Estonia urges Ramstein countries to allocate 0.25% of GDP to Ukraine annually
stories.summary: Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna urged Ramstein coalition countries to allocate 0.25% of GDP annually to military aid for Ukraine. Estonia has already adopted this benchmark and is calling on allies to follow its example.

stories.title: Trump-Xi meeting was 'good', says White House
stories.summary: The White House described the Trump-Xi meeting as "good" but made no mention of discussions on Taiwan. Taipei indicated it had received no surprise messaging from the summit so far.

stories.title: Ukraine hit by second day of large-scale Russian missile and drone strikes
stories.summary: Russia struck Ukraine with large-scale missile and drone attacks for a second consecutive day, with Kyiv bearing the heaviest bombardment. At least eight people were killed in the capital, including a 13-year-old, and 44 were injured. Officials warned Moscow may be attempting to overwhelm Ukrainian air defense systems.

stories.title: USVs could be ‘alternate options’ for missions for stretched manned fleet: Navy official
stories.summary: A U.S. Navy official indicated that unmanned surface vessels are emerging as alternative, modular force elements for missions where deploying a large manned combatant ship would be too costly or disproportionate to the task.

stories.title: Butkevych at the Lviv Media Forum — we can neither flee nor freeze, because our reality is us
stories.summary: Former prisoner of war and human rights defender Butkevych spoke at the Lviv Media Forum in Ukraine, arguing that propaganda constitutes a war over whether people act as agents of reality or are reduced to objects of manipulation.

stories.title: Houthis, Yemen government agree biggest prisoner swap of war
stories.summary: Yemen's internationally recognized government and Houthi rebels agreed to exchange more than 1,600 prisoners under a UN-backed deal. It is the largest detainee swap since the Yemeni civil war began.

stories.title: Blacklists, corruption and frontline needs: Ukraine tackles an arms-export puzzle
stories.summary: Ukraine, after years of struggling to supply its approximately one million active-duty soldiers, is grappling with whether to allow domestic arms manufacturers to export weapons abroad. The decision involves balancing frontline needs, corruption concerns, and international blacklist considerations.

stories.title: 'We have learned to live with our neighbours': Liberia's President Joseph Boakai
stories.summary: Liberian President Joseph Boakai told FRANCE 24 he has been in communication with Guinean military leader Mamady Doumbouya following Guinea's deployment of troops to their shared border a month earlier. Boakai said the border situation is coming under control and stressed Liberia's commitment to avoiding conflict with its neighbors.

stories.title: Nigel Farage bought £1.4m property in cash shortly after receiving £5m gift
stories.summary: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage purchased a £1.4 million property in cash shortly after receiving a £5 million personal gift from crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne. Farage described the gift as a reward for his 27 years of Brexit campaigning. He faces a parliamentary investigation into the payment.

stories.title: Israel to sue New York Times over article describing its rape of Palestinians
