stories.summary: U.S. inflation rose to 3.8 percent year-over-year in April 2025, the highest since 2023, according to Bureau of Labor Statistics data. The increase was driven largely by rising energy prices linked to the ongoing U.S. war in the Middle East.

stories.title: Anduril wins Army contract for prototype C2 missile defense system
stories.summary: Anduril Industries has been awarded a U.S. Army contract to develop a prototype command-and-control missile defense system. The system will use Anduril's Lattice software platform to integrate data from multiple existing missile defense systems into a unified operational picture.

stories.title: Starmer replacement remains to be found as pressure for PM to resign grows
stories.summary: A second junior minister resigned from UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer's government on May 12 as more Labour lawmakers called on him to step down. Despite growing pressure, no clear replacement candidate has emerged within the party, though some potential contenders have been identified.

stories.title: Zelensky, Fedorov meet CEO of American company Palantir to discuss defense cooperation
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Digital Transformation Minister Mykhailo Fedorov met with Palantir Technologies CEO Alex Karp to discuss defense cooperation. Discussions covered technological development for both military operations and civilian applications.

stories.title: Oil prices rise for third day in a row as Iran ceasefire talks stall
stories.summary: Oil prices rose for a third consecutive day as US-Iran ceasefire negotiations stalled. Brent crude futures climbed nearly four percent to approximately $108 per barrel after President Trump said the ceasefire was "on life support."

stories.title: Naomi Shloush's 'Academic bimbo' confronts Mizrahi identity in modern Israel
stories.summary: Naomi Shloush's book "Academic Bimbo" explores Mizrahi identity in modern Israel, confronting themes of stigma, belonging, and exclusion.

stories.title: Russia cuts 2026 GDP growth forecast to 0.4% from 1.3%
stories.summary: Russia's government cut its 2026 GDP growth forecast to 0.4 percent, down from a previous projection of 1.3 percent. Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak announced the revised figure.

stories.title: Noam Bettan shines in Eurovision rehearsal as Israel faces antisemitism campaign
stories.summary: Israeli Eurovision contestant Noam Bettan rehearsed in Basel ahead of the competition, performing inside a rotating structure with dancer Lihi Freud. Israel's participation in the 2026 contest has drawn protests and boycott campaigns.

stories.title: Los Angeles's housing crisis: Essential workers priced out of the city
stories.summary: In Los Angeles, soaring property prices and rents are pushing essential workers—including nurses, teachers, and firefighters—out of the city and far from their workplaces. Many face long commutes as home ownership becomes increasingly unaffordable, highlighting a deepening housing crisis in one of America's largest cities.

stories.title: Namibia: Diesel Costs Bite Mining Operations
stories.summary: Rising diesel costs and global supply disruptions are pressuring mining operations in Namibia, as highlighted during a media visit to Swakop Uranium in Arandis.

stories.title: When food becomes memory: Alon Shaya's culinary tribute to Holocaust survivors
stories.summary: Israeli-American chef Alon Shaya created a culinary project transforming Holocaust survivors' stories into dishes, aiming to preserve identity, resilience, and remembrance through food.

stories.title: 'Upside-Down Love': An Israeli-Palestinian memoir of marriage across borders
stories.summary: Israeli-American lawyer Sari Bashi published a memoir titled "Upside-Down Love" about her marriage to a Palestinian. The book recounts a relationship shaped by legal restrictions and physical distance imposed by border controls.

stories.title: 'Digital Warrior': How a lone soldier shaped Israel's global narrative after October 7
stories.summary: An account details how a lone Israeli soldier contributed to shaping Israel's international media narrative after the October 7 attack, describing involvement in real-time information operations.

stories.title: Kenya: At Least 11 Arrested As Police Disperse Protesters Near Africa Forward Summit Venues
stories.summary: At least 11 people were arrested in Nairobi after Kenyan police dispersed groups of protesters attempting to reach venues hosting the Africa Forward Summit.

stories.title: Nearly 50 countries join Ukraine’s coalition to return children abducted by Russia
stories.summary: Nearly 50 countries have joined Ukraine's International Coalition for the Return of Ukrainian Children, with Switzerland and Cyprus among the latest members. The coalition works to locate and repatriate minors taken during Russia's war.

stories.title: Winners for life 2026: “Hasidut Be-Class” takes the stage in Jerusalem
stories.summary: A tribute concert called "Hasidut Be-Class" was held at Sultan's Pool in Jerusalem in support of Israel's emergency response system. The event is part of the Winners for Life 2026 initiative.

stories.title: South Africa: Granny Flees Flooded Shack As Storms Kill Three in Western Cape
stories.summary: Severe storms in South Africa's Western Cape killed three people and displaced more than 41,000 across 26 informal settlements. In Khayelitsha, Cape Town, residents including 50-year-old Nomabhaso Veli fled flooded shacks as the province declared a disaster.

stories.title: Suparco says Eidul Azha likely to fall on May 27
stories.summary: Pakistan's Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (Suparco) forecast that the Zilhajj crescent moon could be sighted on May 17, projecting Eidul Azha to fall on May 27.

stories.title: How Israel's 7 October law differs from Ben-Gvir's death penalty
stories.summary: Israel's new 7 October law allows special trials and possible death sentences for Palestinians accused of involvement in the attack. The legislation differs from earlier death penalty proposals pushed by National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir.

stories.title: Why the Iran war is threatening whales near South Africa
stories.summary: Increased shipping traffic linked to the Iran conflict is raising the risk of ship strikes on whales in waters near South Africa. The rerouting of vessels has heightened exposure of whale populations to maritime hazards.

stories.title: Damage after Russia's overnight attack in Kyiv region reported in three districts
stories.summary: Russian drones struck nine facilities overnight on May 12 across the Fastiv, Vyshhorod, and Bila Tserkva districts of the Kyiv region, causing damage to infrastructure.

stories.title: 'Too Israel-focused, too Jewy': How publishing closes its doors to Jewish writers - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece discusses how political pressures, fear, and quiet boycotts in the publishing industry are reportedly narrowing opportunities for Jewish writers and Israel-related voices in the literary world.

stories.title: US-Iran conflict likely to dominate strategic calculations during Trump’s China visit
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump arrives in China on May 13 for a three-day state visit focused on trade and economic ties. The ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict is expected to influence strategic discussions between Washington and Beijing.

stories.title: IDF says it carried out weeklong raid on Hezbollah sites beyond Lebanon’s Litani River
stories.summary: The Israeli Defense Forces said they conducted a weeklong operation targeting Hezbollah sites north of the Litani River in Lebanon. Separately, Hezbollah's leader stated that the group's weapons are not a subject of Israel-Lebanon negotiations.

stories.title: Hezbollah leader vows to never surrender, calls for Lebanon to withdraw from negotiations
stories.summary: Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem vowed that the group would never surrender and called on Lebanon to withdraw from negotiations. Qassem stated that Lebanon would not return to conditions that existed before March 2.

stories.title: Chad's 'At the Heart of Art' festival empowers a new generation of talents
stories.summary: The third edition of the "At the Heart of Art" festival concluded in N'Djamena's Bakara district in Chad, showcasing music and performance by young Chadian artists as a vehicle for youth empowerment.

stories.title: Uganda: Museveni Calls for End to Raw Exports, Pushes Africa Toward Value Addition
stories.summary: Ugandan President Museveni outlined a post-election economic plan focused on industrialization, value addition, and skills development, arguing that exporting raw materials while importing finished goods prevents prosperity for Uganda and Africa.

stories.title: Turkey supporting efforts to reopen Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said in Doha that Turkey supports efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and opposes its use as a weapon in the Iran conflict. He added that Ankara is contributing to Pakistan-led negotiations seeking a diplomatic end to the US-Iran war.

stories.title: In a bind over rare earths, Europe watches US-China tussle from the sidelines
stories.summary: European officials are watching U.S.-China tensions over rare earth minerals with concern, as China has expanded export controls with an extraterritorial element that could restrict products made in third countries containing Chinese-origin rare earth content. Europe remains largely on the sidelines of the dispute.

stories.title: Opposing Taiwan independence is in America’s own interest
stories.summary: As U.S. President Donald Trump prepares to visit China, the article discusses Taiwan's role as one of the most sensitive issues in U.S.-China relations. It argues that a clear U.S. stance on Taiwan independence could help avoid a broader conflict with Beijing and stabilize trade and geopolitical cooperation.

stories.title: Huckabee: Israel sent Iron Dome, personnel to UAE amid Iran war
stories.summary: US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee revealed that Israel deployed Iron Dome missile defense systems and military personnel to the UAE during the Iran war. This represents the first publicly acknowledged Israeli military deployment to the Emirates since the conflict began.

stories.title: 'It started on October 7': How war reshaped Israel's defense-tech boom
stories.summary: Israel's defense-technology sector has experienced rapid growth since October 7, with battlefield demands accelerating innovation. The country has emerged as a central player in a rapidly evolving global defense-tech landscape.

stories.title: Dela Rosa’s flight turns Philippine Senate into battleground for ICC accountability
stories.summary: Philippine Senator Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa, a former national police chief and close ally of ex-President Rodrigo Duterte, evaded an International Criminal Court arrest warrant by taking refuge in the Philippine Senate. The standoff has turned the chamber into the center of a legal and political dispute over ICC accountability.

stories.title: President, PM pay tribute to shepherd who sacrificed his life while averting suicide attack in Attock
stories.summary: Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif honored a shepherd named Liaqat who died confronting a suicide bomber near a security post in Attock's Jand tehsil, on the Punjab–Khyber Pakhtunkhwa border.

stories.title: 'Am I a murderer?' Yad Vashem restores a Jewish ghetto policeman's Holocaust confession
stories.summary: Yad Vashem has restored and published a Holocaust-era diary written by a Jewish ghetto policeman. The document, which had been buried and later distorted, contains the author's personal confession about his wartime role.

stories.title: One radar sees 250 km out. The other measures altitude at 300 km range. Ukraine’s drones just took both out in Donetsk Oblast
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone forces and special operations units struck two Russian radar systems in Donetsk Oblast—one with a 250-km detection range and another capable of measuring altitude at 300 km. Additional targets included fuel depots and military bases.

stories.title: Defense Intelligence publishes data on companies involved in production of Russian Pantsir-S1 air defense system
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Intelligence (HUR) published details on companies involved in manufacturing the 72V6 combat vehicle, a component of Russia's Pantsir-S1 anti-aircraft missile and gun system.

stories.title: Pakistan scrambles to salvage US-Iran diplomacy as ceasefire faces collapse
stories.summary: Pakistan rejected allegations that it provided military aid to Iran, amid efforts to mediate between the US and Iran. US President Donald Trump described the existing ceasefire as being on "life support" due to stalled negotiations.

stories.title: Israeli army chief warns reserve forces could 'collapse' amid manpower crisis
stories.summary: Israeli military chief of staff Eyal Zamir warned Knesset lawmakers that the army's reserve forces could collapse within months. He urged the government to pass legislation expanding conscription and extending mandatory military service to 36 months.

stories.title: CYBERCOM requests 2,660 percent increase in AI for cyber operations
stories.summary: U.S. Cyber Command has requested a 2,660 percent funding increase for artificial intelligence capabilities in cyber operations, totaling $138 million. The funds are intended to deliver measurable improvements across ISR, offensive cyber, defensive cyber, and integrated foundational activities.

stories.title: Israel sent Iron Dome to UAE during Iran war, Huckabee confirms
stories.summary: US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee confirmed that Israel deployed Iron Dome air defense batteries to the United Arab Emirates during the Iran war. The move represents a significant step in military cooperation between Israel and the UAE.

stories.title: Kenya: Gachagua Moves to Supreme Court to Strike Out Appeal On Impeachment Bench
stories.summary: Former Kenyan Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua filed a motion at the Supreme Court seeking to strike out an appeal challenging the composition of the High Court bench handling petitions related to his impeachment.

stories.title: If Starmer gets his way, Reform - not the Greens - will be his legacy
stories.summary: The article discusses the political implications for UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer, arguing his approach could strengthen the Reform party rather than the Greens. It examines parallels with Jeremy Corbyn's earlier insurgent politics within the Labour movement.

stories.title: Elon Musk, Apple's Tim Cook to head to China with Trump, per White House
stories.summary: The White House announced that Elon Musk and Apple CEO Tim Cook will accompany President Trump on his visit to China. Beijing said it is prepared to work with the U.S. toward greater stability.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces strike two Russian radars, fuel, ammunition depots in Donetsk region
stories.summary: Operators from the Ukrainian Unmanned Systems Forces' 1st Separate Center struck PRV-16 and P-18 radar systems, a fuel depot, an ammunition storage site, and Russian temporary deployment points in the Donetsk region.

stories.title: Malawi: Kamuzu Stadium Turned Into a Place of Tears As Malawi Received 15 Bodies From Zimbabwe Bus Tragedy
stories.summary: Kamuzu Stadium in Malawi served as a receiving site for 15 coffins carrying Malawians killed in a bus crash in Zimbabwe, drawing large crowds of mourners.

stories.title: IDF to establish haredi-manned suicide drone factory, aiming to counter Hezbollah threat - report
stories.summary: The IDF plans to establish a factory staffed by ultra-Orthodox (haredi) personnel to produce suicide drones, according to Army Radio. The initiative aims to counter the growing threat from FPV drones operated by Hezbollah in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Kuwait says it has arrested four IRGC affiliates
stories.summary: Kuwait's interior ministry announced the arrest of four individuals it said were affiliated with Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps after they attempted to enter the country by sea. A member of Kuwait's armed forces was injured during clashes with the infiltrators.

stories.title: New Israeli law sets military tribunal for Hamas October 7 militants
stories.summary: Israel's parliament passed legislation on Monday establishing a military tribunal to prosecute hundreds of Palestinian militants involved in the October 7, 2023 attack. Lawmakers said the measure would help address national trauma from the assault.

stories.title: Video: Philippine senator flees ICC arrest over role in drug war
stories.summary: Philippine Senator Ronald Dela Rosa took refuge in the country's parliament to avoid arrest by police acting on an International Criminal Court warrant. The ICC sought his detention over his alleged role in the Philippines' drug war.

stories.title: Iran war creates new must-have for summer holidays — the plan B
stories.summary: The Iran conflict is affecting summer holiday planning, with travelers opting for short-haul European destinations and train travel to avoid potential flight disruptions and rising air fares.

stories.title: Iran expands operational definition of Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran has expanded its operational definition of the Strait of Hormuz from an estimated 20-30 miles to between 200 and 300 miles, according to Iranian media reports. The move broadens the area Iran considers within the strait's operational scope.

stories.title: Malaysia, Tamil Nadu share deep ties, says PM Anwar Ibrahim; congratulates new Tamil Nadu CM Joseph Vijay
stories.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim congratulated Joseph Vijay on becoming Tamil Nadu's new Chief Minister, highlighting the deep cultural and historical ties between Malaysia and Tamil Nadu.

stories.title: IDF uses robots to advance beyond Lebanon’s Litani River, FPV drones continue challenging military
stories.summary: The Israeli military reported using ground robots to advance beyond Lebanon's Litani River and said it killed approximately 15 Hezbollah fighters over three days of operations. FPV drones continue to pose significant challenges to IDF forces in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Can China counter US sanctions with its trade power?
stories.summary: Economic tensions between the United States and China are escalating, spanning sanctions and rare earth mineral exports. Analysts are examining whether China can leverage its trade power to counter US sanctions pressure.

stories.title: 173 Indians among foreigners arrested in latest cyber crime crackdown in Sri Lanka
stories.summary: Sri Lankan authorities arrested 198 foreigners, including 173 Indians and 25 Nepalese nationals, in the southern resort areas of Galle, Hikkaduwa, and Midigama on May 11, 2026. The arrests were part of a crackdown on cyber crime operations.

stories.title: Estonia appoints Tiina Intelmann as new ambassador to Ukraine
stories.summary: Estonian President Alar Karis appointed Tiina Intelmann as Estonia's new ambassador to Ukraine.

stories.title: Russia, Ukraine resume strikes as truce expires, one dead: authorities
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine resumed strikes against each other after a truce expired, with at least one person killed. Ukrainian military officials in Kyiv warned residents of enemy UAVs over the capital and urged them to seek shelter.

stories.title: Peace deal hopes fade after Trump rejects ‘garbage’ Iran proposal
stories.summary: Iran called for an end to hostilities on all fronts, including Lebanon, as hopes for a peace deal faded after U.S. President Trump rejected Tehran's counterproposal to a peace plan.

stories.title: Peace deal hopes fade after Trump rejects 'garbage' Iran proposal
stories.summary: Prospects for a U.S.-Iran peace deal dimmed on Tuesday after President Donald Trump described Tehran's counterproposal as "garbage" and said a ceasefire was "on life support." Iran rejected Washington's proposal and maintained its own list of demands.

stories.title: US top diplomat Rubio discusses Iran, Strait of Hormuz with Britain and Australia
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio held discussions with British and Australian counterparts on the Iran conflict and efforts to restore freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Israel passes law to publicly try and execute Palestinians linked to 7 October attacks
stories.summary: The Israeli Knesset passed a law enabling public trials and potential execution of Palestinians linked to the 7 October attacks. The legislation gained broad political support, with Israel's justice minister calling it one of the Knesset's most important moments.

stories.title: Spain reports new hantavirus case as outbreak grows to 11
stories.summary: Spain confirmed a new hantavirus case involving a passenger evacuated from a cruise ship at the center of an outbreak. The World Health Organization has confirmed 11 cases total, including three deaths. The patient is quarantined in a military hospital in Madrid.

stories.title: Burnham allies warn against quick ‘coronation’ of Streeting if Starmer quits
stories.summary: Allies of Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham warned against a quick "coronation" of Health Secretary Wes Streeting as Labour leader if Prime Minister Keir Starmer resigns. They called on Labour's ruling body to ensure Burnham could stand for a parliamentary byelection to enter the leadership race.

stories.title: Key events in ties among United States, China and Taiwan
stories.summary: The Trump administration approved $11 billion in arms sales to Taiwan, prompting China to launch its most extensive military exercises around the island. The developments mark an escalation in US-China tensions over Taiwan.

stories.title: Melania, Rush Hour director returns to China with Trump’s delegation
stories.summary: Film director Brett Ratner, known for the Rush Hour franchise and the documentary Melania, is traveling to China as part of U.S. President Donald Trump's delegation. Ratner plans to advance preparations for Rush Hour 4, including meetings with potential Chinese film distribution partners.

stories.title: How a fake Iraqi officer infiltrated Lebanon's security agencies
stories.summary: An Iraqi man was uncovered after allegedly posing as a senior security official and infiltrating Lebanon's political and security circles. The suspect reportedly gained access to high-level contacts before his deception was discovered by Lebanese agencies.

stories.title: After the Raj, the most powerful weapon in Pakistan's arsenal is a name
stories.summary: A report examines how Pakistan named its May 2024 retaliatory military operation against India "Operation Bunyan um Marsoos," and the editorial challenges newsrooms faced in correctly transliterating the Arabic-origin name across various media outlets.

stories.title: We were there. The Supreme Court did not tie the IDF’s hands on the Gaza border
stories.summary: Two former senior IDF officers disputed claims that Israel's Supreme Court restricted open-fire rules before the 7 October attacks. They argued such assertions are a pretext to avoid establishing a state commission of inquiry into the security failures.

stories.title: Hegseth faces new round of questioning from Congress on the Iran war and more
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Hegseth and military chief Caine face congressional questioning on the Iran war and the proposed $1.5 trillion defense budget. The budget emphasizes increased spending on drones, warships, and missile defense systems.

stories.title: TV Rain Editor-in-Chief Jailed 8 Years in Absentia Over War ‘Fakes’
stories.summary: Tikhon Dzyadko, editor-in-chief of the independent Russian outlet TV Rain, was sentenced to eight years in prison in absentia on charges of disseminating false information about Russia's armed forces.

stories.title: Palestine Action trial lawyer wins appeal against contempt of court charge
stories.summary: Human rights barrister Rajiv Menon KC won an appeal against a contempt of court referral stemming from his closing speech during the trial of six Palestine Action activists. The activists were tried for a 2024 protest at Elbit Systems UK's arms factory in Filton, near Bristol.

stories.title: Eyeing migrant returns, EU moves to bolster Syria ties
stories.summary: The European Union announced steps to strengthen ties with Syria, partly aimed at facilitating the return of migrants. New EU funding will support the rehabilitation of a hospital near Homs, and officials said they would explore ways to improve Syrian access to financing.

stories.title: Was Abe Foxman the last ‘Jewish pope’?
stories.summary: Abe Foxman, the longtime director of the Anti-Defamation League, died at age 86. He was widely regarded as a leading voice against antisemitism in the post-Holocaust era and a prominent figure in American Jewish communal life.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: Israeli strikes kill six in south Lebanon, says state media
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed six people in southern Lebanon, according to state media. U.S. President Donald Trump warned that the ceasefire in the broader West Asia war was on "life support" after rejecting Iran's latest counteroffer.

stories.title: Israeli MPs back special tribunal with death penalty powers for alleged 7 October attackers
stories.summary: Israel's Knesset voted 93-0 to establish a livestreamed special military tribunal with death penalty powers for Palestinians convicted of involvement in the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack. The remaining 27 lawmakers were absent or abstained. The measure has drawn comparisons to the 1962 Adolf Eichmann trial.

stories.title: Pakistan extends countrywide austerity drive after U.S., Iran fail to strike deal
stories.summary: Pakistan extended its countrywide austerity drive after the United States and Iran failed to reach a deal. Key measures include a 50 percent reduction in fuel allowances for official vehicles, exempting operational vehicles such as ambulances and public buses.

stories.title: Russian forces launch 24 attacks on Chernihiv region over past day
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out 24 strikes on settlements in Ukraine's Chernihiv region over the past day, primarily using first-person-view (FPV) drones.

stories.title: Ukraine’s IMF lifeline depends on tax reforms parliament keeps stalling
stories.summary: Ukraine faces a funding bottleneck as parliament has stalled a $614 million parcel tax reform now six weeks past its deadline. The tax measure is required to unlock $8.1 billion in IMF financing.

stories.title: Daily Briefing May 12: Extremist settlers dealt a blow with EU sanctions
stories.summary: The European Union imposed sanctions on extremist Israeli settlers, in a move seen as a significant blow to settlement activity. Separately, developments include Trump's comments on Iran, a new Gaza police force, and diplomatic tensions involving Israel's US envoy.

stories.title: Rwanda: Exports to China Surge 92 Percent As Demand Rises
stories.summary: Rwanda's exports to China surged 92% in 2025, reaching $160.8 million compared to $83.7 million the previous year, according to the Rwanda Development Board.

stories.title: Brics foreign ministers to meet in New Delhi this week
stories.summary: The annual BRICS foreign ministers' meeting will take place in New Delhi on May 14–15, India's foreign ministry confirmed. The bloc now includes Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran, and the UAE, with India chairing for 2026.

stories.title: EU agrees to sanctions on Israeli settlers after Hungary’s new government lifts veto
stories.summary: The European Union agreed to impose sanctions on Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank after Hungary's new Prime Minister Peter Magyar lifted the veto previously maintained by his predecessor Viktor Orbán. The move ends a prolonged deadlock over the long-awaited measures.

stories.title: Liberia: Tweah's Verdict Reflects Judicial Independence, Says Cso Group
stories.summary: A civil society group in Liberia, the Independent Societal Watch Advocates, defended Justice Minister Oswald Tweh amid criticism over the government's handling of a $6.2 million corruption case involving former Finance Minister Samuel Tweah.

stories.title: US negotiating establishment of new bases in Greenland in high level talks with Denmark - report
stories.summary: The United States is negotiating with Denmark to establish new military bases in Greenland, according to reports. Sources indicate the US has proposed that three new bases be formally designated as US sovereign territory.

stories.title: Israel will prosecute Oct 7 suspects in Eichmann-style tribunal
stories.summary: Israel's new law will allow the prosecution of October 7 suspects before a military tribunal. The proceedings will be broadcast publicly and archived, drawing comparisons to the trial of Adolf Eichmann.

stories.title: Historian Achille Mbembe: Africa’s ‘rule of gerontocracy’ is coming to an end
stories.summary: Historian and political theorist Achille Mbembe, speaking at the Africa Forward Summit at Strathmore University, argued that Africa is undergoing a profound transformation. He stated that the era of gerontocratic rule has ended in the minds of the people, even as institutional change remains slow.

stories.title: New Israeli law sets military tribunal for Hamas fighters linked to October 7 attack
stories.summary: Israel's Knesset passed a law establishing a military tribunal to try hundreds of Palestinian fighters linked to the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack. The attack killed at least 1,200 people, and Israel's subsequent assault on Gaza killed more than 72,000 Palestinians.

stories.title: Turkey’s Aselsan eyes growth in networked, mass-producible weapons, CEO says
stories.summary: Turkish defense firm Aselsan is pursuing growth in networked and mass-producible weapons systems, according to CEO Ahmet Akyol. In an interview, Akyol stated that the technologies discussed could realistically enter inventory by 2027.

stories.title: European Union adopts new sanctions Israeli settlers over violence in West Bank
stories.summary: European Union foreign ministers agreed on May 12 to impose new sanctions on Israeli settlers over violence against Palestinians in the West Bank, after Hungary's change of government ended months of blockage. The EU also moved to sanction Hamas leaders; Israel condemned the settler sanctions as baseless.

stories.title: An Israeli ‘Excursion’ in Babylon
stories.summary: Palestinian-Jordanian editorial cartoonist Emad Hajjaj published a cartoon in The New Arab/Al-Araby Al-Jadeed commenting on Israeli military operations in Iraq-related contexts. The cartoon is part of the publication's daily editorial cartoon series.

stories.title: Aukus costs balloon with more cash and staff for submarine agency amid ongoing search for nuclear waste dump
stories.summary: Australia's budget for the AUKUS submarine program has increased by more than A$430 million over four years, with the Australian Submarine Agency's funding jumping to A$512 million in the next financial year. Concerns persist about whether the sovereign nuclear-powered submarine fleet will ultimately be delivered.

stories.title: Starmer criticised by Holocaust survivors for smearing Palestine marches
stories.summary: More than 40 British Holocaust survivors and their descendants sent an open letter to Prime Minister Keir Starmer criticizing him for linking attacks on Jewish people to pro-Palestine marches. The letter was also addressed to Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood and Metropolitan Police Commissioner Mark Rowley.

stories.title: New power outages reported in five regions following Russian attacks – Ukrenergo
stories.summary: As of the morning of May 12, power outages caused by Russian attacks affected consumers in the Donetsk, Kharkiv, Sumy, Chernihiv, and Mykolaiv regions. Separately, bad weather knocked out electricity in six settlements in the Zakarpattia region.

stories.title: German firms in China more upbeat about economy despite Iran war, trade headwinds: survey
stories.summary: German companies operating in China have grown more optimistic about the country's economic outlook, according to a German Chamber of Commerce survey. Thirty-seven percent of respondents expected improvement over the next six months, up 22 percentage points from the prior year, despite the Iran war and trade tensions.

stories.title: US-China summit tests ties as tensions grow over Taiwan, trade, AI technology
stories.summary: A US-China summit is testing bilateral relations as tensions escalate over Taiwan, trade, and AI technology. Despite President Trump claiming a good relationship with President Xi Jinping, divisions between Washington and Beijing continue to deepen.

stories.title: A Kyiv Oblast kindergarten was hit hours after Russia’s “ceasefire” ended
stories.summary: A kindergarten in Kyiv Oblast was struck hours after Russia's declared ceasefire ended. Russian forces also targeted locomotive infrastructure in Dnipro, power facilities in Mykolaiv, and shelled Zaporizhzhia and other regions.

stories.title: The crisis is Sudan is much worse than what is acknowledged
stories.summary: The humanitarian crisis in Sudan remains severe even in Khartoum, where active fighting has subsided. Aid organizations say the situation is far worse than publicly acknowledged.

stories.title: Iran sends mass text message to Israelis, inviting them to share intelligence
stories.summary: Iran sent mass text messages in Hebrew to Israeli citizens, urging them to share intelligence by contacting Iranian embassies. Israel's National Cyber Directorate warned recipients not to click any links included in the messages.

stories.title: Why the ‘Hebrew Hammer’ is becoming one of Israel’s loudest allies in Washington
stories.summary: The article profiles a figure known as the "Hebrew Hammer" who has become an increasingly prominent pro-Israel voice in Washington. He is noted for his outspoken defense of Israel and stance against antisemitism.

stories.title: UAE attacked Iran last month: WSJ
stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that the United Arab Emirates attacked an Iranian refinery on Lavan Island around the time U.S. President Donald Trump announced a ceasefire following a five-week air strike campaign against Iran.

stories.title: China’s Foreign Minister to skip BRICS Delhi meet for ‘scheduling reasons’
stories.summary: China's Foreign Minister will not attend the BRICS meeting in Delhi, citing scheduling reasons. Beijing indicated it would not send any other high-level official as a replacement.

stories.title: UK’s Starmer to ‘get on with governing’, defies calls to quit
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer told his cabinet on Tuesday he would continue governing despite mounting calls from within Labour for his departure following poor local election results. He acknowledged responsibility for the losses but noted no formal leadership challenge had been initiated.

stories.title: France and Kenya look for future partnerships at Africa Forward summit
stories.summary: Dozens of heads of state convened in Kenya for the two-day Africa Forward summit, co-hosted with France, where more than 23 billion euros in investment has been pledged. The event marks the first time the summit is held in an English-speaking country, reflecting France's pivot toward Anglophone Africa as its influence in former French-speaking colonies declines.

stories.title: Over 370 Afghans killed in Pakistan conflict in first 3 months of 2026: UN
stories.summary: A United Nations report found that over 370 Afghan civilians were killed in Pakistan-related conflict during the first three months of 2026. Fighting between the Taliban and Pakistani forces intensified in February, with many casualties attributed to air raids.

stories.title: Proposed Law of Return amendment sparks debate over conversion standards in Israel
stories.summary: Israeli lawmakers are debating a proposed amendment to the Law of Return that would change conversion standards. Religious coalition members frame the bill as restoring halachic standards, while critics warn it would expand religious establishment control over Jewish identity.

stories.title: Zelensky: Russia chose to end partial truce, Ukraine will respond in kind
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Russia ended a partial ceasefire that had held for several days by launching more than 200 strike drones at Ukraine overnight. He said Ukraine would respond in kind.

stories.title: Peshawar court acquits 74 PTI activists in May 2023 violence case
stories.summary: A Peshawar court acquitted 74 Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf activists charged in connection with violence on May 10, 2023, which resulted in two deaths. Additional sessions judge Faraz Ahmad ruled the prosecution's case rested on unsubstantiated allegations.

stories.title: Turkey-Syria border gate to reopen after 12-year closure
stories.summary: Turkey announced it will fully reopen a border crossing with Syria that had been closed for 12 years. The gate was partially reopened in 2019 for limited purposes including trade and government crossings, but will now permit civilian passage.

stories.title: Nigeria: WHO, EU Launch Health Support Project As Nigeria Battles Multiple Disease Outbreaks
stories.summary: The World Health Organization and European Union launched a joint health support project in Nigeria called EU SPIN, coordinating with Nigerian authorities and other development partners to address multiple ongoing disease outbreaks in the country.

stories.title: Somalia: Somali Opposition Plans May 16 Protest in Mogadishu Over President's Term
stories.summary: Somali opposition politicians announced a planned protest in Mogadishu for May 16, accusing President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud of attempting to extend his presidential term beyond constitutional limits.

stories.title: More than 110 Nobel laureates call on Iran to release gravely ill activist Narges Mohammadi
stories.summary: More than 110 Nobel laureates called for the immediate release of jailed Iranian human rights activist and Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi. She was transferred from Zanjan prison to a Tehran hospital amid concerns over her rapidly deteriorating health.

stories.title: Trump 'very disappointed' in Kurds who just 'take, take, take'
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump expressed being "very disappointed" with Kurdish groups, accusing them of failing to provide military support to Iranian opposition forces. Kurdish leaders have denied claims that they received US weaponry intended for Iranian opposition groups during the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: USA’s Johnny Cardoso expected to miss World Cup through ankle injury
stories.summary: Atletico Madrid midfielder Johnny Cardoso of the US men's national team is expected to miss the World Cup due to an ankle injury. He joins a growing list of injured players for tournament co-hosts the United States.

stories.title: Zelensky’s ex-chief of staff named as suspect in money-laundering probe
stories.summary: Ukraine's National Anti-Corruption Bureau and Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office named Andriy Yermak, President Zelenskyy's former chief of staff, as a suspect in an alleged 460-million-hryvnia money-laundering scheme. The announcement was made late Monday and was not connected to other ongoing events.

stories.title: At least nine people killed in explosion at Pakistan market
stories.summary: At least nine people were killed and about 30 wounded in a blast at a market in Sarai Naurang, located in Lakki Marwat district of northwestern Pakistan. The cause of the explosion is under investigation.

stories.title: Amnesty, Albanese urge Eurovision to bar Israel over genocide
stories.summary: Amnesty International and UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese called for Israel's suspension from the Eurovision Song Contest ahead of the semi-finals. The calls cite allegations of genocide in Gaza as grounds for barring Israel's participation.

stories.title: Police raids reveal Indonesia as new hub for scam syndicates
stories.summary: Indonesian police raids have exposed signs that online gambling and scam syndicates, displaced from traditional hubs like Cambodia and Myanmar, are establishing operations in Indonesia. Authorities arrested hundreds of foreign nationals in Jakarta, and analysts warned that weak law enforcement and a porous visa regime made the country attractive to criminal networks.

stories.title: Moscow court sentences TV Rain editor-in-chief Tikhon Dzyadko in absentia to 8 years in prison on ‘false information’ charges
stories.summary: A Moscow court sentenced TV Rain editor-in-chief Tikhon Dzyadko in absentia to eight years in prison on charges of spreading alleged false information about the Russian military.

stories.title: Los Angeles-area mayor to plead guilty to acting as Chinese propaganda agent
stories.summary: The mayor of Arcadia, California, has agreed to plead guilty to a federal charge of acting as an unregistered foreign agent of China. U.S. officials said the mayor spread propaganda on behalf of Beijing.

stories.title: Ukraine's air defense downs 192 of 216 Russian drones in overnight attack
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces shot down 192 of 216 drones launched by Russian forces in an overnight attack beginning the evening of May 11.

stories.title: FO terms report claiming Pakistan allowed Iranian military aircraft to park at airbase as 'misleading and sensationalised'
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Office dismissed a CBS News report alleging that Islamabad allowed Iranian military aircraft, including an Air Force RC-130, to park at Nur Khan Air Base during mediation efforts in the Middle East conflict. The FO called the report "misleading and sensationalised."

stories.title: Congo-Brazzaville asks to open talks with IMF for new economic programme
stories.summary: The Republic of Congo has formally requested to open negotiations with the International Monetary Fund to establish a new economic and financial program for the country.

stories.title: ‘Blood libel’: Israel rejects NYT column alleging widespread rape of Palestinian inmates
stories.summary: Israel's ambassador to the US rejected a New York Times opinion column by Nicholas Kristof alleging widespread sexual abuse of Palestinian inmates. The ambassador highlighted ties between the cited Euro-Med Monitor organization and Hamas officials.

stories.title: Russia tried to swap abducted Ukrainian children like POWs, Sybiha reveals
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha disclosed that Russia attempted to exchange abducted Ukrainian children as part of prisoner-of-war swaps. Ukraine rejected the proposal; only about 2,000 of an estimated 20,000 deported children have been returned.

stories.title: Macron presents France 'as the ethical partner with Africa' at summit in Kenya
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron attended the Africa Forward summit in Nairobi, Kenya, seeking to redefine France's relationship with African countries as a partnership of equals. The effort comes as France distances itself from its "Françafrique" legacy of economic, political, and military influence over former colonies, having withdrawn most of its troops from the region.

stories.title: Gaza's survival economy: Small businesses rise from war rubble
stories.summary: Palestinians in Gaza are launching small businesses amid the destruction of war, creating what observers describe as a survival economy. Without formal employment or fixed incomes, residents are relying on creativity and innovation to sustain their livelihoods.

stories.title: Ugandan president, 81, sworn in for new term after 40 years at the helm
stories.summary: Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni, 81, was sworn in on Tuesday for another five-year term, extending his 40-year rule. His son, army chief General Muhoozi Kainerugaba, is widely seen as his presumptive heir.

stories.title: First US visit to China since 2017 amid geopolitical tension
stories.summary: China expressed readiness to work with the United States for greater global stability ahead of President Trump's visit to Beijing—the first by a U.S. president to China since 2017. The Iran war is expected to dominate the agenda, while Beijing has signaled it also wants Taiwan to be central to discussions.

stories.title: Iranians concerned about war extending as Iran and US fail to find common ground
stories.summary: U.S. President Trump rejected Iran's counterproposals to a peace deal, while Tehran responded that it was unconcerned with Washington's dissatisfaction. The U.S. wants Iran to halt uranium enrichment and surrender its stocks before lifting sanctions. Residents in Tehran expressed concern about the war continuing despite the current ceasefire.

stories.title: Military strikes, gang massacres in Nigeria kill around 100 civilians
stories.summary: Nigerian military operations and attacks by armed groups known as "bandits" killed approximately 100 civilians in a single day across multiple locations in Nigeria, making it one of the deadliest days in the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Three-day ceasefire ends with fresh wave of Russian attacks on Ukraine – Europe live
stories.summary: Russia launched drone strikes on Ukrainian energy facilities and apartments after a three-day ceasefire expired, killing at least one person. Separately, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz urged Germany to reform or risk falling behind, in a speech to trade unionists that drew jeers and boos.

stories.title: Trump’s China visit opens door to ‘casual’ networking between business chiefs
stories.summary: U.S. business leaders accompanying President Trump on his state visit to Beijing will have opportunities to network with Chinese counterparts at the Capital Club Beijing. The delegation includes high-profile figures such as Elon Musk and Tim Cook.

stories.title: Russian attack damages homes and vehicles in Zhytomyr
stories.summary: A Russian air attack on May 12 damaged residential buildings, utility structures, and vehicles in the city of Zhytomyr.

stories.title: China’s Hengrui seals US$15.2 billion deal with US pharmaceutical giant BMS
stories.summary: China's Jiangsu Hengrui Pharmaceutical signed a global collaboration and licensing deal worth up to $15.2 billion with U.S.-based Bristol Myers Squibb. Hengrui's shares rose in both Hong Kong and Shenzhen trading.

stories.title: Rubio Aims to Reset U.S.-India Ties
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is planning a visit to New Delhi this month aimed at resetting U.S.-India relations. The diplomatic effort is expected to face significant challenges.

stories.title: China parents conceive baby to collect umbilical cord blood to save daughter with severe disorder
stories.summary: A 15-year-old girl in China's Guangdong province suffering from thalassemia, a severe inherited blood disorder, is recovering after receiving an umbilical cord blood transplant from her newborn brother, whom her parents conceived specifically to help save her.

stories.title: Trump 'very disappointed' in Kurds who just 'take, take, take'
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump expressed frustration with Kurdish leaders, accusing them of only taking from the United States. Kurdish leaders denied receiving US weaponry to fight the Iranian government during the conflict.

stories.title: Iranians mourn children killed in US bombing of school
stories.summary: Iranians mourned children killed in a U.S. bombing of a school in Minab, Hormozgan Province, on February 28—the deadliest single attack in the Iran war. The strike killed 155 people, including 120 children. A preliminary U.S. military investigation reportedly found the intended target was an adjacent IRGC military base.

stories.title: Mass wedding brings brief joy to couples in devastated Gaza
stories.summary: Palestinian couples held a mass wedding ceremony in Gaza amid rubble and widespread displacement caused by ongoing conflict. The event offered a brief moment of celebration for residents enduring dire humanitarian conditions.

stories.title: UAE attacked Iran in April: Sources
stories.summary: Sources report that the United Arab Emirates carried out attacks on Iran in April, targeting a refinery on Iran's Lavan Island. No further details on the scale of the strikes or Iran's response were provided.

stories.title: How France works to beat the hantavirus chain of transmission
stories.summary: French authorities are racing to contain a hantavirus outbreak by quarantining 22 identified close contacts. One contact is set to be hospitalized in Rennes in western France. The government announced it would hold two crisis meetings daily to combat the virus's chain of transmission.

stories.title: Christian Zionism: What it is and how it affects the US and Israel
stories.summary: Christian Zionism, an Evangelical belief system supported by figures including Pete Hegseth and Mike Huckabee, continues to influence US-Israel relations. The movement is regarded as offensive by many Jewish communities despite its political prominence.

stories.title: Brazilian flotilla activist returns home, alleges torture during Israel detention
stories.summary: Brazilian activist Thiago Avila returned to São Paulo on Monday after being detained and deported from Israel. He alleged he was tortured during ten days in Israeli custody and said he witnessed abuses against Palestinian prisoners. Avila had been involved in a flotilla activism effort.

stories.title: Somalia: The Iran War Is Costing Children's Lives in Somalia
stories.summary: The conflict in the Middle East, including disruptions at Dubai's Jebel Ali port, has affected critical maritime shipping routes. Aid organizations report that the downstream effects are impacting children's welfare in Somalia.

stories.title: France pitches 'partnership of equals' as African summit enters second day
stories.summary: On the second day of the Africa Forward summit in Nairobi, French President Emmanuel Macron announced that 23 billion euros in investment had been raised for the African continent. France is seeking to position itself as an equal partner with African nations, moving away from its neocolonial past as it completes military withdrawal from West African countries.

stories.title: Israel sent Iron Dome battery and air defence personnel to UAE
stories.summary: US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee confirmed that Israel sent an Iron Dome battery and operating personnel to the United Arab Emirates. Huckabee cited the deployment as evidence of the deepening relationship between the two countries under the Abraham Accords.

stories.title: ChaiFlicks – Stream Jewish entertainment from Israel & more – 50% off! - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: ChaiFlicks, a Jewish entertainment streaming service, is offering a promotional subscription rate. This is a sponsored advertisement and not a news article.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: Iran could enrich uranium to weapons grade if attacked, senior lawmaker warns
stories.summary: A senior Iranian lawmaker, Ebrahim Rezaei, warned that Iran could enrich uranium to weapons-grade levels of 90 per cent if attacked, and said parliament would review such a move. The Iranian government also stated that internet access in Tehran would return to normal after the war concludes.

stories.title: Ukraine records new series of grain shipments by Russia to Egypt – Vlasiuk
stories.summary: Ukrainian official Vlasiuk reported that at the end of April, Russia shipped Ukrainian grain from the occupied ports of Mariupol and Sevastopol to Egypt using falsified documents.

stories.title: Israeli military kills six in Lebanon, issues more displacement threats
stories.summary: Israeli forces carried out a deadly airstrike in southern Lebanon that killed six people, while issuing additional displacement orders to civilians. The attack occurred just days before Israeli and Lebanese officials are scheduled to meet in Washington.

stories.title: Russian drone attack causes power outages in Mykolaiv region
stories.summary: Russian drones targeted energy infrastructure in the Mykolaiv region during a morning attack, causing power outages across the area.

stories.title: Israeli lawmakers set up special tribunal, allow for death penalty for Hamas-led 2023 attackers
stories.summary: The Israeli Knesset passed a measure 93-0 establishing a special tribunal with the authority to impose the death penalty on those convicted of participating in the Hamas-led October 7, 2023 attack. The vote reflected broad parliamentary support in the 120-seat body.

stories.title: 100 million barrels lost every week Strait of Hormuz is shut, Saudi Aramco CEO says
stories.summary: Saudi Aramco CEO stated that the closure of the Strait of Hormuz has caused a loss of 100 million barrels of oil per week. Oil prices continued climbing after President Trump said the Iran ceasefire was on "massive life support." Trump also proposed scrapping the U.S. federal gas tax to ease the war's impact on consumers.

stories.title: Budget 2026 Australia: Jim Chalmers announces capital gains tax and negative gearing reform for housing
stories.summary: Australian Treasurer Jim Chalmers announced significant capital gains tax and negative gearing reforms in the 2026 federal budget, aiming to help first home buyers and promote intergenerational fairness. The changes, described as the most ambitious since the Howard era, come despite economic uncertainty linked to the Iran war.

stories.title: Ethiopia’s $51.8bn debt burden tests IMF reform push as US support returns
stories.summary: Ethiopia faces a $51.8 billion debt burden as the IMF pursues reform efforts in the country. Economists have raised concerns about rising debt-servicing costs and persistent hard-currency shortages, even as Washington and the World Bank expand financing.

stories.title: Uganda and DR Congo sign six new bilateral agreements
stories.summary: Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo signed six new bilateral agreements on Monday aimed at strengthening cooperation between the two countries.

stories.title: US climber dies in avalanche on Nepal’s Mount Makalu
stories.summary: American climber Shelley Johannesen, 53, died on Mount Makalu in Nepal after being caught in an avalanche while descending from the summit on Monday. She is the latest fatality in Nepal's spring climbing season, which has also claimed the lives of Czech climber David Roubinek and three Nepali guides in the Himalayas.

stories.title: Russia attacks railway infrastructure in Dnipropetrovsk region, train driver injured
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked railway infrastructure in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region on the morning of 12 May, damaging a locomotive and railcars. A train driver was injured in the strike.

stories.title: Tshisekedi turns to evangelical churches in DRC third-term battle
stories.summary: Congolese President Félix Tshisekedi is cultivating ties with evangelical and revivalist pastors as he pursues a potential third term. The strategy aims to counterbalance the Catholic Church, which has emerged as a leading opponent of constitutional changes in the DRC.

stories.title: Uber Hong Kong warns proposed permit cap risks triggering 70% rise in fares
stories.summary: Uber Hong Kong warned that a proposed government cap of 10,000 to 15,000 ride-hailing permits could raise fares by 70 per cent and leave 40 per cent of peak-hour bookings unfulfilled. The company currently has over 30,000 active drivers in the city, meaning the cap could halve its workforce.

stories.title: Foreign firms tie return to Iraq to stronger security guarantees
stories.summary: Foreign companies operating in Iraq are conditioning their return on stronger security guarantees from the Iraqi government. The withdrawal of firms has disrupted investment in Iraq's oil, gas, and electricity sectors, as well as visa services and humanitarian programs.

stories.title: Asean explores ‘tentative’ Myanmar re-engagement with virtual talks
stories.summary: ASEAN is considering re-engaging with Myanmar's military-backed government through a planned virtual meeting between Southeast Asian foreign ministers and a junta-appointed representative. ASEAN Secretary General Kao Kim Hourn confirmed the meeting was expected soon, on the sidelines of the bloc's summit in the Philippines. Myanmar has been largely frozen out of ASEAN activities since its 2021 coup.

stories.title: Iran urged against ‘weaponising’ Hormuz amid fragile ceasefire
stories.summary: The US-Iran ceasefire is at risk of collapse after President Trump called Iran's latest negotiating proposal "garbage." Turkey and Qatar urged Iran not to weaponize the Strait of Hormuz as diplomatic efforts continue.

stories.title: Iran to discuss enrichment as US ceasefire hangs in balance
stories.summary: Iran has signaled willingness to discuss its uranium enrichment program as the US-Iran ceasefire remains fragile. President Trump rejected Iran's latest proposal, calling it "garbage," raising concerns the truce could collapse.

stories.title: Tax cuts and cost of living help proposed by Labour-linked groups allied to Streeting and Burnham
stories.summary: Labour-affiliated groups linked to Health Secretary Wes Streeting and Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham have proposed competing policy visions as pressure mounts on UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer to resign. The Labour Growth Group and the Tribune group put forward plans including sweeping tax cuts and cost-of-living assistance.

stories.title: LIVE: UK’s Starmer under pressure as ministers quit, MPs call on PM to go
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces a political crisis after multiple ministers resigned and Labour MPs called for his departure. The upheaval follows significant election losses for the Labour Party.

stories.title: The Bahamas goes to polls in three-way battle with immigration a key issue
stories.summary: Voters in the Bahamas headed to the polls on Tuesday in a general election featuring a record number of voters. Immigration, particularly from neighboring Haiti, and the rising cost of living—exacerbated by gas price spikes linked to the Middle East conflict—are key issues. Former basketball star Rick Fox is among the high-profile candidates.

stories.title: Trump rejects ‘garbage’ Iran peace plan before heading to China
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump rejected Iran's response to a peace proposal, calling it "garbage" and declaring the month-long ceasefire on "massive life support." The remarks pushed Brent crude above $106 per barrel. Trump is expected to discuss the conflict with Chinese President Xi Jinping at a summit in Beijing on Thursday.

stories.title: China’s ‘dark factory’ more than doubles production efficiency for J-20 jets
stories.summary: China has more than doubled the production efficiency of stealth fighter jet components at a "dark factory" that uses autonomous vehicles and AI-driven machinery to operate nearly 24 hours a day with minimal human intervention. The facility can now produce the structural framework of an aircraft in near darkness, according to Science and Technology Daily.

stories.title: Hong Kong, mainland China spur surge in Asia-Pacific commercial property deals
stories.summary: Commercial property investment in the Asia-Pacific region rose 22 per cent year-on-year to $51.1 billion in the first quarter, according to MSCI data. Hong Kong contributed $1.8 billion, with early signs of recovery in office and retail segments across Hong Kong and mainland China driving the surge in deal volumes.

stories.title: War update: 174 combat clashes over past day, 32 Russian assaults halted in Pokrovsk sector
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces recorded 174 combat engagements with Russian troops along the front line on 11 May. The Pokrovsk sector saw the heaviest activity, with 32 Russian assaults halted by Ukraine's Defense Forces.

stories.title: Surge in gang violence in Haiti’s capital leaves hundreds displaced
stories.summary: Gang violence in northern neighborhoods of Port-au-Prince, Haiti, displaced hundreds of residents over the weekend. Families fled along the road to Haiti's main airport as armed clashes intensified.

stories.title: Real-life Transformers: China’s Unitree debuts ‘mecha’ robot that shifts from 2 legs to 4
stories.summary: Chinese robotics firm Unitree Robotics unveiled the GD01, a manned "mecha" robot capable of switching between bipedal and four-legged movement. The high-strength alloy machine weighs 500 kg with a pilot, is designed for civilian transport, and carries a starting price of 3.9 million yuan (approximately $573,674).

stories.title: Iran says it’s deployed mini submarines in contest to control Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran announced it has deployed mini submarines in the Strait of Hormuz. Each vessel is reportedly capable of carrying two torpedoes or two Chinese-designed C-704 anti-ship cruise missiles, signaling Tehran's efforts to assert control over the strategic waterway.

stories.title: Babiš didn’t scrap Czechia’s shell pipeline to Ukraine—he just stopped paying for it
stories.summary: The new Czech government under Prime Minister Andrej Babiš maintained the country's artillery shell procurement pipeline for Ukraine but stopped funding it with Czech government money. External donors are now covering the full cost of the program.

stories.title: Kharkiv region targeted by overnight drone attacks, fires break out
stories.summary: Russian forces launched overnight drone attacks on the town of Velykyi Burluk and the village of Bezruky in Ukraine's Kharkiv region on 12 May. The strikes caused fires in the targeted areas.

stories.title: Zelenskyy says Russia fired over 200 drones at Ukraine as truce expires
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reported that Russia launched over 200 drones at Ukraine following the expiration of a truce. Attacks on Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region killed one person and wounded four others, according to the local administration chief.

stories.title: France’s Macron announces $27bn investment in Africa at Kenya summit
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron announced $27 billion in investment commitments for Africa at the Africa Forward summit held in Kenya. The summit comes as France seeks to rebuild influence amid fading ties with its former African colonies, while Kenya pursues expanded trade relationships.

stories.title: SC overturns its own conviction of ex-minister Anwar Saifullah in graft case
stories.summary: Pakistan's Supreme Court overturned its own 2016 conviction of former petroleum minister Anwar Saifullah in a corruption reference. The court held that an appellate court should not substitute its own view when another conclusion on the same evidence was possible.

stories.title: India: New Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay cracks down on state-run TASMAC liquor shops
stories.summary: Newly appointed Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay ordered the closure of 717 state-run TASMAC liquor stores located near religious sites and schools in his first major policy decision.

stories.title: BBC unmasks key people smuggler in network behind most small boat crossings
stories.summary: The BBC identified a 28-year-old Iraqi Kurd operating under the alias "Kardo Ranya" as a key people smuggler linked to the network responsible for most small boat crossings across the English Channel. He has so far evaded arrest.

stories.title: Balochistan PA seeks tax reduction  for women’s hygiene products
stories.summary: The Balochistan Assembly adopted resolutions calling on Pakistan's federal government to reduce taxes on women's hygiene and sanitary products and to strengthen minority representation at provincial and local levels. The resolutions were jointly moved by JUI-F female members.

stories.title: ‘Whole morning revolves around gas’: Pakistan’s fuel crisis enters kitchens
stories.summary: Pakistan is experiencing a deepening fuel crisis that is severely affecting household cooking routines. Women across the country report waking early and restructuring their daily schedules around unpredictable gas availability.

stories.title: Chaos in Philippines as Duterte ally wanted by ICC takes refuge in senate to avoid arrest
stories.summary: Former Philippine police chief Ronald dela Rosa, a longtime ally of ex-President Rodrigo Duterte, sought refuge in the Philippine Senate to avoid arrest and potential transfer to the International Criminal Court in The Hague. CCTV footage showed dela Rosa fleeing through senate hallways from government agents. Another Duterte ally offered him protective custody.

stories.title: Russian attacks hit Dnipropetrovsk region overnight, killing one and injuring four
stories.summary: Russian overnight attacks on Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region killed one person and injured four others. The strikes were part of continued Russian assaults on the region.

stories.title: Minister announces ‘ad ban’ on channel that laid off 170 employees
stories.summary: Pakistan's information minister announced an advertising ban on a TV channel that laid off 170 employees. Members of the Parliamentary Reporters Association staged a walkout from the National Assembly press gallery to protest layoffs and non-payment of dues by private TV channels.

stories.title: Daily Quiz: On earthquakes
stories.summary: A daily quiz was published on the anniversary of the devastating May 2015 Nepal earthquake, testing readers' knowledge of earthquakes, seismic science, and some of history's deadliest tremors. The quiz is informational rather than news coverage.

stories.title: Oct. 7 sexual violence was patterned, documented, prosecutable, new report argues
stories.summary: A new report by a civil commission argues that sexual violence committed during the Hamas-led 7 October 2023 attacks followed identifiable patterns and is prosecutable. The report alleges Hamas and collaborators weaponized bodies, families, and digital platforms during the massacre and subsequent captivity.

stories.title: Denial of Hamas's October 7 sexual atrocities must come to an end - editorial
stories.summary: An editorial calls for an end to denial of sexual atrocities committed during the Hamas-led 7 October 2023 attacks on Israel. It urges international accountability and commitment to honouring victims.

stories.title: Inside the 300-page report Hamas hoped no one would uncover
stories.summary: A 300-page report presents evidence of systematic sexual violence carried out by Hamas during the 7 October 2023 attacks on Israel. The report was compiled nearly three years after the assault.

stories.title: Starmer is fighting to stay in power. Here’s what could happen
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces a serious leadership challenge after more than 70 Labour lawmakers publicly called for his departure following heavy losses in local elections. Several ministerial aides have resigned. A formal leadership contest has not yet been triggered, but pressure continues to mount within the party.

stories.title: Internal displacements caused by violence or conflict at record high in 2025
stories.summary: The Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre reported that conflict-driven internal displacements reached a record 32.3 million in 2025, surpassing disaster-related displacements for the first time since data collection began in 2008. The figure was 60 per cent higher than the previous year, with 82.2 million people displaced worldwide in total.

stories.title: Would you invest in a play? Hong Kong sets the stage for tokenised funding
stories.summary: Hong Kong fintech firm Esperanza Fintech Group plans to tokenize a stage play produced by film star Louis Koo and featuring actress Fish Liew, converting production costs and profits into tradeable digital units via blockchain. CEO Dan Ronald Leung said this would be the firm's fifth token-based entertainment investment project this year.

stories.title: PM extends conservation, austerity steps till June 13
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif extended a countrywide austerity drive until June 13 amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. The premier and senior officials, including Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, also met with President Asif Ali Zardari to discuss a possible 28th Constitutional Amendment.

stories.title: Russia’s war casualty toll in Ukraine up by 1,020 over past day
stories.summary: Russia's total estimated combat losses in Ukraine from 24 February 2022 to 12 May 2026 have reached approximately 1,343,050 personnel. An estimated 1,020 Russian troops were lost in the preceding 24 hours.

stories.title: M23 pulls back from eastern DRC towns as ceasefire pressure mounts
stories.summary: The Rwanda-backed M23 armed group withdrew from several areas in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo amid mounting ceasefire pressure. Local residents and DRC military officials confirmed the pullback.

stories.title: Israel issues new evacuation orders for four south Lebanon towns
stories.summary: The Israeli military issued evacuation orders for residents of four southern Lebanese towns—Arzoun, Tayr Debba, Al-Bazouriyah, and Al-Hawsh—ahead of planned military operations. Israeli forces also destroyed a solar-powered water pumping station in Deir Mimas, despite an existing ceasefire arrangement.

stories.title: In first official confirmation, US envoys say Israel sent Iron Dome to UAE
stories.summary: US Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz confirmed at an Israeli Independence Day event in New York that Israel sent Iron Dome air defense systems to the UAE. The system was used to defend against Iranian missile attacks during the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Moscow’s Victory Day ceasefire reduced combat but became Russia’s stockpile window, ISW finds
stories.summary: The Institute for the Study of War found that Moscow's Victory Day ceasefire reduced combat temporarily but was used by Russia to stockpile weapons. A Ukrainian brigade near Lyman reported Russia held back Molniya drones before the truce and deployed them during the pause while moving up reserves.

stories.title: Trade disputes, Taiwan and Iran war: Can US and China reach a consensus?
stories.summary: US and Chinese officials are preparing for talks amid escalating disputes over trade, Taiwan, and the Iran war. The meeting will highlight growing contrasts between the positions of President Trump's administration and Chinese President Xi Jinping's government.

stories.title: Developer of education tool Canvas issues apology after hack
stories.summary: Instructure, the developer of the widely used education platform Canvas, issued an apology following a hack. The company's CEO stated that Canvas remains fully operational and safe to use despite the security breach.

stories.title: Kevin Warsh clears key Senate hurdle in bid to lead U.S. Federal Reserve
stories.summary: Kevin Warsh cleared a key Senate procedural vote in his bid to become the next chair of the U.S. Federal Reserve. The Republican-controlled Senate is expected to confirm him at a time when the central bank's independence faces scrutiny.

stories.title: Is Africa ready for the AI revolution? The scramble for resources, jobs, digital sovereignty
stories.summary: At the Africa Forward summit in Nairobi, discussions centered on Africa's readiness for the AI revolution, including questions of digital sovereignty and data storage. Countries such as Zambia, Zimbabwe, and Ghana have rejected deals to store citizens' data in the U.S. France is positioning the summit as an opportunity to offer an alternative to U.S. and Chinese tech dominance.

stories.title: Adaptive deterrence urged to counter India’s hostile posture
stories.summary: Pakistani strategic affairs experts at a Centre for International Strategic Studies event in Islamabad warned that the regional security environment with India is becoming increasingly fragile. They urged adaptive deterrence measures, predicting future conflicts will focus on cyber, hybrid, and narrative strategies.

stories.title: Brazilian activist claims torture during detention in Israel after flotilla interception
stories.summary: Brazilian activist Thiago Ávila alleged he was tortured during detention by Israeli authorities following the interception of a Gaza-bound aid flotilla. Ávila made the accusations after his release and return to Brazil.

stories.title: A changed world
stories.summary: A commentary reflects on the one-year anniversary of Pakistan's May 2024 military conflict with India, which followed the Pahalgam incident. The piece notes Pakistan's claimed successes, including the downing of multiple Indian aircraft, while acknowledging losses on both sides.

stories.title: Russian drone attack leaves homes, kindergarten damaged in Kyiv region
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack overnight damaged residential buildings and a kindergarten in Ukraine's Kyiv region. No casualty figures were immediately reported.

stories.title: DocAviv hosts 10 days of screenings throughout Tel Aviv
stories.summary: The DocAviv film festival is hosting its 28th edition with 10 days of screenings across Tel Aviv. Subjects covered include Icelandic rapids, the creator of Pippi Longstocking, and social networks.

stories.title: Report says UAE carried out secret strikes on Iran, hit refinery on Lavan Island
stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that the UAE secretly carried out strikes against Iran during the ongoing US-Israeli conflict, including hitting a refinery on Lavan Island in early April. Iran reportedly responded by launching ballistic missiles at the UAE.

stories.title: Pakistan parked Iranian planes on its airbases to escape U.S. airstrikes: report
stories.summary: A report states that Pakistan allowed Iranian military and civilian aircraft to be parked at its air bases to protect them from US airstrikes during the conflict. Iran also reportedly moved civilian aircraft to neighboring Afghanistan for the same purpose.

stories.title: Palestine weekly wrap: Israeli settlers rampage through West Bank villages
stories.summary: Israeli settlers attacked multiple West Bank villages, uprooting olive trees, seizing Palestinian land, and displacing families. The incidents reflect a pattern of unchecked settler violence across the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Pakistan struck a rehab centre and killed 269 Afghans. Their families want to know why
stories.summary: A Pakistani airstrike on March 16 struck a rehabilitation center, killing 269 Afghans according to reports, with the UN suggesting the actual death toll may be higher. There are calls to investigate the strike as a potential war crime.

stories.title: The Other Border Problem: How Russia and China’s Lawfare Threaten the Arctic
stories.summary: Russia and China are increasingly using lawfare tactics to challenge Western claims and influence in the Arctic, which is becoming a contested space. Their methods include excessive maritime regulations, coordinated challenges to continental shelf claims, and the use of shadow fleets to avoid accountability.

stories.title: BJP leader back to head India's Assam state for second time in a row
stories.summary: Himanta Biswa Sarma, a senior BJP leader credited with expanding the party's presence in India's northeast, has returned to lead the state of Assam for a second consecutive term.

stories.title: Trump says he supports suspending US gas tax with prices remaining high amid Iran war
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump expressed support for suspending the federal gas tax as fuel prices remain elevated amid the ongoing war with Iran. The surge in gas prices poses a political risk for Trump's Republican Party ahead of midterm elections.

stories.title: Conflict created more internal displacement than disasters in 2025: Monitors
stories.summary: Monitoring organizations reported that armed conflict drove more internal displacement worldwide than natural disasters in 2025. With new wars continuing into 2026, analysts expect violence-driven displacement figures to rise further.

stories.title: Kenya: Bolt Raises Fares By 6pc Amid Rising Fuel Costs
stories.summary: Ride-hailing platform Bolt raised fares by 6 percent in Kenya to help drivers cope with increased operational costs driven by rising fuel prices.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: The US-Iran ceasefire faces growing uncertainty after President Trump called Iran's latest proposal "totally unacceptable." Meanwhile, Israeli strikes in Lebanon continue, oil prices are rising, and concerns over disruption at the Strait of Hormuz are intensifying.

stories.title: Bannu attack
stories.summary: Terrorists attacked a police outpost in Bannu district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, on the night of May 9, killing 15 officers and injuring three. The assault involved an explosive-laden truck, heavy weaponry, and drones in a coordinated multi-directional attack.

stories.title: Gaborone gold rush: how Botswana rose to the top of men’s sprinting
stories.summary: Botswana has emerged as a force in men's sprinting, highlighted by a home victory in the men's 4x400m relay at the World Athletics Relays in Gaborone. Olympic 200m champion Letsile Tebogo, 22, ran the second leg, while Collen Kebinatshipi anchored the win by overtaking South Africa. The country credits investment in young athletes for its rise.

stories.title: Starving on the front lines: Food supply in crisis as Ukraine fights Russia
stories.summary: Photographs of emaciated Ukrainian soldiers have revealed a severe food supply crisis on the front lines of the Russia-Ukraine war. Reports indicate that inadequate rations are affecting troops on both the Ukrainian and Russian sides of the conflict.

stories.title: Govt dusts off oil refining policy as Hormuz disruptions bite
stories.summary: Pakistan's government has revived its long-delayed petroleum refining policy in response to oil supply disruptions caused by hostilities near the Strait of Hormuz. The petroleum minister described local refineries as critical national assets and said removing implementation bottlenecks was essential.

stories.title: Africa Forward Summit Day 2: Macron pitches new French partnership model
stories.summary: The second day of the Africa Forward summit in Nairobi, Kenya, brought together leaders and officials from over 30 African countries. French President Emmanuel Macron used the event to pitch a new model for French partnerships with African nations.

stories.title: U.S. issues new sanctions over Iran’s oil shipments to China
stories.summary: The US Treasury imposed new sanctions targeting Iran's oil shipments to China, following earlier sanctions on individuals and companies aiding Iranian weapons and drone component purchases. The measures aim to disrupt revenue streams supporting Iran's military programs.

stories.title: Why is Israel allowed to take part in the Eurovision song contest?
