stories.summary: Ukrainian company EDRONE showcased its Baton drone interceptor system at the SAHA 2026 defense exhibition in Istanbul, Turkey. The system, designed to protect critical infrastructure, was presented in both fixed-wing and copter-type configurations.

stories.title: Russia is still receiving modernized T-90M, T-80BVM, and T-72B3M tanks. All of them are built on Soviet-era platforms
stories.summary: Russia continues to receive modernized T-90M, T-80BVM, and T-72B3M tanks, all built on Soviet-era platforms. Meanwhile, the T-14 Armata, Russia's planned next-generation tank, has seen virtually no serial production despite extensive official promotion.

stories.title: Lebanon says Israeli strikes killed 39
stories.summary: Lebanese authorities reported that Israeli strikes killed 39 people in Lebanon. The attacks occurred despite a ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hezbollah announced the previous month. Both sides have continued to exchange fire in violation of the deal.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill four in Lebanon, raising Lebanon death toll to 23
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed at least four people in fresh strikes in southern Lebanon, bringing the day's death toll to at least 23. Lebanon's National News Agency reported a drone strike on a motorcycle near the Toul–Doueir road and airstrikes in Nabatieh that killed three young men.

stories.title: Merz says Europe wants a strong NATO and shares US goal of ending Iran war
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, speaking in Stockholm, said Europe wants to maintain a strong NATO alliance and shares the US goal of ending the Iran war, despite transatlantic differences the conflict has exposed.

stories.title: Ukrainians welcome respite from Russian attacks, Moscow says peace still far off
stories.summary: Ukrainians welcomed a three-day US-brokered ceasefire from May 9 to 11, providing a respite from Russian attacks. Moscow stated that a lasting peace agreement remains far off.

stories.title: Oil chiefs warn Hormuz closure exposes fragility of global energy system
stories.summary: Senior oil and gas industry figures warned that the closure of the Strait of Hormuz during the Iran conflict has exposed deep structural vulnerabilities in global energy supply chains. They said the disruption is expected to drive a fundamental shift in the energy landscape.

stories.title: Ex-minister tells UK cabinet to boot Starmer or she’ll challenge him herself
stories.summary: Former UK minister Catherine West threatened to challenge Prime Minister Keir Starmer for the Labour Party leadership if no replacement plan emerges by May 11. Starmer's Labour suffered its worst governing-party losses in local elections since 1995, prompting growing calls from lawmakers for him to resign.

stories.title: German General: Russia expanding military near NATO, may use it for attack
stories.summary: A senior German general warned that Russia is expanding its military capabilities along NATO borders and could, under certain conditions, decide to attack Alliance territory. He emphasized that credible deterrence remains essential to preventing such an escalation.

stories.title: Russia planned major naval counteroffensive against Ukraine in 2026. Drones were built, but they can’t be used
stories.summary: Russia reportedly planned a major naval counteroffensive against Ukraine for 2026 using unmanned drones. According to Ukrainian Defense Ministry advisor Serhii Beskrestnov, a single decision rendered the built drones unusable, collapsing the entire unmanned naval campaign before it launched.

stories.title: Latmiya: Inside the Ashura rituals shaping Iran’s wartime narrative
stories.summary: Since the 12-day Iran-Israel war in June 2025, mourning recitations known as latmiyah, rooted in Ashura rituals, have become a prominent feature of Iran's wartime atmosphere. Performed in halls across Iran and widely shared on social media, the chants emphasize themes of martyrdom, sacrifice, and war.

stories.title: Indonesian rescuers find 1 body after volcano eruption as search continues for 2 more
stories.summary: Rescuers on Indonesia's Halmahera island recovered the body of a woman killed during the eruption of Mount Dukono on May 8. Search operations continued for the bodies of two Singaporeans still missing after the eruption.

stories.title: Abbas takes five wickets to put Pakistan ahead in Bangladesh Test
stories.summary: Pakistani bowler Mohammad Abbas took five wickets to restrict Bangladesh to 413 in the first Test in Dhaka. Debutants Azan Awais (85 not out) and Abdullah Fazal (37 not out) helped Pakistan reach 179-1 at stumps on day two.

stories.title: Israeli settlers force Palestinian family to exhume and rebury their father
stories.summary: In the occupied West Bank, Israeli settlers forced a Palestinian family to exhume and rebury their father. The United Nations condemned the incident, describing it as appalling and emblematic of the dehumanization of Palestinians.

stories.title: Putin says he thinks Ukraine war is 'coming to an end'
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin said he believes the war in Ukraine is "coming to an end," speaking as Russia and Ukraine observe a three-day ceasefire in their four-year conflict.

stories.title: Putin says he thinks Ukraine war 'coming to an end'
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin stated he believes the war in Ukraine is coming to an end. He made the remarks as Moscow and Kyiv observed a three-day ceasefire during the four-year conflict.

stories.title: Russian Widows, Mothers of Soldiers Killed in Ukraine Join Victory Day March in Chita
stories.summary: In the Russian city of Chita, widows and mothers of soldiers killed in Ukraine participated in the annual Victory Day march for the first time. The event commemorates the Soviet victory over Nazi Germany in World War II.

stories.title: Putin says Ukraine war 'heading to an end' despite ceasefire violations
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin declared the Ukraine war is heading toward an end during a press conference, despite both Russia and Ukraine accusing each other of violating a three-day US-brokered ceasefire. The temporary truce coincided with Russia's World War II victory celebrations.

stories.title: GHQ to host ceremony marking one year since Marka-i-Haq victory on Sunday
stories.summary: Pakistan's General Headquarters in Rawalpindi will host a ceremony on Sunday marking one year since the Marka-i-Haq military victory. Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir will serve as chief guest, joined by the air and naval chiefs of staff.

stories.title: Israel to release two Gaza flotilla activists ahead of deportation: rights group
stories.summary: Israel is preparing to release Gaza flotilla activists Saif Abukeshek and Thiago Avila after more than a week of detention. A rights group confirmed the imminent release ahead of their deportation.

stories.title: Russia said to be sending Iran drone parts via Caspian Sea, bypassing Hormuz blockade
stories.summary: According to the New York Times, Russia has been shipping drone parts to Iran via the Caspian Sea, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz. The shipments could allow Tehran to rapidly restock its drone arsenal while evading sanctions and avoiding contested Persian Gulf routes.

stories.title: Missing Singaporeans Located Near Mt. Dukono Crater Rim
stories.summary: Indonesian authorities located missing Singaporean nationals near the crater rim of Mount Dukono following an eruption of the volcano. The group was found in the vicinity of the active crater in Indonesia's North Maluku province.

stories.title: Ukraine deploys AI-powered turret that can shoot down FPVs. Operator’s only job is to press button to confirm strike
stories.summary: Ukraine has deployed an AI-powered turret system capable of shooting down first-person-view drones, with the operator only needing to confirm each strike. The K-2 Brigade recorded the first combat use, and more than ten frontline units are now operating the system across key sectors.

stories.title: Russian attacks leave one civilian killed, three injured in Kherson region
stories.summary: A 58-year-old woman was killed and three others were injured in Russia's attacks on Ukraine's Kherson region. The fatality resulted from a Russian drone strike targeting civilian areas.

stories.title: Iran demands guarantees for World Cup participation
stories.summary: The Iranian Football Federation submitted 10 conditions to FIFA regarding Iran's participation in the upcoming World Cup, hosted by the United States, Mexico, and Canada. The demands come amid rising tensions over the team's involvement in the tournament.

stories.title: Jewish settler attack wounds two Palestinian women in occupied West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian communities south of Nablus in the occupied West Bank, throwing stones at homes in the Wadi al-Hajj Issa area between Jurish village and Aqrabah. The Palestinian Red Crescent treated two women wounded in the assault, including a 35-year-old pregnant woman and a 65-year-old.

stories.title: Russian forces using heavy hexacopters to mine roads on Sloviansk front
stories.summary: Russian forces are deploying heavy hexacopter drones to lay mines on roads in the Sloviansk sector of the front in eastern Ukraine. The tactic represents an evolving use of unmanned aerial vehicles in the conflict.

stories.title: UK deploys warship to Middle East with eye on potential Hormuz mission
stories.summary: The United Kingdom is deploying a warship to the Middle East as part of a joint British-French effort to ensure safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz. The initiative comes as the US and Iran explore a potential diplomatic off-ramp from their 10-week conflict.

stories.title: Kremlin says peace in Ukraine is still a very long way off
stories.summary: The Kremlin stated on May 9 that a peace agreement to end the war in Ukraine remains far off due to the complexity of the issues involved. Moscow said the United States was rushing to broker a deal but acknowledged significant obstacles to reaching any accord.

stories.title: Australia’s antisemitism inquiry should alarm every Jew - opinion
stories.summary: An Australian Royal Commission on antisemitism has raised concerns about the extent of anti-Jewish sentiment in the country. The inquiry's findings point to what commentators describe as a deeper crisis of antisemitism.

stories.title: Tucker Carlson’s pivot
stories.summary: Tucker Carlson, formerly a prominent MAGA loyalist, has repositioned himself as an antiwar commentator. Observers debate whether this shift reflects genuine conviction or strategic rebranding.

stories.title: Greece conducts controlled blast of mystery naval drone explosives
stories.summary: Greek authorities conducted a controlled detonation of explosives found on an unmanned naval drone discovered by fishermen in a cave. The vessel is suspected to be of Ukrainian origin.

stories.title: Germany’s business ties to Russia delayed aid to Ukraine, historian says
stories.summary: A historian argues that Germany's close business and political ties with Russia delayed Berlin's support for Ukraine at the start of Russia's full-scale invasion. Fears of nuclear escalation and belief in Russian invincibility also contributed to the hesitation.

stories.title: Trump’s feuds and tensions with US allies likely to outlast Iran war
stories.summary: The US-led strikes on Iran have deepened rifts between the Trump administration and NATO allies as well as Gulf partners. Many of these allies opposed the conflict and are now dealing with its economic fallout, with tensions expected to persist beyond the war.

stories.title: European states to send planes to evacuate citizens from hantavirus-hit cruise ship
stories.summary: Germany, France, Belgium, Ireland, and the Netherlands are sending planes to evacuate their citizens from a cruise ship bound for Tenerife that was struck by a deadly hantavirus outbreak. The EU is dispatching two additional planes for remaining European citizens. WHO chief Tedros arrived in Spain to oversee the disembarkation in the Canary Islands.

stories.title: Syria and Lebanon make ‘significant progress’ at talks on joint interests
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister and Syrian President met in Damascus to discuss shared concerns including security, transport, and energy cooperation. Officials described the talks as yielding significant progress on joint interests.

stories.title: A look at the new capabilities Pakistan employed against India during Marka-i-Haq
stories.summary: One year after the brief but intense Pakistan-India military confrontation known as Marka-i-Haq, an analysis examines the advanced weaponry and military technology Pakistan employed, including missiles and network-linked warfare capabilities. The conflict ended with a US-brokered ceasefire.

stories.title: Global oil stocks drop almost 270 million barrels since start of Iran war
stories.summary: Global oil inventories have fallen by approximately 270 million barrels since the start of the Israeli-US war on Iran, driven by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Bloomberg data shows stockpiles declined about 4.8 million barrels per day between March 1 and April 25, pushing reserves toward their lowest levels since 2018.

stories.title: MPs from Labour’s left to urge Ed Miliband to consider leadership bid
stories.summary: Labour left MPs in the UK are expected to urge former minister Ed Miliband to consider a leadership bid against Keir Starmer. Former minister Catherine West said she would launch her own challenge if no cabinet minister came forward by Monday.

stories.title: Eurovision warns Israel over vote manipulation
stories.summary: The Eurovision Song Contest has warned Israel over alleged vote manipulation for the second consecutive year. Israel's first-place finish in 2025 had previously prompted changes to voting rules.

stories.title: War update: 51 frontline clashes since dawn, Pokrovsk, Huliaipole sectors see fiercest fighting
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked Ukrainian positions 51 times since dawn, with the heaviest fighting concentrated in the Pokrovsk and Huliaipole sectors. Russian forces also continued shelling Ukrainian border areas.

stories.title: Israel to release Gaza flotilla activists today ahead of deportation: rights group
stories.summary: Israel announced it will release Spanish national Saif Abu Keshek and Brazilian Thiago Avila, two activists seized from a Gaza-bound flotilla intercepted by the Israeli navy in international waters off Greece on April 30, before deporting them.

stories.title: Lebanon, Syria make 'significant progress' in addressing issues
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam led a delegation to Damascus on Saturday for talks with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa. Officials reported significant progress in addressing longstanding bilateral issues between Lebanon and Syria.

stories.title: UK sending warship to Middle East ahead of Hormuz mission
stories.summary: The United Kingdom is deploying a warship to the Middle East in preparation for a potential mission to secure the Strait of Hormuz. Britain and France announced last month that military plans to restore trade flows through the strait were progressing.

stories.title: Iran keeps US waiting for its response to latest proposal after flareups in fighting
stories.summary: Iran has delayed its response to the latest US diplomatic proposal amid renewed fighting, citing suspicions about Washington's seriousness. Pakistan has insisted that diplomacy is ongoing, while the UK dispatched a warship to the Strait of Hormuz ahead of a potential naval mission.

stories.title: Steve Rosenberg: This year's Victory Day parade in Moscow felt very different
stories.summary: BBC Russia editor Steve Rosenberg reported that Moscow's 2025 Victory Day parade on Red Square notably lacked the military hardware typically displayed by the Kremlin to project power internationally.

stories.title: Could and would Ukraine target Putin?
stories.summary: A temporary ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine took effect as President Putin oversaw a Victory Day military parade in Moscow's Red Square. The parade was notably stripped of the military hardware and technological displays typically featured in previous years.

stories.title: “Nowhere left to go”: Gaza residents return to rubble after Israeli strike
stories.summary: Al Jazeera correspondent Tareq Abu Azzoum reported from Al-Shati Refugee Camp in Gaza, where residents returned to destroyed homes following overnight Israeli airstrikes. Displaced civilians described having no remaining safe locations.

stories.title: Qatari LNG tanker heads to Strait of Hormuz in first transit since Iran war began
stories.summary: A Qatari LNG tanker, the Al Kharaitiyat, departed Ras Laffan and is approaching the Strait of Hormuz en route to Port Qasim in Pakistan. If completed, it would be the first known transit by a Qatari LNG carrier through the strait since the US-Israeli war on Iran began.

stories.title: Israeli attacks across Lebanon kill at least 19
stories.summary: Israeli attacks across Lebanon killed at least 19 people despite an existing US-brokered ceasefire. A new round of ceasefire negotiations is expected next week.

stories.title: Nigeria army says killed 50 militants in northeast
stories.summary: The Nigerian army reported killing 50 Islamist militants in the country's northeast on Thursday. Forces repelled a coordinated assault by the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) on the headquarters of the military's 27th brigade.

stories.title: US says naval blockade on Iran continues, 58 vessels diverted
stories.summary: US Central Command stated that its naval blockade on Iran remains in effect. Since mid-April, US forces have diverted 58 commercial vessels and disabled four others to prevent them from reaching Iranian ports.

stories.title: Putin attends scaled-back WWII victory parade as worries deepen over Ukraine war
stories.summary: Russia held its annual Victory Day parade on Moscow's Red Square amid growing domestic anxiety over the war in Ukraine. President Vladimir Putin presided over the event as concerns mount about the conflict's trajectory.

stories.title: Drug supplier, extortionist arrested in separate police operations in Karachi
stories.summary: Karachi's Special Investigation Unit arrested an alleged crystal methamphetamine and heroin supplier at the Lyari riverbed and an extortionist in separate operations, with the narcotics suspect apprehended after a reported encounter.

stories.title: Over 1.2 million Syrians return since fall of Assad
stories.summary: More than 1.2 million Syrians have returned to the country since the fall of the Assad regime in 2024. However, some displaced Syrians remain reluctant to return, citing poor living conditions.

stories.title: Czech analyst: Russia resembles ‘Third Reich’ and must be defeated
stories.summary: A Czech analyst characterized Russia as resembling the "Third Reich" and argued it must face military defeat and accountability. The comparison was drawn in the context of Russia's ongoing war in Ukraine.

stories.title: Peru opens war crimes probe into Israeli soldier over Gaza war
stories.summary: Peruvian prosecutors opened a preliminary investigation into an Israeli soldier accused of war crimes and genocide committed during the war in Gaza. The probe marks a notable legal action by a Latin American country regarding the conflict.

stories.title: Israeli settlers force Palestinians to exhume body after burial
stories.summary: Israeli settlers in the West Bank forced a Palestinian family to dig up a recently buried relative's body. The settlers claimed the burial site was too close to their settlement, compelling the family to exhume the remains for reburial elsewhere.

stories.title: Feared Iran oil slick smaller, may be from infrastructure
stories.summary: An oil slick detected near a small Gulf island off the west coast appeared smaller than initially feared and may have originated from existing infrastructure rather than military strikes. The exact cause of the apparent spill has not yet been confirmed.

stories.title: Syrian president discusses security with Lebanon PM
stories.summary: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa and Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam met in Damascus on Saturday to discuss economic cooperation and security coordination. The meeting aimed to strengthen bilateral ties established since the overthrow of Bashar al-Assad.

stories.title: Poland and Russia Can’t Stop Arguing Over History. Does it Matter?
stories.summary: Poland and Russia continue to dispute the interpretation of World War II events more than 80 years after they occurred. The historical disagreements remain a significant point of tension between the two countries.

stories.title: Israeli attacks kill 18 in Lebanon, 3 Israeli soldiers injured
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes killed at least 18 people across multiple locations in southern Lebanon on Saturday, including in Nabatieh, Nahrain, Saadiyat, Haboush, and Saksakiyeh, despite an existing ceasefire arrangement. Three Israeli soldiers were wounded by a Hezbollah drone near the Lebanese border in northern Israel.

stories.title: Gaza flotilla activists to be released from detention, deported from Israel
stories.summary: Two Gaza flotilla activists are expected to be released from Israeli detention and deported. Israel's Shin Bet security agency informed the Adalah legal center of the pending release, and lawyers are monitoring the process.

stories.title: Frontier Airlines plane fatally strikes person during takeoff at Denver airport
stories.summary: A Frontier Airlines plane struck and killed a person on the runway at Denver International Airport during takeoff late Friday, causing an engine fire. Passengers were safely evacuated after the individual reportedly jumped a perimeter fence and walked onto the runway.

stories.title: ‘On level of atomic bomb’: Iran highlights Hormuz importance amid US talks
stories.summary: An Iranian politician emphasized the strategic importance of the Strait of Hormuz amid ongoing US-Iran talks, describing it as a capability that could affect the entire global economy with a single decision.

stories.title: Iran questions ‘seriousness’ of the US to Turkish foreign minister
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told Turkish counterpart Hakan Fidan in a phone call that recent US military escalations and ceasefire violations raise doubts about Washington's seriousness regarding diplomacy. The remarks came amid ongoing US-Iran ceasefire negotiations.

stories.title: German historian: Berlin long mistakenly equated soviet WWII victims with Russia alone
stories.summary: A German historian argued that German society and politics long mistakenly equated Soviet World War II victims exclusively with Russia. Ukraine and Belarus, which were the main arenas of the Nazi war and the Holocaust, were historically marginalized in German remembrance until Russia's 2022 invasion.

stories.title: Why Welsh voters turned their backs on the Labour party
stories.summary: Labour suffered a dramatic collapse in Wales's Senedd elections, finishing third after more than a century as the dominant political force. Voters cited disregard from UK Labour leadership and struggling public services among reasons for the party's decline.

stories.title: No-bid contract to turn DC’s reflecting pool blue goes to firm with ties to Trump
stories.summary: The U.S. government awarded a $6.9 million no-bid contract to Atlantic Industrial Coatings, based in New Canton, Virginia, to paint and restore the Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool in Washington, DC. The New York Times reported the firm had previously renovated a swimming pool at President Trump's Virginia golf course, raising questions about the contracting process.

stories.title: Ukrainians mark end of WWII amid fragile ceasefire with Russia
stories.summary: Ukrainians marked the end of World War II as a temporary ceasefire with Russia took effect. Residents in Zaporizhzhia, Kharkiv, and Kyiv drew parallels between past and present suffering, expressing cautious hope mixed with skepticism about whether the pause could lead to peace negotiations.

stories.title: Three Indian-origin men in Canada convicted of couple’s murder
stories.summary: Three men of Indian origin were convicted in Canada for the murder of a couple found dead at their home in Abbotsford, British Columbia, in May 2022. No further details on the motive or sentencing were immediately available.

stories.title: New Israeli strike in southern Lebanon kills seven, including a young girl
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike in southern Lebanon killed seven people, including a young girl, on Saturday. The strike was part of a series of Israeli bombardments carried out despite the ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah.

stories.title: 'End of an era': EU flag outside parliament signals shift in Hungary
stories.summary: The European Union flag was raised alongside Hungary's national flag outside parliament in Budapest, signaling a potential shift away from years of confrontation with Brussels. The change follows the political transition from Viktor Orbán's government, which had frequently clashed with the EU on rule-of-law and Ukraine policy.

stories.title: Pakistan security forces kill 5 terrorists in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
stories.summary: Pakistani security forces killed five terrorists in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, with four of the dead identified as members of the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). The engagement took place in the Tank district, according to a military statement.

stories.title: Ukrainian National Guard breaks through Russian defense line near Vovchansk
stories.summary: Ukraine's National Guard "R.U.G" assault regiment of the Khartiia second corps breached Russian defensive lines near Vovchansk. The unit crossed the line of combat engagement and cleared forward Russian positions during an assault operation.

stories.title: UAE and Turkey leaders discuss regional issues in phone call
stories.summary: UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan held a phone call discussing bilateral cooperation and regional stability. They also discussed the UAE's participation in the Saha Expo 2026 defence and aerospace exhibition in Istanbul.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill at least one in south Lebanon while 12-year-old girl in critical condition
stories.summary: Israeli strikes hit southern Lebanon on Saturday, killing at least one person in Nabatieh. A Syrian man and his 12-year-old daughter were targeted on a motorbike outside Israeli-designated evacuation areas, in what Lebanese authorities described as a ceasefire violation.

stories.title: Qatar and Egypt discuss US-Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: Qatar's Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani and Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty discussed supporting a ceasefire between the US and Iran during a phone call. The Qatari foreign ministry said both diplomats focused on de-escalation and regional stability.

stories.title: European nations dispatch planes to evacuate citizens from hantavirus-hit cruise ship
stories.summary: Germany, France, Belgium, Ireland, and the Netherlands dispatched planes to evacuate citizens from the MV Hondius cruise ship after a deadly hantavirus outbreak on board. The EU, the United States, and the United Kingdom are also arranging transport for remaining passengers.

stories.title: Michael Jackson biopic revives legend of Jewish music mogul Walter Yetnikoff
stories.summary: A new biopic about Michael Jackson highlights the role of Jewish music executive Walter Yetnikoff, who reportedly pressured MTV to air the "Billie Jean" video. Jackson's estate credits that moment with opening opportunities for a generation of Black artists.

stories.title: Niger suspends nine French media bodies: Watchdog slams ‘abusive’ decision
stories.summary: Niger's military government suspended nine French media organizations, a move condemned by a media watchdog as abusive. The junta has banned dozens of local and foreign reporters since overthrowing the civilian government in 2023.

stories.title: Budget electric cars lure Europe’s drivers after fuel price jump
stories.summary: Rising fuel prices linked to the Middle East conflict are driving lower-income European households toward budget electric vehicles. The shift reflects growing consumer interest in affordable EVs as an alternative to increasingly expensive fossil fuels.

stories.title: Bahrain arrests dozens of Shia clerics as crackdown intensifies
stories.summary: Bahraini authorities arrested dozens of Shia clerics in an intensifying crackdown, including some of the country's most prominent religious figures. The detainees were accused of having links to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

stories.title: Russia-Ukraine war changes Germany’s strategic culture, Bundeswehr general says
stories.summary: A Bundeswehr general stated that Russia's full-scale war against Ukraine has fundamentally shifted Germany's strategic culture and security policy, introducing the concept of "integrated security" involving broader societal participation in national defense.

stories.title: ‘Broken Glass’ 2026: History repeats itself as Britain's Jews face new wave of terror - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece draws parallels between historical attacks on Jewish communities and a current wave of violence targeting synagogues and Jewish-owned businesses in the UK and other countries.

stories.title: Army is fighting 'aggressive' NATO-backed force in Victory Day speech: Russian President Putin
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin used his Victory Day speech on Red Square to assert that Russia is fighting an "aggressive" NATO-backed force. The annual parade was significantly scaled back, with no military hardware displayed for the first time in nearly two decades and few foreign dignitaries attending.

stories.title: Ethiopia: Ethiopian Economic Reform Attracts Zimbabwean Investors - Ambassador Rashid
stories.summary: Ethiopia's ongoing economic reforms are attracting increasing interest from Zimbabwean investors, according to Ambassador Rashid Mohammed. The diplomatic engagement highlights growing economic ties between the two African nations.

stories.title: East Africa: Ethiopia Spearheads Digital Hub for African Content Creators
stories.summary: Ethiopia is developing digital infrastructure aimed at empowering African content creators, according to Deputy Permanent Representative Bereket Driba. The initiative positions Ethiopia as a hub for digital storytelling on the continent.

stories.title: Ethiopia: Ethiopia's President Taye Holds Talks With UN Official Li Junhua On Dev't Goals
stories.summary: Ethiopian President Taye Atske-Selassie met with UN Under-Secretary-General for Economic and Social Affairs Li Junhua at the National Palace in Addis Ababa. The discussions focused on development goals and UN cooperation with Ethiopia.

stories.title: Africa: Ethiopia's Multifaceted Achievements Serve As Model for Africa, Say Social Media Influencers
stories.summary: African social media influencers attending the ASMIS 2026 summit in Addis Ababa praised Ethiopia's progress in infrastructure, technology, and cultural preservation. Participants said the country's achievements offer a model for other African nations.

stories.title: How has the Six Day War of 1967 shaped Israel of 2026? - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece examines how the 1967 Six Day War has shaped Israel through 2026. The author argues the war marked a turning point in the Jewish world's renewed engagement with the State of Israel.

stories.title: Hungary’s new PM takes oath of office, ending Orban’s 16-year rule
stories.summary: Peter Magyar was sworn in as Hungary's new prime minister, ending Viktor Orban's 16-year rule. Magyar called for regime-change celebrations, with supporters hoping he will strengthen ties with the EU and distance Hungary from Russia.

stories.title: U.S. ready to send team to Russia for talks on Ukraine, President Trump says
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced he is prepared to send an American negotiating team to Moscow for talks aimed at addressing the war in Ukraine.

stories.title: 'No home left' for Gazans stranded in West Bank
stories.summary: Gazans stranded in the occupied West Bank, including in Nablus, are unable to return home due to the ongoing war. Among them is Sameer Abu Salah from Khan Yunis, who had been working in Tel Aviv and is now living under the bleachers of a Nablus stadium with other displaced men.

stories.title: US, Iran no closer to ending war as Tehran’s response awaited
stories.summary: A period of relative calm held around the Strait of Hormuz on May 9 following days of sporadic clashes between the United States and Iran. Washington awaited Tehran's response to its latest proposals aimed at ending over two months of fighting and opening peace negotiations.

stories.title: Pedestrian dies in US after being hit by Frontier Airlines plane at Denver airport
stories.summary: A pedestrian was killed after being struck by a Frontier Airlines plane during takeoff at Denver International Airport. The individual had reportedly jumped a perimeter fence onto the runway. The collision caused an engine fire, forcing passenger evacuation.

stories.title: Reporters Notebook: Israel’s northern border amid peace and war
stories.summary: Communities along Israel's northern border are showing signs of quiet resilience, resuming daily life despite ongoing security tensions. The area continues to face rising threats amid the broader regional conflict.

stories.title: Zelensky, Costa discuss Ukraine's EU integration steps
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met with European Council President Antonio Costa to discuss steps toward Ukraine's integration into the European Union.

stories.title: US removes 13.5 kilos of highly enriched uranium from Venezuela's RV-1 reactor
stories.summary: The U.S. National Nuclear Security Administration removed 13.5 kilograms of highly enriched uranium from Venezuela's former RV-1 research reactor at the Venezuelan Institute for Scientific Research in Miranda state. The operation was coordinated with the United Kingdom, the IAEA, and Venezuela's transitional government.

stories.title: Palestinians run West Bank freedom marathon along separation wall
stories.summary: Palestinians participated in a freedom marathon in the West Bank, running alongside the Israeli separation wall. Participants highlighted how the barrier separates them from their land and families.

stories.title: African nations showcase art at Venice Biennale
stories.summary: Four African nations—Guinea, Equatorial Guinea, Sierra Leone, and Somalia—made their debut at the Venice Art Biennale this year. The growing presence of African countries at the exhibition reflects the continent's expanding role in the global art scene.

stories.title: Any Iran deal without proxy restrictions is strategic surrender - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that any nuclear deal with Iran that does not include restrictions on its regional proxy networks would constitute a strategic concession. While such a deal might stabilize markets, it could strengthen Iran's regime and its allied militias.

stories.title: Voices from the Arab press: Extending the ceasefire without Iran's supreme leader
stories.summary: A weekly compilation features opinions and analyses from Arabic-language media worldwide. Topics include discussion of extending ceasefire arrangements without the involvement of Iran's supreme leader.

stories.title: Putin says Russian army fighting 'aggressive' Nato-backed force in Victory Parade address
stories.summary: President Vladimir Putin used his Victory Day parade address on Red Square to claim Russian forces in Ukraine are fighting an aggressive NATO-backed force. He described Russia's war aims as just. Ukrainian long-range attacks prompted the Kremlin to scale back this year's celebrations and tighten security.

stories.title: Israel to deport Gaza flotilla activists detained for past week
stories.summary: Israel plans to deport two Gaza flotilla activists, Thiago Avila and Saif Abukeshek, who were detained for the past week. Israeli authorities accused them of links to a group allegedly controlled by Hamas.

stories.title: French world heritage site Chateau de Chambord in danger
stories.summary: The Château de Chambord, a Renaissance-era UNESCO World Heritage site in central France, is deteriorating due to extensive structural damage including holes, cracks, and moisture infiltration. Renovation work is underway on the François I Wing, with the full restoration estimated to cost €37 million.

stories.title: One dead in US after being struck by taking off Frontier Airlines plane
stories.summary: One person was killed at Denver International Airport in Colorado after jumping a perimeter fence and being struck by a Frontier Airlines plane during takeoff. Authorities are investigating the circumstances of the incident.

stories.title: Russia remains greatest security threat to Europe, says Bundeswehr general
stories.summary: A Bundeswehr general declared that Russia remains the greatest security threat to Europe for the foreseeable future and urged Germany to strengthen its defense capabilities to prevent open military conflict.

stories.title: Another Israeli strike hits south of Beirut
stories.summary: Israeli forces struck areas south of Beirut on Saturday, with Lebanese media reporting a strike shortly after two earlier ones targeting the Saadiyat highway. The Israeli military said an explosive drone launched from Lebanon was found near the northern border. Hezbollah claimed responsibility for the drone attack.

stories.title: Crunch Clasico as Barca look to pounce on Real unrest
stories.summary: Barcelona host Real Madrid in the season's second Clásico, seeking to secure a second consecutive La Liga title. Real Madrid enter the match amid reported internal unrest and poor form.

stories.title: Israeli settlers force Palestinian family to exhume father’s body in West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank forced a Palestinian family to exhume their father's body from a cemetery near Jenin on Friday. The settlers claimed the grave was too close to the re-established settlement of Sa-Nur, approximately 300 meters away. The family reportedly had obtained Israeli permits for the burial.

stories.title: Moscow marks Victory Day amid tight security
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin presided over a scaled-down Victory Day military parade on Moscow's Red Square, marking the 80th anniversary of Nazi Germany's defeat. For the first time in nearly two decades, heavy weapons were absent from the display. A US-brokered three-day ceasefire with Ukraine was in effect during the event.

stories.title: Cheap energy from Russia, cheap goods from China, and cheap security from America are all over. Europe needs its own defense alliance
stories.summary: Former NATO Secretary General Anders Fogh Rasmussen argued that Europe can no longer rely on cheap Russian energy, Chinese goods, or American security guarantees. He called for Europe to build its own defense alliance, warning that NATO is disintegrating.

stories.title: Danish rightwing leader asked to form government after Frederiksen fails to form coalition
stories.summary: Denmark's King Frederik asked centre-right politician Troels Lund Poulsen to attempt to form a new government after Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen failed to assemble a ruling coalition. Frederiksen's Social Democrats had won the most votes in the March parliamentary elections but could not secure enough coalition support.

stories.title: EU chief urges increased humanitarian access in south Lebanon
stories.summary: EU crisis management chief Hadja Lahbib called for increased humanitarian access in southern Lebanon, where aid has struggled to reach areas affected by Israeli strikes. She spoke ahead of an expected EU aid delivery, noting that humanitarian supplies are ready but often cannot reach those in need.

stories.title: Israeli settlers force Palestinian family to exhume father’s body in West Bank
stories.summary: In the West Bank near Jenin, Israeli settlers under military protection forced a Palestinian family to exhume their recently buried father's remains. The settlers claimed the grave was too close to the re-established settlement of Sa-Nur, despite the family having obtained burial permits.

stories.title: Israel to release Gaza flotilla activists after global pressure
stories.summary: Israel is set to release Gaza flotilla activists Thiago Avila and Saif Abukeshek from detention following growing international criticism. The two were seized by the Israeli navy and held for over a week.

stories.title: Israel to release two detained Gaza flotilla activists
stories.summary: Israel is set to release detained Gaza flotilla activists Saif Abu Keshek and Thiago Avila. Their lawyer told Al Jazeera they will be deported to their home countries.

stories.title: Two Israeli strikes hit south of Beirut
stories.summary: Two Israeli strikes hit areas along the Saadiyat highway in Lebanon, roughly 20 kilometers south of Beirut, on Saturday. Lebanese media and AFP described the strikes as violations of the ceasefire with Israel. An AFP correspondent reported damaged cars and emergency workers at the scene.

stories.title: Neither US nor Iran can sustain strait of Hormuz standoff indefinitely
stories.summary: Ongoing exchanges of fire between the United States and Iran in the Strait of Hormuz underscore the instability of the standoff, which analysts say neither side can sustain indefinitely. The U.S. and Israel demonstrated military superiority during a 38-day war but face economic and strategic pressures to resolve the crisis.

stories.title: Trump heads to China weakened as Xi gains leverage ahead of summit
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump is heading to a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping in a weakened position, as the Iran war disrupts global energy supplies and strains Washington-Beijing relations. Analysts suggest Xi has gained leverage amid the economic uncertainty affecting the US.

stories.title: Drone strikes private household in Sumy community
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a private household in Vakalivshchyna, part of the Bytytsia community in the Sumy region of Ukraine, damaging a residential building and outbuildings.

stories.title: Bahrain rounds up dozens over alleged links to Iran’s IRGC
stories.summary: Bahrain's interior ministry announced the arrest of 41 individuals over alleged links to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Legal proceedings against all detainees are reportedly under way.

stories.title: Surfers in war-torn Gaza find rare moments of joy taking to the waves
stories.summary: Despite severe shortages and widespread devastation in Gaza, a small group of surfers in Gaza City continue to take to the waves. The surfers find rare moments of relief through the sport amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Syrian authorities arrest Assad-era military general
stories.summary: Syrian authorities arrested Sahr Fajr Hassan, a military general from the Assad era, as part of an ongoing crackdown on former regime military and security officials following the government's ouster in December 2024.

stories.title: 300 defense factories, 500,000 workers: North Korea’s arms industry reaches records amid Russia’s demand for shells in war
stories.summary: North Korea's arms industry has reportedly expanded to approximately 300 defense factories employing 500,000 workers, driven by Russia's demand for artillery shells for its war in Ukraine. North Korean officials claim current shell production has quadrupled compared to normal levels.

stories.title: UK sending warship to Hormuz, says defence ministry
stories.summary: The United Kingdom announced it will deploy the destroyer HMS Dragon to the Strait of Hormuz as part of a multinational coalition jointly led by the UK and France to secure the strategic waterway when conditions allow.

stories.title: Israeli forces bomb Gaza home after evacuation orders
stories.summary: Israeli forces issued evacuation orders and then bombed a home in Gaza, marking the first time since the October ceasefire that Israel has used such orders before conducting strikes in the territory.

stories.title: Traffic advisory issued ahead of Marka-i-Haq event in Islamabad
stories.summary: Islamabad authorities issued a traffic advisory for May 10 ahead of a Marka-i-Haq anniversary ceremony at the National Monument at Zero Point. Top civilian and military leadership were expected to attend the event celebrating Pakistani forces' victory against India the previous May.

stories.title: Settlers dig up Palestinian grave near Sha-Nur, forcing family to relocate burial
stories.summary: Near the Sha-Nur settlement in the occupied West Bank, Israeli settlers reportedly exhumed a Palestinian grave. Palestinian sources allege IDF soldiers assisted the settlers, while the IDF denies involvement and says the family relocated the body voluntarily.

stories.title: 9 May parade Russia held without single tank featured one thing Moscow has never shown before
stories.summary: Russia's May 9 Victory Day parade in Moscow's Red Square was held without a single tank for the first time, featuring instead a display the Kremlin had not previously shown publicly. The scaled-down event reflected shifts in Russia's military posture.

stories.title: 100 Hong Kong-linked ships ‘stranded in Strait of Hormuz’ amid Middle East war
stories.summary: Approximately 100 Hong Kong-linked ships and an estimated 2,300 seafarers are stranded in the Strait of Hormuz due to the risk of attack amid the US-Israel war against Iran. Hong Kong Shipowners Association chairman Richard Hext said sailing through the strait remains very dangerous despite a recent temporary US-Iran ceasefire.

stories.title: Shortest military parade in modern Russian history held in Moscow
stories.summary: Russia's Victory Day parade on Red Square on May 9 lasted approximately 45 minutes, making it one of the shortest military parades in modern Russian history.

stories.title: Iran says will play World Cup, demands hosts accept conditions
stories.summary: Iran announced it will participate in the upcoming FIFA World Cup, scheduled from June 11 to July 19, but demanded that host organizers accept its conditions. Iran's participation had been uncertain leading up to the tournament.

stories.title: Iran says will play in World Cup, but demands soccer officials linked to IRGC be allowed
stories.summary: Iran said it will participate in the 2026 World Cup but demanded that soccer officials linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps be permitted entry. Both the US and Canada have indicated they will bar individuals connected to the IRGC, which is designated a terrorist organization.

stories.title: 'Atmosphere closer to wartime': Moscow’s muted Victory Day reflects growing security fears
stories.summary: Russia's scaled-down Victory Day celebrations on May 9 reflected heightened security concerns amid the ongoing war in Ukraine. Chatham House analyst Grégoire Roos told FRANCE 24 that internet shutdowns, tighter security, and fears of Ukrainian drone strikes created an atmosphere closer to wartime than national celebration.

stories.title: ‘A year of resistance’: Cuba’s private sector faces Trump’s oil blockade
stories.summary: The US oil blockade on Cuba is severely impacting the country's private sector, particularly small family-run businesses. Firms are struggling with chronic power outages and fuel shortages caused by the restrictions.

stories.title: Nigeria: National Security Adviser Ribadu Holds Talks With VP Vance and Secretary Rubio in Washington DC
stories.summary: Nigeria's National Security Adviser Ribadu held talks with US Vice President Vance and Secretary of State Rubio in Washington, DC. The discussions focused on deepening cooperation in security, counterterrorism, regional stability, and strategic partnership.

stories.title: Five reported killed, including girl, in Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon reportedly killed five people, including a girl. The IDF issued evacuation warnings to nine villages and said it struck 85 Hezbollah targets in southern Lebanon and an underground weapons site in the Beqaa Valley over the past day.

stories.title: Trump’s feuds, tensions with allies likely to outlast Iran war
stories.summary: Analysts suggest that diplomatic tensions between President Trump and traditional U.S. allies, intensified during the Iran war, are likely to persist beyond the conflict. Trump's actions have revived concerns among partners about American reliability in future crises.

stories.title: Ukraine's defense minister shows AI turret used in combat to intercept drones on battlefield
stories.summary: Ukraine's defense minister showcased an AI-powered turret designed to intercept enemy drones on the battlefield. The system was developed through the Brave1 defense technology cluster and is already in active combat use.

stories.title: At UN, Pakistan raises alarm at Israel's systematic annexation of occupied West Bank
stories.summary: Pakistan's UN Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad raised concerns at an Arria-formula meeting about Israel's systematic annexation of the occupied West Bank, expansion of illegal settlements, and forced displacement of Palestinians. He called for international community intervention.

stories.title: ‘Watching us is like watching a cousin’: the online creators reshaping Africa’s news ecosphere
stories.summary: African online creators are reshaping how current affairs are consumed across the continent. South African TikTok creator Amahle-Imvelo Jaxa gained 100,000 followers in three days after posting a viral video about South African peacekeepers in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and tensions between the South African and Rwandan presidents.

stories.title: Trump airport branding deal opens new route to profit for family
stories.summary: A licensing and merchandising agreement at a renamed Florida airport grants President Donald Trump's family a new revenue stream. The deal emerged as Spirit Airlines ceased operations, citing high fuel prices linked to the U.S.-Iran conflict.

stories.title: Beijing urges France to respect one-China principle during high-level talks
stories.summary: Chinese top diplomat Wang Yi held talks in Beijing with French presidential adviser Emmanuel Bonne, urging France to respect the one-China principle. Wang called for strengthening the China-France strategic partnership free from external interference.

stories.title: US-Iran war no closer to ending as Gulf clashes flare
stories.summary: The United States and Iran traded fire in the Strait of Hormuz despite a month-old ceasefire, with the UAE coming under renewed attack. A US intelligence assessment concluded that Iran could withstand a naval blockade for months.

stories.title: Israel allocates $345m for bypass roads in occupied West Bank
stories.summary: Israel's National Bureau for Defending Land and Resisting Settlements reported that Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich and Transportation Minister Miri Regev approved 1 billion shekels ($345 million) for bypass road construction on Palestinian lands in the occupied West Bank, adding to $2.4 billion previously allocated.

stories.title: Moscow marks Victory Day with a scaled down Red Square parade under tight security
stories.summary: Russia held its annual Victory Day parade on May 9 in Moscow's Red Square under heightened security and in a scaled-down format, with no tanks, missiles, or heavy equipment. President Vladimir Putin vowed to achieve victory in Ukraine. North Korean troops participated in the parade.

stories.title: May 5 strike on Kramatorsk: Deputy head of district administration dies in hospital
stories.summary: Roman Simashov, deputy head of the Kramatorsk District State Administration, died in hospital from injuries sustained in a Russian strike on Kramatorsk on May 5.

stories.title: Indonesian rescuers retrieve body from Mount Dukono as search continues
stories.summary: Rescuers recovered the body of an Indonesian woman killed during a volcanic eruption on Mount Dukono on Halmahera island, while search operations continued for two missing Singaporeans. The 20 hikers had climbed the volcano despite safety restrictions before the eruption on Friday.

stories.title: Iran says it will play at 2026 World Cup if hosts address ‘concerns’
stories.summary: Iran stated it is willing to participate in the 2026 FIFA World Cup, provided host nations address its concerns. Iran's participation has been uncertain since the US and Israel launched military operations against the country.

stories.title: Conflict inflames tensions at Venice Biennale of Art
stories.summary: Russia returned to the Venice Biennale of Art after being absent since its February 2022 invasion of Ukraine, sparking international outcry and inflaming tensions among participating nations over the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Bahrain arrests 41 individuals linked with Iran's IRGC terrorist activities in the Kingdom
stories.summary: Bahrain arrested 41 individuals accused of forming the core of an IRGC-linked network in the kingdom. Authorities charged them with espionage for foreign entities and sympathy with what Bahrain described as Iranian aggression.

stories.title: Indian sailor killed in dhow fire near Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: An Indian sailor was killed in a fire aboard a dhow near the Strait of Hormuz. The remaining crew members were rescued by a passing vessel in the area.

stories.title: Guardian reporter and colleagues detained and beaten by Somali police
stories.summary: Guardian journalist Mohamed Bulbul and two colleagues, Abdihafid Nor Barre and Abdishakur Mohamed Mohamud, were detained and beaten by Somalia's US-trained counter-terrorism police in Mogadishu after Bulbul reported on a woman allegedly tortured in prison.

stories.title: UK Jews’ fears grow as Green, Reform surge elects candidates accused of antisemitism
stories.summary: In UK local elections, the Green Party and Reform UK saw gains, electing candidates who have been accused of espousing antisemitic views and anti-Israel conspiracy theories, raising concerns among British Jewish communities.

stories.title: Moscow begins scaled-back Victory Day parade as 3-day Ukraine truce kicks in
stories.summary: Russia held its annual Victory Day parade on Moscow's Red Square on Saturday with scaled-back events amid security concerns. A three-day ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine took effect for the occasion, following an appeal from US President Donald Trump.

stories.title: Russian drone attack in Zaporizhzhia region damages house, evacuation vehicle, injures two
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack in the Zaporizhzhia region injured two people after one UAV struck a residential house and another hit an evacuation vehicle.

stories.title: Israel set to release two Gaza flotilla activists, representatives say
stories.summary: Two Gaza flotilla activists — a Spanish national and a Brazilian national — are set to be released from Israeli detention after being captured in international waters aboard a humanitarian aid vessel bound for Gaza. A rights group representing them reported they suffered abuse in Israeli prison.

stories.title: Why U.S. Project Freedom couldn’t secure free navigation in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The US initiative known as Project Freedom failed to secure free navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. President Donald Trump cited progress in negotiations with Iran as the reason for calling off the operation.

stories.title: Rosenberg: Scaled-back Victory Parade in Moscow's Red Square
stories.summary: The BBC's Russia editor reported from Moscow that the annual Victory Day military parade on Red Square was quieter and more scaled back than in previous years.

stories.title: Putin attends WW2 victory parade, worries deepen over Ukraine
stories.summary: President Vladimir Putin attended Russia's annual World War II Victory Day parade in Moscow, where soldiers and sailors — some of whom served in Ukraine — marched before Putin and Russian veterans.

stories.title: Officer who cracked serial rapist Worboys case says justice system ‘close to exploding’
stories.summary: Former senior investigating officer Tim Grattan-Kane, who led the arrest of London black-cab rapist John Worboys in 2008, has warned that similar drug-facilitated sexual assaults may still be occurring. He cited the rise of drink spiking and an overstretched criminal justice system that he described as being "close to exploding."

stories.title: Meet China’s moon porter for Chang’e-8 mission: a 4-wheeled robot with 2 arms
stories.summary: China's Hong Kong University of Science and Technology developed a four-wheeled, dual-armed robot rover to serve as an AI-powered porter for the Chang'e-8 lunar mission, scheduled for 2029. The 100-kilogram robot will transport and deploy instruments on the moon's surface.

stories.title: Ukraine-Russia talks at impasse, but US ready to mediate if opportunity arises – Rubio
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that peace talks between Ukraine and Russia are at a standstill. He said the United States remains ready to mediate if an opportunity to resume negotiations arises.

stories.title: Iran's 'fake opposition': The controversial campaign to legitimize the MEK
stories.summary: The People's Mojahedin Organization of Iran (MEK) has evolved from a student-led Marxist movement into an exiled group advocating regime change in Tehran. The organization remains highly controversial, with critics questioning a campaign to legitimize its standing.

stories.title: 'Disposable spies': Poland records unprecedented number of Russian espionage cases
stories.summary: Poland's internal security service, the ABW, reported an unprecedented number of Russian espionage and hybrid attack cases on Polish territory since 2024. Researchers noted that Russian intelligence services have employed amateur "single-use agents" to lay the groundwork for more complex operations against Poland.

stories.title: Pakistan, Bangladesh sign agreement to combat drug trafficking
stories.summary: Pakistan and Bangladesh signed a memorandum of understanding to strengthen cooperation against drug trafficking and narcotics abuse during Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi's visit to Dhaka. Both countries also agreed to establish a secretary-level joint working group.

stories.title: Israeli strikes pound southern Lebanon, hit targets elsewhere
stories.summary: Israeli forces continued striking southern Lebanon, issuing near-daily evacuation orders despite an existing truce. The strikes have killed scores of people across the region.

stories.title: Israel orders nine south Lebanon villages evacuated amid strikes
stories.summary: Israel issued evacuation orders for nine villages in southern Lebanon amid ongoing airstrikes that have killed scores of people. Such orders have become a near-daily occurrence despite a truce being in place.

stories.title: British PM Starmer vows to fight on after local polls drubbing
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer vowed to continue governing after his Labour Party suffered significant losses in local elections. Starmer declared he was "not going to walk away" despite the electoral setback.

stories.title: 'No Other Land' filmmaker warns UN of Israeli settler violence
stories.summary: Basel Adra, Oscar-winning co-director of the documentary 'No Other Land,' addressed the UN Security Council about increasing Israeli settler violence. He urged the body to take action against the escalating attacks.

stories.title: Palestinian Christian body warns EU they are under existential threat
stories.summary: A delegation from the Higher Presidential Committee for Church Affairs in Palestine met EU officials in Brussels to warn that Israeli policies threaten the survival of the Palestinian Christian community. Reverend Dr Mitri Raheb highlighted the dramatic decline in the Palestinian Christian population during the meeting.

stories.title: Canvas cyberattack: Disruptions aplenty as universities cancel or postpone exams, assignments
stories.summary: The Canvas learning management platform, operated by Instructure, suffered a cyberattack after staff detected unauthorized activity on April 29. The disruption forced multiple universities to cancel or postpone exams and assignments.

stories.title: Israel kills five in Gaza in past day, raising death toll to 72,736
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed at least five Palestinians and wounded 15 in Gaza over the past day, according to medical sources. The cumulative death toll since October 2023 has reached 72,736, with 172,535 wounded. Rescue teams report that many victims remain trapped under rubble.

stories.title: Russia holds scaled-back WW2 victory parade as worries over war in Ukraine deepen
stories.summary: Russia held a scaled-back Victory Day parade on Red Square on May 9 to mark the Soviet Union's defeat of Nazi Germany. The event honors the 27 million Soviet citizens who died in World War II, though concerns over the war in Ukraine prompted reduced celebrations.

stories.title: SBU detains Russian agent in Odesa who plotted killing of senior Ukrainian Navy officer ahead of 'Victory Day'
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) detained a Russian agent in Odesa who was planning to assassinate a senior Ukrainian Navy officer ahead of Russia's Victory Day celebrations.

stories.title: Displaced Lebanese children keep learning amid displacement
stories.summary: A school in Sidon, southern Lebanon, is serving as a shelter for displaced families while continuing to hold classes for children uprooted by the conflict.

stories.title: Met Gala 2026 | When India showed up — with steel, saris and mangoes
stories.summary: Several Indian designers and celebrities attended the 2026 Met Gala in New York, incorporating traditional elements such as saris and cultural motifs into their outfits amid broader debate over billionaire patronage of the event.

stories.title: While Russia held its 9 May parade, Warsaw activists placed crosses and photos of killed Ukrainian children outside Russian Embassy
stories.summary: On May 9, activists from Euromaidan-Warsaw placed crosses and photos of killed Ukrainian children outside the Russian Embassy in Warsaw during Russia's Victory Day parade, calling Russia a terrorist state waging a genocidal war in Ukraine.

stories.title: UK local elections: "Starmer must address voters' frustration over change"
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces mounting pressure after the Labour Party suffered significant losses in local elections across England, Wales, and Scotland. Reform UK made notable gains in the contests. The results have prompted questions about Starmer's leadership less than a year after Labour returned to government.

stories.title: Russian forces launch eight attacks on Donetsk region over past day, one wounded
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled Ukraine's Donetsk region eight times on May 8, injuring one person. The attacks damaged residential buildings and a gas pipeline in the area.

stories.title: Hong Kong home market maintains upwards momentum as eager buyers snap up new flats
stories.summary: Hong Kong's residential property market continued its upward trend as all 154 units at Sun Hung Kai Properties' Lime Spark project sold out, and 93% of Henderson Land's Highwood Phase 2 flats found buyers, with home prices rising nearly 8% in 2026.

stories.title: India, IOM discuss expanding, diversifying regular migration pathways
stories.summary: India's Minister of State for External Affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh held discussions with the International Organization for Migration on expanding and diversifying regular migration pathways. The talks also covered India's implementation of the Global Compact for Migration and IOM activities within the country.

stories.title: How Israel's creation mirrors Greek independence - and why it's overlooked - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece draws parallels between Israel's founding and Greece's independence, arguing both involved diaspora nationalism and population displacement. It contends that Israel faces disproportionate scrutiny compared to Greece.

stories.title: U.S. authorities cancel cruise ship worker visas as part of child sexual abuse images case
stories.summary: U.S. Customs and Border Protection reported that authorities boarded eight cruise ships in late April and identified 27 crew members, mostly from the Philippines, involved in child sexual abuse imagery offenses. The individuals' visas were cancelled. Charges relate to the receipt, possession, transportation, distribution, or viewing of such material.

stories.title: Israel police accused of assaulting Palestinian govt prosecutor
stories.summary: A Palestinian citizen of Israel employed as a government prosecutor was allegedly assaulted and arrested by Israeli police following a neighbour's complaint.

stories.title: Army exercises in Morocco focus on countering Sahel threats
stories.summary: The annual African Lion military exercise, held in Morocco for over two decades, brought together multiple foreign contingents for land, air, and naval drills focused on countering security threats emanating from the Sahel region.

stories.title: Russian Uragan MLRS can wipe out city block in 8.8 seconds. Ukraine just destroyed one of its loaders 40 km behind front
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces destroyed a loader for Russia's Uragan multiple-launch rocket system approximately 40 kilometers behind the front line using drones, after Russia had repositioned heavy equipment further from the front to avoid losses.

stories.title: Heroism and grief: 6 residents’ stories from Wang Fuk Court fire hearings
stories.summary: Residents of the fire-ravaged Wang Fuk Court estate in Hong Kong testified at public hearings, recounting acts of heroism, grief, and ignored safety warnings before the blaze — the city's deadliest in decades.

stories.title: ‘Largely slop’: Trump’s new counterterrorism strategy is scant on substance but heavy on enemies
stories.summary: The Trump administration released a 16-page counterterrorism strategy document authored by counter-terrorism adviser Sebastian Gorka. Critics have characterized the memo as light on substantive policy while heavily targeting political opponents, the Biden administration, and other groups. Gorka reportedly used vulgar language to dismiss critics of the administration's military engagement in Iran.

stories.title: ‘We’re going backwards’: Five civil rights activists slam the supreme court’s gutting of Voting Rights Act
stories.summary: Civil rights activists, including veterans of the 1965 Selma marches, have criticized the U.S. Supreme Court's recent decision to weaken the Voting Rights Act. Sheyann Webb-Christburg, who marched in Selma at age eight, called the ruling a means to silence voters. Organizers described it as part of a long history of Black voter disenfranchisement.

stories.title: ‘The worst kind of predator’: Louisiana pastor found guilty for third time of molesting teen boys
stories.summary: Terry Reed, a 66-year-old pastor from suburban New Orleans, Louisiana, has been convicted of sexually molesting two minors. This is the third time Reed has been found guilty of abusing teenage boys. Prosecutors said he used biblical verses to manipulate and justify his behavior, and he faces up to 40 years in prison.

stories.title: ‘Not decoupling’: what US-China trade data signals ahead of Xi-Trump summit
stories.summary: China's merchandise exports to the United States fell 10.2% year-on-year in early 2026 as President Trump prepares to visit Beijing for a summit with President Xi Jinping that could shape future economic relations between the two nations.

stories.title: Tehran could withstand blockade for four months, CIA report shows, as fighting flares
stories.summary: Fighting around the Strait of Hormuz escalated in early May 2026, marking the largest flare-ups since a ceasefire began a month earlier. The UAE came under renewed attack on May 8, 2026. A CIA report indicates Tehran could withstand a naval blockade for approximately four months.

stories.title: Ukraine marks Europe Day as integral part of European family – Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky marked Europe Day by affirming Ukraine's place as an integral part of the European family, describing the celebration as reflecting a genuine commitment rather than a formality.

stories.title: Russia’s “Great Victory” cult wasn’t built in 1945 — it was constructed in 1965
stories.summary: An analysis argues that Russia's May 9 Victory Day commemoration is not an unbroken tradition from 1945 but was largely constructed as a national narrative beginning in 1965 under Soviet leadership.

stories.title: Israel doubts US optimism in Iran talks as critical issues on nuclear concessions remain unsolved
stories.summary: US officials have expressed optimism about a potential deal with Iran, but Israel remains skeptical. Israeli officials stress that significant unresolved differences persist between Washington and Tehran, particularly on nuclear concessions.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill at the least three in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes killed at least three people in the Tyre district of southern Lebanon on Saturday, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. The strikes hit a car traveling near the Martyr Mohammed Saad High School between Burj Rahhal and al-Abbassieh.

stories.title: Starmer gives Brown and Harman new roles as pressure grows over election mauling – UK politics live
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer appointed former Prime Minister Gordon Brown as a special envoy on global finance and gave Harriet Harman a new role. The moves came as Starmer faces growing internal pressure over Labour's heavy election losses, with several frontbenchers reportedly suggesting his time in office should not extend beyond year's end.

stories.title: Bahrain arrests 41 over alleged links to Iran’s IRGC
stories.summary: Bahrain's interior minister announced the arrest of 41 individuals over alleged connections to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, according to the state news agency.

stories.title: Al-Qard Al-Hasan, Hezbollah main funding source, resumes activities despite IDF strikes during war
stories.summary: Al-Qard Al-Hasan, described as Hezbollah's main funding source, has resumed operations despite Israeli military strikes that targeted around 30 of its branches. The Saudi-owned Al-Arabiya network reported that a branch in Beirut's Haret Khreik neighborhood is again operational.

stories.title: US military kills two people in new eastern Pacific Ocean attack
stories.summary: The US military carried out a strike in the eastern Pacific Ocean that killed two people. It was the third such US attack in the region during May alone.

stories.title: Trump's feuds, tensions with allies likely to outlast Iran war
stories.summary: President Donald Trump's decisions to withdraw some U.S. troops from Germany and threaten force reductions elsewhere in Europe are straining alliances beyond the immediate Iran conflict. Traditional partners from Europe, the Middle East, and the Indo-Pacific have expressed growing concern about U.S. reliability in future crises. Some allied nations are reportedly beginning to pursue independent security arrangements.

stories.title: Russian shelling hits 20 settlements in Kherson region, three civilians injured
stories.summary: Russian attacks struck 20 settlements in Ukraine's Kherson region over the past day, injuring three civilians.

stories.title: Russian occupation troops fighting  in Ukraine are inspired by WWII “generation of victors,” says Putin at 9 May parade at Red Square
stories.summary: President Putin told troops at the May 9 Red Square parade that Russian forces in Ukraine are inspired by the World War II 'generation of victors.' This year's parade featured no heavy military equipment columns; since 2022, Russia has reportedly lost thousands of tanks, armored vehicles, and artillery systems in Ukraine.

stories.title: Jordan sees collapse in tourism since Iran war
stories.summary: Jordan has experienced a sharp decline in tourism since a war involving Iran erupted in the Middle East in late February. The ancient city of Petra, normally a major tourist destination, has seen visitor numbers plummet as the regional conflict continues.

stories.title: Cricket gives special dimension to India-Trinidad and Tobago ties: Jaishankar
stories.summary: Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar arrived in Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago, on May 8, 2026, concluding a three-nation Caribbean tour that included Jamaica and Suriname. Jaishankar highlighted cricket as a unique element strengthening bilateral ties between India and Trinidad and Tobago.

stories.title: Opinion: Germany's 'constructive dialogue' is a sham, a cloak used to shield its support of a genocidal regime
stories.summary: On April 21, Germany and Italy blocked a motion by Spain, Ireland, and Slovenia to suspend the EU-Israel trade agreement over human rights concerns. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul described the move as inappropriate, advocating instead for continued dialogue with Israel.

stories.title: Israel pushes US to Iran war return, targeting energy sector
stories.summary: Israeli officials are reportedly urging the United States to target Iran's energy infrastructure and resume military operations against Tehran. The push aims to draw Washington into a broader confrontation with Iran.

stories.title: 'Integrity costs something': Eurovision winners want Israel out of the contest
stories.summary: Several former Eurovision winners have called for Israel's exclusion from the contest, citing the humanitarian situation in Gaza. They argue that the competition cannot be separated from political reality.

stories.title: Gaza at the Venice Biennale: Where language falls short, threads take over
stories.summary: A tapestry titled the Gaza Genocide Tapestry has been co-commissioned for display at the Venice Biennale. The artwork was created to address the ongoing conflict in Gaza through textile art.

stories.title: Artists strike to protest Israeli participation ahead of Venice Biennale
stories.summary: Around 12 national pavilions at the Venice Biennale closed or partially shuttered in protest against Israeli participation, with some flying Palestinian flags. Police clashed with demonstrators who attempted to reach the Israeli installation.

stories.title: In Victory Day Speech, Putin Says Russia Fighting 'Aggressive' NATO-Backed Force in Ukraine
stories.summary: In his Victory Day speech marking the 81st anniversary of the Soviet World War II victory, Russian President Vladimir Putin stated that Russia is fighting an aggressive NATO-backed force in Ukraine, declaring the cause just.

stories.title: British leader Keir Starmer under pressure after heavy election losses
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces mounting pressure to set a departure timeline after Labour lost more than 1,400 English council seats in local elections. The party also suffered significant defeats in Welsh and Scottish parliament votes held on Thursday.

stories.title: Russian drone hits civilian car in Zaporizhzhia region, leaving one dead, two injured
stories.summary: A Russian FPV drone struck a civilian vehicle in the Polohy district of Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, killing one man and injuring two others.

stories.title: Wanted ‘Hong Kong Parliament’ member could be deported from Thailand
stories.summary: Zhang Xinyan, a member of the overseas opposition group "Hong Kong Parliament," was arrested in Thailand for overstaying her visa and reportedly faces deportation to mainland China. The group said Zhang had been sworn in as a member last year. The type of visa she held was not immediately clear.

stories.title: Germany's 'constructive dialogue' is a sham, a cloak used to shield its support of a genocidal regime
stories.summary: Germany and Italy blocked an EU motion by Spain, Ireland, and Slovenia to suspend the EU-Israel trade agreement. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul rejected the initiative and advocated for continued engagement with Israel.

stories.title: One Nation wins Farrer byelection as Coalition vote collapses
stories.summary: One Nation's David Farley won the Farrer byelection in New South Wales, Australia, marking the party's first-ever lower house seat. He defeated independent candidate Michelle Milthorpe in the race for the seat vacated by former Liberal leader Sussan Ley. The result reflected a significant collapse in the Coalition vote.

stories.title: Iran mulls US peace plan as Hormuz strikes threaten ceasefire
stories.summary: Iran is considering a US peace proposal amid ongoing strikes near the Strait of Hormuz that threaten ceasefire efforts. President Trump has threatened further escalation if Iran does not respond positively to the plan.

stories.title: Iran keeps US waiting for response on ceasefire plan
stories.summary: Iran questioned the seriousness of U.S. diplomacy while delaying its response to Washington's latest negotiating position following renewed naval clashes in the Gulf. A parallel ceasefire on the Lebanon front is also under strain amid daily exchanges of fire between Israel and Iran-backed Hezbollah.

stories.title: China unveils Hanyuan-2, the world’s first dual-core quantum computer
stories.summary: China unveiled Hanyuan-2, described as the world's first dual-core quantum computer, according to state media outlet Science and Technology Daily. The system reportedly uses neutral atoms, reducing energy consumption compared to conventional quantum computers. Officials said the development marks a new stage in Chinese quantum computing technology.

stories.title: Scaled-back Victory Day parade held in Moscow
stories.summary: Russia held a scaled-back Victory Day parade on Red Square in Moscow. President Vladimir Putin used the occasion to pledge victory in what he termed the 'special military operation' in Ukraine.

stories.title: UN says 40,000 Palestinians displaced in West Bank since start of 2025
stories.summary: The United Nations reported that approximately 40,000 Palestinians have been internally displaced in the occupied West Bank since the beginning of 2025 due to Israeli military operations and settler violence. At least 42 people, including 12 children, were displaced by home demolitions in the first week of May alone.

stories.title: IMF's Executive Board approves $1.3bn financing for Pakistan's reform programme, flags heightened risks from Middle East war
stories.summary: The IMF Executive Board approved the latest review of Pakistan's reform programme, releasing $1.32 billion in financing under existing arrangements.
