stories.title: African countries warn citizens of xenophobic attacks in South Africa
stories.summary: Kenya, Malawi, Lesotho, and Zimbabwe have warned their citizens in South Africa to remain cautious and stay indoors due to xenophobic attacks targeting foreigners. Ghana has lobbied the African Union to take action in response to the violence.

stories.title: Ukraine proposes “Brave Sweden” to Stockholm and moves toward finalizing Gripen contracts
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov visited Sweden to discuss defense cooperation, including Ukraine's proposed 'Brave Sweden' initiative. Talks advanced toward finalizing contracts for Swedish-made Gripen fighter jets.

stories.title: Cornell publishes footage defending president from claims he hit anti-Israel activists with car
stories.summary: Cornell University released footage defending its president against claims that he struck anti-Israel activists with his car. The president said students had surrounded and blocked his vehicle while banging on its windows.

stories.title: Kharkiv allocates over UAH 1.8B to support AFU – Mayor Terekhov
stories.summary: Kharkiv Mayor Ihor Terekhov announced that the city has allocated more than 1.8 billion Ukrainian hryvnias from its budget to support the Armed Forces of Ukraine since the start of the full-scale war. An additional 300 million hryvnias is planned for the current year.

stories.title: Iran says supreme leader overseeing decisions, says Iranian foreign ministry
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson stated that Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is directing all key national decisions and that no action proceeds without his approval. The statement addressed questions about Khamenei's absence from public view since the early stages of the war with the US and Israel.

stories.title: Zehut party leader to run in elections on joint list with ex-Otzma Yehudit chair
stories.summary: Israel's Zehut party leader announced a joint electoral list with the former chair of Otzma Yehudit. The alliance was described as an effort to provide a unified political home for Israel's faith-based nationalist voters.

stories.title: Palestinian boy mourns father killed in Israeli strike on security post
stories.summary: A Palestinian boy grieved the loss of his father, who was among three people killed when an Israeli airstrike hit a security post in Gaza.

stories.title: US issues new Cuba sanctions as UN experts warn of ‘energy starvation’
stories.summary: The United States imposed new sanctions on a military-controlled Cuban conglomerate. UN experts have warned that an effective US fuel blockade is causing what they describe as 'energy starvation' in Cuba.

stories.title: UK police make third arrest over attempted arson at London synagogue
stories.summary: British counter-terrorism police arrested a 19-year-old man on May 7 in connection with an attempted arson attack on a synagogue in north London last month. The arrest is the third made in the ongoing investigation.

stories.title: White House calls Mark Hamill ‘sick’ after Star Wars actor posts Trump gravesite image
stories.summary: The White House condemned actor Mark Hamill after he posted an AI-generated image on Bluesky depicting President Donald Trump in a shallow grave. The image included the inscription 'If Only' alongside a gravestone reading 'Donald J Trump 1946-2024.'

stories.title: Zelensky advises against visiting Moscow on May 9
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky advised representatives of countries with ties to Russia against visiting Moscow on May 9. He issued the recommendation amid ongoing Russian strikes and threats against Ukraine.

stories.title: Diplomatic anchor or strategic space for Iran: Saudi airspace becomes new challenge for Trump
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia informed the United States it would not permit US military flights through its airspace after President Trump announced Operation Project Freedom. The decision created a new diplomatic and strategic challenge for Washington's military operations in the region.

stories.title: Pro-Palestinian protester pleads guilty to involuntary manslaughter in death of Jewish man
stories.summary: Loay Alnaji, a former professor, pleaded guilty to involuntary manslaughter for striking pro-Israel counterprotester Paul Kessler during a 2023 demonstration in California. Kessler, who was Jewish, died from the injuries. Alnaji is expected to serve approximately six months in jail followed by probation.

stories.title: Sudan: Paramilitary leader Daglo says ready to fight for decades
stories.summary: RSF paramilitary leader Mohamed Hamdan Daglo declared that fighting in Sudan would continue "for decades" until the Sudanese army is "uprooted." The statement came as the civil war between the RSF and Sudan's armed forces continues to rage across the country.

stories.title: Lebanon death toll rises to 2,727 as Israeli raids continue
stories.summary: Lebanon's Ministry of Public Health reported that 2,727 people have been killed and 8,438 wounded in Israeli military operations since March 2. Officials said strikes remain concentrated in towns and cities across southern Lebanon, where bombardment has intensified.

stories.title: ‘This is my last voice note’: how piracy returned to Somalia and Yemen
stories.summary: Three ships were hijacked near the Gulf of Aden, raising concerns about the resurgence of piracy along key maritime routes off the coasts of Somalia and Yemen.

stories.title: Cambridge to retake ‘prematurely shared’ AS-level mathematics exam on June 9
stories.summary: Cambridge International Education cancelled an AS-level mathematics exam after the paper was prematurely shared, affecting candidates in Africa, Europe, the Middle East, Pakistan, and South Asia. A replacement exam is scheduled for June 9.

stories.title: Southern Poverty Law Center pleads not guilty in federal fraud case
stories.summary: The Southern Poverty Law Center pleaded not guilty to an 11-count federal indictment alleging fraud and money laundering conspiracy. Prosecutors claim the SPLC funneled over $3 million to paid informants monitoring right-wing extremist groups through a now-defunct program.

stories.title: Top Pentagon tech officials optimistic Mythos-style AI tools will improve cyber defense
stories.summary: Pentagon Chief Technology Officer Emil Michael and Cyber Policy chief Katie Sutton expressed optimism about AI tools like Mythos that can patch vulnerable code at high speed. They described these tools as a new generation of cyber defense capabilities.

stories.title: Moscow’s airports experience  largest aviation disruption of 2026 after Russia breaks ceasefire with Ukraine
stories.summary: Moscow's airports experienced the largest aviation disruption of 2026 after Russia broke its ceasefire with Ukraine. Passengers have been sleeping on terminal floors as chaos extended into a third consecutive day.

stories.title: Wadephul: Germany not to yield to Russian threats, to keep diplomats in Kyiv
stories.summary: German official Johann Wadephul stated that Germany will not yield to Russian intimidation and will maintain its diplomatic mission in Kyiv. The announcement signals Berlin's continued commitment to operating its embassy in the Ukrainian capital despite Kremlin pressure.

stories.title: Mali: More than 30 killed in twin central attacks
stories.summary: More than 30 people were killed in two separate attacks in central Mali, according to local, security, and administrative sources.

stories.title: Jordan tourism sector faces downturn as visitor numbers plunge amid Iran war
stories.summary: Jordan's tourism sector, which accounts for roughly 14 percent of the country's economy, is experiencing a sharp downturn due to the Iran war disrupting regional travel. The sector supports about 60,000 direct jobs and 300,000 related livelihoods, with last year's seven million visitors generating $7.8 billion in revenue.

stories.title: Israeli suspected of attacking French nun in Jerusalem charged with religious hate crime
stories.summary: An Israeli man was charged with assault motivated by religious hostility after allegedly shoving a French Catholic nun to the ground and kicking her in Jerusalem. Israel's state attorney's office announced the charges on Thursday.

stories.title: Russians turn to cash and paper maps as internet outages spread, Russia’s Central Bank says
stories.summary: Russia's central bank reported that demand for cash among Russian citizens rose during March and April amid spreading internet outages. Russians have also increasingly turned to paper maps as digital services face disruptions across the country.

stories.title: Colorado fire-bombing suspect pleads guilty to all state charges
stories.summary: Mohamed Soliman, a 46-year-old Egyptian national, pleaded guilty in Colorado to dozens of felony counts including first-degree murder related to a fire-bombing attack. The charges include two separate definitions of the first-degree murder offense.

stories.title: Photo shows Israeli soldier desecrating a Virgin Mary statue in Lebanon
stories.summary: A photograph showing an Israeli soldier placing a cigarette in the mouth of a Virgin Mary statue in the village of Debel in South Lebanon went viral. The IDF said it launched an investigation and would discipline the soldier. Last month, another soldier was filmed smashing a Jesus statue in the same village.

stories.title: Gulf states urge UN action to ensure Strait of Hormuz safety
stories.summary: Gulf states submitted a draft UN resolution demanding that Iran halt attacks and the use of pin-point mines in the Strait of Hormuz and ensure the passage of humanitarian aid through the waterway.

stories.title: Russia continues to violate Kyiv-proposed ceasefire, Zelenskiy says
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Russia continued to violate a Kyiv-proposed ceasefire on Thursday. He warned that Ukraine would continue its long-range strikes if Russian assaults persisted.

stories.title: “We know Russians, and these are means they use”: Germany won’t evacuate its Kyiv embassy ahead on Russia’s Victory Day
stories.summary: Germany announced it will not evacuate its embassy in Kyiv despite Russian pressure ahead of Russia's Victory Day celebrations. German officials characterized the pressure to empty Kyiv's diplomatic quarter as a known Russian intimidation tactic.

stories.title: Brazil senator targeted with search warrant as Banco Master probe widens
stories.summary: Brazilian federal police served a search and seizure warrant on Senator Ciro Nogueira as part of an expanding investigation into the now-defunct lender Banco Master. The action was authorized by a Supreme Court ruling on Thursday.

stories.title: US to host third round of talks between Israel and Lebanon next week
stories.summary: The United States will host a third round of negotiations between Israel and Lebanon next week. Military representatives from both sides are set to participate for the first time, with discussions aimed at advancing concrete measures for disarming Hezbollah.

stories.title: With ceasefires on three fronts, hoped-for war gains suspended in dangerous limbo
stories.summary: Israel is navigating ceasefires on three fronts — Gaza, Lebanon, and Iran — with significant military gains achieved but key objectives still unmet. The situation remains precarious as negotiations continue under pressure from the Trump administration to reach deals.

stories.title: Kremlin says Putin’s security is being tightened for Victory Day events
stories.summary: The Kremlin announced that security for President Vladimir Putin is being tightened ahead of Victory Day events. Putin is expected to oversee a military parade on Moscow's Red Square and deliver a speech.

stories.title: Kremlin aide says further peace talks are pointless until Ukraine withdraws troops from the Donbas
stories.summary: Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov told Interfax that Russia sees no purpose in continuing trilateral peace talks with Ukraine and the United States until Ukrainian forces withdraw from areas of the Donbas. The statement represents a formal condition for resuming negotiations.

stories.title: Russian bomb strike on Zaporizhzhia region leaves three people injured
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out an airstrike on the village of Shchaslyve in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region. Three people were injured and a residential house was destroyed in the bombing.

stories.title: “The World in Front of Me” – New York - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Photographer Bill Aron reflected on his work documenting Jewish life in 1970s New York, including the Lower East Side and the countercultural Havurah movement. The project shaped both his career and personal life.

stories.title: 12 US Senate Dems: IDF mass evacuations in Iran, Lebanon ‘likely’ violate international law
stories.summary: Twelve US Senate Democrats sent a letter to US Central Command questioning the legality of Israeli mass evacuation orders in Iran and Lebanon, calling them likely violations of international law. The IDF responded that the practice aims to protect civilians and complies with the laws of war.

stories.title: Masood expresses confidence in bowling as Pakistan set to face Bangladesh in first Test tomorrow
stories.summary: Pakistan Test captain Shan Masood expressed confidence in his bowling attack ahead of the first Test against Bangladesh in Mirpur. Pakistan is visiting Bangladesh after being whitewashed at home by Bangladesh in August 2024.

stories.title: Qatar envoy backs UN resolution to keep Hormuz open
stories.summary: Qatar's UN ambassador, Alya Ahmed Saif al-Thani, endorsed a draft Security Council resolution aimed at safeguarding navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. She described the proposal as critically important for regional and global stability, warning that the current situation threatens energy security and worsens humanitarian crises.

stories.title: Russia says Armenia is being dragged into EU’s ‘anti-Russian orbit’
stories.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry stated on May 7 that Armenia was being drawn into what it described as the European Union's "anti-Russian orbit." The remarks reflect Moscow's concern over Yerevan's deepening ties with the EU.

stories.title: British Greens battle antisemitism scandal as Jewish leader Zack Polanski targets local elections
stories.summary: Zack Polanski, a Jewish leader within the British Green Party, is targeting upcoming local elections amid an antisemitism scandal in the party. Polls suggest he could deliver significant gains, potentially making him one of the most prominent Jewish progressives globally.

stories.title: Can China help end the Iran war?
stories.summary: Chinese and Iranian foreign ministers held a meeting amid an ongoing ceasefire between Iran and its adversaries. The discussions centered on whether Beijing can play a role in bringing the conflict to an end.

stories.title: 'Significant hatred': Number of antisemitic incidents in Denmark remains at historic high
stories.summary: A report found that antisemitic incidents in Denmark remain at historic highs. Jewish institutions including the Jewish Community, Jewish Culture Festival, and Jewish Information Center have received hate messages, death threats, and demands to distance themselves from Israel.

stories.title: Moscow’s Victory Day parade to proceed without military hardware; ‘Immortal Regiment’ march canceled
stories.summary: Moscow's Victory Day parade on May 9 will proceed without military hardware for the first time since 2007, as Russia's war against Ukraine enters its fifth year. The traditional Immortal Regiment marches have also been canceled or moved online in several Russian cities and regions.

stories.title: Spain summons Israeli envoy over detention of flotilla activist
stories.summary: Spain summoned Israel's ambassador over the detention of a flotilla activist, marking the latest diplomatic confrontation between Madrid and Tel Aviv. The dispute is rooted in ongoing tensions over the war in Gaza and pro-Palestinian activism.

stories.title: Russia Scolds Ally Armenia for Hosting Zelensky
stories.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova criticized ally Armenia for hosting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. Zakharova also warned Yerevan against pursuing closer ties with the European Union.

stories.title: Russian strikes leave 41 people killed, over 970 injured in Kharkiv in one year
stories.summary: Russian shelling killed 41 people and injured more than 970 in Kharkiv over the past year. The attacks destroyed or damaged some 13,000 sites across the Ukrainian city.

stories.title: Breathe Pakistan 2026: Need for multi-sectoral approach towards climate action highlighted
stories.summary: The second Breathe Pakistan International Climate Change Conference concluded in Islamabad, with experts calling for a multi-sectoral approach to climate action and greater engagement of women and youth. Pakistan remains among the most climate-vulnerable nations despite contributing minimally to global emissions.

stories.title: Inside the Israeli bloc that could topple Netanyahu
stories.summary: Political rivals of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have formed an alliance ahead of upcoming elections. Questions remain about whether the bloc is cohesive enough to unseat him from power.

stories.title: 'Shutdown': Moody's expects Dubai hotel occupancy to plummet to 10 percent
stories.summary: Moody's projects that Dubai hotel occupancy will drop to 10 percent from a pre-war level of 80 percent by the end of the second quarter of 2026. The decline is attributed to the US-Israeli war on Iran, which began on February 28, severely reducing visitor numbers to the emirate.

stories.title: ISIL-linked Australian women arrested at airports
stories.summary: Australian authorities arrested three women with alleged links to ISIL at airports in Melbourne and Sydney. Details on specific charges or the nature of their alleged ties to the group were not immediately disclosed.

stories.title: How does budget reconciliation work? Here’s everything you need to know.
stories.summary: A report outlines the U.S. congressional budget reconciliation process used to draw up the annual military spending plan. The piece explains the procedural mechanisms Congress employs to pass defense budgets.

stories.title: 3 children killed, several injured in South Waziristan attack: security sources
stories.summary: Two separate attacks in South Waziristan, Pakistan, killed three children and injured several others. An explosion near a civilian settlement in Gawa Khwa was attributed to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan, while mortar shells were fired at civilians in Angoor Adda by Afghan Taliban forces.

stories.title: Secret GRU-linked department at top Russian university trains hackers and saboteurs, investigation finds
stories.summary: A joint investigation by The Insider, The Guardian, Le Monde, Der Spiegel, Frontstory, and VSquare found that a secret department at Bauman Moscow State Technical University's military training center is training hackers and saboteurs for Russia's GRU military intelligence agency. Journalists reviewed over two thousand internal documents including curricula and student lists.

stories.title: Israel’s attacks and pressure sowing seeds for division in tense Lebanon
stories.summary: Analysts say Israel is leveraging military strikes and political pressure to exploit existing divisions within Lebanon. The strategy reportedly aims to force concessions from Lebanese officials amid ongoing tensions.

stories.title: Breathe Pakistan 2026: Need for multi-sectoral approach to climate action highlighted
stories.summary: The second Breathe Pakistan International Climate Change Conference concluded in Islamabad, with experts calling for a multi-sectoral approach to climate action and greater engagement of women and youth. The conference, organised by DawnMedia, highlighted that Pakistan remains among the most climate-vulnerable nations despite contributing minimally to global emissions.

stories.title: At least three children killed, several injured in South Waziristan attack: security sources
stories.summary: At least three children were killed and several people injured in two separate attacks in South Waziristan, Pakistan. An explosion hit a civilian settlement in the Gawa Khwa area, while mortar shells were fired at civilians by Afghan Taliban forces in the border tehsil of Angoor Adda.

stories.title: Grunis Committee urges High Court to reject petitions against Gofman Mossad appointment
stories.summary: The Grunis Committee recommended that Israel's High Court of Justice reject petitions challenging Prime Minister Netanyahu's appointment of his military secretary, Gofman, as the next Mossad chief. The court is scheduled to hear the case on Tuesday, following two legal challenges to the decision to replace outgoing director Barnea.

stories.title: Russian Economy Shrinks in the First Quarter
stories.summary: Russia's GDP contracted by 0.5% in the first quarter, significantly underperforming the Central Bank's earlier projection of 1.6% annualized growth for the period.

stories.title: Pakistan expects agreement between US and Iran 'sooner rather than later': FO
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Office spokesperson Tahir Andrabi said during a weekly briefing in Islamabad that Pakistan expects an agreement between the United States and Iran "sooner rather than later." He expressed optimism that the parties would reach a peaceful, sustainable solution benefiting regional and international stability.

stories.title: Man pleads guilty to murder, other charges, for firebomb attack on Colorado demonstrators
stories.summary: Mohamed Sabry Soliman pleaded guilty in Boulder County District Court to murder and other charges for a firebomb attack on demonstrators supporting Israeli hostages in Gaza in Boulder, Colorado, on June 1. One person was killed and a dozen others injured in the attack. Soliman faces life in prison without parole.

stories.title: Lawyer: Major human rights debates ahead on new Civil Code draft
stories.summary: Ukraine's draft new Civil Code contains modern provisions reflecting societal changes, but some clauses are expected to spark significant debate during the second parliamentary reading. Lawyers note that major human rights questions remain unresolved in the legislation.

stories.title: Iran says ceasefire and ending war top priorities in talks
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said securing a ceasefire and ending the war are Tehran's top priorities in ongoing discussions. He added that Iran is reviewing a US proposal and will convey its decision through Pakistani mediators.

stories.title: Hamas disarmament talks stuck between Israeli security and Gaza guarantees - exclusive
stories.summary: Negotiations over the Trump administration's 20-point Gaza peace plan continue, with Hamas not yet agreeing to disarm. Key sticking points include security guarantees, Israeli withdrawal terms, and the future role of the Israeli Security Forces in Gaza.

stories.title: 4 children killed, 20 people injured as roof of classroom collapses in Dera Ghazi Khan school
stories.summary: At least four children were killed and 20 people injured when a classroom roof collapsed at a private school in Dera Ghazi Khan, Punjab, Pakistan. The injured included 16 students, two teachers, and two labourers. Rescue 1122 personnel reached the site within four minutes of the incident.

stories.title: ‘We are prepared’: DG ISPR highlights indigenous military capabilities on Marka-i-Haq anniversary
stories.summary: Pakistan's ISPR Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry stated at a press conference in Islamabad that Pakistan's armed forces are "prepared," highlighting indigenous military capabilities. The remarks came during commemorations of the one-year anniversary of Marka-i-Haq, referencing the 2024 military conflict with India.

stories.title: Spain awards UN rapporteur Albanese top civilian honour
stories.summary: UN Special Rapporteur on the occupied Palestinian territories Francesca Albanese was awarded Spain's Order of Civil Merit. The honor recognized her work documenting alleged violations of international law in the Gaza Strip.

stories.title: Iraq's historic marshes revive as water returns after years of drought
stories.summary: Rising water levels are reviving Iraq's historic Chibayish Marshes after years of drought that left large areas cracked and dry. Buffalo herders and fishermen are returning to previously abandoned areas as the wetlands recover.

stories.title: Woman killed by partner at home in London feared ‘he was on the warpath’, court hears
stories.summary: Annabel Rook, 46, a social enterprise co-founder from Stoke Newington in north London, left a voice message to her sister saying her partner was "on the warpath" weeks before she was fatally stabbed. Clifton George, 45, is on trial at a London court accused of murdering Rook during an argument at their home last June.

stories.title: Russian historian who studied Soviet repression arrested on terrorism charges
stories.summary: Oleg Novoselev, a Russian historian who studied Soviet-era political repression in the Urals, has been detained and transferred to a pre-trial detention center in Yekaterinburg on terrorism charges.

stories.title: Man pleads guilty to Colorado firebombing, groups call for family reprieve
stories.summary: A man pleaded guilty to a June 2025 firebombing in Colorado that targeted supporters of Israeli captives held in Gaza. Advocacy groups are calling for leniency for the assailant's family, saying they have been unjustly targeted.

stories.title: Zelensky sets tasks for Umerov ahead of U.S. talks
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky outlined key tasks for National Security and Defense Council Secretary Rustem Umerov ahead of his negotiations in the United States. The assignments are intended to guide Ukraine's diplomatic agenda in the upcoming talks.

stories.title: US sanctions Iraqi minister accused of aiding Iran oil sales
stories.summary: The United States imposed sanctions on Iraq's deputy oil minister, accusing him of helping Iran circumvent restrictions on its oil exports. The measures target the official's alleged role in facilitating Iranian oil sales through Iraqi channels.

stories.title: Bahrain backs UN resolution on Strait of Hormuz security and navigation
stories.summary: Bahrain's UN ambassador Jamal Alrowaiei voiced support for a US- and Gulf-co-sponsored draft Security Council resolution to safeguard shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The resolution calls on Iran to cease attacks and threats against merchant vessels in the waterway.

stories.title: Whirlpool warns of ‘recession-level’ slump as Iran war and tariff ruling hit sales
stories.summary: Whirlpool slashed its earnings forecast and announced price increases of 10 percent, with an additional 4 percent hike planned, citing the Iran war and tariff impacts. The appliance company reported a nearly 10 percent revenue drop as consumer confidence collapsed, calling conditions a "recession-level industry decline" in the U.S. market.

stories.title: British ambassador to Israel outlines UK's plan to protect country's Jews
stories.summary: British Ambassador Walters outlined the United Kingdom's plans to protect Jewish communities in Britain. He acknowledged that the issue also concerns Jewish individuals and families in Israel who maintain ties to or wish to travel to the UK.

stories.title: Miss Israel lashes out over alleged snub by Rama Duwaji
stories.summary: A social media dispute erupted between Miss Israel and media personality Rama Duwaji over an alleged public snub. The incident highlighted growing tensions over Israel's international image amid escalating boycott calls related to its military operations in Gaza.

stories.title: Still no sign of a solution in Iran: US president says the war will be over soon
stories.summary: President Donald Trump again stated that the war with Iran would be over 'soon,' echoing similar claims he has made repeatedly since March. Despite these assertions, no concrete resolution to the conflict has materialized.

stories.title: Bennett sues former ally, now a Likud minister, for libel over claim he is mentally unwell
stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett filed a libel lawsuit against Likud minister Idit Silman, a former political ally, over public claims that he was mentally unwell and heavily medicated during his time as prime minister. A Religious Zionism MK and a right-wing TV channel are also named in the suit.

stories.title: UK police make third arrest over attempted arson on London synagogue last month
stories.summary: UK police arrested a 19-year-old man in connection with an attempted arson at a synagogue in Finchley, London, on April 15. Authorities said 30 people have been arrested so far in relation to recent synagogue arsons, with eight charged and one guilty plea.

stories.title: A small town in Germany braces for end to decades of life with US troops
stories.summary: The Bavarian town of Vilseck, Germany, which has hosted U.S. forces since the end of World War Two, is preparing for the potential departure of American troops. President Donald Trump's decision to withdraw at least 5,000 troops from Germany could significantly impact the community.

stories.title: US targets Cuba nickel operation in move with implications for China-linked supply chains
stories.summary: The Trump administration sanctioned Moa Nickel SA, a joint venture between Canada's Sherritt International and Cuba's state-owned General Nickel Company. Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced the move as part of broader pressure on Havana's military-controlled economy. The sanctions could disrupt China-linked battery supply chains that depend on Cuban nickel.

stories.title: Iran destroyed hundreds of structures at US military sites
stories.summary: Satellite imagery analyzed by The Washington Post revealed that Iranian strikes damaged or destroyed hundreds of structures and pieces of equipment at US military installations. The findings illustrate the scale of damage inflicted by Iran on American military sites.

stories.title: Trump's 'irresponsible war' to blame for economic slowdown, German minister says
stories.summary: German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil blamed U.S. President Trump's military actions against Iran for contributing to an economic slowdown in Germany. Klingbeil described the conflict as an "irresponsible war" that is harming the German economy.

stories.title: US and Iran close to temporary truce, Pakistani officials claim
stories.summary: Pakistani officials said the United States and Iran are close to a temporary agreement to halt the war in the Middle East. Officials in Islamabad indicated a basic interim deal could be reached as early as this weekend, with Tehran reportedly reviewing a U.S. proposal.

stories.title: Tensions over pro-Israel lobbying group highlight rifts in Democratic primaries
stories.summary: WASHINGTON, May 7 - A growing number of Democratic primary challengers are making opposition to the American Israel Public Affairs Committee a campaign issue as they seek to unseat party incumbents ba

stories.title: Tel Aviv Museum of Art gives voice to the female IDF observers of Oct. 7
stories.summary: The Tel Aviv Museum of Art displayed ten video testimonies from female IDF observers who witnessed the October 7 Hamas attack. The exhibition featured no archival footage or maps—only the women's faces and accounts.

stories.title: Saab CEO optimistic Ukraine Gripen deal could be finalized this year
stories.summary: Saab's CEO expressed optimism that a deal to supply Gripen fighter jets to Ukraine could be finalized this year. A senior Ukrainian official said Kyiv was ready for the agreement, though Sweden's defense minister indicated that challenges remain before it can be completed.

stories.title: How Trump’s Minneapolis immigration blitz hobbled US federal crime fighting
stories.summary: A federal immigration enforcement operation in Minneapolis ordered by the Trump administration has dramatically slowed other federal investigations and prosecutions of serious crimes. The blitz diverted resources from ongoing federal crime-fighting efforts in the area.

stories.title: How Trump's Minneapolis immigration blitz hobbled federal crime fighting
stories.summary: MINNEAPOLIS, May 7 - The Trump administration blitz that flooded Minnesota with immigration agents also dramatically slowed other federal investigations and prosecutions into an array of serious crime

stories.title: Trump shelved ‘Project Freedom’ after Saudis refused use of bases and airspace
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia refused to allow the United States to use its Prince Sultan airbase and airspace for "Project Freedom," a military escort operation for oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz. The refusal prompted President Trump to shelve the plan shortly after it was announced.

stories.title: ASELSAN at SAHA 2026: Introducing next-generation multi-domain defense systems
stories.summary: Turkish defense firm ASELSAN presented its latest multi-domain defense systems at the SAHA 2026 exhibition. The portfolio includes electronic warfare, counter-UAV, airborne, and naval capabilities integrated within a unified operational framework.

stories.title: Ireland to join Agreement on Special Tribunal
stories.summary: Ireland informed the Council of Europe of its readiness to join the Enlarged Partial Agreement establishing a Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression against Ukraine. The move adds Ireland to the group of nations supporting accountability for the conflict.

stories.title: How Gaza became one of the defining issues in UK local elections
stories.summary: Pro-Palestine candidates and activists reported that anger over the Labour Party's stance on Gaza became one of the defining issues in UK local elections. The conflict's influence on British domestic politics has grown as voters increasingly factor foreign policy into their choices.

stories.title: Greenland’s PM slams ‘indecent’ bid to buy locals’ signatures for US adhesion petition
stories.summary: Greenland's Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen condemned reports that an American individual offered locals US$200,000 each to sign a petition supporting Greenland's incorporation into the United States. The criticism follows repeated statements by President Trump that annexing the Danish autonomous territory is necessary for U.S. national security.

stories.title: Prisoner accused of Lostprophets singer’s murder boasted to guards about fame, court told
stories.summary: Rico Gedel is accused of murdering former Lostprophets singer Ian Watkins at HMP Wakefield, a high-security prison, on October 11. Leeds Crown Court heard that Gedel stabbed Watkins in the head and neck with a homemade knife, then boasted to guards about potential fame. Watkins had been serving a 29-year sentence for child sexual offences.

stories.title: Iran mocks Trump’s ‘Project Freedom’ as adversaries wrestle over talks to end war
stories.summary: Iran mocked President Trump's "Project Freedom" initiative after it was abruptly suspended. Reports revealed Saudi Arabia's refusal to grant the U.S. access to its bases was the actual reason for the cancellation, rather than Trump's public suggestion that a peace deal opportunity had emerged.

stories.title: Superbike rider killed in crash during qualifying in Northern Ireland
stories.summary: A superbike rider was killed during qualifying at the North West 200 race in Northern Ireland. The fatality is the 20th in the event's history but the first since 2016; the race is set to celebrate its centenary in 2029.

stories.title: Nigerian army frees seven children kidnapped from an orphanage
stories.summary: The Nigerian army announced it freed seven children and two adults who had been held captive following a kidnapping from an orphanage the previous month. Troops carried out the rescue operation, though further details on the location were not specified.

stories.title: Israeli soldier pictured desecrating Virgin Mary statue in Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military launched an inquiry after a viral photo showed one of its soldiers desecrating a statue of the Virgin Mary in the Christian village of Debel in southern Lebanon. The military said it identified the soldier and that he would face disciplinary action.

stories.title: Iran hit US bases harder than Washington first revealed, satellite imagery shows - report
stories.summary: New satellite imagery reportedly reveals that Iranian strikes caused more damage to US military bases across the Middle East than Washington initially disclosed. The findings raise questions about base defenses and Iran's targeting capabilities.

stories.title: Russian forces hit passenger train in Mykolaiv region
stories.summary: Russian forces struck railway infrastructure in Ukraine's Mykolaiv region, damaging a locomotive and two buffer wagons. No casualties were reported.

stories.title: How Hezbollah drones are testing Israel's strategy in Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah has deployed low-cost fibre-optic drones that are exposing vulnerabilities in Israel's battlefield defenses in Lebanon. The Israeli military has been forced into a reactive posture as it struggles to counter the evolving drone threat.

stories.title: Russia says Ukraine launched a major drone attack after Moscow shunned ceasefire offer
stories.summary: Russia faced a major Ukrainian drone attack after Moscow rejected a ceasefire offer from Kyiv. Tensions have escalated as Russia's Victory Day celebrations approach and U.S.-led peace efforts have failed to gain traction.

stories.title: Keeping the Lebanese army weak: A hardened US military doctrine at Israel's service
stories.summary: The United States' legal obligation to maintain Israel's "qualitative military edge" has contributed to keeping the Lebanese Armed Forces under-funded and under-equipped, according to an analysis. This comes as the international community calls on the Lebanese army to disarm Hezbollah, one month after Israeli strikes on "Black Wednesday" killed 361 people in Lebanon.

stories.title: Yekaterinburg Police Arrest Soviet Repression Researcher on ‘Terrorism’ Charges
stories.summary: Oleg Novoselov, a researcher of Stalin's Great Terror of the 1930s in the Urals and former volunteer at the human rights group Memorial, has been arrested in Yekaterinburg on terrorism charges.

stories.title: 19 Kenyans killed fighting in Russia-Ukraine war, 32 missing
stories.summary: Kenya's foreign minister disclosed that 19 Kenyan citizens have died fighting on the Ukrainian frontline and 32 others remain missing. The announcement comes amid growing criticism over reports of Kenyans being forcibly enlisted into the Russian army.

stories.title: French far-right leaders court Israel envoy ahead of vote
stories.summary: French far-right leaders Marine Le Pen and Jordan Bardella met with the Israeli, German, and US ambassadors ahead of France's upcoming election. The diplomatic meetings signal the National Rally's efforts to bolster its foreign policy credentials before voters go to the polls.

stories.title: Why has the US sanctioned Iraq’s deputy oil minister for helping Iran?
stories.summary: The United States accused Iraqi deputy oil minister Ali Maarij al-Bahadly of helping Iran evade sanctions and export oil through Iraq. Washington imposed sanctions on al-Bahadly for his alleged role in facilitating the transfers.

stories.title: Ohio GOP primary candidate who asked AI bot to praise Hitler loses, gets 17.5% of vote
stories.summary: Casey Putsch, an Ohio Republican primary candidate who had asked an AI chatbot to praise Hitler, lost in a landslide to Trump-backed Vivek Ramaswamy but still received 17.5 percent of the vote. Tuesday's other races highlighted Trump's continued influence over the GOP and a winning streak for Democrats in special elections.

stories.title: 'Shutdown': Moody's expects Dubai hotel occupancy to plummet to 10 percent
stories.summary: Moody's projects that hotel occupancy in Dubai could drop to approximately 10 percent amid a severe downturn in the UAE's tourism sector. The decline has been attributed to the disruption caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran, which began on 28 February.

stories.title: Russia, Ukraine trade attacks ahead of Kremlin's World War II commemoration parade
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine exchanged major attacks on Friday as Moscow's self-declared two-day truce—intended to protect its World War II Victory Day parade on Red Square—collapsed. Ukraine had never agreed to the ceasefire and criticized Putin for pausing hostilities solely to stage a military parade on Saturday.

stories.title: Man arrested ‘with weapon’ near ex-prince Andrew’s home, UK police say
stories.summary: Norfolk police in eastern England arrested a man near the Sandringham Estate after he was found wielding a weapon and behaving in an intimidating manner close to Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's home. UK media reported the suspect wore a balaclava and allegedly threatened the former prince. He was detained on suspicion of a public order offence and possession of an offensive weapon.

stories.title: Umerov arrives in U.S. for talks
stories.summary: Rustem Umerov, secretary of Ukraine's National Security and Defense Council and head of the Ukrainian negotiating group, arrived in the United States for talks.

stories.title: Israel says it killed Hezbollah commander in first strike on Beirut since ceasefire
stories.summary: Israel said it killed a commander of Hezbollah's elite Radwan force in an airstrike on Beirut, marking the first Israeli attack on the Lebanese capital since a ceasefire was agreed last month.

stories.title: Gaza movie wins best short film award at 'Italian Oscars'
stories.summary: A short film titled "Everyday in Gaza," documenting the struggles of Palestinians living under bombardment and displacement, won best short film at Italy's equivalent of the Academy Awards. The film highlights conditions in Gaza during the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: The next Army chief won’t inherit a force, he’ll inherit an argument
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that the next U.S. Army chief of staff will need to make the case for the continued relevance of land power in an era increasingly dominated by drone warfare and other modern technologies.

stories.title: Spain honours UN rapporteur Albanese for Gaza advocacy
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez awarded the Order of Civil Merit to UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese for her advocacy during Israel's war on Gaza. Albanese has accused Israel of genocide and war crimes against Palestinians, with over 72,500 Palestinians killed in the conflict.

stories.title: Lebanon, Israel to hold new talks in Washington May 14-15: US
stories.summary: US officials announced that Lebanon and Israel will resume negotiations in Washington on May 14–15. Tensions remain elevated following Israeli military operations targeting Hezbollah in Lebanon.

stories.title: Israel army investigating after soldier seen desecrating Virgin Mary statue in Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli soldier was photographed placing a cigarette in the mouth of a statue of the Virgin Mary.

stories.title: Royal Navy tracks Russian frigate for one month off UK coast
stories.summary: Britain's Royal Navy tracked the Russian frigate Admiral Grigorovich daily throughout April as it sailed from the Atlantic to the North Sea. The Russian vessel escorted six Russia-linked ships, including at least three under economic sanctions, through the Dover Strait. Four UK ships and helicopters maintained continuous surveillance as Moscow increased its maritime presence near British waters.

stories.title: Iranian's Pezeshkian claims to have met with Iran's missing supreme leader - report
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian claimed to have met with Iran's missing Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, praising his vision and sincerity. The claim comes amid prolonged speculation about Khamenei's absence from public life.

stories.title: Did the US military turn a blind eye to recruiting neo-Nazis? | Matt Kennard
stories.summary: British investigative journalist Matt Kennard, co-founder of Declassified UK and author of "Irregular Army," discussed how the US military allegedly overlooked the recruitment of neo-Nazis during the War on Terror. His reporting includes accounts from service members whose commanders reportedly valued their extremist ideology.

stories.title: Ukrainian Defense Forces strike Russian missile ship in Kaspiysk, depots in Luhansk region
stories.summary: On the night of May 7, 2026, Ukrainian Defense Forces struck a Project 22800 Karakurt-class small missile ship at the Russian naval base in Kaspiysk, Dagestan, along with military depots in the Luhansk region.

stories.title: War and peace: key themes of Pope Leo's first year in office
stories.summary: One year after his election, Pope Leo XIV has emerged as an important counterpart to U.S. President Trump on matters of war and peace. The direction he intends to take the Catholic Church remains unclear.

stories.title: China’s use of propaganda may outwit US if Taiwan conflict arises, experts warn
stories.summary: Security experts warned that China has studied information-warfare tactics used during the conflicts in Iran and Ukraine and could deploy similar propaganda strategies against the United States in a Taiwan Strait crisis. Retired U.S. Lieutenant General S. Clinton Hinote said he was struck by Iran's propaganda efforts since February and cautioned that Beijing would replicate such approaches.

stories.title: Senate Democrats press top media regulator Brendan Carr to back off ABC
stories.summary: Eight Senate Democrats sent a letter to FCC Chair Brendan Carr urging him to rescind an order requiring ABC to apply early for renewal of its eight owned-station television licenses. The licenses were not originally due for renewal until 2028–2031, but the FCC's order moved the deadline to the end of May.

stories.title: Trump calls for ‘incitement’ charges against top Democrat Hakeem Jeffries
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump called for "incitement" charges against House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, the top Democrat in the House of Representatives. Trump cited Jeffries's remarks about "maximum warfare" in the context of electoral redistricting maps.

stories.title: Israel and Lebanon to hold talks in Washington in mid-May
stories.summary: A US State Department official confirmed that Israel and Lebanon will hold talks in Washington on May 14 and 15. The discussions come amid ongoing regional tensions.

stories.title: London police investigate after car drives toward Jewish students
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police are investigating an incident in which a car drove toward Jewish students near a school identified as the Hasmonean High School for Boys. The school declined to comment.

stories.title: Rutgers drops commencement speaker over pro-Palestine posts
stories.summary: Rutgers University canceled a commencement address by alumnus Rami Elghandour following scrutiny over his social media posts accusing Israel of war crimes in Gaza.

stories.title: Israeli settler attacks leaves three Palestinians suffocated in occupied West Bank
stories.summary: Three Palestinians suffered suffocation in Masafer Yatta in the occupied West Bank after armed Israeli settlers attacked their vehicle near Khirbet al-Fakhit. The settlers reportedly pelted the car with stones, smashed its windows, and sprayed pepper spray at the passengers, causing severe breathing difficulties.

stories.title: Europe defense autonomy is in reach at €50 billion a year: German experts
stories.summary: A new paper by German defense experts identifies ten central capability gaps that Europe must address to achieve defense autonomy without U.S. military assistance. The study estimates the cost at approximately €50 billion per year.

stories.title: Speaker Stefanchuk denies restrictions on LGBT rights in draft Civil Code
stories.summary: Ukrainian parliament speaker Ruslan Stefanchuk stated that the draft of Ukraine's new Civil Code does not contain provisions restricting LGBT rights and maintains the existing legal framework.

stories.title: Russian Military Accuses Ukraine of Launching Drone Attacks From Latvian Airspace
stories.summary: Russia's military accused Ukraine of launching drone attacks from Latvian airspace. Latvian officials confirmed two drones crashed on their territory, with one causing a brief fire at an oil storage facility.

stories.title: Two men first in British history to be found guilty of spying for China
stories.summary: Chi Leung Wai, a UK Border Force officer, and Chung Biu Yuen, a Hong Kong trade official based in London, were found guilty at the Old Bailey of assisting a foreign intelligence service. They are the first people in British history convicted of spying for China. The pair conducted surveillance of dissidents as part of a "shadow policing" operation.

stories.title: A small town in Germany braces for end to decades of life with US troops
stories.summary: A small Bavarian town in Germany that has hosted U.S. military forces since the end of World War II faces significant changes as the U.S. military considers withdrawing from the country. The community is bracing for the economic and social impact of potentially losing decades of American troop presence.

stories.title: Australian women and children linked to ISIS return from Syria, several arrested
stories.summary: Australian women and children linked to ISIS were repatriated from Syria, with several individuals arrested upon arrival. A heavy police presence was reported at Sydney and Melbourne airports as the two groups landed.

stories.title: Spain summons Israeli envoy to protest detention of Spanish flotilla activist
stories.summary: Spain summoned Israel's envoy after Israeli forces detained Spanish-Palestinian activist Saif Abu Keshek, whom Israel accused of being a leading member of a group allegedly affiliated with Hamas. The incident is the latest diplomatic clash between Madrid and Tel Aviv over the Gaza war and pro-Palestinian activism.

stories.title: Two former Chinese Defence Ministers sentenced to death for corruption
stories.summary: Two former Chinese defence ministers, Wei Fenghe and Li Shangfu, were sentenced to death for corruption. Both had served under President Xi Jinping and were expelled from the ruling Communist Party in 2024. They were also former members of the Central Military Commission.

stories.title: “He was just shocked”: Russia’s UN ambassador walked out of diplomatic event after seeing Lviv craft beer
stories.summary: At an informal beer-tasting event for UN permanent representatives in New York, Ukraine presented craft beers from Lviv's Pravda brewery. Russia's UN ambassador reportedly walked out of the diplomatic gathering upon seeing the Ukrainian selections.

stories.title: US pushing Israeli de-escalation ahead of new talks: Lebanese official
stories.summary: A Lebanese official told Al Jazeera that the US is pressing Israel to de-escalate ahead of new negotiations. Lebanese and Israeli delegations are expected to hold talks in Washington, DC, the following week.

stories.title: Israeli attack kills son of Hamas leader negotiating with Trump-led board
stories.summary: Azzam Al-Hayya had been struck in an Israeli attack on the night of May 6.

stories.title: Three children killed in explosion in Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
stories.summary: Three children were killed in an explosion in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. Police reported that a motorcycle had allegedly been parked outside a house by an unidentified individual shortly before the blast.

stories.title: ‘Worst year in memory’: parties describe climate of abuse on campaign trail for May elections
stories.summary: Candidates across multiple political parties in England, Scotland, and Wales reported death threats, intimidation, and harassment during campaigning for local and devolved elections. The Green Party described the 2025 campaign as the worst for abuse in memory, with incidents occurring both online and in person.

stories.title: Lebanon Latest Israeli strikes Beirut despite ‘ceasefire’
stories.summary: Israel carried out an airstrike on Beirut's southern suburbs, marking the first such attack since an April 16 US-brokered ceasefire was announced. The strike raised questions about the durability of the ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: IDF cancels events in north amid concern over potential Hezbollah revenge attacks
stories.summary: The Israeli military canceled events in northern Israel over concerns about potential Hezbollah retaliatory attacks. Three people were reported killed in southern Lebanese villages as the IDF targeted Hezbollah infrastructure, and Prime Minister Netanyahu warned that no terrorist is safe following the killing of a Radwan force chief in Beirut.

stories.title: EU not to evacuate diplomats from Kyiv amid Kremlin threats
stories.summary: The European Union announced it will not evacuate diplomats from Kyiv despite Russian threats of massive missile strikes on the Ukrainian capital. The EU stated it would maintain its full diplomatic presence in the city.

stories.title: Iran’s president says he has spoken to the country’s Supreme Leader
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian announced that he met with Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. The meeting came amid speculation about the supreme leader's public visibility and decision-making role during the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: The BJP’s Bengal victory exposes the erosion of Indian democracy
stories.summary: The BJP's election victory in West Bengal, India, followed a sweeping electoral roll revision. Critics say the circumstances of the win raise serious concerns about the integrity of the democratic process.

stories.title: Rwandan singer dies as he was being released from prison
stories.summary: A Rwandan singer and former university lecturer who was a vocal critic of the government and the ruling Rwandan Patriotic Front party died while being released from prison. Further details about the circumstances of his death were not immediately available.

stories.title: Lebanon PM to discuss border, refugees with Sharaa in Syria
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister is set to meet Syrian leader Ahmed al-Sharaa to discuss border demarcation, security cooperation, and the return of Syrian refugees to Syria.

stories.title: European Union strikes deal to ban sexualised AI deepfakes
stories.summary: The European Union reached a deal to ban sexualised AI deepfakes, explicitly prohibiting so-called nudifier applications. EU lawmaker Michael McNamara said the legislation marks the first time EU law has drawn a clear line against using AI to humiliate, exploit, or endanger people.

stories.title: Israel strikes Beirut and southern Lebanon despite truce
stories.summary: Israel struck Beirut's southern suburbs and southern Lebanon on Thursday despite an existing truce. The Israeli military said it killed the commander of Hezbollah's elite Radwan Force unit in the Beirut strike, one day after targeting a Hezbollah commander in the first such attack on the area since the ceasefire began.

stories.title: Brazil’s Lula to discuss fighting organized crime, tariffs in Trump meeting
stories.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva traveled to Washington for talks with President Donald Trump on issues including organized crime and tariffs. The Thursday meeting was only their second official encounter, following talks in Malaysia last year, as Lula seeks to boost his domestic standing ahead of October elections.

stories.title: Levin says he’ll let Supreme Court ‘disappear’ if his justice picks are not selected
stories.summary: Israeli Justice Minister Yariv Levin threatened to let the Supreme Court "disappear" if his preferred justice candidates are not selected. His comments came as a deadline to submit a timeline for convening the Judicial Selection Committee was about to expire.

stories.title: Rosenberg: Russia's Victory Day parade with no tanks a sign Ukraine war not going to plan
stories.summary: Analyst Joel Rosenberg noted that Russia's Victory Day parade in Moscow on Saturday will feature no military hardware for the first time in nearly two decades. Rosenberg characterized the absence of tanks and equipment as a sign that the war in Ukraine is not proceeding as planned for Russia.

stories.title: Zelensky: Ukrainian long-range sanctions reach Perm again – over 1,500 km from frontline
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky reported that Ukrainian long-range strikes again reached the city of Perm, located over 1,500 kilometers from the front line. The strikes targeted sites linked to Russia's military industry.

stories.title: Iran’s President Pezeshkian seeks to quash divided leadership narrative
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian sought to project unity among Tehran's top leadership amid US pressure during disputes over the Strait of Hormuz. Officials emphasized solidarity to counter narratives of division within Iran's government.

stories.title: Ukraine’s air defense intercepted nearly 6,000 Russian aerial targets in April — at 90% effectiveness rate
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces intercepted nearly 6,000 Russian aerial targets in April, achieving a 90 percent effectiveness rate. Some 5,861 targets were destroyed before reaching their intended destinations.

stories.title: First case of hantavirus diagnosed in Israeli after visit to Eastern Europe
stories.summary: An Israeli citizen was diagnosed with hantavirus after traveling to Eastern Europe. The patient contracted a European strain of the virus, distinct from the South American Andes strain linked to the ongoing outbreak aboard the cruise ship MV Hondius.

stories.title: Circus troupe tackles jihadist nightmares of Burkina Faso's children
stories.summary: A four-member acrobatic troupe called Dafra Circus from Burkina Faso has created a show titled "Souffle" ("Breath") addressing the impact of the country's jihadist conflict on children. The performance aims to help young audiences process the trauma caused by ongoing violence.

stories.title: MSF says Israel has 'manufactured malnutrition crisis' in Gaza
stories.summary: Médecins Sans Frontières released a report accusing Israel of manufacturing a malnutrition crisis in Gaza through restrictions on humanitarian aid. The report highlighted catastrophic conditions for pregnant women and newborns.

stories.title: Why Israel fears a US-Iran deal could leave Tehran’s nuclear threat intact - opinion
stories.summary: Israeli officials fear that a US-Iran nuclear deal could delay rather than dismantle Tehran's nuclear threat. Concerns include that such an agreement would give Iran time to recover economically and maintain Hezbollah as a strategic deterrent.

stories.title: Saudi source denies report on Trump U-turn over Hormuz operation
stories.summary: A Saudi source denied a US media report claiming President Donald Trump paused an American military operation to guide ships through the Strait of Hormuz after Saudi Arabia intervened. NBC News had reported that Riyadh refused to allow US forces to use Saudi airspace and bases for the operation.

stories.title: What is the future of the PKK?
stories.summary: An analysis examined the future of the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) as it navigates disarmament talks in Turkey and a shrinking presence in Syria. The developments carry significant implications for regional security across the Middle East.

stories.title: Ukraine fires hundreds of drones at Russia after Moscow threat
stories.summary: Kyiv has intensified its strikes on Russian energy sites in recent weeks.

stories.title: Tanzania: Concerns Grow Over Civic Space Restrictions After Tanzania-Kenya Summit Remarks
stories.summary: The East Africa Law Society raised concerns about remarks made during the Tanzania-Kenya Business Summit held in Dar es Salaam on May 4, 2026. EALS warned the statements may signal coordinated cross-border enforcement actions targeting civic actors across the East African Community.

stories.title: Kenya: Heavy Rainfall to Hit Nairobi and 30 Counties
stories.summary: The Kenya Meteorological Department issued a warning of heavy rainfall expected to affect Nairobi and 30 other counties beginning Thursday evening and continuing through the following week.

stories.title: Germany allocates about 0.55% of GDP to Ukraine, leaving room to increase support – political analyst
stories.summary: A political analyst noted that Germany currently allocates approximately 0.55% of its GDP to support Ukraine. The assessment suggests Berlin has significant room to increase its level of assistance to Kyiv.

stories.title: Middle East war will slow down economic growth in Africa as cost of living crisis soars, IMF warns
stories.summary: The IMF warned that the Middle East war involving Iran is expected to reduce economic growth across Africa by 0.3 percentage points. Rising energy and food prices linked to the conflict put an estimated 20 million people in Africa at risk of food insecurity.

stories.title: Nigeria: How Nigeria Should Respond to the South Africa Xenophobia
stories.summary: Xenophobic violence in South Africa has displaced and harmed Black immigrants, including many Nigerians. Commentators are calling on Nigeria to exercise regional leadership and pursue a diplomatic response to the crisis.

stories.title: Can nuclear power resolve the energy crisis?
stories.summary: The conflict with Iran has prompted several European countries to reconsider nuclear energy as part of their strategic response to energy insecurity. Sweden, Belgium, and Italy are rolling back previous restrictions, while France and the UK are advancing new nuclear projects.

stories.title: Luxembourg MEP is recruiting European Parliament colleagues for June trip to Russia — and meetings with State Duma
stories.summary: A Luxembourg member of the European Parliament is recruiting colleagues for a trip to Russia in June, including proposed meetings with State Duma members. The visit would coincide with the St. Petersburg International Economic Forum on June 3.

stories.title: Rapper Kodak Black due in court in Florida on felony drug charge
stories.summary: Florida rapper Kodak Black, whose legal name is Bill Kahan Kapri, was scheduled to appear in an Orlando court on May 7 on a felony charge of trafficking MDMA. The charge stems from a November incident in which gunshots were allegedly fired near a children's educational building.

stories.title: Christianity under pressure? Israel’s interfaith crisis - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Prof. Michal Bar-Asher Siegal of JPPI discussed the growing strain on Jewish-Christian relations in Israel and the decline of meaningful interfaith dialogue in a conversation hosted by the Times of Israel.

stories.title: When mysticism goes mainstream- with Daniel Matt - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Scholar Daniel Matt discussed what is gained and lost when the Kabbalah, a Jewish mystical tradition historically reserved for an elite few, becomes a mainstream spiritual practice.

stories.title: 75 Gaza doctors, medics in Israeli prisons face torture, abuse
stories.summary: A new report states that 75 Gaza doctors and medical workers remain detained in Israeli prisons, including hospital director Hussam Abu Safiya. Detainees reportedly face torture and medical neglect.

stories.title: Pentagon turns to AI targeting to help troops shoot drones
stories.summary: The Pentagon is deploying AI-powered targeting technology to help troops detect and shoot down drones more quickly. The system can distinguish threats from non-threats, such as birds, faster than human operators.

stories.title: Iranian FA says will meet FIFA to seek World Cup assurances in next few days
stories.summary: The Iranian Football Association announced plans to meet with FIFA in the coming days to seek assurances regarding the 2026 World Cup. Canada, a co-host of the tournament alongside the US and Mexico, denied entry to Iranian football official Mehdi Taj over alleged links to the IRGC.

stories.title: Is the Zabar’s Story A Jewish Story? with David Zabar - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: David Zabar recounted the history of Zabar's, the iconic New York City food store, tracing the family's journey from surviving a pogrom to building a successful business in America.

stories.title: Israel needs long-term Iran strategy before US nuclear deal holds it back for good - analysis
stories.summary: Analysis suggests Israel needs a long-term strategic vision regarding Iran before a potential US nuclear deal constrains its options. Commentators warn that without a plan beyond military action on multiple fronts, years of conflict may yield limited results.

stories.title: UAE to document Iran attacks to support legal bid
stories.summary: The UAE announced the formation of a national committee to document Iran's attacks on its territory in support of a legal action seeking reparations. Major sites including Dubai's Palm development, airports, and energy facilities were among those hit by more than 2,800 Iranian drones and missiles.

stories.title: Norway's Svalbard archipelago, a pawn on Russia's chessboard
stories.summary: Norway's Svalbard archipelago, located near the North Pole, hosts two long-standing Russian settlements within the NATO member's territory. Moscow has shown increasing interest in the strategically located Arctic region.

stories.title: Sudan: Sudan's RSF Paramilitary Group Detains Journalist Adam Issac Minan
stories.summary: The Committee to Protect Journalists called for the immediate release of journalist Adam Issac Minan, who was kidnapped by Sudan's Rapid Support Forces on April 5, 2026, in Kutum, North Darfur state.

stories.title: Kremlin says it has no plans to compensate businesses for losses from internet outages
stories.summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters that Russia has no plans to compensate businesses for losses caused by internet outages. He stated that support measures were not under consideration by the government.

stories.title: The Origins Of Zionism – David Matlow - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: David Matlow, founder of The Herzl Project and owner of the world's largest private collection of Theodor Herzl memorabilia, discussed the origins of Zionism in a Times of Israel interview.

stories.title: Belarus building infrastructure deeper inside territory, Russia may use it later, SBGS spox says
stories.summary: A spokesperson for Ukraine's State Border Guard Service reported that Belarus is constructing infrastructure facilities deeper inside its own territory, away from the Ukrainian border. Officials warned Russia could later use these sites to deploy additional military forces and equipment.

stories.title: Kippahgate: from controversy to the classroom with Alex Sinclair - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Academic Alex Sinclair discussed the controversy surrounding his kippah embroidered with both Israeli and Palestinian flags, which led to his arrest. The kippah was returned with the Palestinian flag removed.

stories.title: Masada: the siege that became a legend - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A Times of Israel feature examined the historical siege of Masada, questioning whether the widely accepted narrative of mass death on the mountaintop is accurate.

stories.title: Moscow mayor reports more than 30 drones shot down approaching city; roughly 100 flights canceled or delayed at Moscow airports
stories.summary: Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin reported that more than 30 drones were shot down approaching the city between midnight and noon on May 7. Approximately 100 flights were canceled or delayed at Moscow airports. Authorities said no casualties or significant damage were reported.

stories.title: Three women connected to IS militants arrested in Australia
stories.summary: Australian authorities arrested three women returning from Syria over alleged links to the Islamic State group. Police are considering terrorism-related charges against the detainees.

stories.title: Africa: South Africa Denies Xenophobia Surge As Fake Videos Fuel Diplomatic Tension Across Africa
stories.summary: South Africa's government condemned the circulation of what it called fake videos and images purportedly showing attacks on foreign nationals. The controversy has fueled diplomatic tensions with several African states over concerns of xenophobic violence.

stories.title: Nigeria: Kingsley Moghalu @63 - Profile of a Visionary Architect of Governance and Economic Transformation
stories.summary: Nigerian economist and former Central Bank deputy governor Kingsley Moghalu marked his 63rd birthday, recognized for his career spanning the United Nations, global finance, and public policy in Nigeria.

stories.title: Australian women linked to ISIS arrested, accused of slavery after Syrian return
stories.summary: Four Australian women and nine children detained in northeast Syria for alleged links to ISIS are set to return to Australia. The Australian government stated it would provide no assistance for their repatriation. The women face accusations of slavery-related offenses.

stories.title: US lifts its 1997 ban on importing Ukrainian weapons — Russia remains only country on list
stories.summary: The United States lifted a 1997 ban on importing Ukrainian weapons, a Cold War-era restriction that had grouped Ukraine with other former Soviet republics. Russia now remains the only country subject to the import prohibition.

stories.title: Pakistan witnessed surge in terrorist incidents post-Marka-i-Haq, DG ISPR says
stories.summary: Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry is currently addressing a press conference. The deputy chief of naval staff (operations), Rear Admiral Shafaat Ali,

stories.title: Nigeria: Hisbah Arrests Seven Men for Alleged Swapping Wives in Bauchi
stories.summary: The Hisbah religious police in Bauchi State's Katagum Zone arrested seven men allegedly linked to the Wuddadu group in Azare for alleged wife-swapping.

stories.title: WHO says cruise ship hantavirus outbreak ‘not the start of a pandemic’
stories.summary: The World Health Organization stated that a deadly hantavirus outbreak on the cruise ship MV Hondius in the Atlantic Ocean is not the start of a pandemic. WHO official Maria Van Kerkhove emphasized the situation is not comparable to Covid-19.

stories.title: Lula arrives at the White House to mend fences with Trump after a year of tariffs and disputes
stories.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva visited the White House on May 7 for a working session with President Donald Trump. It is Lula's first official Washington visit since returning to power in 2023, aimed at easing bilateral tensions over tariffs and diplomatic disputes.

stories.title: Breathe Pakistan: International Renewable Energy Agency official calls for investing in solar infrastructure
stories.summary:
The second day of the second edition of the Breathe Pakistan International Climate Change Conference, organised by DawnMedia, is currently underway in Islamabad.
Despite contributing minimally to glob

stories.title: Roskomnadzor Is Coming for Your Sims
stories.summary: Russia's media regulator Roskomnadzor has filed lawsuits against several major international video game companies. The legal action targets firms that refused to store Russian gamers' personal data on servers located inside Russia.

stories.title: Report: Ukrainian drones hit Russian industrial facility; eyewitnesses say 1 strikes residential building
stories.summary: Perm Krai Governor Dmitry Makhonin confirmed that Ukrainian drones struck an industrial facility in the Perm region. Eyewitness accounts reported that at least one drone hit a residential building in the area.

stories.title: In Zakarpattia region, authorities investigate possibility that forest fire is set on behalf of Russians
stories.summary: Authorities in Ukraine's Zakarpattia region are investigating whether a forest fire in the town of Volovets was deliberately set on behalf of Russia. The probe includes examining whether local residents were recruited to start the blaze.

stories.title: Tensions high in West Bengal after BJP aide shot dead and hundreds arrested
stories.summary: Tensions escalated in the Indian state of West Bengal after a top political aide of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's BJP was shot dead following the party's victory in state legislative elections. Hundreds were arrested as violence erupted after BJP defeated the Trinamool Congress, which had governed the state for 15 years.

stories.title: French far-right leaders quietly meet Israeli, German envoys ahead of run for presidency
stories.summary: French National Rally leaders Marine Le Pen and Jordan Bardella quietly met with Israeli and German ambassadors as the party seeks to distance itself from its historical reputation for antisemitism ahead of a presidential bid.

stories.title: Son of Hamas’s chief negotiator Khalil al-Hayya said killed in IDF strike on Gaza City
stories.summary: Hamas reported that Azzam al-Hayya, son of chief negotiator Khalil al-Hayya, was killed in an Israeli military strike on Gaza City. The group also accused Israel of killing three police officers in separate strikes.

stories.title: Israel says it killed Hezbollah commander in first strike on Beirut since ceasefire
stories.summary: Iran ally Hezbollah has responded to those strikes by firing and launching armed drones towards Israeli soldiers

stories.title: China urged to forge ‘spear’ for cognitive warfare amid great power rivalry
stories.summary: Chinese scholars from Renmin University's Chongyang Institute for Financial Studies urged Beijing to adopt a more assertive approach to cognitive warfare amid great power rivalry. They called for strengthened "cognitive sovereignty" and an improved cognitive warfare system.

stories.title: Somalia's drought fallout worsened by aid cuts and ongoing conflict
stories.summary: Somalia faces a worsening drought that is driving up malnutrition rates, compounded by cuts in humanitarian aid and ongoing armed conflict. Relief organizations are working to prevent another hunger catastrophe.

stories.title: World oil prices drop 5 percent on hopes over US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Global oil prices fell more than five percent amid optimism over ongoing US-Iran negotiations. Brent crude dropped 5.1 percent to $96.06 per barrel, while West Texas Intermediate lost 5.5 percent to $89.87.

stories.title: Eisenkot, Liberman hold ‘lengthy meeting’ agreeing to deepen coordination amid merger reports
stories.summary: Israeli party leaders Gadi Eisenkot and Avigdor Liberman held a lengthy meeting and agreed to deepen coordination between their parties. The talks have fueled speculation about a possible merger ahead of upcoming elections.

stories.title: Propaganda war: The Gen Z team behind Iran’s hit anti-Trump videos
stories.summary: Young Iranian content creators have produced satirical Lego animations depicting U.S. President Donald Trump as a puppet of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, while portraying Iran as a defender of the oppressed. The videos represent a propaganda effort by Tehran in its ongoing conflict with the United States.

stories.title: Superdry co-founder James Holder jailed for eight years for raping woman
stories.summary: Superdry co-founder James Holder, 54, was sentenced to eight years in prison for raping a woman in Cheltenham, England. Holder followed the victim to her flat after a night out and carried out the assault.

stories.title: Russian “Karakurt” missile corvette just got hit at its Caspian Sea base — days after another one was struck in Baltic
stories.summary: A Russian Karakurt-class missile corvette was struck at its Caspian Sea base, days after another vessel of the same class was hit in the Baltic Sea. Russia uses these corvettes to launch long-range strikes against Ukrainian civilian infrastructure.

stories.title: Can Israel's war economy survive its growing global isolation?
stories.summary: Israel's war economy faces growing strain as public opinion shifts in the US and Europe. Dependent on American aid and European trade, Israel confronts mounting pressure from governments and protesters to cut support, including demonstrations outside a BAE Systems facility in Rochester, England.

stories.title: Election monitors note instances of voters in England turned away over ID
stories.summary: European election observers from the Council of Europe recorded instances of voters in England being turned away from polling stations on May 7 due to confusion over photo ID requirements. The issue was not deemed widespread but will be included in the observers' report on the local elections.

stories.title: South Sudan's President Kiir sacks army chief, finance minister in latest reshuffle
stories.summary: JUBA, May 7 - South Sudan's President Salva Kiir has dismissed the country's military chief and a finance minister who had been in post for less than three months, state media reported late on Wednesd

stories.title: Pentagon will ‘never again’ rely on a single AI provider, official says
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Undersecretary Emil Michael announced the Pentagon will no longer rely on a single artificial intelligence provider. He said new agreements with major technology companies reflect a shift toward flexible contracts, amid an ongoing dispute between the department and AI firm Anthropic.

stories.title: USF commander confirms new strike on oil facility in Perm
stories.summary: Robert Brovdi, commander of Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces, confirmed a new drone strike on an oil facility in Perm, Russia. The target is located approximately 1,550 kilometers from the front line.

stories.title: South Africa: A timeline of recurring waves of xenophobic violence
stories.summary: South Africa has experienced recurring waves of xenophobic violence for nearly two decades, from deadly riots in 2008 to the emergence of the Operation Dudula movement. Thousands of foreign nationals have been repeatedly displaced.

stories.title: Miss Israel says Mamdani’s wife shunned her at NYC café
stories.summary: Miss Israel Melanie Shiraz alleged that Rama Duwaji, wife of academic Mahmood Mamdani, shunned her at a New York City café after learning she was Israeli. Shiraz posted a clip of the interaction online.

stories.title: Russia to restrict mobile internet in Moscow on Victory Day, including whitelisted sites and SMS
stories.summary: Russia's Digital Development Ministry announced that mobile internet access in Moscow will be restricted on May 9, Victory Day. The restrictions will also apply to whitelisted websites and SMS services.

stories.title: Thailand, Cambodia pledge to forge lasting peace at Asean meet after border clashes
