stories.summary: Thailand and Cambodia agreed to pursue trust-building measures and establish lasting peace at an ASEAN meeting in the Philippines. The two countries experienced deadly border clashes involving air strikes and artillery exchanges in July and December of the previous year.

stories.title: US to prioritize destruction of Islamist terror groups, Muslim Brotherhood seen as root problem
stories.summary: The US Counterterrorism Strategy identifies Islamist terror groups, particularly those backed by state actors, as ongoing threats. The strategy views the Muslim Brotherhood as a root problem and signals that destroying such groups will be a priority.

stories.title: China pours US$6.1b into Brazil, making it Beijing’s top investment worldwide: report
stories.summary: China invested $6.1 billion in Brazil in 2025 across a record 52 projects, making Brazil Beijing's top global investment destination. The 45% increase in value far outpaced overall foreign investment growth in Brazil, according to the China-Brazil Business Council.

stories.title: South Sudan's President Kiir fires army chief and finance minister
stories.summary: South Sudan's President Salva Kiir dismissed the country's army chief and a finance minister who had been in office for less than three months, continuing a pattern of high-level government reshuffles.

stories.title: Fears of renewed Gaza war as Hamas disarmament talks stall
stories.summary: Israeli media reports indicate that Israel may resume military operations in Gaza due to a deadlock in disarmament negotiations with Hamas. The stalled talks have raised fears of renewed fighting in the territory.

stories.title: Iran denies involvement in Korean ship incident in Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran denied involvement in damage to a South Korean vessel in the Strait of Hormuz, stating that safe passage through the waterway depends on compliance with Iranian regulations.

stories.title: Drones attack one of Russia’s largest oil refineries in Perm again
stories.summary: Perm region Governor Dmitry Makhonin confirmed that drones attacked one of the region's industrial facilities on Thursday, May 7. The strike targeted what is described as one of Russia's largest oil refineries in the Perm area.

stories.title: Israeli settler to go on trial over attack on French nun in Jerusalem
stories.summary: Israeli settler Yona Simcha Schreiber will stand trial for assaulting a 48-year-old French Catholic nun on Mount Zion in Jerusalem. Israel's justice ministry said the charge is assault motivated by hostility toward a religious group. Schreiber resides in a West Bank settlement.

stories.title: Spain awards UN legal expert Francesca Albanese one of its highest civilian honours
stories.summary: The Spanish government awarded UN special rapporteur Francesca Albanese one of its highest civilian honours. The Italian human rights lawyer was recognized for her work documenting alleged violations of international law in Gaza in her role as UN rapporteur on Palestinian territories.

stories.title: After refusing Ukraine’s ceasefire, Russia is now signaling strikes on Presidential Office, Parliament, and embassies in Kyiv on 9 May
stories.summary: After rejecting Ukraine's ceasefire proposal, Russia reportedly signaled plans to strike Kyiv's Presidential Office, Parliament, and foreign embassies on May 9. The EU refused to withdraw its diplomats from the Ukrainian capital.

stories.title: Russian attacks kill 27 before deadline for ceasefire proposed by Kyiv
stories.summary: Russian attacks across eastern Ukraine killed at least 27 people on Tuesday, including 12 in one of the year's deadliest single strikes, hours before a ceasefire deadline proposed by Kyiv. Russia had announced a limited ceasefire for May 8–9 for World War Two commemorations, while Ukraine proposed an open-ended ceasefire starting Wednesday.

stories.title: After killing Hezbollah Radwan commander, will the terror group weaken? - analysis
stories.summary: Israel carried out strikes that killed a commander in Hezbollah's elite Radwan Force in Lebanon. Analysts are debating whether the elimination will have a lasting weakening effect on the group or whether Hezbollah will quickly replace its lost personnel.

stories.title: Israel says it killed Hezbollah commander in first strike on Beirut since ceasefire
stories.summary: Israel confirmed it killed a commander of Hezbollah's elite Radwan force in an airstrike on Beirut, the first Israeli strike on the Lebanese capital since a ceasefire was agreed last month. Israeli forces remain deployed south of the Litani River and continue strikes in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Israel's war priorities sidelined as Trump pushes toward a limited deal with Iran
stories.summary: Washington and Tehran are pursuing a limited agreement rather than a comprehensive peace deal as the Iran conflict threatens global economic stability. Israel is not directly involved in the negotiations, and Prime Minister Netanyahu has resisted subjecting Israel's campaign against Hezbollah to any U.S.-Iran deal.

stories.title: French aircraft carrier pre-positions for possible Hormuz mission
stories.summary: France's aircraft carrier Charles de Gaulle was heading toward the southern Red Sea on Wednesday to pre-position for a potential mission to restore navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. An aide to President Emmanuel Macron said the move signals France's readiness and capability to secure the strategic waterway.

stories.title: War in the Middle East: Satellite imagery reveal scale of damage to US bases in Gulf
stories.summary: A Washington Post investigation using satellite imagery verified by Iranian state-affiliated media revealed damage to at least 228 structures or pieces of equipment at U.S. military sites across the Middle East since the war began.

stories.title: Israel's Noam Bettan dazzles in second Eurovision rehearsal as FBI helps with security
stories.summary: Israeli contestant Noam Bettan performed a well-received second Eurovision rehearsal. The FBI is assisting with security for the event, while Austrian police announced preparations for heightened security measures throughout the week surrounding the contest.

stories.title: United Kingdom votes in key local elections that put Starmer's leadership to the test
stories.summary: British voters went to the polls on May 7 to fill more than 5,000 local council seats across England, six mayoral positions, and seats in the Scottish and Welsh devolved parliaments. Analysts describe the elections as a major test for Prime Minister Keir Starmer's Labour leadership since taking office in July 2024.

stories.title: Fake rumours, real killings: Inside Congo’s deadly health misinformation crisis
stories.summary: In Tshopo province in northeastern Democratic Republic of Congo, health misinformation spread through villages in late 2023, including false rumors about a mysterious illness. The disinformation crisis has been linked to real-world violence and killings in the region.

stories.title: Authorities search home linked to 1996 killing of college student Kristin Smart
stories.summary: Authorities in San Luis Obispo County, California, continued searching a home linked to the 1996 disappearance of 19-year-old college student Kristin Smart, whose remains have never been found. Paul Flores was convicted of her murder in 2022 and sentenced to 25 years to life.

stories.title: Starmer under pressure: 'Many Labour MPs can’t see UK PM leading them into next general election'
stories.summary: British local elections on May 7 are seen as a critical test for Prime Minister Keir Starmer, who faces growing criticism over economic stagnation and the cost of living crisis. Analysts suggest many Labour MPs doubt Starmer can lead the party into the next general election.

stories.title: Amid speculation of merger, Eisenkot and Liberman say they’re ‘deepening cooperation’
stories.summary: Israeli party leaders Gadi Eisenkot of Yashar and Avigdor Liberman of Yisrael Beytenu announced they are deepening cooperation between their parties. Opposition figure Yair Golan urged Eisenkot to join either the Democrats or the Together party led by Bennett and Lapid.

stories.title: Hong Kong seeks more details from WHO on hantavirus outbreak on cruise ship
stories.summary: Hong Kong health authorities contacted the WHO seeking more details on a hantavirus outbreak aboard the cruise ship MV Hondius in the Atlantic. The city's Centre for Health Protection is ramping up prevention efforts against the rare disease strain, which is capable of limited human-to-human transmission.

stories.title: Gold futures set for Hong Kong comeback as mainland China’s appetite for the metal grows
stories.summary: The Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing is planning to relaunch gold futures in coming months to capitalize on growing demand from mainland China. Financial Secretary Paul Chan announced plans to introduce additional gold products and facilities.

stories.title: Bennett-Lapid merger kicks off, Gantz left in the dust: Is this the end of the Netanyahu era?
stories.summary: Israeli politicians Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid have begun a political merger, while Benny Gantz has been sidelined. The realignment is reshaping the opposition landscape and the broader challenge to Prime Minister Netanyahu's leadership.

stories.title: Tech billionaire Chen Tianqiao’s MiroMind halts China services after Meta and Manus saga
stories.summary: MiroMind, the AI startup founded by Chinese tech billionaire Chen Tianqiao, is suspending its MiroThinker services in mainland China, Hong Kong, and Macau. The move reflects a broader trend of globally ambitious Chinese tech firms retreating from the domestic market amid geopolitical tensions.

stories.title: China’s Tongji University punishes top cancer researcher Wang Ping for misconduct
stories.summary: Shanghai-based Tongji University disciplined cancer researcher Wang Ping after finding academic misconduct in a 2025 Nature study. The university determined that 14 of 15 figures in the study, which examined valine deprivation as a cancer treatment, contained problematic data.

stories.title: Ramzi Mallat's Leighton House installation confronts Orientalism
stories.summary: Artist Ramzi Mallat has installed a new work at Leighton House in London, incorporating Syriac evil eye charms to confront themes of Orientalism, protection, and power.

stories.title: The curious case of Shay Gal: Israeli arms company distances itself from Turkey critic
stories.summary: Israel Aerospace Industries distanced itself from Shay Gal after he publicly declared Turkey the 'next Iran.' The company stated that Gal had not been employed there for some time.

stories.title: US-Israel war on Iran leaves Jordan’s Petra nearly empty of tourists
stories.summary: Tourism at Petra, Jordan, has sharply declined as a result of the broader Middle East conflict involving the US and Israel against Iran. Local Jordanians who depend on tourism revenue are facing severe economic losses.

stories.title: Africa: $340 Million UN Nairobi Expansion 'Signals Global Shift Toward Africa'
stories.summary: The United Nations is investing nearly $340 million to expand its headquarters in Nairobi, Kenya, marking one of its largest non-peacekeeping infrastructure investments in Africa. UN Secretary-General António Guterres is expected in Kenya to oversee the project.

stories.title: Driscoll reveals new plan to buy cheaper interceptors with Army-owned IP
stories.summary: U.S. Army Secretary Dan Driscoll outlined a plan to purchase cheaper missile interceptors by breaking down the weapon into subsegments and acquiring each component's intellectual property separately. The approach would give the Army sole ownership of the interceptor design.

stories.title: Sudan RSF paramilitary leader Hemedti says ready to fight for decades
stories.summary: RSF leader Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo (Hemedti) declared that his paramilitary forces are prepared to fight for decades in Sudan's war against the regular army. He warned that RSF fighters remain positioned outside the army-controlled capital, Khartoum.

stories.title: Fire breaks out in Dnipro following Russian attack; factory damaged
stories.summary: A Russian attack on the city of Dnipro, Ukraine, caused a fire and damaged a food processing plant. The blast wave from the strike shattered windows at the factory.

stories.title: US lawmakers demand transparency on Israel's nuclear programme
stories.summary: US lawmakers are demanding transparency regarding Israel's nuclear programme, arguing that maintaining silence on Israel's nuclear arsenal undermines coherent non-proliferation policy across the Middle East.

stories.title: Gulf states derailed Trump's 'Project Freedom' by cutting US access to airspace and bases
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia and Kuwait suspended US access to airspace and military bases, derailing President Trump's 'Project Freedom' plan to ensure ship passage through the Strait of Hormuz. The move forced an abrupt US reversal on the initiative.

stories.title: After cancer revelation, court orders PM to submit sealed medical records in libel case
stories.summary: An Israeli court ordered Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to submit sealed medical records by May 13 in a libel case. The order followed a journalist's request to summon Netanyahu's doctors to testify about his health after a cancer revelation.

stories.title: Israeli army disables rocket-tracking system over Iran intelligence fears
stories.summary: The Israeli army's Home Front Command disabled a rocket-tracking alert system in northern Israeli communities over fears of Iranian intelligence infiltration. The decision has caused distress among residents as hostilities along Israel's northern border continue.

stories.title: Pakistan hopeful about agreement between US and Iran: FO
stories.summary:
Foreign Office (FO) spokesperson Tahir Andrabi said on Thursday that Islamabad was hopeful about an agreement between the US and Iran and was expecting it to happen soon.
He said while responding to a

stories.title: Rubio meets with Pope Leo at the Vatican
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Pope Leo at the Vatican on Thursday. A State Department spokesman described the meeting as reflecting a strong US-Vatican relationship, despite tensions between President Trump and the pope over comments regarding the Iran war.

stories.title: Iran war undermines Dubai economic 'safe haven' appeal
stories.summary: Recent missile and air strikes on the UAE during a ceasefire period have undermined Dubai's reputation as an economic safe haven. The attacks have shaken investor confidence in the emirate's security model amid the broader Iran war.

stories.title: South Sudan's President Kiir fires army chief and finance minister in latest reshuffle
stories.summary: South Sudan's President Salva Kiir fired the country's army chief and a finance minister who had been in office for less than two weeks. The dismissals are part of the latest government reshuffle in Juba.

stories.title: Miriam Adelson honored by IAC with Defender of Am Yisrael award in Los Angeles
stories.summary: The Israeli-American Council honored Miriam Adelson with its Defender of Am Yisrael lifetime achievement award at a Beverly Hills gala. The ceremony coincided with celebrations marking Israel's 78th Independence Day.

stories.title: Russian Union of Journalists expelled from International Federation of Journalists
stories.summary: The International Federation of Journalists expelled the Russian Union of Journalists from its membership. No further details on the specific reasons or timeline were provided in the initial report.

stories.title: Sri Lanka’s former President Chandrika Kumaratunga wishes Vijay on ‘remarkable achievement’
stories.summary: “I recall with pleasure the long and cordial association between Tamil Nadu and Sri Lanka and look forward to our continued friendly relationship under your governance,” said Sri Lanka’s former Presid

stories.title: Austria: Police report 3 dead in shooting in Linz, say no further danger to public
stories.summary: Three people were killed in a shooting in the city of Linz, Austria. Police reported a large presence in the northern part of the city and stated there was no ongoing threat to the public.

stories.title: Israel kills son of Hamas leader Khalil al-Hayya in Gaza strike
stories.summary: Israel killed the son of Hamas leader Khalil al-Hayya in a strike on Gaza. Al-Hayya had accused Israel of undermining efforts to secure the second phase of the Gaza ceasefire deal shortly before the strike.

stories.title: Rubio meets pope in Vatican amid ongoing feud between Trump and Catholic leader
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Pope Leo at the Vatican amid an ongoing feud between President Trump and the Catholic leader. The State Department said they discussed the Middle East situation and reaffirmed the US-Vatican relationship and shared commitment to peace.

stories.title: Iran’s Pezeshkian says he recently met with yet-to-be-seen supreme leader
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian reported meeting Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, the son of the slain former supreme leader, without specifying the exact date. Pezeshkian described Khamenei as humble and sincere; the supreme leader has not been publicly seen.

stories.title: Israeli army disables rocket-tracking system over Iran intelligence fears
stories.summary: The Israeli military disabled a rocket-tracking system in northern Israel over concerns that Iran could exploit the intelligence it provides. Civil officials and emergency responders warned the move leaves northern Israel operationally blind and less protected against missile strikes.

stories.title: South Africa condemns 'fake videos' of alleged xenophobic attacks
stories.summary: South Africa's government condemned what it called fake videos purporting to show xenophobic attacks within the country. Ghana has called on the African Union to dispatch a fact-finding mission to investigate the mounting claims of xenophobia.

stories.title: Chad declares national mourning after deadly Boko Haram ambush
stories.summary: Chad declared national mourning after a Boko Haram ambush near Lake Chad killed two generals. The attack follows a recent Boko Haram assault in the same region that left dozens of people dead.

stories.title: Chad declares three days of national mourning after Boko Haram attack
stories.summary: Chad declared three days of national mourning following a Boko Haram attack that killed two generals in the Lake Chad Basin region on Wednesday. The volatile area has seen repeated jihadist violence.

stories.title: Israel strikes south of Beirut, Salam rules out normalisation
stories.summary: An Israeli strike on a southern suburb of Beirut killed a senior Hezbollah commander on Wednesday night. The attack came ahead of planned Lebanon-Israel talks in Washington next week. Lebanese official Salam ruled out normalisation with Israel.

stories.title: Is Russian oil becoming a lifeline for Southeast Asia?
stories.summary: Southeast Asian governments are increasingly turning to Russian oil, gas, and fertilizer imports as supplies are squeezed by the Iran conflict. The region is resisting EU pressure, treating Russian energy as essential for economic stability.

stories.title: Gulf states derailed Trump's 'Project Freedom' by cutting US access to airspace and bases
stories.summary: Gulf states, led by Saudi Arabia, reportedly derailed the US military plan known as "Project Freedom" to reopen the Strait of Hormuz by denying American forces access to their airspace and bases. Saudi frustration with Washington's announcement of the plan reportedly prompted the decision.

stories.title: Somali pirates abandon hijacked UAE dhow due to dwindling supplies
stories.summary: Somali pirates abandoned the UAE-flagged dhow Fahad-4, which was carrying lemons and had been hijacked in late April. The vessel had been used as a mothership to launch attacks on other ships before dwindling supplies forced the pirates to leave.

stories.title: Venice Biennale targeted by strike action and protests over Israel's involvement
stories.summary: Protests and a 24-hour cultural strike are targeting Israel's participation in the Venice Biennale. A coalition of Italian and international unions and activist groups organized the action, marking the first strike within the prestigious arts festival. Russia's involvement also drew protests.

stories.title: Dharavi, India's largest slum, braces for major redevelopment plan
stories.summary: Dharavi, a densely populated slum in Mumbai housing nearly one million people, is set to undergo a major redevelopment plan. The project aims to build skyscrapers, sanitation systems, parks, schools, and hospitals. However, the required relocation of residents is raising concerns among families who have lived and worked in Dharavi for generations.

stories.title: Iran conducting near-daily prisoner executions in secrecy, say rights groups
stories.summary: Rights groups report that Iran is conducting near-daily prisoner executions in secrecy, with 24 people reportedly killed in March alone. Families are often not informed until after executions have occurred and face harassment and pressure not to speak publicly, compounded by an ongoing internet blackout.

stories.title: Once the city of peace, Geneva sees the United Nations' presence fade
stories.summary: The article examines the declining presence of the United Nations in Geneva, drawing parallels to the League of Nations' departure from the Palais Wilson in 1937 before its dissolution. The city, historically known as a center of international diplomacy, is seeing a reduced role in multilateral affairs.

stories.title: Al-Qaeda-linked fighters in Mali set fire to food trucks
stories.summary: Al-Qaeda-linked fighters in Mali set fire to food trucks as part of an ongoing blockade of roads surrounding the capital, Bamako. The attacks are disrupting supply lines to the city.

stories.title: Ancient Ziggurat of Ur restored in Iraq using traditional methods
stories.summary: Restoration work is underway at the ancient Ziggurat of Ur in southern Iraq, using traditional construction methods to preserve the monumental stepped temple.

stories.title: Rubio meets US pope in bid to ease tensions
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Pope Leo XIV at the Vatican in an effort to ease tensions after President Trump criticized the pope over his comments on the Iran war.

stories.title: Angola and Gabon strengthen ties with new cooperation agreements
stories.summary: Angola and Gabon signed new cooperation agreements following talks between the two nations' leaders. Gabonese President Oligui Nguema said Libreville sought to benefit from Angola's experience in tourism and agriculture as Gabon works to reduce its dependence on oil revenues.

stories.title: Member of Secretive Anti-Censorship Group Flees Russia, Citing FSB Pressure
stories.summary: Sofia Chepik, a member of the secretive Russian anti-censorship group Scarlet Swan, has fled Russia citing pressure from the FSB security service. Scarlet Swan had earlier called for protests against the Russian government's internet restrictions.

stories.title: 'People don't want wars anymore': Inside Lebanon's shifting calculus on Israel
stories.summary: A growing number of Lebanese citizens are reportedly shifting their views on peace with Israel as Hezbollah's influence weakens and war fatigue deepens. Many are beginning to see normalization not as betrayal but as a practical necessity.

stories.title: Why is the US seeking UN help to open Hormuz after undermining it?
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has called on the United Nations to help find a solution for passage through the Strait of Hormuz while peace talks between the US and Iran continue.

stories.title: All Hail the Military
stories.summary: This entry is a series exploring systems of power that sustain militarism. It does not report on a specific news event and contains no summarizable conflict or security development.

stories.title: Drone attacks team of electricians in Dnipropetrovsk region
stories.summary: In the Dnipropetrovsk region of Ukraine, a Russian FPV drone struck a vehicle carrying a team of electricians who were traveling to conduct power-restoration work. The attack targeted civilian infrastructure workers engaged in repair operations.

stories.title: Iran war threatens next harvest, UN official says. Which countries are most at risk?
stories.summary: A UN official warned that the ongoing conflict involving Iran threatens the next agricultural planting season, with the Strait of Hormuz blockaded since joint US-Israeli strikes began in February. Countries already facing fertiliser shortages and surging costs are at heightened risk of food insecurity.

stories.title: Spain's leader Sanchez awards UN's Francesca Albanese Order of Civil Merit
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez awarded the Order of Civil Merit to Francesca Albanese, the UN special rapporteur on Palestine. Albanese had been sanctioned by the US for her work. Sanchez said public responsibility includes a moral obligation not to look away.

stories.title: Polls open in U.K. local elections seen as a verdict on Keir Starmer's leadership
stories.summary: Starmer's center-left Labour Party is bracing for big losses in voting that will choose about 5,000 local councilors and a handful of mayors across England, as well as semi-autonomous parliaments in S

stories.title: The Only Way Is Essex star Jake Hall found dead in Mallorca
stories.summary: Former The Only Way Is Essex star Jake Hall, 35, was found dead at a villa in Mallorca, Spain. He was reportedly found unresponsive with head wounds caused by shards of glass.

stories.title: Private firms can help stop Western sanctions from ‘strangling’ China’s military: general
stories.summary: A senior Chinese military official, Major General Zhang Zhan of the National University of Defence Technology, urged greater private-sector involvement in defence research. He warned that Western sanctions led by the United States and its allies risk "strangling" China's defence innovation efforts in a "grim and complex" situation.

stories.title: The illusion of a sovereign Lebanon: Why past agreements keep collapsing - analysis
stories.summary: Analysis suggests that negotiations with Lebanon's government risk repeating past failures unless Hezbollah's control over state institutions is addressed. Previous agreements have collapsed due to the group's entrenched influence on Lebanese governance and security.

stories.title: Britons set to punish Starmer's Labour in local polls
stories.summary: Millions of British voters cast ballots on Thursday in local and regional elections across the UK. The results are widely expected to deal a significant blow to Prime Minister Keir Starmer's Labour party.

stories.title: India-administered Kashmir launches campaign to fight youth drug addiction
stories.summary: Authorities in India-administered Kashmir have launched a campaign aimed at combating youth drug addiction in the region.

stories.title: UK construction firms face some of sharpest cost rises in nearly 30 years
stories.summary: UK construction firms are facing some of their steepest input cost increases since 1997, according to a recent industry survey. Rising prices for fuel and raw materials are linked to the ongoing war in Iran. Input cost inflation reached its highest level since June 2022, when commodity prices spiked following Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: China says ties with U.S. remain stable ahead of Trump visit despite ‘disruptions’
stories.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met with members of a U.S. bipartisan congressional delegation in Beijing ahead of Donald Trump’s visit to China

stories.title: Daily Quiz | Major events on May 7
stories.summary: The article presents a daily quiz covering major events that occurred on May 7, including birthdays, war scenarios, and other historical happenings. No substantive news content was provided.

stories.title: State indicts man for attacking nun in Jerusalem’s Old City
stories.summary: Israeli authorities indicted a man for attacking a nun in Jerusalem's Old City near King David's Tomb. The suspect, identified as Shreiber, was arrested shortly after the incident, which drew widespread condemnation.

stories.title: Daily Briefing May 7 – Golders Green terror shows rising threat to world Jews
stories.summary: Times of Israel editor David Horovitz discussed the Golders Green terror incident in northwest London as evidence of rising threats to Jewish communities worldwide. He also addressed Trump's deal-making efforts with Iran and Lebanon and Israeli Finance Minister Smotrich's political stance.

stories.title: 'Stop the Game': Irish celebrities urge boycott of Israel match
stories.summary: Irish footballers, musicians, and actors are calling on the Republic of Ireland to boycott upcoming matches against Israel over the war on Gaza. The campaign urges sporting bodies to refuse participation.

stories.title: Gaza health ministry reports nine dead in Israeli strikes
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed at least six people in the Gaza Strip over the past day, according to the Gaza health ministry. Three additional people died from wounds previously sustained in Israeli air strikes.

stories.title: 2,400 hectares of forest burn near Chernihiv region border due to Russian aggression
stories.summary: Approximately 2,400 hectares of forest are burning near the border of Ukraine's Chernihiv region as a result of Russian military activity. Firefighting efforts are unable to fully extinguish the blaze due to the ongoing threat posed by enemy drones in the area.

stories.title: A 26-year-old Russian flew into Argentina to break Milei. He’s not flying out
stories.summary: Argentine authorities arrested 26-year-old Russian national Dmitry Novikov in Lanús, Argentina. Novikov allegedly ran Russia's largest Latin American influence operation in 2024, targeting Argentine President Javier Milei for his support of Ukraine.

stories.title: Doctors Without Borders charity says Israel has ‘manufactured malnutrition crisis’ in Gaza
stories.summary: Médecins Sans Frontières (Doctors Without Borders) accused Israel of manufacturing a malnutrition crisis in Gaza. The organization reported that the crisis has led to increased levels of premature births and higher mortality rates among infants born to malnourished mothers.

stories.title: Spain's leader Sanchez awards UN's Francesca Albanese Order of Civil Merit
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez awarded UN Special Rapporteur on Palestine Francesca Albanese the Order of Civil Merit on May 7, 2026. Sanchez described Albanese as a voice upholding the conscience of the world.

stories.title: UK voters head to the polls in local elections
stories.summary: Voters across England, Scotland, and Wales are casting ballots in local elections across the United Kingdom.

stories.title: Venice Biennale targeted by strike action and protests over Israel's involvement
stories.summary: International and Italian unions and activist groups called a 24-hour cultural strike at the Venice Biennale on Friday to protest Israel's involvement in the event. The Art Not Genocide Alliance organized demonstrations in Venice on May 6, 2026.

stories.title: Hantavirus-hit cruise ship leaves Cape Verde for Canary Islands
stories.summary: The cruise ship MV Hondius, linked to a deadly hantavirus outbreak of the South American Andes strain, departed Praia, Cape Verde, with nearly 150 passengers and crew. The vessel is headed to Spain's Canary Islands as health authorities work to contain the disease.

stories.title: Uganda: Kabale Leaders Clash Over Sovereignty Law As Fears Grow Over Civil Liberties
stories.summary: Political leaders in Uganda's Kabale District are divided over the recently passed Protection of Sovereignty Act, 2026. Critics warn the law could restrict civic freedoms, while supporters argue it is necessary for national regulation and accountability.

stories.title: UniCredit to Sell Part of Russian Subsidiary to UAE Investor
stories.summary: Italian bank UniCredit announced plans to sell part of its Russian subsidiary to a UAE-based investor. The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027 and will result in an estimated $3.5 billion hit to the bank's profits.

stories.title: Doctors Without Borders says Israel has 'manufactured malnutrition crisis' in Gaza
stories.summary: Doctors Without Borders on Thursday accused Israel of having deliberately restricted food and aid in Gaza, creating a “manufactured malnutrition crisis” with particularly devastating impacts on infant

stories.title: Rubio meets Pope Leo at Vatican to defuse tensions with Trump
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Pope Leo at the Vatican for approximately two and a half hours in an effort to defuse tensions stemming from President Trump's attacks on the Catholic leader over the Iran war. Rubio also met with senior Vatican officials, including top diplomat Cardinal Pietro Parolin.

stories.title: Why Beijing wants provinces to find their own ‘productive forces’
stories.summary: Beijing is directing Chinese provinces to develop specialised economic roles rather than simply pursuing overall growth. As planning shifts from the 14th to the 15th five-year plan, the central government is treating provinces as implementation units in a territorial division of labour.

stories.title: Two drones from Russia crash in Latvia, damage oil storage facility
stories.summary: Two drones originating from Russian territory entered NATO member Latvia and crashed, the Latvian army reported on Thursday. One of the drones damaged an oil storage facility in the country.

stories.title: Iran denies ship attack as Trump warns of renewed bombing, eyes deal
stories.summary: Tehran’s embassy in Seoul said it “firmly rejects and categorically denies” allegations that its armed forces were behind a blast aboard the Panama-flagged HMM Namu, which caught fire on May 4

stories.title: Mali's junta leader appoints new army chief of staff following attacks
stories.summary: Mali's junta leader appointed a new chief of the general staff for the armed forces, less than two weeks after a coordinated wave of attacks struck the country. The leadership change signals a military reorganization in response to the security crisis.

stories.title: China announces suspended death sentences for former defence ministers
stories.summary: China announced suspended death sentences for two former defense ministers. The move follows the recent purging of several top officials from China's military leadership.

stories.title: UN: At least 70 civilians killed and over 500 wounded in Ukraine since early May
stories.summary: The United Nations reported that at least 70 civilians have been killed and more than 500 wounded in Ukraine since early May as a result of intensified Russian attacks across the country.

stories.title: Russia strikes Kharkiv residential district as drone attacks escalate
stories.summary: A major Russian drone offensive struck Kharkiv's Novobavarskyi residential district and other Ukrainian cities. The attacks injured civilians and destroyed homes, though Ukraine's air defenses intercepted a number of the incoming drones.

stories.title: Court extends custody of man suspected in two highly publicized rape cases
stories.summary: An Israeli court extended the custody of a man suspected in two high-profile rape cases. Shaylee Atary, whose husband was killed on October 7 while saving her and their baby, alleges the suspect raped her in 2011. He is also accused of raping Naama Shahar in 2022.

stories.title: MSF accuses Israel of manufacturing a malnutrition crisis in Gaza
stories.summary: Médecins Sans Frontières accused Israel of manufacturing a malnutrition crisis in Gaza, stating it identified its first cases of child malnutrition in January 2024, three months after the war began.

stories.title: US reinstates deportation proceedings against Palestinian green-card holder student
stories.summary: The US Board of Immigration Appeals reinstated deportation proceedings against Mohsen Mahdawi, a Palestinian permanent US resident who led anti-war protests at Columbia University. Mahdawi was detained by ICE during a citizenship interview in Vermont in mid-April last year.

stories.title: Why this lifelong Conservative turned on the British establishment | Peter Oborne
stories.summary: British journalist Peter Oborne, a lifelong Conservative, discusses in an interview how the Iraq war set a template for Gaza and criticizes Labour leader Keir Starmer for never condemning Israeli war crimes.

stories.title: South Africa: Kouga Dam Floods Force Gamtoos Valley Residents Out of Their Homes
stories.summary: Flooding from the overflowing Kouga Dam in South Africa's Eastern Cape has forced residents of Gamtoos Valley from their homes. Disaster teams are relocating families to community halls, while Nelson Mandela Bay dams are also filling rapidly.

stories.title: German tourist awarded €1,000 after losing out on sunloungers at Greek hotel
stories.summary: A court in Hanover, Germany, awarded a tourist nearly €1,000 after he and his family were unable to secure sunloungers at a hotel on the Greek island of Kos in 2024. The family reportedly had to lie on concrete despite daily early-morning attempts to find available loungers.

stories.title: Iran war could affect stability of Swiss power supply, authorities say
stories.summary: The Swiss Federal Electricity Commission warned that the US-Israeli war on Iran has created uncertainty about gas availability for the coming winter. In an extreme scenario, the conflict could affect the stability of both European and Swiss electricity supplies.

stories.title: Man to plead guilty in Colorado firebomb attack on pro-Israel demonstrators
stories.summary: Mohamed Sabry Soliman was scheduled to plead guilty on Thursday to murder and other charges stemming from a firebomb attack on a pro-Israel demonstration in Boulder, Colorado, on 1 June 2025. The attack killed one person and injured a dozen others during a rally supporting Israeli hostages in Gaza. Soliman faces up to life in prison without parole.

stories.title: At Least 1 Killed in Belgorod Region Amid Major Ukrainian Drone Barrage Against Russia
stories.summary: At least one person was killed in Russia's Belgorod region during a major Ukrainian drone barrage. The Russian military reported intercepting 347 Ukrainian drones across the country and in annexed Crimea between Wednesday and Thursday.

stories.title: Kenya: Mudavadi - 19 Kenyans Killed in Russia-Ukraine War, 42 Missing
stories.summary: Kenya's Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi revealed that at least 19 Kenyan nationals have been killed in the Russia-Ukraine conflict, with 42 others still missing. Concerns are growing over foreign recruitment of Kenyans into the war.

stories.title: At Least 1 Killed in Belgorod Region Amid Ukrainian Drone Barrage
stories.summary: Russia's military reported intercepting nearly 350 Ukrainian drones across the country and in annexed Crimea between Wednesday and Thursday. At least one person was killed in the Belgorod region during the drone barrage.

stories.title: At Least 1 Killed in Belgorod Region Amid Major Ukrainian Drone Barrage
stories.summary: At least one person was killed in Russia's Belgorod region during a major Ukrainian drone barrage. Russia's military reported intercepting nearly 350 Ukrainian drones across the country and in annexed Crimea between Wednesday and Thursday.

stories.title: Kongsberg Q1 orders more than double, eyes US expansion
stories.summary: Norwegian defense and technology firm Kongsberg reported that its first-quarter orders more than doubled. The company is pursuing expansion into the United States. Recent contracts included a joint selection with Salt Ship Design to deliver a standardized vessel design concept for the Royal Norwegian Navy.

stories.title: Israel says ceasefire void if Hamas won't disarm, Board of Peace tells Palestinians
stories.summary: The US-backed Board of Peace informed Gaza technocratic committee officials that Israel considers itself not bound by ceasefire commitments if Hamas refuses to disarm. The communication was conveyed by High Representative Nickolay Mladenov in a letter obtained by the Times of Israel.

stories.title: Kenya: Court Battle Intensifies As Gachagua Challenges Senate Impeachment Procedure
stories.summary: Former Kenyan Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has escalated his legal challenge against his impeachment by filing new prayers and reliefs in court. His legal team seeks to overturn the Senate impeachment procedure that led to his removal from office.

stories.title: Iran builds proxies, Qatar peddles influence: Decoding Doha's double game - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis examines the differing strategies of Iran and Qatar in the Middle East. Iran is described as operating through proxy forces, while Qatar is characterized as providing financial support, political influence, and legitimacy to various actors in the region.

stories.title: Mali: Separatists Hold Many Malian Soldiers Captive
stories.summary: Separatist groups in Mali are holding many Malian soldiers captive. Many of the soldiers were captured after a joint force of separatists and jihadists overran the military position in the northern city of Kidal.

stories.title: US and Iran explore short-term deal to end fighting
stories.summary: The United States and Iran are exploring a short-term deal to end fighting. Hopes that even a partial agreement could lead to the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz moved financial markets.

stories.title: Iran reviewing US proposal as Trump pressures Tehran for deal
stories.summary: Iran is reviewing the latest US proposal to end hostilities as President Trump threatens renewed bombing if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed. Negotiations between Washington and Tehran continue.

stories.title: Russian forces carry out more than 40 strikes on Chernihiv region border
stories.summary: Russian forces conducted 41 strikes on the border area of Ukraine's Chernihiv region over a 24-hour period, primarily using FPV drones. The attacks caused confirmed destruction and damage to the area.

stories.title: Ministerial panel to vote on bill that would bar citizenship for non-Orthodox converts
stories.summary: An Israeli ministerial panel is set to vote on a bill that would bar citizenship for non-Orthodox converts. Reform movement leaders condemned the proposal, saying it would alienate Diaspora Jews and collapse the bridge between Israel and Jewish communities abroad.

stories.title: Man who attacked nun in Jerusalem indicted for assault with religious hatred motivation
stories.summary: A 36-year-old man named Yona Schreiber was indicted in Jerusalem for assaulting a nun, with prosecutors citing religious hatred as a motivation. Prosecutors are seeking to keep Schreiber in custody through the legal proceedings; the charges carry up to six years in prison.

stories.title: India’s military turns to green energy options as Iran war prompts new strategy
stories.summary: India's military is exploring alternative energy sources, including biogas, green fuels, and solar and wind power, in response to surging oil and gas prices caused by supply disruptions from the Iran war. Analysts say the trend is likely to accelerate among Asian countries heavily dependent on energy imports.

stories.title: Russians strike Kharkiv, fire breaks out, casualties reported
stories.summary: Russian forces launched a drone strike on the Novobavarskyi district of Kharkiv, Ukraine, igniting a fire and causing casualties. The attack targeted a populated area of Ukraine's second-largest city.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: Iran denies ship attack as Trump warns of renewed bombing, eyes deal
stories.summary: Iran denied responsibility for a blast aboard the Panama-flagged vessel HMM Namu, with Tehran's embassy in Seoul categorically rejecting allegations its armed forces were involved. Meanwhile, President Trump warned of renewed bombing against Iran while simultaneously pursuing a diplomatic deal.

stories.title: Irish footballers and celebrities urge boycott of Israel matches
stories.summary: An Irish campaign group and prominent footballers and celebrities are urging a boycott of Israel's matches in the UEFA Nations League, citing Israel's conduct in the war on Gaza.

stories.title: Iran's president says he recently met with the supreme leader
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said he recently met with Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, who had suffered severe wounds at the start of the US-Israeli war on Iran. Pezeshkian described the meeting as humble and deeply cordial.

stories.title: Turkiye unveils its first intercontinental ballistic missile: What we know
stories.summary: Turkey unveiled its first intercontinental ballistic missile, the Yildirimhan, which has a reported range of 6,000 km, a maximum speed of Mach 25, and a payload capacity of 3,000 kg.

stories.title: 'Time to say goodbye': Judge releases Epstein's alleged 'suicide note'
stories.summary: A US judge has released a purported suicide letter written by Jeffrey Epstein, dated weeks before he was found dead in his prison cell. Separately, Swiss health authorities are working to trace contacts of a Swiss man being treated for a human-to-human strain of hantavirus after he traveled freely while infected.

stories.title: More than 50,000 pupils expected to strike over German rearmament policy
stories.summary: Organisers of a nationwide school strike in Germany expect more than 50,000 pupils to boycott classes on Friday to protest the government's rearmament policy. Students aim to oppose what they describe as policies that could turn young Germans into "cannon fodder," despite threats of penalties from education authorities.

stories.title: France's far-right Le Pen and Bardella court Israel, Germany envoys ahead of presidential vote
stories.summary: France's far-right National Rally leaders Marine Le Pen and Jordan Bardella have met with the ambassadors of Germany and Israel in recent months. The outreach is part of the party's effort to build diplomatic credibility ahead of next year's French presidential elections.

stories.title: Can Asian economies cope with the fallout from the Iran war?
stories.summary: Asian economies are facing rising fuel costs, inflation, and debt pressures linked to the fallout from the war on Iran, raising questions about their ability to cope with the economic disruption.

stories.title: AI ‘blueprint’ coming soon to NGA to help ‘operationalize’ GEOINT
stories.summary: Lt. Gen. Michelle Bredenkamp, the new director of the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, announced that an AI "blueprint" will soon be released to help operationalize geospatial intelligence. In her first major speech leading NGA, she also revealed the agency has established a new Rapid Capabilities Office to accelerate integration of commercial technology.

stories.title: Africa sees winners and losers as Iran war pushes up oil prices
stories.summary: Several African countries have sought financial assistance amid economic uncertainty driven by rising oil prices caused by the war on Iran. The conflict is creating both winners and losers across the continent.

stories.title: South Africa: Nelson Mandela Bay Issues Flood Warning Amid Hazardous Conditions
stories.summary: The Nelson Mandela Bay Municipality in South Africa issued a flood warning as heavy rainfall caused widespread flooding and hazardous conditions across the metro. The Disaster Management Centre urged residents, motorists, and pedestrians to exercise extreme caution.

stories.title: Motorbike gunmen kill BJP political aide in India's West Bengal
stories.summary: Gunmen on motorbikes shot and killed Chandranath Rath, 41, a close aide of West Bengal BJP chief Suvendu Adhikari, near his home in Kolkata on Wednesday night. The killing came days after the BJP won its first-ever state election victory in West Bengal, securing 207 of 294 assembly seats.

stories.title: Uganda: Uganda's Sickle Cell Patients At Risk As Asthma Goes Undetected
stories.summary: A 16-year-old sickle cell patient in Uganda was treated for two weeks for a suspected chest infection that did not respond to antibiotics. Diagnostic tests, including a chest X-ray and blood work, found no abnormalities, raising concerns that undetected asthma may be putting sickle cell patients at risk.

stories.title: Breathe Pakistan: Envoy notes melting glaciers ‘shared vulnerability’ for countries like Nepal, Pakistan
stories.summary: At the Breathe Pakistan International Climate Change Conference in Islamabad, diplomats highlighted the shared vulnerability of countries like Nepal and Pakistan to melting glaciers. Despite contributing minimally to global emissions, Pakistan remains among the world's most climate-vulnerable nations.

stories.title: Nigeria: Court Convicts Former Minister of Fraud
stories.summary: A Federal High Court in Abuja, Nigeria, convicted former Power Minister Saleh Mamman on 12 counts of fraud and money laundering. The charges were brought by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC).

stories.title: Missile strike on Merefa in Kharkiv region: Death toll climbs to eight
stories.summary: The death toll from a May 4 missile strike on Merefa in Ukraine's Kharkiv region has risen to eight after a seriously wounded man died in hospital. The town is located south of Kharkiv city.

stories.title: Appeals court overturns murder conviction of man who killed girlfriend, orders retrial
stories.summary: A Hong Kong appellate court overturned the murder conviction of Law Wai-man, who was found guilty of killing his girlfriend Lau Lee-chi in 2019. The Court of Appeal ruled that the trial judge failed to properly direct the jury to consider the defendant's violent personality traits and ordered a retrial.

stories.title: Trump’s Europe pullback could open new doors for Israel - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion analysis suggests that the Trump administration's pullback from Europe could create new strategic opportunities for Israel. The shift is reportedly based on a broad U.S. assessment of future challenges and risks.

stories.title: A growing number of US Muslims run for political office in 2026
stories.summary: A growing number of Muslim Americans are running for political office in the 2026 US midterm elections at federal, state, and local levels. This represents a significant increase compared to a decade ago, when Muslim candidacies were far less common.

stories.title: Did Saudi Arabia force Trump to pause Hormuz 'Project Freedom'?
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia reportedly threatened to ban US military aircraft from its airspace and deny access to its bases if the US proceeded with 'Project Freedom' to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The threat reportedly forced President Trump to pause the operation.

stories.title: Did Saudi Arabia force Trump to pause Hormuz 'Freedom' project?
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia reportedly threatened to bar the U.S. military from its airspace and bases, forcing President Trump to pause his "Project Freedom" plan to escort vessels through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: How China Is Winning the Global AI Race
stories.summary: An analysis argues that advanced U.S. artificial intelligence models are too costly for much of the world, giving China a competitive advantage in the global AI race. The high price of cutting-edge American AI technology is limiting its adoption in many countries.

stories.title: Marka-i-Haq: ISPR says any hostile design against Pakistan will be countered with greater strength, resolve
stories.summary: Pakistan's military media wing, ISPR, warned that any hostile design against the country would be met with 'even greater strength, precision and resolve.' The statement marked the anniversary of last year's military conflict with India, which Pakistan has dubbed 'Marka-i-Haq' (Battle of Truth).

stories.title: Russia’s economy slows as war costs mount, budget deficit widens, and rate cuts near their limit
stories.summary: Russia's economy is showing signs of strain after five years of full-scale war in Ukraine, with a widening budget deficit, limited room for further interest rate cuts, and accumulating systemic problems. While some indicators such as low unemployment and a strong ruble appear positive, analysts note they conceal underlying vulnerabilities.

stories.title: Rwanda: Kagame Congratulates PSG On Reaching Champions League Final
stories.summary: Rwandan President Paul Kagame congratulated Paris Saint-Germain after the French football club secured a place in the UEFA Champions League final. Rwanda has a longstanding sponsorship partnership with PSG.

stories.title: Why is Israel concerned over a possible US-Iran deal?
stories.summary: Israeli media coverage reveals growing concern that a potential U.S.-Iran agreement could strengthen Tehran's position and impose restrictions on Israel's military operations. The worry reflects broader Israeli anxieties about being sidelined in the negotiations.

stories.title: Local elections across UK test Starmer as Reform UK eyes major gains
stories.summary: UK voters cast ballots on Thursday, May 7, in local and devolved elections across the country. The polls are seen as a major test for Prime Minister Keir Starmer's Labour government, with the Reform UK party expected to make significant gains.

stories.title: Rubio to meet Pope Leo as Trump keeps up attacks on pontiff
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Pope Leo at the Vatican on Thursday amid tensions, as President Trump has continued disparaging attacks on the pontiff over the Iran war. The encounter was described as potentially fraught given the ongoing public disagreements.

stories.title: KP PDMA directs deputy commissioners to take precuationary measures ahead of heatwave
stories.summary: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Provincial Disaster Management Authority directed all deputy commissioners to take precautionary measures ahead of a heatwave expected from May 8 to 10. Temperatures may reach 43–47°C in districts including Dera Ismail Khan, Tank, and Bannu.

stories.title: Israeli soldier pictured desecrating Virgin Mary statue in Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli soldier was photographed placing a cigarette in the mouth of a Virgin Mary statue in the Christian village of Debel in southern Lebanon. The Israeli military said it would discipline the soldier involved.

stories.title: Israeli military investigates soldier's act against Virgin Mary statue in Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military is investigating a soldier who was photographed placing a cigarette in the mouth of a Virgin Mary statue in Lebanon. This marks the second incident targeting a Christian religious figure in the country within weeks.

stories.title: Russia Tells Foreign Embassies in Kyiv to Evacuate as It Warns of ‘Retaliatory’ Strikes
stories.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry warned foreign embassies in Kyiv to evacuate, citing planned retaliatory strikes on the Ukrainian capital. Moscow said it would target Kyiv if Ukrainian attacks disrupted annual Victory Day celebrations on May 9.

stories.title: Russia Tells Foreign Embassies to Evacuate Kyiv as It Warns of ‘Retaliatory’ Strikes
stories.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry warned foreign embassies to evacuate Kyiv, stating that Russia would target the Ukrainian capital with retaliatory strikes if Ukrainian attacks on Saturday disrupted annual Victory Day celebrations in Russia.

stories.title: Russian attacks cause new power outages in frontline regions, says Ukrenergo
stories.summary: Ukraine's national grid operator Ukrenergo reported that Russian attacks as of the morning of May 7 have caused power outages affecting consumers in the Donetsk, Dnipropetrovsk, Zaporizhzhia, Kharkiv, and Sumy regions.

stories.title: Novelist JM Coetzee declines to attend Jerusalem writers festival over ‘genocidal campaign in Gaza’
stories.summary: Nobel laureate and South African novelist J.M. Coetzee declined an invitation to the Jerusalem International Writers Festival, citing Israel's military campaign in Gaza. He communicated his decision in a letter to the festival's artistic director.

stories.title: Hong Kong restaurants can apply from May 18 to become dog-friendly venues
stories.summary: Hong Kong restaurants can apply from May 18 to June 8 for licences to admit dogs under a new scheme, with the first designated venues expected to welcome pets from July. The Food and Environmental Hygiene Department will cap applications at 1,000 restaurants in the first phase.

stories.title: Dubai hotel occupancy projected to fall to 10 percent due to Iran war, report says
stories.summary: Hotel occupancy in Dubai is projected to plummet to 10 percent in the second quarter of 2026, down from 80 percent before the Iran war began in late February. Moody's Analytics described the decline as an effective shutdown of large parts of the hospitality sector, according to the Wall Street Journal.

stories.title: Somalia: Racing to Reverse the Hunger Tide
stories.summary: The World Food Programme warned that Somalia faces another potential hunger catastrophe as humanitarian needs surge and funding declines. Four years after a major donor mobilization averted famine, drought and resource shortfalls are again threatening the Horn of Africa nation.

stories.title: Palestine Coalition files complaint against London police chief
stories.summary: The Palestine Coalition filed a formal complaint against Metropolitan Police Commissioner Mark Rowley in London. The group is demanding he retract certain accusations and issue a full public apology.

stories.title: Inspector failed to spot illegal alterations, Hong Kong fire probe hears
stories.summary: A Hong Kong public inquiry into a deadly housing estate fire heard that a building inspector failed to conduct a site visit and mistook illegal alterations to emergency staircases for protective measures. Senior maintenance surveyor Nick Yung Siu-lun admitted basing his assessment solely on documents.

stories.title: Junta leader Assimi Goita target of April attacks, Malian army says
stories.summary: Mali's military confirmed that last month's coordinated attacks in the country targeted junta leader Assimi Goita. Separately, allied Burkina Faso banned French television channel TV5 Monde over allegations of disinformation.

stories.title: What are US proposals to end war, and will Iran agree to them?
stories.summary: Iran says it is reviewing a US proposal to end the US-Israeli war against it, a conflict that has triggered a global crisis. The outcome of Tehran's deliberations remains uncertain.

stories.title: Kumanjayi Little Baby: Advocates say five-year-old’s death ‘should not be politicised’ as hundreds gather at vigils
stories.summary: Hundreds gathered at vigils across Australia to mourn five-year-old Warlpiri girl Kumanjayi Little Baby, whose body was found in Alice Springs. Advocates and the national body representing First Nations children called for an end to the politicisation of her alleged murder.

stories.title: New Zealand expands sanctions against Russia
stories.summary: On May 7, New Zealand's government imposed new sanctions on 20 Russian individuals and entities for their support of Russia's war against Ukraine. The move expands New Zealand's existing sanctions regime targeting those involved in the conflict.

stories.title: WHO warns of more hantavirus cases in 'limited' outbreak
stories.summary: The World Health Organization warned on May 7 that additional hantavirus cases may emerge but expects the outbreak to remain limited if precautions are taken. The alert followed the deaths of three cruise ship passengers from the disease.

stories.title: Israeli army disables Hezbollah rocket tracking system in north
stories.summary: Israel's military disabled a key Hezbollah rocket tracking system used by northern local authorities during attacks. The system was cut off over concerns that data could be leaked to Iran.

stories.title: Reopening strait of Hormuz would have limited impact on cargo flows, says Maersk
stories.summary: Maersk CEO Vincent Clerc said reopening the Strait of Hormuz would have a "limited impact" on cargo flows, as the shipping industry contends with sharply higher energy costs from the conflict. Maersk's fuel bill has nearly doubled, adding up to $500 million in monthly costs, which the company has passed on to customers through higher freight rates.

stories.title: Liberia: Boakai Sends War Crimes, Anti-Corruption Court Bills to Legislature
stories.summary: Liberian President Joseph Boakai formally submitted draft legislation to establish a Special War Crimes Court and a National Anti-Corruption Court. Both bills have been forwarded to the National Legislature for consideration.

stories.title: Trump takes another U-turn on Iran
stories.summary: The article references President Trump reversing his position on Iran policy, though specific details of the latest shift were not provided in the available text.

stories.title: Israeli strikes on Lebanon's Nabatieh kill one person
stories.summary: Israeli warplanes and drones struck Nabatieh in southern Lebanon on Wednesday, killing one person and injuring several others. The strikes destroyed two residential buildings near the Evangelical School and cut the main road to Nabatieh al-Fawqa.

stories.title: India loses information war to country that wasn't technically allowed online
stories.summary: During the May 2025 India-Pakistan conflict, Pakistan waged an effective information warfare campaign on social media despite limited internet infrastructure. The article examines how both sides used platforms like X to amplify favorable narratives and suppress damaging ones during the hostilities.

stories.title: Kimi developer Moonshot AI valued at US$20b as it navigates China’s new IPO rules
stories.summary: Chinese AI start-up Moonshot AI, developer of the Kimi chatbot, raised about $2 billion in a new funding round led by Long-Z Investments and Meituan's venture arm, boosting its valuation to over $20 billion. The Beijing-based company has raised a total of $3.9 billion over the past six months.

stories.title: As new Holocaust memorial stone laid in Berlin, relative says plaque serves as substitute for grave
stories.summary: A new Holocaust memorial 'stumbling block' stone was laid in Berlin for Nazi victim Johanna Berger by project initiator Gunter Demnig. Berger's great-nephew said the plaque serves as a substitute for a grave and brings the family's history to a certain conclusion.

stories.title: Vladimir Putin Is Much Weaker Than You Think
stories.summary: An analysis assesses that Russian President Vladimir Putin's strategic position is weaker than widely perceived. The piece argues that Putin, long known for outmaneuvering adversaries, is facing diminishing room for maneuver.

stories.title: Over half of Israeli adults are overweight or obese, Knesset Health Committee told
stories.summary: The Knesset Health Committee was told that over half of Israeli adults are overweight or obese, with 31.4% of seventh graders also overweight. Officials attributed the problem to high medication costs, inadequate health services in low-income areas, and insufficient educational materials in Arab and Ethiopian communities.

stories.title: DRC leader Tshisekedi hints at possible rule beyond second term amid eastern war
stories.summary: DRC President Felix Tshisekedi suggested he may seek a third term and hinted at potentially delaying the presidential election scheduled for 2028 due to ongoing conflict in the country's eastern regions. Tshisekedi, in power since 2019, is constitutionally limited to two five-year terms under current DRC law.

stories.title: France resumes genocide probe against Rwanda ex-president's widow
stories.summary: A French court on Wednesday ordered the resumption of an investigation into Agathe Habyarimana, widow of former Rwandan president Juvenal Habyarimana, over alleged complicity in the 1994 genocide. Investigating magistrates had dismissed the case last year citing insufficient evidence. The probe, which began in France in 2007, will now continue.

stories.title: Burkina Faso junta secretly detained journalist and others, advocacy group says
stories.summary: Reporters Without Borders reported that Burkina Faso's military authorities secretly detained and abused investigative journalist Atiana Serge Oulon and dozens of others at a makeshift facility in the capital. Oulon, editor of the newspaper L'Événement, was taken from his home by armed men in civilian clothes in June 2024.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: Iran reviewing peace proposal as Trump says a deal ‘very possible’
stories.summary: The US and Iran have offered conflicting messages over the likelihood of a deal being reached imminentlyHere are the latest pictures from the Dahiyeh neighbourhood of southern Beirut, where rescue wor

stories.title: Rubio set to meet Pope Leo in bid to ease tensions after Trump’s criticism of the pontiff - Europe live
stories.summary: Relations between the Vatican and Washington are increasingly fraught after the US president lashed out at the pope over his criticism of the war in IranEarlier today, Pope Leo welcomed Poland’s prime

stories.title: 2 former Chinese defence ministers handed suspended death sentences
stories.summary: Two former Chinese defence ministers, Wei Fenghe and Li Shangfu, received suspended death sentences after being found guilty of corruption by a military court. Wei was convicted of accepting bribes, while Li was convicted of both accepting and offering bribes. Both were previously expelled from the Communist Party in 2024.

stories.title: DR Congo president hints at extending his term and delaying polls
stories.summary: Democratic Republic of Congo President Félix Tshisekedi indicated he would accept a third presidential term if the public supports it, despite being constitutionally due to step down in 2028. His comments have raised concerns about a potential delay to scheduled elections.

stories.title: China seeks improved US ties and ‘harmony’, FM Wang Yi tells visiting American senators
stories.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi told visiting US Senator Steve Daines that Beijing hoped to “truly stabilise and improve” Sino-American ties, a week before a highly anticipated summit between Xi Jinp

stories.title: Islamic State-linked women arrive home in Australia from Syria
stories.summary: A group of nine women and children has landed in Melbourne while another woman and her child arrived in Sydney.

stories.title: Powerful US utilities secretly fund ‘grassroots’ groups to sway cities away from switch to public power
stories.summary: As communities push for publicly owned electricity, private utilities may be deploying dark money and local front groups to stop themThe utility industry is quietly dispatching a network of front grou

stories.title: China woman fired due to husband’s rival firm job receives US$101,000 for unjust dismissal
stories.summary:
A Shanghai company has been ordered to pay a woman employee 690,000 yuan (US$101,000) for illegally firing her because her husband works for a rival firm.
Xuhui District People’s Court made the ruling

stories.title: Air Defense Forces shoot down 92 of 102 Russian drones
stories.summary: Ukraine's Air Defense Forces intercepted 92 of 102 Russian drones launched against the country between the evening of May 6 and the following day. Ten drones were not successfully shot down during the barrage.

stories.title: Hamas official confirms killing of leader’s son in Gaza City
stories.summary: Hamas official Basim Naim confirmed that Azzam al-Hayya, son of Hamas political bureau chief Khalil al-Hayya, was killed in an Israeli airstrike on Gaza City. He is the fourth of al-Hayya's sons to be killed by Israeli attacks, including one killed in a strike in Doha, Qatar.

stories.title: US reinstates deportation proceedings against Palestinian green-card holder student
stories.summary: The United States has reinstated deportation proceedings against Mohsen Mahdawi, a Palestinian green-card holder and Columbia University student. Mahdawi, a pro-Palestine activist who led anti-war protests at Columbia, was previously detained for two weeks during his citizenship interview.

stories.title: Taiwan warns of China 'maneuvering' ahead of Trump-Xi summit
stories.summary: Taiwan warned that China may be maneuvering diplomatically ahead of an upcoming summit between President Trump and President Xi Jinping in Beijing. Taipei said it is closely monitoring for any shifts in U.S. policy regarding Taiwan.

stories.title: What is China’s anti-sanctions law and how does it work?
stories.summary: China invoked its 2021 anti-sanctions law for the first time, ordering the blocking of U.S. sanctions targeting five Chinese oil refineries. The law was designed to counter foreign sanctions that Beijing considers unjustified.

stories.title: Israeli soldier mocks Virgin Mary statue in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: An image of an Israeli soldier placing a cigarette in a Virgin Mary statue's mouth in southern Lebanon went viral. The incident followed a previous episode weeks earlier in which a statue of Jesus was bludgeoned in the same region.

stories.title: Latvian police debunk fake claim that Ukrainian drone hit passenger train
stories.summary: Latvia's State Police debunked online claims that a Ukrainian drone struck a passenger train on the Rīga–Daugavpils line on May 5. Authorities said the fire was likely caused by engine damage, not a drone strike.

stories.title: South Africa: Floods Smash Gqeberha As 2,000 Flee to Shelters
stories.summary: Severe flooding struck the city of Gqeberha in South Africa's Eastern Cape, forcing approximately 2,000 residents into 25 emergency shelters. The provincial health department closed a local clinic after storm water flooded the facility, and humanitarian organization Gift of the Givers issued urgent appeals for food and blankets.

stories.title: Rubio faces challenge in Pope Leo meeting after Trump's criticism over Iran
stories.summary: America's top diplomat, Marco Rubio, will meet the first US pope, Leo XIV, on Thursday, seeking to ease Washington-Vatican tensions while also promoting President Donald Trump's agenda. The US secreta

stories.title: US Rubio seeks to ease tensions with US pope after Trump's attacks
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is heading to the Vatican and Italy on a fence-mending visit after President Donald Trump’s broadsides against Pope Leo XIV and the U.S.-Israeli war in Iran have alie

stories.title: Trump sees swift end to war as Iran reviews US peace proposal
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump predicted a swift end to the war with Iran as Tehran considered a US peace proposal that sources said would formally end the conflict while leaving unresolved key US demands

stories.title: UK voters cast ballots in elections expected to deal blow to Starmer
stories.summary: Millions of British voters cast their ballots on Thursday in local and regional elections that are expected to ​deal a huge blow to Prime Minister Keir Starmer's Labour Party and renew questions over

stories.title: War update: 157 clashes on front lines, most battles reported in Pokrovsk and Huliaipole sectors
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Forces recorded 157 combat clashes with Russian forces along the front lines on May 6. The heaviest fighting was reported in the Pokrovsk and Huliaipole sectors.

stories.title: What to know about hantavirus, the illness linked to a cruise ship outbreak
stories.summary: A hantavirus outbreak aboard a cruise ship has killed three passengers and sickened others. The rodent-borne virus typically spreads through inhalation of contaminated rodent droppings rather than person-to-person transmission. Global health officials say the risk to the general public remains low.

stories.title: Argentina probes link to deadly hantavirus outbreak on Atlantic cruise
stories.summary: Argentine officials are investigating whether their country is the source of the hantavirus outbreak on an Atlantic cruise that departed from Argentina for Antarctica. Argentina is experiencing a surge in hantavirus cases, which local researchers link to climate change. The WHO consistently ranks Argentina as having Latin America's highest incidence of the disease.

stories.title: Indonesia posts fastest first-quarter growth in 3 years, but headwinds loom
stories.summary: Indonesia’s economy grew 5.6 per cent during the first quarter of 2026, its fastest pace in more than three years, but analysts warn that the coming months will pose significant tests for Southeast As

stories.title: Iran’s stance on US war negotiations explained
stories.summary: Iran has outlined its position on ongoing war negotiations with the United States. Tehran's approach to the diplomatic process reflects its broader strategic considerations amid the conflict.

stories.title: Iran accuses US of ceasefire breach after ships, Hormuz struck
stories.summary: Iran accused the United States of violating their ceasefire agreement after strikes were reported in several areas in and around the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Trump ramps up pressure as Iran reviews US peace proposal
stories.summary: Iran is reviewing a new US proposal aimed at ending the conflict, with discussions focusing on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and addressing Tehran's nuclear program. President Trump has ramped up pressure on Iran to accept terms.

stories.title: Trump ramps up pressure on Tehran amid ongoing talks
stories.summary: Tehran is reviewing a new American proposal aimed at ending the conflict, while President Trump pressures Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and limit its nuclear program. Diplomatic talks between the US and Iran are ongoing.

stories.title: Trump says Iran deal 'very possible' as Israel bombs Beirut
stories.summary: President Trump suggested an Iran deal is "very possible" as diplomatic efforts continue. Meanwhile, an Israeli airstrike on Beirut killed a commander of Hezbollah's elite Radwan Force.

stories.title: Cruise ship with hantavirus outbreak heads to Spain's Canary Islands after 3 are evacuated
stories.summary: Two hantavirus patients and one suspected case were evacuated Wednesday from the cruise ship at the center of the deadly outbreak. The vessel then departed Cape Verde for Spain's Canary Islands with nearly 150 people on board, all isolated in their cabins.

stories.title: Antisemitism has become ‘almost fashionable’ among Australians, Jillian Segal tells royal commission
stories.summary: On its fourth day of public hearings, royal commission into antisemitism also hears Jewish Australians have been pressured to resign and verbally abusedGet our breaking news email, free app or daily n

stories.title: Britons set to punish Starmer's Labour in local polls
stories.summary: Polling stations opened Thursday across the United Kingdom for local elections expected to deliver significant losses for Prime Minister Keir Starmer's Labour Party. Opinion polls predict poor results for Labour, potentially intensifying calls for Starmer to resign or face a party leadership challenge amid rising support for hard-right and left-wing populist movements.

stories.title: Stitching lives back together for Central African Republic's child soldiers
stories.summary: In Bria, in eastern Central African Republic, former child soldiers aged 14 to 17 are learning to sew as part of reintegration efforts after being recruited by armed groups. The diamond-rich eastern region of the CAR has been devastated by years of armed conflict involving multiple militias.

stories.title: Rwanda, Botswana sign six cooperation deals
stories.summary: Rwanda and Botswana signed six cooperation agreements covering aviation, tourism, education, transport, and agriculture during a visit by Rwandan President Paul Kagame. The visit was among the first state visits hosted by Botswana's President Boko since taking office.

stories.title: South Sudan: MSF Forced to Close Lankien Hospital After 31 Years
stories.summary: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) has permanently closed its hospital in Lankien, Jonglei State, South Sudan, after the facility was bombarded on February 3. The closure ends 31 years of continuous medical support to the community. MSF called for an independent investigation into the attack.

stories.title: Planes carrying IS-linked family members land in Australia, with police expected to make arrests
stories.summary: Group of 13 women and children left Syria for Australia on Wednesday, with authorities saying some adults may be chargedGet our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcastThirteen women and ch

stories.title: Australia to tour Pakistan for 3-match ODI series beginning on May 30
stories.summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board announced that Australia's men's cricket team will tour Pakistan for a three-match ODI series. The first match is scheduled for May 30 at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium, with the remaining two matches in Lahore on June 2 and 4.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones target Russia’s main army logistics hub—days before Putin’s Victory parade
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones targeted the 200-hectare Nara complex in Russia, the Defense Ministry's primary logistics hub for distributing military cargo to armed forces. The strikes came just days before President Putin's Victory Day parade.

stories.title: Israel says it coordinated delivery of rat pesticides to Gaza to counter infestation
stories.summary: Israel coordinated the delivery of hundreds of cartons of specialized poisons and 20 tons of pesticide to Gaza through the U.S.-led Coordination Center. The effort targets a rodent infestation worsened by warm weather and sewage conditions in tent cities.

stories.title: Britons on hantavirus-hit ship to be asked to isolate back in UK for 45 days
stories.summary: Two British nationals who left MV Hondius before outbreak was detected are already self-isolating at home, say officialsWhat is hantavirus?British passengers onboard a cruise ship hit with a deadly ou

stories.title: Rubio arrives at Vatican to meet Pope Leo amid Trump attacks
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio traveled to the Vatican to meet Pope Leo. Vatican Secretary of State Cardinal Pietro Parolin confirmed the meeting was requested by the American side, amid tensions between the Trump administration and the papacy.

stories.title: Russian army kills three residents of Donetsk region and injures six others
stories.summary: The Russian army killed three civilians and wounded six others in the Donetsk region of Ukraine over a 24-hour period on May 6, according to local authorities.

stories.title: Iran releases video said to show US drone shot down over Hormuz
stories.summary: Iranian state media released video footage purportedly showing the wreckage of a U.S. drone that Iran claims it shot down over the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Dueling Victory Day ceasefires for war in Ukraine collapse almost immediately
