stories.title: UK PM Starmer says some pro-Palestinian marches could be banned, cites intifada chants
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer said some pro-Palestinian marches could be banned, particularly those featuring calls for intifada. The remarks followed a rise in antisemitic incidents, including a stabbing attack in the north London suburb of Golders Green.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: A Middle East Eye briefing highlighted intensifying pressure on Iran, continued violence in Lebanon, and rising geopolitical strain. Air defense activity in Israel, new U.S. sanctions on Iranian-linked networks, and maritime disruptions were noted. Diplomatic signals between Washington and Tehran remained mixed amid ongoing military activity.

stories.title: Twenty-four companies join private air defense initiative
stories.summary: Twenty-four Ukrainian companies from regions including Kharkiv, Odesa, Kyiv, Poltava, and Zakarpattia have joined a private air defense initiative aimed at bolstering Ukraine's defensive capabilities.

stories.title: China’s UN Envoy: Hormuz closure will dominate Trump-Xi talks
stories.summary: China's UN Ambassador Fu Cong stated that maintaining the ceasefire and reopening the Strait of Hormuz are urgent priorities. He indicated that the Hormuz closure is expected to dominate upcoming talks between President Trump and President Xi.

stories.title: 2026 already this century’s worst year for the press: RSF Press Freedom Index
stories.summary: Reporters Without Borders' 2026 Press Freedom Index declared this year the worst for press freedom since the index began 25 years ago. For the first time, over half of the world's countries fall into "difficult" or "very serious" categories for press freedom.

stories.title: 'Very profitable business': Trump says US Navy seizing Iranian oil ‘like pirates’
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump described the U.S. Navy's seizure of Iranian ships and cargo near the Strait of Hormuz as acting "like pirates" and called it "a very profitable business." The U.S. is conducting a naval blockade of Iranian ports, while Iran has blocked most non-Iranian shipping through the strait.

stories.title: US to ‘close its flagship Gaza mission’
stories.summary: The Trump administration is preparing to shut down the Civil-Military Coordination Centre near Gaza, a US military-run body tasked with monitoring the Israel-Hamas ceasefire and boosting aid flows. The closure marks another setback for Trump's Gaza peace plan amid repeated Israeli attacks since the October truce.

stories.title: US awards F-16 upgrade contract for Pakistan, other states
stories.summary: The US Air Force awarded a $488 million contract to Northrop Grumman for long-term engineering support of APG-66 and APG-68 radar systems used on F-16 fighter aircraft. Pakistan is among the countries covered by the deal, with work to continue through March 2036.

stories.title: Record-breaking May warmth soon to blow away as cold front moves towards eastern Australia
stories.summary: A high-pressure system pushed temperatures 10 to 14°C above average across four Australian states in early May, setting records in multiple regions. A cold front is forecast to move toward eastern Australia, bringing rain, thunderstorms, and significantly cooler conditions.

stories.title: Russian forces attack infrastructure facility in Kryvyi Rih
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked an infrastructure facility in the Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rih, with residents reporting explosions in the area.

stories.title: ‘Roommates’ and ‘How to Make Challah’: Different slices of Jewish American pie
stories.summary: The Times of Israel reviewed two films exploring Jewish American life: the Netflix comedy "Roommates" starring Sadie Sandler, currently the number-one film in Israel, and the 13-minute intergenerational indie short "How to Make Challah."

stories.title: U.S. withdrawing 5,000 troops from Germany, U.S. officials say
stories.summary: The United States will withdraw approximately 5,000 troops from Germany over the next six to 12 months, the Pentagon confirmed. The move follows clashes between President Trump and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who criticized Washington's strategy in the US war with Iran.

stories.title: Two men shot dead in apparent underworld hit in central Israel
stories.summary: Two men were shot dead in what police believe was an underworld hit connected to an ongoing feud between crime families in the central Israeli cities of Ramle and Lod. The incident occurred hours before a separate fatal shooting in the southern city of Rahat.

stories.title: The 35-minute miracle: Inside Jerusalem’s best-kept Dead Sea escape
stories.summary: A travel feature highlights the proximity of Jerusalem to the Dead Sea, describing it as a 35-minute trip to what the article calls the lowest and most healing place on Earth.

stories.title: Trump says 'not happy' with Iran proposal, claims hostilities 'terminated'
stories.summary: President Trump said he was "not happy" with Iran's latest negotiation proposals and claimed Iranian leadership was divided into multiple factions. In a letter to congressional leaders, Trump stated that hostilities with Iran had "terminated" following a ceasefire declared on April 7, 2026.

stories.title: US blockade costs Iran $4.8 billion, US Navy acting 'sort of like pirates,' Trump says - report
stories.summary: Pentagon officials said over 40 vessels carrying oil and contraband have been redirected since the US blockade of Iran began on April 13, costing Iran an estimated $4.8 billion. President Trump described the US Navy's actions as operating "sort of like pirates."

stories.title: Summer holidays up in the air as Europe braces for jet fuel shortage
stories.summary: Dutch low-cost airline Transavia announced cancellations of flights in May and June due to surging kerosene prices linked to the ongoing Middle East conflict. European carriers are bracing for further disruptions and potential jet fuel shortages heading into the summer travel season.

stories.title: Russian army strikes Mykolaiv's energy sector with drones
stories.summary: Russian forces used drones to strike energy infrastructure in the Ukrainian city of Mykolaiv, targeting the region's power sector.

stories.title: US bypasses congressional review for military sales of nearly $11 billion to Middle East allies
stories.summary: The United States bypassed congressional review to approve nearly $11 billion in military sales to Middle East allies. The move came nine weeks into the US- and Israeli-led war against Iran.

stories.title: U.S. approves military sales of over $8.6 billion to West Asia allies
stories.summary: The US approved military sales exceeding $8.6 billion to allies in West Asia, including Israel and Gulf states. The announcements came as the US-Israel war against Iran entered its ninth week, more than three weeks after a fragile ceasefire took effect.

stories.title: Hezbollah’s cheap drones pose challenge for Israel – like ‘children’s toys’
stories.summary: Hezbollah's low-cost fibre-optic drones are creating significant tactical challenges for Israeli forces in southern Lebanon. The drones have killed two soldiers and one civilian contractor in under a week, despite a ceasefire in place since mid-April. The fibre-optic guidance makes them resistant to electronic jamming.

stories.title: China urges reversal of UNIFIL departure from Lebanon as conflict escalates
stories.summary: China has called for the reversal of UNIFIL's withdrawal from Lebanon as fighting between Israel and Hezbollah continues to escalate. The UN peacekeeping mission in southern Lebanon has suffered a growing number of casualties amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Turkish activist slams Israel’s illegal interception of Gaza aid flotilla, calls it ‘piracy’
stories.summary: Turkish activist Suayb Ordu accused Israeli forces of committing "piracy" by intercepting the Global Sumud Flotilla in international waters. Israeli forces seized 22 Gaza-bound humanitarian aid ships and detained over 180 activists. Ordu alleged detainees were subjected to torture and abuse.

stories.title: Spirit Airlines says they are going out of business
stories.summary: U.S. carrier Spirit Airlines announced it was ceasing all operations immediately after government bailout negotiations collapsed. All flights were cancelled as the company said it was going out of business.

stories.title: Octopus interceptor drone proves its effectiveness in combat conditions — General Staff
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff announced that the Octopus drone interception system has demonstrated its effectiveness in real combat conditions, proving the viability of the innovative interceptor technology.

stories.title: US to withdraw 5,000 troops from Germany, Pentagon says
stories.summary: The Pentagon announced that U.S. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth ordered the withdrawal of approximately 5,000 American troops from Germany. The decision reflects tensions with the NATO ally over disagreements regarding Washington's war on Iran. U.S. bases in Germany are used for operations across the Middle East, Europe, and Africa.

stories.title: Iran war: What’s happening on day 64 as Trump rejects Tehran’s proposal
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump rejected Iran's latest peace proposal, stating it contained demands he could not accept. The rejection came on day 64 of the ongoing conflict between the United States and Iran.

stories.title: 'Still on a war footing': Tehran shares new proposal on ending Iran war
stories.summary: Iran has put forward a new proposal aimed at advancing stalled peace negotiations with the United States. FRANCE 24 reported that Tehran remains "on a war footing" while seeking diplomatic progress to end the conflict.

stories.title: Russia strikes port infrastructure in Izmail
stories.summary: Russian forces struck port infrastructure in the city of Izmail in Ukraine's Odesa region.

stories.title: Canada police expand case over protest at event platforming Israeli soldiers
stories.summary: Toronto police filed additional charges against four individuals involved in a protest at a Students Supporting Israel event at Toronto Metropolitan University. Charges include "taking part in a riot while masked" and, in two cases, "public incitement of hatred." The event featured Israeli soldiers who had served in Gaza.

stories.title: US embassy warns citizens in UK as threat level raised to ‘severe’
stories.summary: The U.S. embassy in the United Kingdom raised its threat advisory level to "severe" and warned American citizens to avoid schools, churches, and tourist locations. Citizens were also advised to vary their travel routes.

stories.title: WSJ: Iran war exposes gaps in US defence systems
stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that the US–Iran war has revealed vulnerabilities in American defense systems, giving rival nations including China, Russia, and North Korea insight into US military capabilities. Iranian drones reportedly challenged elements of the THAAD system, with damage reported to radar infrastructure in Jordan and the United Arab Emirates.

stories.title: BBC News to bear deepest cuts amid 2,000 planned job losses
stories.summary: The BBC announced that its news division will face 15% budget cuts, exceeding the corporation-wide 10% target, as part of a £600 million savings plan. The restructuring could eliminate up to 2,000 jobs across the organization, marking the largest round of layoffs at the public broadcaster in 15 years.

stories.title: ‘There is real danger’: landline phone users voice fears over digital switchover
stories.summary: Residents in rural areas of the United Kingdom, including the Scottish Highlands, report losing all communication during power outages after landlines were switched from copper cable to broadband connections. Campaigners are calling for the digital switchover deadline to be extended from 2027 to 2030, citing inadequate backup systems.

stories.title: ‘People can see it – but can’t use it’: mystery of completed East-West Rail line that has no passenger trains
stories.summary: The East West Rail line connecting Oxford to Milton Keynes was completed in 2024 and has carried freight trains through Winslow, Buckinghamshire, since late that year. However, promised passenger services have not launched, and no start date has been announced despite over a decade of government commitments.

stories.title: 40pc children in seven cities have lead in their blood, study finds
stories.summary: A study by Pakistan's Ministry of National Health Services and UNICEF found that 40 percent of children aged 12–36 months in high-risk areas of seven Pakistani cities had lead in their blood. Over 2,100 children were sampled in industrial areas including Haripur and Islamabad.

stories.title: Israel orders evacuations in multiple Lebanon towns
stories.summary: The Israeli military issued evacuation warnings for residents of several towns in southern Lebanon, including Qaaqaait al-Jisr, Adchit al-Shaqif, Jebchit, and others. The orders followed continued Israeli strikes in the region, including an attack on Habboush that killed at least eight people.

stories.title: At least 11 dead in western Mexico after bus careens off highway
stories.summary: At least 11 people died and 31 were injured when a tourist bus crashed in Mexico's western state of Nayarit during the Labor Day holiday weekend. The accident occurred when the bus careened off a highway.

stories.title: 23 killed in Israeli attacks on Lebanon, Anadolu reports
stories.summary: Anadolu Agency reported that 23 people were killed in 41 Israeli strikes across Lebanon on Friday, despite a ceasefire in place since April 17. Hezbollah said it conducted 10 retaliatory operations targeting Israeli troops in southern Lebanon, while Israel reported two soldiers were wounded.

stories.title: US withdrawing 5,000 troops from Germany, US officials say
stories.summary: The Pentagon announced the withdrawal of 5,000 U.S. troops from Germany amid a growing rift between President Trump and European allies over the Iran war. Defense Secretary Hegseth ordered the drawdown following a review of U.S. force posture in Europe.

stories.title: Iran's enriched uranium likely at Isfahan, IAEA discusses extraction with Russia, US - report
stories.summary: IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi stated that Iran's enriched uranium is likely still held at the Isfahan nuclear complex. The IAEA is reportedly in discussions with Russia and the United States regarding the potential extraction of the material.

stories.title: Government ‘confident’ that 75% of Wang Chi House owners will take buy-back offer
stories.summary: The Hong Kong government expressed confidence that at least 75% of Wang Chi House homeowners would accept a buy-back offer by the end of June. Deputy Financial Secretary Michael Wong said few of the 248 flat owners were likely to change their minds. Wang Chi House was the only block undamaged in the Wang Fuk Court fire.

stories.title: Hezbollah says it hit Israeli troops in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced a series of attacks on Israeli military positions in southern Lebanon, targeting troops and vehicles in areas including Bint Jbeil, Hula, and Biyyada. The group said it used explosive drones and artillery to strike targets including a Hummer vehicle in Taybeh and a Merkava tank.

stories.title: SBU detains repeat offender in Mykolaiv for directing Russian strikes on Ukrainian forces
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) detained a man in Mykolaiv accused of tracking coordinates of Ukrainian defense forces and relaying them to Russia for missile and drone strikes. The suspect was described as a repeat offender.

stories.title: Seven members of Hariri organization indicted for extortion, threats, planting of explosive devices
stories.summary: Seven members of a Hariri-linked organization were indicted on charges of extortion, threats, and planting explosive devices. The indictments followed raids conducted on April 12 in Arab villages and the West Bank, during which 11 suspects were arrested.

stories.title: What to watch in Israel: 'Fauda' season 5, 'Unconditional' lead wave of new releases
stories.summary: A roundup of new Israeli television releases highlights the premiere of "Fauda" season 5 and "Unconditional" among a wave of new productions in Israel's TV industry.

stories.title: Middle East war live: Trump tells US Congress that hostilities in Iran 'have terminated'
stories.summary: President Donald Trump formally notified House Speaker Mike Johnson and Senate President Pro Tempore Chuck Grassley that hostilities between the U.S. and Iran had ended with the April ceasefire. The letters came after a 60-day War Powers Act deadline for securing congressional approval for the conflict had passed.

stories.title: 'If we sleep, they bite': Rats and weasels infest camps for displaced Gazans
stories.summary: In the Gaza Strip, the daily battles are now with rats, weasels, and other pests spreading diseases.

stories.title: Counting gains from Beijing, Taiwanese opposition leader Cheng Li-wun eyes US trip in June
stories.summary: Taiwanese opposition leader Cheng Li-wun of the Kuomintang party is planning a visit to the United States in June following her recent meeting with Chinese Communist Party leader Xi Jinping in Beijing. Cheng aims to present what she calls a "new road map" for cross-strait stability to Washington officials.

stories.title: Why India’s logistics pact with Russia signals its Arctic ‘footprint’ ambition
stories.summary: India and Russia signed the Reciprocal Exchange of Logistics Agreement (RELOS) in Moscow, covering military exercises, training, and humanitarian missions. Analysts say the pact is expected to boost Russia's influence in the Indian Ocean and expand India's presence in the Arctic, though it does not grant mutual access to military bases.

stories.title: Cuba condemns new US sanctions as 'illegal' and 'abusive'
stories.summary: Cuba condemned newly imposed U.S. sanctions as illegal and abusive. The measures add to an existing U.S. blockade on oil shipments to Cuba, which has already caused widespread blackouts and fuel shortages across the island.

stories.title: Trump says US forces are ‘like pirates’ taking Iranian oil
stories.summary: President Donald Trump compared US naval forces to pirates as they intercepted Iranian ships and cargo near the Strait of Hormuz, part of an ongoing US blockade targeting Iranian oil exports.

stories.title: Khamenei urges focus on domestic production, calls for economic jihad
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei issued a Labour Day message calling for an "economic and cultural jihad," urging citizens to prioritize domestically produced goods. He said Iran had proven its military strength and must now defeat adversaries on the economic front, while asking business owners to avoid layoffs.

stories.title: Pashinyan expects Zelensky to visit Yerevan next week
stories.summary: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan announced that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is expected to visit Yerevan on May 4.

stories.title: India repatriates seafarers amid ongoing maritime crisis
stories.summary: Indian seafarers stranded in Khorramshahr, Iran, during the ongoing war were repatriated to Mumbai, describing harrowing conditions including missiles overhead and no internet access. The Forward Seamen's Union of India urged the government to address the situation.

stories.title: Iran war protester speaks to Al Jazeera from top of Washington bridge
stories.summary: A 45-year-old man climbed to the top of the Frederick Douglass Memorial Bridge in Washington, D.C., to protest the US war on Iran, drawing public attention from his elevated position.

stories.title: US judge blocks Trump from ending protections for 2,800 Yemeni nationals
stories.summary: A U.S. federal judge blocked the Trump administration from ending Temporary Protected Status for more than 2,800 Yemeni nationals, preventing planned termination of protections that allow them to live and work in the United States.

stories.title: With gallows humor, UK author Howard Jacobson takes on post-Oct. 7 ‘bloodlust’ for Jews
stories.summary: British-Jewish author Howard Jacobson published a new novel titled "Howl," depicting a Jewish teacher unraveling in response to the world's reaction to the October 7 Hamas attack. The book uses dark comedy to address antisemitism and contemporary events.

stories.title: Havana slams new Trump sanctions as ‘collective punishment’ of Cuban people
stories.summary: The Cuban government condemned new sanctions imposed by US President Donald Trump, characterizing them as collective punishment against the Cuban people.

stories.title: 45% of fire safety shutdowns run past new 2-month cap after Tai Po blaze
stories.summary: Official data from Hong Kong shows that nearly 45% of fire safety system shutdowns for maintenance over the past two years exceeded the new two-month maximum imposed after the deadly Wang Fuk Court fire in Tai Po. The Fire Services Department said the updated rules would also apply to ongoing projects with pre-existing shutdown notices.

stories.title: A year after corporal punishment ban, Thailand needs to curb resurgence
stories.summary: One year after Thailand legally banned corporal punishment, the practice appears to be resurging. Traditional attitudes normalizing physical discipline of children, reflected in cultural proverbs and school practices, continue to pose challenges to enforcement of the ban.

stories.title: Romania issues air raid alert during Russian drone attack on Odesa region
stories.summary: Residents of Tulcea County in Romania received an air raid alert after a Russian drone attack targeted Ukraine's Odesa region. Romanian authorities issued the RO-ALERT warning due to the proximity of the strikes to Romanian territory.

stories.title: China questions ceasefire as Israel continues bombardment in Lebanon
stories.summary: China's UN envoy Fu Cong said there is no genuine ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon, describing the situation as a "lesser fire" and calling on Israel to stop its bombardment. The remarks came as China assumed the rotating presidency of the UN Security Council for May.

stories.title: Japan’s Takaichi to hold talks in Vietnam on economic security, critical minerals
stories.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is set to hold talks in Vietnam focused on economic security and critical mineral supply chains. The discussions aim to strengthen Japan-Vietnam partnership amid Tokyo's diplomatic tensions with China and disruptions caused by the Middle East crisis. Takaichi will also present Japan's updated free and open Indo-Pacific vision.

stories.title: Peru probes trafficking of citizens to fight for Russia in Ukraine
stories.summary: Peru's public prosecutor launched an investigation into the trafficking of Peruvian citizens who were lured to fight for Russia in Ukraine, reportedly deceived by false promises of employment.

stories.title: Gaza aid flotilla activists, including former Pakistani senator Mushtaq Ahmad, released after Israeli interception
stories.summary: Over 100 activists from the Global Sumud Flotilla, including former Pakistani senator Mushtaq Ahmad, were released to the Greek island of Crete after Israeli forces intercepted their Gaza-bound aid ships in international waters near Greece. The flotilla had departed Barcelona on April 12 in an attempt to break Israel's Gaza blockade.

stories.title: Trump 'not satisfied' with Iran's new proposal; says truce 'terminated' hostilities, as War Powers deadline arrives
stories.summary: Iran submitted a new peace proposal to the United States via Pakistan, but President Trump said he was "not satisfied" with the offer. Although a ceasefire has held since April 8, the two sides remain divided over Iran's nuclear program and control of the Strait of Hormuz, with no second meeting yet scheduled.

stories.title: Trump says US-Iran talks ongoing by phone
stories.summary: President Trump said US-Iran negotiations are continuing by phone after he cancelled a planned trip to Islamabad, citing the distance and an unsatisfactory deal. Discussions reportedly focus on a ceasefire framework, reopening the Strait of Hormuz, lifting the blockade, and deferring nuclear issues.

stories.title: China says UN should revisit decision to withdraw Lebanon peacekeeping mission
stories.summary: China has called on the United Nations to reconsider its decision to withdraw the peacekeeping mission from Lebanon. Israeli strikes across Lebanon since March 2 have killed more than 2,500 people.

stories.title: Man sentenced to 10 months in prison for urinating on tefillin cabinet, looting charity boxes
stories.summary: A man was sentenced to 10 months in prison for urinating on a tefillin cabinet and looting charity boxes. The presiding judge, Alex Akhter, ruled the defendant acted knowingly and was "consumed by hatred toward Jews."

stories.title: Sinking the ‘condom flotilla’: How Israel took control of the Global Sumud Flotilla narrative
stories.summary: Israeli officials conducted a combined operation to neutralize the Global Sumud Flotilla and counter its international media narrative. The effort reportedly aimed to control both the physical encounter and public perception of the incident.

stories.title: German minister pushes oil firms to lower pump prices
stories.summary: German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil urged oil companies to pass savings from a government fuel tax cut on to consumers. The measure, effective since May 1, reduces energy taxes on diesel and petrol by about 0.17 euros per litre and runs through June. Authorities said they will monitor pricing closely.

stories.title: US says 45 ships turned back under Iran blockade
stories.summary: US Central Command said it has turned back 45 commercial vessels as part of the American blockade of Iran's ports, imposed on April 13. Centcom stated US forces continue patrolling international waters to enforce compliance and restrict shipping linked to Iranian trade routes.

stories.title: Implementation of conscription plan: Havryliuk addresses parliament on traffic stops and body cameras at TCR servicemen
stories.summary: Ukrainian Deputy Defense Minister Havryliuk addressed parliament regarding the implementation of a conscription plan, discussing traffic stops and the use of body cameras by Territorial Recruitment Center personnel. Joint teams of recruitment centers and National Police conduct traffic blocks based on local defense council decisions.

stories.title: US synagogue helps Palestinians raise money for Gaza, finds common ground over falafel
stories.summary: A US synagogue hosted a daylong fundraiser for Palestinians in Gaza, organized through relationships between a rabbi, a Palestinian restaurateur, and a Duke University neurosurgeon. The event sought to promote peace and reconciliation.

stories.title: Kumanjayi Little Baby’s relatives share grief at ‘child ripped away’ as NT chief minister foreshadows charges
stories.summary: Relatives of five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby, a Warlpiri girl from the Gurindji community, shared their grief after her body was found in Alice Springs, Northern Territory, five days after she went missing from Old Timers town camp. The Northern Territory chief minister foreshadowed that charges would be filed in connection with her death.

stories.title: Judge protects Yemeni refugees, slams Trump administration’s push to end special status
stories.summary: A U.S. judge blocked the Trump administration from ending Temporary Protected Status for Yemeni refugees, criticizing the government's push to terminate the program. The administration has already ended TPS for people from nine countries including Haiti, Venezuela, and Ethiopia.

stories.title: Durian Express? New Southeast Asia rail service cuts fruit prices in China
stories.summary: A new cold-storage rail service linking Thailand, Laos, and China's Yunnan province is enabling faster shipment of durians to the Chinese market, reducing prices. The first goods train carrying Thai durians began its journey through Laos to China, using the route to cut transit times for the fruit that accounts for over 90% of global durian exports.

stories.title: US sanctions China-based oil terminal over Iran trade
stories.summary: The US State Department imposed sanctions on multiple entities, an individual, and a vessel involved in Iranian petroleum trade, including China-based Qingdao Haiye Oil Terminal Co Ltd. China's embassy criticized the action, opposing what it called unilateral sanctions and long-arm jurisdiction.

stories.title: US withdrawing 5,000 troops from Germany, US officials say
stories.summary: The Pentagon confirmed the withdrawal of 5,000 US troops from Germany, to be completed over six to 12 months. Germany hosts approximately 35,000 active-duty US military personnel, more than any other country in Europe.

stories.title: US Pentagon signs AI deals with Google, Nvidia and SpaceX, focus on ‘lawful’ use
stories.summary: Eight technology companies, including Google, Nvidia, and SpaceX, signed deals with the Pentagon to deploy AI on military systems. The Department of Defense said the agreements aim to establish the US military as an "AI-first fighting force" with decision superiority across all domains.

stories.title: In a divided world, Israel needs a new hasbara playbook - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Israel's traditional public diplomacy efforts are under strain as political polarization reshapes international perceptions. The author calls for a new approach to Israel's public messaging strategy.

stories.title: US military reaches deal with 7 tech firms to use their AI on classified systems
stories.summary: The US military reached agreements with seven technology companies to deploy AI on classified defense systems. Anthropic was excluded after insisting on prohibitions against fully autonomous weapons and surveillance of Americans; the company subsequently sued the Trump administration over government use of its chatbot.

stories.title: Man in Rivne region served with suspicion notice for opening fire on recruitment officers, police
stories.summary: In Ukraine's Rivne region, a 48-year-old serviceman of the Ukrainian Armed Forces was served a suspicion notice after opening fire on employees of a territorial recruitment and social support center and a police officer.

stories.title: US sanctions three Iranian currency exchange firms
stories.summary: The US Treasury Department sanctioned three Iranian foreign exchange firms—Opal Exchange, Radin Exchange, and Tahayyori Guarantee Society—accusing them of helping Tehran convert oil revenues into currencies used by Iran's military and regional proxies. The firms and associates are now barred from the US financial system.

stories.title: Cuba says Trump’s fresh sanctions on its economy amount to ‘collective punishment’
stories.summary: Cuba's government accused the Trump administration of imposing "collective punishment" through new sanctions targeting broad sectors of the Cuban economy, including energy, defense, and mining. A large May 1 procession was held outside the American embassy in Havana in protest.

stories.title: In China at a time of geopolitical flux, I feel right at home
stories.summary: A personal essay reflects on the experience of visiting China during a period of global geopolitical tension, exploring themes of cultural assumptions, professional expectations, and cross-border perceptions.

stories.title: Russian regional outlet says website was hacked to plant fake ‘exclusive interview’ with governor downplaying drone strikes
stories.summary: A regional news outlet in Krasnodar, Russia, reported that its website was hacked and a fabricated interview with Governor Veniamin Kondratyev was planted. The fake article, which appeared to downplay drone strikes in Tuapse, was quickly deleted but preserved in web archives.

stories.title: Northern Irish police charge man with attempted murder after car bomb attack
stories.summary: Police in Northern Ireland charged a 66-year-old man with attempted murder and other offenses following a car bomb attack on the Dunmurry police station in south Belfast over the weekend.

stories.title: 14 IRGC members killed clearing unexploded munitions in Iran
stories.summary: Fars News Agency reported that 14 members of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps were killed and two injured when unexploded ordnance detonated during a clearance operation in Zanjan Province, northwestern Iran. Approximately 1,200 hectares of agricultural land in the area had been affected by remnants of explosives.

stories.title: Trump says he spoke with Iraq PM-designate, voices strong support
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said he spoke with Iraq's prime minister-designate and expressed strong support for his leadership, stating that the designate had won with American help and that the US wanted him to succeed.

stories.title: Trump says he spoke with Iraq PM-designate, voices strong support
stories.summary: President Donald Trump told reporters he spoke with Iraqi prime minister-designate Ali al-Zaidi on Thursday and expressed strong support for him.

stories.title: Trump says no need for congressional approval on Iran war after ceasefire
stories.summary: The Trump administration told Congress that the 60-day War Powers Resolution deadline for seeking approval of military action against Iran has been paused, arguing hostilities ended following a ceasefire in early April. Trump asserted he does not need congressional authorization since there has been no exchange of fire.

stories.title: What to leave behind? Returning Wang Fuk Court residents stuck with tough decisions
stories.summary: Residents of Hong Kong's Wang Fuk Court returned to fire-damaged homes months after a November blaze, facing difficult choices about what to salvage within a three-hour window. Some residents found their upper-floor flats largely intact but struggled to locate valuables under tight practical constraints.

stories.title: China trend of AI replicas of exes sparks debates about emotional cheating, attachment
stories.summary: A growing trend in China involves young people creating AI-powered digital replicas of their ex-partners that mimic speech patterns and mannerisms. The practice has sparked debate over privacy, emotional dependency, and the boundaries of technology in personal relationships.

stories.title: Iran using ceasefire as opportunity to dig out buried missiles, launchers - report
stories.summary: According to U.S. intelligence assessments, Iran is using the current ceasefire period to excavate buried missiles and launchers. Multiple sources indicate Washington believes Tehran intends to rebuild its missile capabilities in preparation for a possible resumption of hostilities if negotiations fail.

stories.title: Iran says US must drop ‘threatening rhetoric’ for diplomacy
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran remains open to diplomacy with the United States if Washington abandons what he called its "expansionist approach" and "threatening rhetoric." The comments were posted on his official Telegram account following calls with regional counterparts.

stories.title: Trump says Iran ‘wants a deal’ but US 'not satisfied'
stories.summary: President Trump said Iran "wants to make a deal" but that the US is "not satisfied" with the latest proposal submitted via Pakistan. Trump indicated uncertainty about whether negotiations would succeed, noting talks are being conducted by phone.

stories.title: Sirens sound as Israel intercepts incoming targets, military says
stories.summary: The Israeli military said its air force intercepted two "suspicious aerial targets" before they entered Israeli airspace, following sirens in northern Israel. Interceptors were also launched after alerts of rocket fire near Kiryat Shmona. The military said it is investigating the results.

stories.title: US pulling 5,000 troops from Germany amid spat with Trump over Iran war
stories.summary: The Pentagon announced the withdrawal of approximately 5,000 US troops from Germany, expected to take six to 12 months. A senior Pentagon official called German criticism of Washington's Iran war policy "inappropriate and unhelpful." Germany currently hosts around 35,000 active-duty US military personnel.

stories.title: From Auschwitz to today: How Israel’s days of memory define who we are - opinion
stories.summary: At Yad Labanim in Israel, an opinion piece reflects on how Holocaust remembrance and commemoration of fallen soldiers merge with present-day security concerns. The author argues these days of memory shape Israel's national identity and resolve.

stories.title: From Malaysia’s book bans to Iran war, Anwar’s reform agenda faces sternest test
stories.summary: Malaysia's ban on two books in mid-April, including a memoir linked to an ally of Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, drew criticism and raised questions about his reformist agenda. The article connects this domestic controversy to broader pressures on Anwar's government, including the regional impact of the Iran war.

stories.title: Iran war live: Trump says no ‘early’ end to war, unhappy with Tehran offer
stories.summary: The White House notified Congress that hostilities with Iran have terminated, despite a continued US troop presence in the Middle East. President Trump indicated he is unhappy with Tehran's latest offer and does not foresee an early end to the conflict.

stories.title: Russia’s media regulator fines Take-Two and Electronic Arts over data storage violations, targets more game studios
stories.summary: Russian courts have filed at least eight administrative complaints since December 2025 against foreign video game studios Take-Two and Electronic Arts over data storage violations. Russia's media regulator is reportedly targeting additional game studios under personal data storage laws.

stories.title: US approves arms sales of over $8.6 billion for Israel and other Mideast allies
stories.summary: The US approved arms sales totaling over $8.6 billion to Israel and other Middle Eastern allies. Israel's package includes $992.4 million in laser-guided weapons kits, while Gulf countries received billions in air defense purchases amid a fragile truce with Iran.

stories.title: Keeping time: How Jews preserved ritual and hope in the Holocaust’s darkest days
stories.summary: A Yad Vashem exhibition chronicles the lives and rituals of Jewish communities before and during the Holocaust. The display focuses on how Jews preserved religious practices and hope during the era's darkest period.

stories.title: War update: 114 clashes on frontline as Russian forces launch 53 airstrikes
stories.summary: Ukrainian and Russian forces engaged in 114 clashes along the front line, while Russian forces launched 53 airstrikes. The fighting occurred across multiple sectors of the conflict zone.

stories.title: Upper, central parts of country expected to see dust storms, rain from May 2-5; extreme heat grips Sindh cities
stories.summary: Pakistan faces contrasting weather conditions, with extreme heat gripping Sindh province while central and northern regions prepare for dust storms, rain, and potential landslides from May 2 to 5. The Pakistan Meteorological Department warned that a westerly weather system would approach the northwest on Saturday evening.

stories.title: Ukraine’s drone forces commander says no part of Russia is safe from strikes, as drones hit oil infrastructure deep inside the country
stories.summary: Robert Brovdi, commander of Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces and known by the call sign "Magyar," told the BBC that Ukrainian drones can now strike Russian territory up to 1,500–2,000 kilometers deep. Brovdi, a former grain trader who volunteered at the war's start, was among the first to deploy drones for reconnaissance and strikes.

stories.title: U.S.'s Hormuz coalition 'not in competition' with France, U.K.-led bid: French FM
stories.summary: French Foreign Minister stated that the U.S.-led Strait of Hormuz maritime coalition is "not in competition" with a separate effort led by the United Kingdom and France. The U.K.-France initiative recently held a meeting with more than 50 countries on maritime security.

stories.title: Rebels take key military camp in Mali's north
stories.summary: Rebel forces captured the Tessalit military camp in northern Mali without any reported clashes. A security source in the city of Gao, located south of Tessalit, confirmed the takeover occurred peacefully.

stories.title: Trump says Iran war 'terminated,' as war powers deadline arrives
stories.summary: President Trump sent a letter to congressional leaders on the 60-day War Powers deadline stating that there has been no exchange of fire with Iran since the ceasefire. Trump characterized the Iran war as "terminated."

stories.title: Israel's death penalty law perpetuates racial discrimination: UN watchdog
stories.summary: A UN watchdog committee stated that Israel's recently enacted death penalty law is effectively applicable only to Palestinians, constituting racial discrimination. The law establishes a 90-day deadline for carrying out executions after a final judgment is issued.

stories.title: 13 terrorists killed in Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa along Afghanistan border
stories.summary: Pakistani security forces killed 13 militants in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province near the Afghanistan border. In Mohmand district, troops detected and engaged a group of fighters attempting to infiltrate across the Pakistan-Afghanistan frontier.

stories.title: New film profiles Jewish feminist who is NYC Sanitation Department’s official artist
stories.summary: A new documentary titled "Maintenance Artist" profiles Mierle Laderman Ukeles, a Jewish feminist artist who has served as the official artist-in-residence at New York City's Sanitation Department for 50 years. The film explores her belief, rooted in Jewish identity, that people transcend their societal roles.

stories.title: US to withdraw 5,000 troops from Germany, fulfilling Trump threat
stories.summary: The Pentagon confirmed the US will withdraw about 5,000 troops from Germany within six to 12 months, following President Trump's threat after German Chancellor Friedrich Merz criticized Washington's lack of strategy in the Iran war. Merz had said Iran was "humiliating" the US in talks.

stories.title: Jailed Iranian Nobel winner Mohammadi hospitalized in ‘catastrophic’ condition
stories.summary: Imprisoned Iranian Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi has been hospitalized in what her rights foundation described as "catastrophic" condition. Her family said the health crisis followed 140 days of systematic medical neglect in prison, including a severe cardiac episode.

stories.title: Trump 'not satisfied' with Iran's latest proposal to end war with U.S.
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said he was not satisfied with Iran's latest peace proposal, which was conveyed through Pakistani mediators. Trump did not specify what shortcomings he found in the offer, and negotiations between Washington and Tehran remain stalled.

stories.title: Israeli authorities taking 2 activists who led Gaza-bound flotilla to Israel for questioning
stories.summary: Israeli authorities detained two activists who led a Gaza-bound flotilla and transported them to Israel for questioning. Solidarity protests erupted in several cities, including Rome, Athens, and Istanbul.

stories.title: US said to be withdrawing 5,000 troops from Germany over Iran war spat
stories.summary: President Donald Trump is reportedly withdrawing approximately 5,000 US troops from Germany following disagreements with European allies over their level of support for Washington's war against Iran.

stories.title: Gaza aid flotilla activists, including former Pakistani senator Mushtaq, released after Israeli interception
stories.summary: Over 100 activists from the Global Sumud Flotilla, including former Pakistani senator Mushtaq Ahmad, were released and transferred to the Greek island of Crete after Israeli forces seized their Gaza-bound aid ships. The flotilla had departed from Barcelona on April 12 before being intercepted in international waters near Greece.

stories.title: Russian hacker pleads guilty to cyberattacks on US, Ukrainian oil and gas facilities
stories.summary: A Russian hacker pleaded guilty to cyberattacks that damaged critical oil and gas infrastructure in the United States, Ukraine, and other countries. The charges carry a maximum sentence of 27 years in prison.

stories.title: Washington to pull some 5,000 US troops from Germany as rift over Iran war widens
stories.summary: The United States plans to withdraw around 5,000 troops from Germany over the next year amid a widening rift between Washington and Berlin over the Iran war. The move follows German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's statement that Tehran was "humiliating" Washington. NATO said Saturday it is consulting with the U.S. on the details.

stories.title: Ukraine says a strike hit Tuapse oil terminal, the fourth attack on the region in 2 weeks
stories.summary: Ukraine reported that a strike hit the Tuapse oil terminal in Russia, marking the fourth attack on that region in two weeks. Separately, Russia struck the western Ukrainian city of Ternopil with over 50 drones, according to Mayor Serhii Nadal.

stories.title: Trump says he is 'not satisfied' after Iran delivers new proposal for peace talks
stories.summary: Iran submitted a new peace proposal to the United States through Pakistan, with the text delivered to Islamabad on Thursday. U.S. President Donald Trump responded from the White House that he was "not satisfied" with the offer, describing Iran's leadership as "disjointed."

stories.title: US withdrawing 5,000 troops from Germany, US officials say
stories.summary: The United States is withdrawing 5,000 troops from Germany, according to U.S. officials. The drawdown comes amid a growing rift between President Donald Trump and European allies over the Iran war.

stories.title: Trump considering option to ‘blast the hell out of’ Iran
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated he is considering intensified military action against Iran, saying he is "not happy" with Tehran's latest peace proposal.

stories.title: Trump's proposed 2027 defense budget excludes military aid to Ukraine – Senator King
stories.summary: President Trump's proposed fiscal year 2027 defense budget does not include military assistance for Ukraine, according to U.S. Senator Angus King.

stories.title: Hegseth orders 5,000 US troops to withdraw from Germany
stories.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth ordered the withdrawal of 5,000 U.S. troops from Germany. Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said the decision followed a review of U.S. force posture in Europe based on theater requirements and conditions on the ground.

stories.title: KP CM Afridi warns of protests against drone attacks
stories.summary: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi warned of protests against drone attacks in the province, citing collateral damage to civilians. Speaking at a cabinet meeting in Peshawar, Afridi condemned the strikes and hinted at legislation to criminalize collateral damage from such operations.

stories.title: Why Beijing now wants its spies executed in Taiwan to come in from decades in the cold
stories.summary: China's Fujian province is framing the historical executions of Communist Party spies in Taiwan within a reunification narrative. A former residence in Fuzhou has become a national pilgrimage site tied to Beijing's messaging toward Taiwan.

stories.title: US believes Iran has lost $4.8 billion in oil earnings due to blockade — report
stories.summary: The United States believes Iran has lost approximately $4.8 billion in oil revenue due to a blockade. Separately, the U.S. reportedly told European allies to expect delays in arms deliveries as the Iran conflict drains stockpiles. Hezbollah fired at least four drones at northern Israel, all intercepted by the IDF.

stories.title: Why Bennett, Lapid's union actually strengthens Netanyahu's hand in next elections - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion analysis argues that the merger between Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid's political movements, while intended to unify Israel's opposition, could inadvertently push right-wing voters back toward Prime Minister Netanyahu.

stories.title: Can Bennett become Israel’s Peter Magyar in the fight for democracy? - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece examines whether former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett could replicate the political realignment achieved by Hungary's Peter Magyar and break Netanyahu's ruling bloc.

stories.title: Injury toll from Russian drone attack on Ternopil rises to 12
stories.summary: The number of people injured in a Russian drone attack on the western Ukrainian city of Ternopil has risen to 12. Ukrainian police established an emergency response hub in the city to coordinate relief efforts following the strike.

stories.title: Syria relies on Russia's oil despite pivot to the West
stories.summary: Syria's oil imports from Russia have surged 75% to approximately 60,000 barrels per day in the current year, making Moscow the country's dominant crude supplier. The increase follows the fall of the Assad government in December 2024, despite Syria's broader diplomatic pivot toward the West.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1528: Ukraine’s “long-range sanctions” cost Russia $7 billion this year — and counting
stories.summary: On day 1,528 of the Russo-Ukrainian war, Ukrainian drones struck a Su-57 stealth fighter base near the Urals, a refinery in Perm, and Buk-M3 air defenses in occupied Donetsk. A Russian drone swarm hit Ternopil, Rivne, Vinnytsia, Cherkasy, and Odesa, knocking Ternopil offline and injuring 10 people.

stories.title: Hong Kong’s population policy is still trapped in a city state mindset
stories.summary: Hong Kong faces calls to develop a comprehensive population policy amid rapid ageing, low fertility, and a shrinking labor force. Academics and policymakers advocate strategies focused on boosting birth rates and attracting immigrants, though critics argue this reflects a limited city-state mindset.

stories.title: China’s UN envoy blasts US ‘bullying’ as sanctions widen before Trump-Xi talks
stories.summary: China's UN envoy criticized U.S. "bullying" and sanctions against Chinese vessels and firms as Beijing assumed the rotating presidency of the UN Security Council. Washington simultaneously sanctioned a China-based petroleum terminal operator as part of efforts to cut Chinese funding to Iran.

stories.title: Palestinian FA chief hits out at Israeli federation VP at FIFA Congress
stories.summary: At the FIFA Congress, Palestinian Football Association chief Jibril Rajoub publicly criticized the Israeli federation's vice president. FIFA President Gianni Infantino had called both officials to the podium and gestured for the Palestinian leader to approach the Israeli representative.

stories.title: Zelensky announces strengthening of air defense: Decisions made for Dnipro and Odesa
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced the reinforcement of air defenses following a large-scale Russian drone attack. Specific decisions have been made to strengthen protection for the cities of Dnipro and Odesa, with intensified work with international partners underway.

stories.title: Board of Peace denies plans to shut down ceasefire coordination HQ in Israel’s south
stories.summary: The Board of Peace denied a Reuters report alleging plans to shut down a ceasefire coordination headquarters in southern Israel. The report claimed the center would be folded into a yet-to-be-formed International Stabilization Force as the ceasefire frays and Hamas disarmament efforts stall.

stories.title: Trump claims hostilities have ended in Iran in letter to congressional leaders
stories.summary: President Trump sent a letter to congressional leaders claiming hostilities with Iran have "terminated," suggesting the 60-day War Powers Act deadline to seek congressional approval no longer applies. Democrats are pushing back against Trump's interpretation. The deadline fell 60 days after the U.S. and Israel launched strikes on Iran on February 28.

stories.title: Tessalit army base taken by rebels
stories.summary: Rebels captured the strategic Tessalit military base in northern Mali near the Algerian border, forcing the army and its Russian mercenary allies to surrender. Separately, in the DRC, former president Joseph Kabila rejected U.S. accusations of backing rebel fighters.

stories.title: US to shut centre intended to monitor Gaza ceasefire as peace plans stall: Report
stories.summary: The United States plans to close a military-run center established to monitor the Israel-Hamas ceasefire in Gaza. Diplomats say the facility has failed to prevent Israeli violations, and broader peace plans have stalled.

stories.title: Trump expands red snapper fishing as critics warn of overfishing
stories.summary: The Trump administration approved red snapper fishing permits granting anglers in Florida, Georgia, and the Carolinas greater control over the fishery. Critics have raised concerns about potential overfishing as a result of the expanded access.

stories.title: Fractures rock Gulf alliance as UAE quits OPEC during Iran war - analysis
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates has withdrawn from OPEC amid the ongoing Iran war, exposing deepening fractures in the Gulf alliance. A summit snub and public criticism have highlighted a widening Saudi-Emirati split with significant implications for energy policy and regional security coordination.

stories.title: At least 12 killed in latest Israeli attacks on Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli strikes on Lebanon have continued, killing at least 12 people in the latest attacks. More than 2,600 people have been killed since March 2, despite an ongoing ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Iranian Nobel laureate Narges Mohammadi hospitalised as health deteriorates
stories.summary: Iranian Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi has been hospitalized after losing consciousness twice and suffering a severe cardiac crisis. Her foundation announced the deterioration of her health.

stories.title: Trump: 60-Day War Powers Deadline ‘Totally Unconstitutional’
stories.summary: President Trump called the 60-day War Powers deadline "totally unconstitutional" as the timeframe for congressional authorization of the Iran conflict expired. The White House argues that the U.S.-Iran ceasefire effectively paused the legal clock.

stories.title: Drone attack on Ternopil: fire contained, nine hits on industrial facilities reported
stories.summary: Rescuers in the western Ukrainian city of Ternopil contained a fire caused by Russian drone strikes that hit nine industrial facilities. The attack targeted the city's industrial infrastructure overnight.

stories.title: The great disconnect: Why Israel is losing America while winning in Iran - opinion
stories.summary: An analysis argues that Israel maintains strong support among U.S. policy circles but is experiencing a steady erosion of public and generational backing in America. The piece highlights a growing disconnect between official U.S.-Israel relations and shifting American public opinion.

stories.title: “Just reaching the front line has become very risky”: Ukraine’s AI drones are hunting Russia’s supply vans
stories.summary: Ukraine is deploying AI-guided drones that can bypass Russian electronic warfare to target supply vehicles heading to the front lines. The technology is reportedly disrupting Russian logistics and making resupply operations increasingly dangerous.

stories.title: Post-Assad Syria still dependent on Russian oil despite shift to the West – Reuters
stories.summary: Despite Syria's post-Assad political shift toward the West, the country remains heavily dependent on Russian oil imports. Domestic crude production stays far below demand, and alternative suppliers have not filled the gap.

stories.title: China drops tariffs on all African nations except Eswatini
stories.summary: A new Chinese trade policy granting tariff-free market access to African nations took effect on Friday. The two-year deal covers 53 of Africa's 54 countries, excluding only Eswatini due to its diplomatic ties with Taiwan.

stories.title: Will the Next Fed Chairman Be More Compliant With Trump?
stories.summary: Kevin Warsh, a potential next Federal Reserve chairman, is expected to face significant pressure from President Trump to cut interest rates. The article examines whether a new Fed leader would be more compliant with the administration's monetary policy preferences.

stories.title: Palestinian football boss refuses Israeli handshake at FIFA event
stories.summary: Palestine Football Association President Jibril Rajoub refused to shake hands with an Israeli FA representative at a FIFA event. Rajoub publicly explained his reasons for the refusal.

stories.title: URIF aims to sign its first three investment agreements by end of 2026
stories.summary: The United States-Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund, established one year ago, plans to finalize its first three investment agreements by the end of 2026. The fund is designed to support reconstruction efforts in Ukraine.

stories.title: Marine Corps fields 3,500 first-person view attack drones
stories.summary: The U.S. Marine Corps has fielded 3,500 first-person-view attack drones, a rapid buildup from zero such systems in service as of October 2025.

stories.title: New US sanctions are 'collective punishment', Cuba's FM says during May 1 marches
stories.summary: Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez condemned a new round of US sanctions as "collective punishment" during May 1 marches outside the US embassy in Havana. Cuba's economic crisis has worsened since US President Donald Trump imposed a severe fuel blockade on the island in January.

stories.title: USF hits four Russian aircraft in Russia's Chelyabinsk region
stories.summary: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces struck four Russian aircraft at the Shagol airfield in Russia's Chelyabinsk region. The targeted aircraft included at least one Su-57 stealth fighter and one Su-34 fighter-bomber.

stories.title: Your Taxes: Israel’s lower mid-market is tempting international M&A buyers
stories.summary: Israel's lower mid-market is attracting international buyers for mergers and acquisitions. Several factors, including favorable bargaining conditions, are contributing to increased interest in Israeli companies from foreign investors.

stories.title: Somali piracy resurfaces in the lightly-protected waters
stories.summary: Piracy is resurging off the coast of Somalia as the Somali government lacks the capacity to patrol its extensive coastline, leaving shipping lanes largely unprotected.

stories.title: Iran delivers new proposal for US talks, Trump says ‘not satisfied’ with offer
stories.summary: Iran delivered a new proposal to Pakistani intermediaries for negotiations with the United States. President Trump said he was not satisfied with the offer, though he confirmed that talks were continuing by phone.

stories.title: Iran submits new proposal to end war; Trump says he’s ‘not satisfied’
stories.summary: Iran submitted a new proposal through Pakistan that envisions the U.S. unwinding its blockade at the start of Strait of Hormuz negotiations rather than as a precondition, and suggests nuclear talks in exchange for sanctions relief. President Trump said he is not satisfied with the offer.

stories.title: BoP denies rumors of Kiryat Gat base closure, says it will establish 'transitional Gaza gov't'
stories.summary: The U.S. Bureau of Planning denied rumors that the Kiryat Gat base in Israel would close and announced plans to establish a transitional government for Gaza. The U.S. military-run center's potential closure would have been a setback for President Donald Trump's Gaza plan, which has already been undermined by Hamas's refusal to disarm.

stories.title: Daytime Russian drone swarm hits western Ukraine, knocking Ternopil offline and injuring 10
stories.summary: A daytime Russian drone swarm struck western Ukraine, knocking the city of Ternopil offline and injuring at least 10 people. Impacts were also reported in the Rivne, Vinnytsia, Cherkasy, and Odesa oblasts.

stories.title: No unfunded requirements in FY27, say some services, COCOMs
stories.summary: The U.S. Army, Navy, and Air Force submitted approximately $3 billion in unfunded requirements for the fiscal year 2027 budget, all for military construction projects. U.S. Southern Command included $229.9 million in additional requests.

stories.title: US judge bars Trump from ending protected status for Yemeni nationals
stories.summary: A U.S. federal judge blocked the Trump administration from terminating Temporary Protected Status for Yemeni nationals. The administration had sought to cancel protections for people from 13 countries as part of a broader immigration crackdown.

stories.title: Russia’s Prosecutor General’s Office sues to seize assets of agribusiness giant Rusagro founder, worth $2.9 billion
stories.summary: Russia's Prosecutor General's Office filed a lawsuit in a Moscow court to seize the assets of Vadim Moshkovich, founder of the agribusiness giant Rusagro. Moshkovich's assets are reportedly valued at approximately $2.9 billion.

stories.title: Russians attack Dnipropetrovsk region nearly 50 times since morning, leaving four injured
stories.summary: Russian forces launched nearly 50 attacks using drones and artillery on two districts of Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region, injuring four people. The strikes began in the morning and continued throughout the day.

stories.title: Norway informed it may face weapons delivery delays from US
stories.summary: Norway's Ministry of Defence has been formally notified by U.S. authorities that delays in deliveries of American weapons systems may occur. The notification was confirmed by the ministry on Friday.

stories.title: US to close its flagship Gaza mission as Trump plan stalls
stories.summary: The U.S. military-run body tasked with monitoring the Israel-Hamas ceasefire and coordinating aid to Gaza is set to be shut down, according to seven diplomats. The closure comes as President Trump's broader peace plan has stalled.

stories.title: Rebel checkpoints reported around Mali’s capital, northern town seized
stories.summary: JNIM militants and Tuareg separatist groups have established checkpoints around Mali's capital and seized a northern town, continuing their offensive against Mali's military government.

stories.title: Trump 'not satisfied' with latest Iranian proposal, says leadership is 'fully disjointed'
stories.summary: President Trump told reporters outside the White House that he is "not satisfied" with the latest Iranian negotiation proposal, calling Iran's leadership "fully disjointed." Trump asserted that Iran wants a deal "because they have no military left."

stories.title: AI actors and writers will not be eligible for Oscars, Academy says
stories.summary: The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences issued new rules stipulating that acting and writing performed by artificial intelligence will not be eligible for Oscar consideration. The updated rules also expand international film category eligibility to include top award winners from major festivals such as Cannes, Venice, and Toronto.

stories.title: Can Iran withstand the US naval blockade?
stories.summary: The Trump administration is attempting to pressure Iran into concessions by imposing a naval blockade aimed at cutting off Iranian oil exports. Questions remain about whether Tehran can withstand the sustained economic pressure.

stories.title: Trump repeats that he is 'not happy' with Iran as deadline to seek approval for war looms
stories.summary: President Trump said on Friday that said a deal has been hard to reach in part because Iranian leadership was "very confused".

stories.title: Iran told Saudi Arabia it planned to 'crush the UAE': Report
stories.summary: Iran reportedly informed Saudi Arabia and Oman of its plans to "crush" the United Arab Emirates, according to a media report. Tehran allegedly boasted about its attacks on the UAE while seeking to exploit divisions among Gulf states.

stories.title: Trump expands Cuba sanctions with global reach, targeting foreign banks and firms
stories.summary: President Trump signed an executive order significantly expanding U.S. sanctions on Cuba, authorizing penalties against foreign companies and financial institutions that do business with the island. The order extends Washington's reach to third-country actors, potentially affecting global firms including those in China.

stories.title: Navy looks to resume purchasing P-8A aircraft
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy is seeking to resume purchases of P-8A Poseidon maritime patrol aircraft. The request follows the P-8A Increment 3 Block 2 variant reaching initial operating capability.

stories.title: Oscars changes allow for double acting nominations while banning AI
stories.summary: The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences announced major Oscars rule changes, including allowing actors to receive multiple nominations in one category and barring AI-generated performances and screenplays from eligibility.

stories.title: US warns shippers that paying Iran to traverse Hormuz may incur sanctions
stories.summary: Iran is demanding payments from commercial vessels for safe passage through the blockaded Strait of Hormuz, including in the form of charitable donations. The U.S. Treasury has warned shippers that complying with these payments may trigger American sanctions.

stories.title: Trump tears up part of EU tariff deal to raise import duties on cars and lorries
stories.summary: President Trump announced he would raise tariffs on cars and lorries imported from the EU from 15% to 25%, accusing Brussels of non-compliance and slow ratification of the tariff deal struck at his Scottish golf course. The move blindsided European leaders on a public holiday.

stories.title: US sanctions China-based operator, others over alleged Iran oil trade links
stories.summary: The United States imposed new sanctions on entities and individuals allegedly involved in Iranian petroleum trade, including China-based Qingdao Haiye Oil Terminal Co. and a Chinese national. The State Department said the terminal operator imported tens of millions of barrels of sanctioned Iranian crude.

stories.title: Photos: Cuba holds May Day celebrations amid US threats
stories.summary: Cuba held May Day celebrations in Havana marking International Workers' Day. The event coincided with the announcement of additional U.S. sanctions targeting the island nation.

stories.title: Florida prosecutors launch criminal investigation into deaths of 31 sloths
stories.summary: Florida prosecutors launched a criminal investigation into the deaths of 31 sloths imported from South American rainforests in Peru and Guyana. The animals, destined for a planned theme park called Sloth World in Orlando, died in an unheated warehouse between December 2024 and February 2025.

stories.title: Ukrainian Jewish school and orphanage struck in overnight Russian drone attack
stories.summary: A Jewish school and orphanage in Ukraine sustained serious damage during an overnight Russian drone attack, though no injuries were reported. Russia launched over 600 drones at Ukraine in under 24 hours.

stories.title: As Gaza is destroyed, a VR project preserves what Israel tried to erase
stories.summary: A virtual reality project is working to digitally preserve sites across Gaza that have been destroyed during Israeli military operations. The immersive experience allows viewers to explore reconstructed Gazan environments and serves as a form of documentation of the enclave's destruction.

stories.title: The future of unmanned surface vessels includes ISR and counter-UAS
stories.summary: Red Cat, known for its aerial drones, launched a new company called Blue Ops to mass-produce unmanned surface vessels. The USVs are intended to support intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance, and counter-drone operations.

stories.title: Trump says Iran seeks terms he ‘can’t agree to’ in latest peace proposal
stories.summary: President Trump stated that Iran's latest peace proposal, transmitted via Pakistan, contains terms he cannot agree to. Negotiations are reportedly continuing by phone.

stories.title: Saffron’s Last Gasp
stories.summary: The ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict is disrupting the global supply of saffron, the world's most expensive spice, much of which originates from Iran.

stories.title: Iran’s largest crypto exchange enables IRGC to move millions despite sanctions
stories.summary: Nobitex, Iran's largest cryptocurrency exchange, has allegedly enabled the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps to move millions of dollars despite international sanctions. The platform was founded in 2018 by brothers with reported ties to a powerful family connected to the Khamenei and Khomeini clans. Nobitex denies receiving government support.

stories.title: Gaza flotilla activists return despite Israel's sea interception
stories.summary: Activists from the Global Sumud Flotilla are regrouping in Greece for a second attempt to deliver aid to Gaza by sea. The effort follows Israel's interception of an earlier flotilla, during which 175 activists were detained.

stories.title: Pentagon freezes out Anthropic as it signs deals with AI rivals
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Defense announced deals with seven artificial intelligence companies but excluded Anthropic from the agreements. The contracts signal the Pentagon's expanding engagement with commercial AI firms for defense applications.

stories.title: What in the World?
stories.summary: A weekly news quiz covers events from the week of April 25, including Iran's offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the UAE's departure from OPEC, and a conference hosted by Colombia.

stories.title: 'Iran's most potent weapon': Telegraph's Adrian Blomfield offers rare frontline glimpse of Hormuz
stories.summary: The Telegraph's Adrian Blomfield reported from the Strait of Hormuz, describing the waterway's complex maritime environment. He noted approximately 300 small speedboats operating at high speeds, creating an ambiguous ecosystem where smugglers, civilians, and military actors are difficult to distinguish.

stories.title: Oscar goes missing after director forced to check it on flight: ‘could be used as weapon’
stories.summary: Director Pavel Talankin's Academy Award went missing after a TSA agent at New York's JFK Airport required him to check the statuette on a transatlantic flight to Frankfurt, citing it as a potential weapon. The airline located the Oscar two days later. Talankin co-directed the best documentary winner Mr Nobody Against Putin.

stories.title: IDF official says Iran war will be ‘one big failure’ if enriched uranium not removed
stories.summary: A senior IDF official warned that the war with Iran will be "one big failure" unless Tehran's enriched uranium stockpile is removed through negotiations. The officer also said the IDF's ability to counter Hezbollah drone threats remains constrained by the terms of the existing truce.

stories.title: Poll finds 61 percent of Americans believe attacking Iran was a mistake
stories.summary: A recent poll indicates that 61 percent of Americans consider the attack on Iran a mistake. Respondents expressed concern about the war's impact on the cost of living and voiced skepticism about the campaign's success so far.

stories.title: Small plane crash in Texas Hill Country leaves five dead
stories.summary: A Cessna 421C crashed among trees at night in Wimberley, Texas, approximately 40 miles southwest of Austin, killing all five people onboard. Hays County Judge Ruben Becerra confirmed the crash occurred late Thursday night.

stories.title: Israel delivers Tamir interceptors to US Marine Corps for MRIC program
stories.summary: Israel delivered Tamir interceptor missiles to the U.S. Marine Corps for the Medium Range Intercept Capability program. The MRIC system uses a truck-mounted Iron Dome launcher paired with Tamir interceptors.

stories.title: Elbit subsidiary Fuse, Mistral to provide US Army THOR  drones
stories.summary: Elbit Systems subsidiary Fuse and partner Mistral will supply the US Army with THOR Group 2 drones. The backpack-portable, fully autonomous multirotor aircraft will provide American units with organic aerial reconnaissance and operational capabilities.

stories.title: Trump ‘not satisfied’ with Iran’s latest peace proposal as talks stall
stories.summary: President Donald Trump expressed dissatisfaction with Iran's latest peace proposal, saying he was not satisfied with what Tehran offered. Iranian state media reported that Tehran submitted a new plan aimed at ending the conflict that began with US-Israeli strikes on February 28. Negotiations remain stalled despite a weeks-long ceasefire.

stories.title: Ukraine hits both Russia’s military and the infrastructure funding it – from a refinery in Perm to air defenses in occupied Donetsk
stories.summary: Ukraine conducted coordinated overnight strikes hitting a refinery in Russia's Perm region, air defense systems, and multiple ammunition and drone storage sites across Russian-occupied territories. The operation targeted both military assets and infrastructure funding Russia's war effort.

stories.title: Ukraine plans army pay hikes, phased discharge — Zelenskyy
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced planned reforms including military pay increases and a phased discharge system for soldiers. The measures aim to boost morale and address complaints about exhaustion and uneven workloads on the frontline.

stories.title: King Charles wins praise for deft handling of Trump on US state visit
stories.summary: King Charles received praise for his diplomatic handling of a state visit to the United States, during which President Trump lifted some tariffs on Scotch whisky. Charles balanced praise for his host with subtle criticism, though the visit's long-term impact on US-UK relations remains uncertain amid divisions over issues including the Iran war.

stories.title: US warns shippers against paying Strait of Hormuz tolls, ‘donations’
stories.summary: The United States issued a warning to international shipping companies not to pay tolls or donations demanded in the Strait of Hormuz. The advisory came as Iranian state media reported that Tehran had submitted a new peace proposal to Washington.

stories.title: ‘It’s the little things’: Israeli mother juggles war, parenthood as her husband serves
stories.summary: An ongoing photojournalism series by Chen G. Schimmel documents the lives of Israeli soldiers' wives managing family responsibilities during wartime. The second installment profiles a mother navigating parenthood while her husband serves in the military.

stories.title: RAF chief calls Falklands defence 'non-negotiable' as Rubio plays down Pentagon memo
stories.summary: RAF Air Chief Marshal Sir Harv Smyth declared the defense of the Falkland Islands "non-negotiable," stating the UK remains on high alert following the leak of a Pentagon memo that considered reviewing US support for British sovereignty over the archipelago. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio played down the significance of the memo.

stories.title: Once the left wing of US Jewry, is J Street now the new center?
stories.summary: J Street, long considered the left wing of the American Jewish political lobby, is increasingly viewed as occupying a centrist position. The shift reflects declining Democratic support for Israel, with J Street's pushback against anti-Zionism placing it closer to the mainstream.

stories.title: Army plans fast follow-up to AI cyber wargame with industry: Officials
stories.summary: The U.S. Army plans to rapidly follow up on an AI-focused cyber wargame conducted with cybersecurity executives from 14 technology firms, exploring a Pacific-war scenario. Officials said the Army aims to fast-track new AI tools and develop policies allowing greater autonomy for AI agents in cyber operations.

stories.title: Average price of gas in California edges past $6 a gallon, highest level in four years
stories.summary: The average gasoline price in California reached $6.06 per gallon, the highest level in four years, while the national average hit $4.39 according to the American Automobile Association. Analysts attributed rising fuel costs partly to the impact of the US war on Iran, noting Americans have paid $21.7 billion more at the pump since the conflict began.

stories.title: IDF: Iron Beam laser saw limited use in Iran war due to lack of batteries, 14 needed
stories.summary: The IDF revealed that Israel's Iron Beam laser defense system saw limited deployment during the Iran conflict due to a shortage of batteries, with 14 units needed. Officials noted Iron Beam's per-shot cost is negligible compared to Arrow and Iron Dome interceptors, which cost millions and tens of thousands of shekels respectively.

stories.title: No magic way to stop Hezbollah's FPV drones from striking, IDF admits
stories.summary: The IDF acknowledged it has no reliable method to fully counter Hezbollah's first-person-view drones striking Israeli positions. However, military officials suggested that removing US-imposed restrictions on IDF operations in northern Lebanon could reduce the drone threat by approximately 80 percent.

stories.title: IDF shifts focus to Iranian nuclear threat as ballistic missiles, regime change fall by the wayside
stories.summary: The Israeli Defense Forces are shifting strategic focus toward Iran's nuclear program, moving away from prioritizing ballistic missile threats or regime change. IDF officers clarified the military never promised regime change in Iran, only the possibility of creating conditions for such an outcome.

stories.title: Trump to put 25% tariffs on EU cars, says bloc not complying with trade deal
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced he would raise tariffs on European Union cars and trucks to 25 percent, accusing the bloc of not complying with a trade deal reached last July with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. The previous agreement had set tariffs at 15 percent on most goods.

stories.title: Israeli Air Force says it dropped 135,000 bombs in recent wars, warns of Syrian military rebuild
stories.summary: The Israeli Air Force disclosed it dropped 135,000 bombs during recent conflicts, including 23,860 munitions requested directly by ground forces for close support in Gaza and Lebanon. The IAF also warned about ongoing Syrian military rebuilding efforts.

stories.title: Andy Burnham has plan to return to Westminster ‘within weeks’, allies say
stories.summary: Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham reportedly has a plan to return to the UK Parliament within weeks through a byelection, with allies saying several Labour MPs are prepared to step aside. Burnham was previously blocked by Labour's ruling body from running in February's Gorton and Denton byelection.

stories.title: Trump’s assumptions are running his Iran policy aground—again
stories.summary: An analysis argues that President Trump's policy assumptions regarding Iran are proving counterproductive, highlighting the need for a more robust interagency decision-making process in Washington.
